english: It is not to be the case that the poor man is not being turned away from necessity. And perhaps what has been said concerning the poor man will be constructed [as an argument], for it is said in the Scripture, 'The rich became poor,' and 'We became very poor'; in agreement with these, what was said concerning the Savior will also be taken: 'As He became rich through our poverty, so that we might become rich through His poverty.'

This also agrees with that concerning the needy: the groaning of the needy, always being in distress and wailing because of the hardship of approaching the destitute. 'I will come' in salvation declares 'I will limit and I will make,' just as He also in the Being placed Himself as heir of all things, the word declaring He limited and manifested Himself as heir. Toward these things, God placed first the apostles and the following in the church, and what was said toward the presbyters of the church: 'The Holy Spirit has placed you to shepherd the church as bishops.' For the word 'placed' shows the demonstration of being limited and made into apostles and bishops.

According to this meaning of preserving, the Savior also said to the Father concerning the disciples: 'Holy Father, keep them; though I am not with them, I kept them, and the evil one did not touch them' (John 17:11). But if this is the meaning because of what was said in Genesis concerning Adam to the serpent: 'He shall guard your head, and you shall guard his heel,' is not 'to guard' (φυλάσαι) and 'to keep' (τηρεῖν) the same thing here? For it appears from it: 'He shall guard your head,' and 'you, his heel.'

The one who is praying sends back the prayer: 'You, Lord, will guard us,' after having done all things from Himself, according to the exhortation saying, 'Keep your heart with all vigilance.' And since these things being made right are not sufficient for the things we strive for against the unforeseen (for if the Lord does not guard a city, in vain the one guarding it stays awake [Ps 127:1]), it is a rule to bring forward a prayer after we have been guarded by ourselves, saying, 'You, Lord, will guard us and will preserve us.' For while He is guarding, let us be courageous, lest we be without counsel for ever; for He is the Most High, O Master, and existing in the high places, according to the approaching height of Your goodness, the [ones]...

You have grown up as a son of men, judging them worthy to have your protection from your providence (Ps 12:4b, 5a). Even if these things are spoken by the Holy [Spirit] in the manner of an embassy, they are not spoken by one subject to the oblivion of God, but by one receiving all things of the petition into himself; and it is clear that the things of his petition are not concerning a sensible light or sleep and death, but concerning the light from the knowledge of God.

For 'enlighten yourselves with the light of knowledge, and draw near to the Lord and be enlightened.' This enlightenment becomes not concerning the sight of the flesh (for this is the sight of the sun) nor any other sensible light of those seeing the sun of righteousness; it is the true light of the eyes of the heart, not of the body, for the noetic powers are the eyes of the inner man. To the one being enlightened, there is blessed life. 'For I am the light of the world,' says the Lord; 'he who walks in me,' he says, 'shall not remain in darkness but shall have the light of life' (John 8:12).

When death comes to the one having been enlightened, it is his sleeping into death, while the one sleeping and dying is the one being in the darkness of ignorance. For he who has given up his eyes to sleep through negligence and laziness will immediately die, falling away from the life which is with virtue; therefore, one must flee from this so-called sleep and death, so that, the eyes of the soul having been enlightened, the enemy may no longer be able to prevail against him, he who formerly thought that we had sinned. (Ps 12:5b, 6)

Since the enemies, those who afflict the righteous, rejoice (Ps 12:6); if it happens that a stumbling occurs because of sin, it is necessary to be grieved for those falling; but even if they rejoice at someone being shaken, I, O Lord, pity my hope in you, and I will not be persuaded to see in myself [the cause]. For I await your salvation coming soon, on which my heart rejoices; for how can he not be glad and rejoice who is experiencing the experience of God's salvation? And if prophecy is being declared concerning the coming of the salvation of God, the Christ, visit. For he, having come for the salvation of the world, brought down those who were leaning upon the shaking ones according to the soul, casting down with them the enemy who was exalting himself.

english: He has loftily enlightened the eyes, so that no one might see the death of the soul. He, having come to visit and having looked upon, ceased the pain; but when [the psalmist] has been made upright, the blessed gift is a victorious song, saying: 'I will sing to the Lord who has done good to me, and I will sing to the name of the Lord Most High' (Ps 109:1). Having truly learned what is said well by the Lord toward those who pray, while He is still speaking to you, I will say: 'Behold, I am here.' And He says these things to those who are present. Having happened to experience what I requested, therefore, through each goodness occurring to us, let us hymn, and let us also say the set hymn, not by contemplation alone but also by singing; for contemplation signifies the seeing, and singing signifies practical energy.

The foolish one lacks not common concepts, but the companionship of skill, rather the one of the virtues, wisdom, concerning which it is written: 'He who acquires wisdom loves himself, and he who guards wisdom will find good things' (Prov 3:7). But what is the natural companionship? The word declares, as if he is not obeying anyone but says in his own heart, 'There is no God' (Ps 10:4). For no one received the words concerning the denial of God. Almost all men, having an unswerving thought concerning God, the first verse has much familiarity, as has been said concerning the devil. For even he is not to anyone, but 'In his own mind': 'I will ascend to heaven, above the stars of heaven I will set my throne; I will be like the Most High' (Ps 108:21).

But as he who knows God keeps His word and turns His commandments into work, not so does everyone sinning, who comes to this by not knowing God; for John writes, that everyone sinning is far from having the knowledge of God, that everyone sinning has not seen Him nor known Him (1 John 3:9). Having cast out from the soul the piety which was preceding and ruling the virtues, [text ends abruptly].

Having space for it, one possesses virtues. But if the intellect is weak, it would be clear if it were to happen from the writings concerning the sons of Eli (1 Sam 2); for they, not knowing the Lord, proven plagues, were sinning, but rather they were impious regarding the priestly service, corrupting the duties of both the law and godliness.

The following will be taken and what is announced in Jeremiah (Jer 31:37) likewise: Offspring upon offspring, deceit upon deceit; all are committing adultery, a gathering of those breaking covenants, what has come out from evil into evil; but 'me he did not fear,' says the Lord. For how will it not be that, having ignorance of God, they are transgressors of his laws? These things being considered generally, it persuades that one has God in memory, so that we may be praised in duties, pursuing them with incorruptible intention.

Among those who have been defiled by corrupting the duties, no one doing goodness is found; for all are wicked, all goodness having been cut off because of hardness of heart (Ps 13:4–5). As wisdom will not enter into a craftily-made soul, nor does it dwell in a body guilty of sin, likewise he who works lawlessness does not receive divine knowledge; for no one sinning sees or knows God, according to that which is written in the Epistle of John (1 John). But he who desires to be a knower sows into righteousness, reaps the fruit of life, and will thus enlighten himself with the light of knowledge.

And since the enemies of the people of God are workers of lawlessness, as if to devour him, they are deprived of the knowledge of God; and someone, preferring to devour and harm him, [acts] according to: 'Bite each other and devour each other; see that you are not consumed by one another' (Lev 26:22). And in Isaiah (Isa 9:5) it is written likewise: 'Syria from the rising of the sun and the Greeks from the setting of the sun, devouring Israel with a maw of mouth.' But if ever they are able to devour the people of God delivered to them, they shall suffer judgment through sin; for Holy Israel belongs to the Lord.

english: The beginning of his judgments: all those eating him shall be filled with calamity, evil or violence upon them, says the Lord.

Those about to eat the people of God unjustly did not call upon the Lord, thinking to carry out all things by their own power and to tyrannize the people of God. For if they had known that they received him through the judgment of God by sin, they would have feared even more, lest they should fall under the same judgment. Therefore it is said to them, having become wilder than is proper: 'Though I was angry a little, they themselves pressed on to evils' (Ps 7:8). Thus, having tyrannized the people of God unjustly, they fell into cowardice. Therefore one should not fear a coward; for fear is not [present], if having received those delivered by the judgment of God, they approached them humanely and gently. But since they did all things harshly and without mercy, having fallen into cowardice, they laid waste to others. And this has risen up.

'Since God is in the generation of the righteous,' you will say, 'a generation of the righteous,' meaning the harmony of the righteous deeds in which the righteous judge is found, or the concord of righteous men and the commonality toward the same end. For if where two or three gather at his assembly, the Lord is found present, how much more would a whole generation of the righteous be found? And those who fulfill the same mind and life, even if they become a generation in different times, after this it would be said that time has called them to this. One who is cowed by a fear that is not fear; and he who fears man and once simply those killing the body, but not being able to kill the soul. For it is said, 'But do not fear anyone other than God.'

In connection with this passion, the Lord reproves Jerusalem saying: 'Who has not been reverent toward a mortal man?' (Ps 13:7). But as for the captivity of the people, it must first be viewed, so that we may subsequently see its return. He who falls away through his own laziness from the doing of good is taken captive by the law of sin, so as to have the power of death under the tyrantically devouring devil. This one, having been found having surrendered to the enemies outside the fatherland (and this is the partaking of virtue), is called back.

The Lord is submissive to the manner of repentance and to the forgiveness of those who have previously sinned; and this is the redeeming of the captives and the turning back of the captivity. When this has been fulfilled by the Lord's cross, as the people believing from the nations have been redeemed, Jacob rejoices. The same, according to the underlying meaning, is Jacob through thought alone, discerning the difference. For if one, doing good things and working according to virtue, overcomes the passions and evils and the working evil powers as a conqueror of them, he is Jacob rejoicing; but if, after the practical life, having obtained a pure heart, he sees God, he is Israel, a mind seeing God. For he does not receive into the voice of the Greeks a divine joy, being rejoiced; no one is grieved to take from a parallel passage the 'Let him rejoice and let him be glad' to be said.

85 Ps 14,1 See if the one living according to the law, having become the pedagogue unto Christ, dwells as a sojourner in the tabernacle of the Lord, wandering around the tent of the testimony. But the one having hastened unto Christ, having adhered to the evangelical teaching, dwells in the holy spirit of God, not another, but of the Son of God, concerning which it was prophetically said: 'The light of the Lord shall appear.' Stand firm, if it be rightly understood: the holy light of God is the God the Word, and his tabernacle is what the man took up. And it is necessary to know beforehand according to the flesh Christ, if he is the only-begotten according to the Father. He who says, 'Even if we have known according to the flesh Christ, but now we know no longer,' who has seen his glory, the glory as the only-begotten from the Father, dwells in the tabernacle, no longer a sojourner but dwelling in the holy spirit of God. And to him it is said: 'Ascend upon a high light,' he who evangelizes Zion. Therefore, the prophet, seeking an equal, says of the one able to say, 'Our citizenship exists in the heavens' (Phil 3:20), asks of the one to whom the Lord answers: 'Going...'

86 Ps 14,3 The one being erased from the appointed things, being a lover of brothers and a companion, hastens to be wise, spending time with the wise, turning himself away from all the weakness of the foolish, lest he be known as one of them. If therefore he turns away from the bad ones, but has understanding with the good (for the wise are good ones).

english: He does not accept reproach from those approaching him, those who always reproach those who have evils approaching them as if they were praising their neighbors and having good friends. To this, the speaker is indifferent: 'Walking in an unblemished way, it did not work for my benefit; speaking righteousness, it did not direct itself before my eyes' (Ps 14:4c).

And the word of an oath of a man is unsearchable, upon which the 'Yes, yes' and 'No, no' are confirmed. If even at times there is a need for God to be a witness to the word toward the 'No', he does this unpretentiously, just as the prophetic apostle leaves behind a pattern and a guide in the Epistles, who says: 'God is my witness, whom I serve in the gospel of his Son' (Luke 22:60); and 'No': 'I call God as witness upon my soul' (Acts 20:26); and again: 'God, who is over all, is my witness, I do not lie' (1 Tim 4:5). For this is an ungraspable faith; for an oath is nothing other than a word with God's witness, a thing being confirmed by God's witness. And however an oath may be held, it does not invalidate an oath to a neighbor.

And it is also to lend spiritually without offspring, as it is signified by what was said to the disciples of Jesus by the Teacher: 'And do not turn away from the one who wishes to borrow from you' (Luke 6:35). For how could anyone say this perceptibly to those saying, 'We have left all and followed you' (Matt 19:21), or those saying with boldness, 'Silver and gold I do not have' (Matt 19:24)? Since, therefore, to lend perceptibly to the saints (whenever it is said they do this) is described, it is necessary to take this spiritually; the one lending must take the intelligible teaching word instead of silver for the sake of gaining something corporeal. For if even those sowing spiritual things receive the fleshly [things] only to be fed (for worthy is the laborer of his food [Luke 10:7]), they do not lend in this way; for they do not receive silver according to the value of the logical [spiritual] things given, but the only food.

And he shall not be shaken forever, because he remained through life having steeled himself in virtues (Ps 14:5ab). For this is the same as what is said here: 'I shall not eat meat forever,' and 'He shall be your slave forever.' He who has heard the words of Jesus and has done them remains unshakeable forever.

For he possesses the houses of his own citizenship, which are named as those having their foundations laid upon Christ, called a rock. They are not as firm as those concerning whom Jesus says, 'Whoever believes in me shall live forever' (John 11:25). There are some such as are standing; and what the apostle writes concerning them: 'Having been founded and rooted in love' (Ephesians 3:17). If that which is not to be shaken for eternity shows a greater endurance of an age, similarly examine the one said: 'And everyone who lives and believes in me shall live forever' (John 11:25).

The saints, remaining unshakeable for eternity, will perfect their life, not being limited by time but remaining always; and this is a symbol of their pillar of victory (Ps 15:1a). And this 'pillar-writing' of David is a prefiguration of the psalm to be set forth. For the deeds of those being destroyed and no longer existing do not turn out to be such; nor do the deeds of sinners have the quality of not remaining. For it is said that the enjoyment of sin is temporary, and that the sin of the sinner and the evil one will not be found. But the life of the saints is not such; for they look toward the things not seen and eternal. It is said, therefore, concerning each of them: 'His righteousness remains for the age of ages.' And since it is called a pillar in another way, as scriptures elsewhere lay down laws calling them tablets and boards, it should be called a 'pillar-writing' of the saints, who have handed down teachings written not on stone tablets but on fleshly tablets, that is, having ears and hearts favorable and well-receiving toward the writing. How he possesses the things of the prefiguration of the psalm, we shall see when God reveals it.

Since I have put my hope in you, O Lord, protect me (Ps 15:1b). For I will not be able to endure harmlessly, with myriads of enemies both visible and invisible attacking. Having prayed these things, he brought forth: 'The Lord is my Lord' (Ps 16:2). Who, sinning, is able to confirm this with his voice? For a slave who makes himself a sinner cannot serve God; for no one, he says, can serve two masters (Matt 6:24). Let it be said also in another way regarding the matter at hand. The apostle writes: 'No one can say, Jesus is Lord, except in the Holy Spirit' (1 Cor 12:3), meaning to say this by deed and disposition. For if it were merely spoken, it would be true...

english: It will not be so, with myriads of heretics and hypocrites saying it is mere utterance and not having the Holy Spirit of God. For the Savior himself says: 'Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord' (Matt 7:22); and I, he says, will confess to them, 'Depart from me, workers of iniquity, I never knew you' (Matt 7:23). And again: 'Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do what I say?' (Luke 6:46). Therefore, the one saying 'Lord Jesus' in the Holy Spirit, not in mere utterance but in diligent work and true disposition, is truly a servant, just as when you hear with the apostles, 'You call me Lord and Teacher, and you say well, for I am so.'

Thus, the one announcing the foregone things by a practical and contemplative life has established an unshakeable pillar crying out, 'If you are my Lord' (Ps 15:2). And since you turn out to be my Lord, I offer you gifts from your own dogmas, not as to one in need; for they, as not having need of our good things, receive them in order to grant back something far more excessive and greater. And not only through things presented sensuously, but also through spiritual things must the voice be presented.

For we perform virtues, as we manage our own bodies through complete temperance. We are what God accepts, not for our own benefit, but as those who ask him to give us the good things from heaven; for for whose grace does God seek human virtue, if not so that he might grant higher things instead of those which we offer to him? The holy ones of God dwell upon his earth (Ps 15:3a). And this heavenly Jerusalem is that in which they have a citizenship in heaven, even as they dwell on earth.

He never says 'not to gather their assemblies,' but 'out of blood' (Ps 15:4bc); nor does he say 'not to remember their names,' but 'through my lips' (Ps 15:4bc). Perhaps, when there are some gathering assemblies out of blood, pouring them out to harm those gathered, he is himself benefiting, rather vivifying those who are called, gathering them not out of blood but out of immortality, remembering their characteristics, not out of superficiality but having depth of disposition. It will also be said thus: even if many prophets and apostles were killed, their blood being poured out, it is not in these many blood-offerings [that the truth lies].

I will gather the assemblies of them, but only into the one single eye of the spotless and unblemished Christ; for this honor is given, so that they might be liberated from their vain, ancestral conduct. Concerning those who have been thus liberated, he will remember not by word alone, but by deep insight. [Ps 15:5a] He who has become above all the world possesses no other portion and inheritance than God; for everyone must renounce all things, so that one might be able to say, 'My portion is God unto the age of ages.' And as for the seed of the inheritance, it is also the cup that brings joy to the righteous portion, the Lord.

It is worth observing how the Lord becomes a cup for someone. Never does he provide moral instruction and thereby nourish the man in secret, becoming bread, supporting the heart of the eater; but he is also a cup according to the theory of truth, providing joy to the one drinking through the agreement of the illumination of knowledge. This cup is provided by the true vine so that the mind might be made to drink and be made glad, as one might graciously say, 'Esau has taken joy into my heart.' [Ps 15:6] And you will understand thus: he who has God harmoniously and his [possessions] will enjoy.

For he who has the Lord as a portion of the inheritance and his [possessions] will enjoy, saying, 'You are the one restoring my inheritance to me'; but he does not restore this, saying, 'Come, inherit the kingdom prepared for you'; for if he is the same, [he says], 'My portion is in the land of the living.' Regarding this spiritual inheritance, given by analogy to faith and excellent life to the heirs, it is fitting that the measuring line fell upon me among the best; for the cord is a symbol of measure and lot.

Indeed, concerning the sensible earth, into which the Hebrews were led by Joshua the son of Nun, being divided, it has been written many times: 'And the cord fell upon the tribe of Judah, and upon Reuben, the other of the twelve, upon this climate, the eastern one, and another past this.' Having observed these things, he who says, 'The measuring line fell upon me among the best,' demonstrates that good things were distributed to him, having entered into the best parts of the inheritance, which his lot shows through these spiritual geometric cords.

english: Such a measuring line an angel holds in his hand to the prophet Zechariah, in order to measure how much the length and width of the true Jerusalem is. Furthermore, it is said: 'For indeed my inheritance is most strong for me,' (Ps 15:5) signifying through this that my inheritance truly becomes the most beautiful.

According to this, the signified 'strongest' is the God, whom Luke the evangelist writes about. Let no one consider the spoken word unsuitable for Christ (Ps 15:7). For if he needed an angelic measurement to show the human, what time would that be? If he was being wise regarding divinity from nature, being wise as God and source of wisdom, yet being wise as a man.

Since the following are said from the face of Christ (Ps 15:8), and the saying—the face from the Lord is my portion of inheritance (Ps 15:8)—is preserved without any change, whoever takes these verses spoken by the Lord does not sin. But those not having their thoughts about God properly ordered take them locally: that the Son is at the right hand of the Father because of 'Sitting at my right hands,' and that the Savior has sat after the ascension at the right hands of majesty, which is impossible to say. For if the Son is at the right hand of the Father locally, it is impossible for the Father to be at the right hand of the Son according to that same meaning; but the Son says: 'I saw the Lord at my right hand' (Ps 16:8). Therefore, it is not otherwise, according to place, to miss the Son at the right of the Father and the Father of the Son, just as 'I am in the Father and the Father in me' (John 10:30) is.

It must be observed, with the Savior understood as man and God, whether it is necessary to interpret these things according to the divinity or according to his economy according to the flesh. But it is not possible to piously take that the Word of God has spoken from the face of God the Father at his right hand and before himself, in such a way that he might remain unshakeable. For the God Word is unturning, nor is he existing by any amount of turning.

Since he denies the reason for the Word not being shaken, who is in the Father and at the right hand of the Father (for he is being in the Father and having him in himself, existing at the right hand and before him), the reason becomes that he who sees him and has him at the right hand is not shaken. Since therefore he denies this, it is rather impious to take these things regarding the only-begotten Son of God apart from his economy according to the flesh; it must be spoken harmoniously, he who has become truly human and humbled himself and became poor while being rich (2 Cor 8:9). For the human has become his, made like us in all things without sin; but his flesh was not without soul, as some wrongly thought. For how could flesh not having a soul say 'he has at the right hand a God and sees him always' so as not to sin? For a sinning movement arises from being shaken.

If these things are impossible (for the body does not see God, nor does it possess the thought of him who is at the right hand and before him), it remains, according to the economy, to speak these things humanly by the Word of God having become flesh truly, perfectly, and truthfully; for he will speak all things from one person, both the God-befitting and the human, as a man indeed has become, having the God at his right hand, he will not be shaken even if bitter things surround him, or if the kings of the earth stand against him and the rulers gather together against the Lord and against his Christ. For indeed, not having been shaken in soul, he did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth, having been tested in all things according to likeness without sin. Furthermore, it is brought forward how his heart rejoiced and his tongue exulted (Ps 34:10) over having the Lord at the right hand and before himself always. It is a praiseworthy exultation and gladness, he who does not become so because of chance things, but because of understanding.

english: From these syllables, it is most clearly shown that the Lord became man; for his soul, the flesh having been laid in the tomb, was in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights, having risen with the flesh, having severed the soul from the body. It is said that the flesh tabernacled in hope because of the resurrection that is to come; for it was not dissolved, suffering any corruption, but having remained unharmed, it was joined again to the soul which was not abandoned to Hades. But if the destined soul, being separated from flesh, stands existing even in Hades, then it is clear that the rational souls of men are not being; for the rational soul, being separated from flesh, does not stand existing, nor does it go into Hades. But truly the soul of Jesus has experienced both; for it has become both in the place of human souls, and having become outside of the flesh, it lives and stands; it is indeed rational and of the same essence as the souls of men, just as the flesh, having come forth from Mary, is of the same essence as the flesh of men. Even if it seemed to have suffered because of the cross, it was not destroyed; the fact that both soul and flesh remained unharmed, having been joined together again, was demonstrated. Again, the holiness of God has not seen corruption, but is also the cause of the resurrection of the others, the dead; for having become the firstborn from the dead, he, our corruptible and mortal being, having clothed himself in incorruption, undergoes death together with the holy of God who has not seen corruption.

The incarnate Word of God, having risen from the dead, sings praises (Ps 15:11), in that he has become man without abandoning even his being as God, having revealed to him the paths leading to eternal life, so that he may be filled with perfect joy, filling the saints with all spiritual joy. His image is the face of God and the character of his substance. And what follows the one who has walked the known paths of life, to have divine delight in the truth and wisdom of God's right hand? And this is the only-begotten Son of God. And since the delight in the right hand of God is found to be unsurpassed, it will be an end that is not sought by any other; for all things have come to pass not for the sake of another, but for its own sake (Ps 15:11).

Some people, acting with arrogance, judge the one praying as being of moderate character; no one would say, 'Hear, O Lord, my righteousness, and let my judgment come forth from your face' (Ps 16:3). But David, not being arrogant, while doing all the will of God, but desiring to be judged with goodness, prayed that his judgment might come forth from the divine face. 'Let my eyes see straightness' (Ps 16:3). One prays to see straightness with the eyes of a man, by which God judges, bringing the judgment forth from his own face; one prays to behold the virtue of straightness. If, however, he prays to see it, he does not yet possess it; thus he is advised not to be arrogant by the way he offers the prayer. These things regarding perfect virtue should be considered, if anyone ever becomes greater than those previously foretold.

And through these things, much boldness of the speaker is manifest (Ps 16:3). For if he says these things concerning God, he manifests much of his own purity; for the heart of everyone who endures in obscurity is tested, and he who is afflicted in everything is not distressed, but enduring until the end, he is proven righteous; such as Job, to whom God said: 'If perhaps I may prove you, you shall be more righteous than I' (Job 2:9). [Or: If it is possible that I may prove you, that you may appear righteous, in the testing of your heart by the Lord and being refined and no iniquity being found in you?]. It is worth following to see what is meant by 'I visited in the night' (Ps 16:3); and indeed, if he calls the state of those in obscurity 'night' because of the dimness and having nothing propitious, in which God, having visited him, left him proven and, having refined through afflictions, showed him clean from all iniquities. It is said, 'I visited in the night' (Ps 16:3) and not thus: because the hidden things of the heart are not manifest to anyone except to Him to whom it is said, 'You alone know the hearts of men'; it was named night, and even those things, although they are dark to others because of the inscrutable, to you, who tested me by visiting me in the night, have been revealed. To this, 'If I had considered iniquity in my heart, do not hear me, Lord' (Ps 16:3) is conjoined.
To declare the works of men and dispositions, even in word, is evil (Ps 16:4a). But what are these works, those about which the apostle writes: 'For where there is jealousy among you...'

Τὸ δὲ ̓Εν σκέπῃ τῶν πτερύγων σου σκεπάσεις με πνευματικῶς ἐκληπτέον· αἱ γὰρ σκεπαστικαὶ τοῦ θεοῦ δυνάμεις πτέρυγες αὐτοῦ καλοῦνται, δι' ω ν σκέπει καὶ εἰς εὐθυμίαν α γει τὸν παρακαλοῦντα ἐξαιρεθῆναι ἀπὸ ἀσεβῶν τῶν ταλαιπωρίαν κατ' αὐτοῦ διανοουμένων. ου τοι δὲ ἀόρατοί τινές εἰσιν ἐχθροὶ ταλαιπώρους ποιοῦντες τοὺς ἁλισκομένους πρὸς αὐτῶν τῷ ὑποβαλεῖν αὐτοὺς ἁμαρτίᾳ. 106 Ps 16,9b–11 Τὸ α γριον καὶ ὠμὸν τῶν ἀνθισταμένων σημαίνει διὰ τοῦ εἰπεῖν περιέχεσθαι τὴν ψυχὴν ἑαυτοῦ ὑπὸ τῶν ἐχθρῶν αὐτοῦ συγκλεισάντων τὸ στέαρ αὐτῶν διὰ τὴν πρὸς υ λην προσπάθειαν. ο λοι γὰρ δι' ο λων ὑλικοὶ καὶ σάρκινοι, πεπραμένοι ὑπὸ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, τυγχάνουσιν καὶ ἀπὸ πολλῆς εὐθυμίας καὶ τρυφῆς στέατος ω σπερ καὶ πιμελῆς ἐπληροῦντο. διὸ ὁ Σύμμαχος Τῷ στέατι αὐτῶν ἀπεφράγησαν· διὸ καὶ λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν ὑπερηφανίαν, οὐδὲν φιλικὸν η καθῆκον εὐσταθῶς προφερόντων. ου τοι οἱ ἐχθροὶ ἀπὸ πολλῆς ἀλαζονείας ἐκβάλλοντες οἱονεὶ τὸν ταῦτα λέγοντα περικυκλοῦσιν ἐπὶ τῷ βλάψαι καὶ ἀπολέσαι τὸν ἐντὸς ἀρκύων γεγενημένον. οὐ γὰρ χρηστόν τι η ἀγαθὸν ἐπιτηδεύουσιν, ἐπεὶ παραβάται θείων νόμων γεγενημένοι διὰ τοῦ τοὺς
english: Are you not men and walking according to man? The works of men happen to be a hindrance to speaking, and the failure to find [truth] in him, having been ignited by God through trials and those nearby (Ps 16:4b).

The paths bearing one toward virtue seem to be hard, having much roughness; for how is the path not hard, which commands the one being struck to a place beyond the jaws, and the rest of the hand to receive insult? In addition to this, a rough path seems to be one through which someone struggles toward death for the sake of the truth. And it is, through injuries, the most bitter of threats, of fire and iron and the assault of wild beasts, the completion of this; except even if these paths and those related to them are hard, they are guarded because of the words of the lips of the protecting God, and they are made smooth as if they were no longer something hard or heavy. For John indeed writes, 'And his commandments are not heavy' (1 John 5:3), and Jesus says to those hearing his words, 'My yoke is good and my burden is light' (Matt 11:30). For from much habituation and training, approaching without interruption, the heavy things appear most light, and the bitter and joyless things are made upright with much ease.

But the paths of the Lord and of his saints happen to be the keeping of the commandments (Ps 16:5a), rather the energies according to virtue, being shown to be smooth and even, having been developed from constantly suffering [toil] by those hurrying to reach their end; and their end is blessedness and the fulfillment of the promises. Let us therefore run according to them, so that we may find salvation, not wavering in our steps, that is to say, not stumbling. And if the Lord should prepare them in his paths, he says of one having obtained this request: 'I ran without lawlessness and directed myself, and I ran the path of your commandments' (Ps 16:6), and 'You have enlarged my heart' (Ps 16:7).

'I have cried out' (Ps 16:7) is to be heard spiritually; for it is not necessary to have cried out toward the invisible God with a loud voice, but with an attentive mind; this is the cry of the inner man. His mercies are wonderful upon those hoping in him, even if they have something more paradoxical regarding the mercies having become through favor, as the God inclining toward us hears the words of the voice.

Nothing else is our power, but the power descending through goodness to receive our words. For this, the eyes of the Lord shall be upon the righteous, and his eyes toward them for their prayer (Ps 16:8).

The right hand of God will be no other than his only-begotten Son, as was said a little earlier: 'Delight is at your right hand unto the end' (Ps 16:7). The devil and his angels, and with them sorcerers and evil men, stand against this, from whom the holy one desires to remain harmless, saying to God: 'Protect me from those standing at your right hand, according to the pupil of my eye, so that my mind may remain harmless; but also cover me in the shelter of your wings from the face of the impious who desire to surround me with misery' (Ps 16:8). It is possible to call the impious and those opposing the right hand of God in various ways, according to the underlying subject. But the voice 'Protect me as the pupil of the eye' does not belong to everyone, but only to the one having been enlightened according to the soul, having the eyes of the heart enlightened. And 'In the shelter of your wings you will cover me' is to be understood spiritually; for the covering powers of God are called his wings, through which he covers and for the sake of good cheer protects the one beseeching to be rescued from the impious who are planning misery against him. For indeed, there are certain invisible enemies making misery for those being caught by them, by bringing them under sin.

The wild and raw [nature] of those standing against signifies, by saying, that his soul is being enclosed by his enemies who have shut their canopy because of the striving toward matter (Ps 16:9). For the others, through [their] lusts, are material and fleshy, having been overcome by sin, and they are being shut out from much good cheer and luxury, just as wheat and oil used to be filled. Therefore, the Ally was blocked from their canopy; therefore also their mouths speak pride, not steadily bearing anything friendly or appropriate. For indeed, the enemies, casting out from much arrogance, surround the one saying these things in order to harm and destroy the one who has become sheltered within. Καὶ τῶν κεκρυμμένων σου ἐπλήσθη ἡ γαστὴρ αὐτῶν· κεκρυμμένα δὲ θεοῦ τὰ ἀνάξια τῆς μνήμης αὐτοῦ, ω ν πάντων τὰ κατάλοιπα τοῖς νηπίοις κατέλειπον μετὰ τὸ πλησθῆναι τὴν κοιλίαν αὐτῶν. ο τι δὲ ἀνάξια τῶν ο ψεων τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ ἐπίληπτα, παρίσταται ἐκ τοῦ Κάϊν ( ̓Εξῆλθεν γὰρ ου τος ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ θεοῦ) καὶ ἐκ τοῦ Οὐ διαμένουσι παράνομοι κατέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν σου. Φέρεται γραφὴ ε χουσα ̓Εχορτάσθησαν υἱῶν· δι' ου ς υἱωνοὺς εἰς κόρον ε σχον. διαμερισθέντες ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ἑαυτῶν, πολύτροπον τὴν βλάβην ε σχον. οὐ μόνον γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ νήπιοι αὐτῶν ἐκορέσθησαν τῶν κεκρυμμένων τοῦ θεοῦ. 109 Ps 16,15 ̓Εκεῖνοι μὲν ου τω, φησίν, καθ' α ει ρηται, ̓Εγὼ δὲ ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ὀφθήσομαι τῷ προσώπῳ σου· οὐ γὰρ τῶν κρυπτομένων ἀπὸ σοῦ ἡ ἀρετὴ ὡς ἡ ἐκείνων κακία. κἀκεῖνοι μὲν αὐθάδεις ο ντες καὶ οἰόμενοι πάντων ει ναι πλήρεις μηδὲν ε χοντες ὡς ἀπεντεῦθεν δοκεῖν αὐτοὺς κεχορτάσθαι, ἐγὼ δὲ ἐκ μέρους γινώσκων α ρτι τότε χορτασθήσομαι, ο τ' α ν ὀφθῇ ἡ δόξα σου ὑφισταμένη κατὰ τὸ ἐρχόμενον τέλειον, ῳ προσβάλλειν τότε δυνατὸν Πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον. δυνατὸν ὀφθησομένην θεοῦ δόξαν ἐκλαβεῖν τὸν μονογενῆ υἱὸν περὶ ου γέγραπται· Οψεται πᾶσα σὰρξ τὸ σωτήριον αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὀφθήσεται ἡ δόξα κυρίου. πληροῦται τούτων ε καστον, ο τ' α ν Θεασώμεθα τὴν δόξαν τοῦ υἱοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας. 110 Ps 17,1 Συναριθμείσθωσαν δὲ τοῖς ἐχθροῖς τοῖς ἀφ' ω ν ἐρρύσθη καὶ ἀόρατοι διάφοροι. ̔Ρηθείη δὲ καὶ πρὸς ἑκάστην λέξιν τὰ φαινόμενα. english: That their eyes are set upon the earth, turning aside and becoming lawless; for this is shown by having set their eyes upon the earth, wanting to observe the passing things and thinking of earthly things, turning aside from not wanting to walk the straight way, but being tossed about by crooked paths. For, they say, those abandoning the straight ways of going, they go in ways of darkness, whose ways are crooked and winding. Not indeed they set their eyes upon the earth, but those bearing the image of the heavenly are setting their eyes upon heaven in order to straighten the straight way that leads up to the heavens (Ps 16:13-14a).

Since you are long-suffering, that you might sleep, you do not receive justice from them who were cutting [me] murderously, Arise therefore, O Lord, that you might cause them to be overshadowed (Ps 16:13). For they will understand having suffered this, so that not always running toward evil they might increase their destruction; for surrounding my soul and doing other things, if not prevented, they harm it most greatly. Therefore overshadow them, so that they may no longer be able against me, you having rescued my soul from each one being such and therefore being named ungodly; for rescue my soul from the ungodly (Ps 16:14). He will take his sword from their hands; for they received it given unrighteously. And they take [it] from them not using it as is necessary. Therefore also in the earth they are few, that is to say, they are cheapened. For those becoming about material and worthless things, striving for them, cast away from the soul its dignity and the wealth it possesses, unless they set the material before them. Therefore also they are not called as in the [unspecified]... Thy rod to those who are not (Ps 16:14b-15).

Of those agreeing upon evil and being of one mind, the division of life is useful; for having set to do evil, being of one mind, they cast [it] away, becoming incomplete, having rebelled against them, as it has happened regarding the building of a tower and a city upon evil for themselves; for God, benefiting them, was holding their tongues together, so that they might no longer know anything said by their neighbors, so that the [unspecified]...

An ignorance, having taken hold, prepares them to turn back upon themselves, showing their purpose to be incomplete. This is what is made manifest in 'They are divided in their lives' and 'Their bellies were filled with your hidden things' (Ps 16:15). For the things unworthy of God's remembrance are hidden, whereas He leaves all the remnants to the infants after their bellies have been filled. What is unworthy of God's things that they seize upon is shown by Cain (for he went out from the presence of God [Gen 4:16]) and by those who do not remain lawful before your eyes. These, having become far from God, have been overwhelmed, and the remnants are left to their infants, having been gorged on filth. For among all those who corrupt, those who harm themselves and become a harm to others are more severe, which is shown by 'And he left the remnants to his infants.' For it is not possible to deceive those who truly are; therefore it is written concerning them: 'Because they wronged the infants, they shall be slain, and the scrutiny shall condemn the ungodly' (Ps 109:8). A scripture is brought forward: 'The sons were gorged; through the sons they ate filth.' Having been divided in their lives, they ate a manifold harm. For not only they, but also their infants were satiated with the hidden things of God.

They indeed are not, he says, as it is said, 'But I shall be seen in righteousness before your face' (Ps 16:15); for the virtue of the hidden ones from you is not like their wickedness. And those, being self-willed and thinking they are full of all things, having nothing, it seems they were sent to be gorged; but I, knowing in part, shall be satiated then, when your glory shall be seen standing according to the coming perfection, to face a Person face to face. It is possible to receive the glory of God when the Only-begotten Son is seen, as it is written: 'All flesh shall see his salvation, and the glory of the Lord shall be seen' (Luke 2:30). This is fulfilled in this, that we might behold the glory of the Son, a glory as the Only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. And they were counted among the enemies from whom he was rescued, and they are invisible differences. And the phenomena shall be spoken against each word. To the end.

english: It says, to the child of the Lord, David. A conclusion to be taken from these things is victory over all enemies; for on account of this both wars and everything contributing to the excellence of a king exist. And it is rightly said that it is not the other things, but this itself, that triumphs. For since victory exists, it is not necessary to give thanks to anyone else but to God who granted it. For it is said to him by Ezra: 'From you is the victory.'

David refers the song to the Lord, as his child and servant, having wisely and faithfully expressed all the words of thanksgiving on that day (that is, in that light), in which all the enemies and Saul the king of Israel were overthrown, and David was rescued unharmed from them. And these things are [said] as regarding the history.

But since it seems to many of the faithful that the song is present from the face of the Savior, it must be said that the triumphal hymn is to be spoken concerning the resurrection from the dead, his being rescued from all the guarding nations and the empty peoples who studied [to destroy him], but also from the kings who stood against him and the rulers gathered against him. And you say that he was rescued also from the hand of Saul, who was then ruling the Jews, in a certain way; for it was not an inaccurate representation of their manner, being wrathful and having with them an evil spirit, saying they did not have a god for a king; for how could they not be about to deny God, to be ruled by some base person? (Ps 17:5b,6).

'Streams of iniquity' were called, as another says, and because of entering into iniquity those who do not bravely stand against the trials. And if the preceding words concern the death that follows those who sin, and the harmony having with it slavery, then the pains of death and slavery are the sins that exist toward death. In accordance with this understanding, you will say 'streams of iniquity' [referring to] the currents of wickedness, and 'snares of death' [referring to] those which practically constitute sins toward death.

According to the previous explanation, the present passages fit the economy of the Lord according to the flesh. For 'My soul is greatly troubled, and my soul is very sorrowful near death' (Ps 17:7) possesses much intimacy with the Now.

Prayer has much boldness from a pure conscience, since to call upon the Lord is not a mere report, but to cry out to God. Lest it be not in agreement with us that God is the Father and Jesus Christ is Lord. We shall call God the Father and the Son Lord, unless both are said of the same one as Father and Son of God and Lord, being through the same divinity and lordship. How then, having said 'He heard my voice from His holy temple?' (Ps 17:7) It is said metaphorically that his cry enters into the ears of God. To this, one says: that having heard God, the one who prayed will become out of the distress, believing that, having cried again to God, he receives him into the ears and before him the upward-sent cry. Another saying: the one who perceived through the calling from His holy temple that the Paraclete had breathed upon him, is emboldened that he will find the outcome of those things for which he cried, the cry being sent up from a pure disposition into the ears of God and before Him.

These oracles remove from the deceived those having faith like a grain of mustard seed (Ps 17:8b); for if Paul says that faith as a grain of mustard seed removes [them]. Among these was also the spirit of moon-sickness about which the Savior says: 'If you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you say to this mountain, Move from here to there' (Ps 17:9). english: They sent up smoke, which is consumed by the coming wrath, making coals. Coals were kindled from it. These coals signify, on the one hand, punishments, and on the other hand, the piercing, hot words of God that purify the thoughts of the soul.

Punishments are signified in: 'If your enemy hungers, feed him; if he thirsts, give him drink; for so doing you will heap coals of fire on his head' (Rom 12:20). And in: 'Coals of fire shall fall upon them, and you shall cast them down; they shall not help you' (Isa 51:6). The piercing word is shown in Isaiah: 'And he was sent among the seraphim.' Thus, prepared for the virtue of the soul, it warms and fires the thoughts to show them bright and splendid, but it will consume the deeds of sinners while purifying them; those not receiving this fire will be consumed by the eternal fire.

The phrase 'He inclined the heavens and came down' (Ps 18:10) follows the word concerning the economy and the descent. Since the Savior is said to dwell in the heavens, having become man, he changes his dwelling; for he became lowly and walked among men on earth. He dwells in the heavens not locally, nor does he descend transitively (for these are things pertaining to bodies), but according to the saying 'he dwells in the heavens.' For existing in the form of God, having taken the form of a servant, he descended, without any local change occurring to him.

And 'He rode upon the cherubim and flew' (Ps 18:10). The cherubim are understood as a voice for a multitude of knowledge; there is much knowledge there, but more ungraspable. One ascending from there flies through an elevated and ethereal intellect. It should not be thought that the name signifies the fullness of knowledge possessed by immortal animals. And God, having ascended upon these rational animals, flies through sharp intellect.

'He spread himself upon the wings of the winds' (Ps 134:1). If the saying is taken regarding the sensible winds, it means God, according to His providential word, mounting the wings of the winds, that is, by their lifting up as He Himself wills; for 'He draws out the winds from His treasuries' (Job 37:9). But if one were to take the winds as those blowing like judgments, lifting up wise men being moved by the spirit,

God rides upon the wings of these, which are higher and more lofty thoughts. There are winds of teaching, as the Apostle Paul says regarding heretics, speaking of every wind of teaching in the cunning of men, in craftiness toward the method of error. But not as false teachers are the winds upon whose wings the wandering spirits of the people ride; rather, God, riding upon the wings of every wind of true teaching, blows where He wills. And this is to be spread upon the wings of winds.

Previously and truly, the God who dwells is unapproachable light, the Son who is true light, and the Holy Spirit who is the possession of knowledge and wisdom, just as of this light it is said, 'And the light is with Him' (John 1:14). Secondly, by reason of the incomprehensibility concerning His essence, it is said that His hiddenness is called darkness. For that which is indistinct and incomprehensible because of the depth of the matter is called darkness. In this way, it is said that He perceives a parable and a dark speech; and God, uncovering the deeps out of darkness, makes manifest and clear those things hidden under indistinctness and difficulty of comprehension.

His tabernacle is around Him. Just as he who is contained under a tabernacle cannot be seen unless he has entered into it, so also the God surrounded by indistinctness and difficulty of comprehension cannot be seen unless one has entered into the interior of the covering of that difficulty. Immediately, regarding Moses, it is said how he entered into the cloud where God was (Exodus 19:9). For having understood the thought, the creation, and the providence concerning God, he knew that God is contained by these; thus, having slightly passed through this tabernacle concerning Him, he might behold from the image (which is not the image) the one according to the image, and from the creation and providence, the Creator and Provider.

In many places of the Scripture, we find clouds being carried allegorically. For he who said 'the vineyard of Israel,' speaking of clouds receiving commands not to rain upon it, we find no others but the prophets. It is not only with them that 'Thus says the Lord' and 'The word of the Lord came to me' are found; until these clouds, the truth shines. For these clouds are souls.

english: Flowing as a rain of spiritual words, they are of the air, not of the earth; for having detached themselves from earthly things and no longer thinking of them, they are lifted up and exalted by their own virtue and by the active spirit of the air.

The water within them, before having attained clarity and manifestation through Jesus, is said to be a dark thing, being difficult for the many to see. But when God has spoken in the Son at the end of days, the law and the prophets shall be fulfilled: they shall come together before him in a bright shining (that is to say, his illumination), visible clouds and distinct, because of the presence of what was pre-proclaimed by them (Ps 17:13b–15).

Since no apology remains for those sinning, coming out of dark clouds into light through clarity, there immediately follows the bright shining of the clouds with hail and coals of fire. This is signified by the punishments through the pre-proclamations and having attained the manifestation of what was prophesied concerning Christ.

God immediately thunders from heaven, either through the loud voice of the words being fulfilled by Jesus, or by casting the highest words of theology concerning the only-begotten Son into each mind, not only having cried out this: 'This is my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased,' but also the Most High gives a voice to those who discourse highly concerning Christ, who did not reveal his own Son to them in flesh, but the Father in heaven revealed his own Son.

Just as for those prepared in mind for the vision of God and the hearing of the Word, the Lord thunders from heaven and the Most High gives his voice, so that, being lifted up by the thunder coming from heaven, they may fall away from earthly things and fly toward heaven, bearing the image of the heavenly, and may receive the high things of the thoughts being given by the Most High; but to those who are of contrary disposition, the Lord sends arrows sufficient to throw into confusion those who previously were of one mind concerning evil.
But now the arrows say the words pre-proclaiming the punishments; for the threats are sufficient to disturb and agitate the soul, and he shall clarify even the threats spoken in enigmas...

He will light up like lightning, and will throw into confusion those scattered by the aforementioned arrows. For those being scattered cast off their agreement toward evil, having become in turmoil and confusion.

[Ps 17:16a] When all the aforementioned things have happened, the springs of the waters will be seen. And if someone says that the springs of the waters are those sown among us concerning God and good thoughts, he will say that these will be seen when the ignorance and malice lying upon the soul are withdrawn. For these, having been removed, will not hide the springs of good things in us. But if someone says that every God-breathed scripture, though spiritual, is veiled by ambiguity, [he says] that the springs will be seen; stand firm! For if we turn now to the Lord, the veil of ignorance and ambiguity will be removed, and the springs of the waters lying within will be seen, so that it is easy to draw from each one, according to [Ps 36:9] 'Draw water with joy from the springs of salvation.' For this water of gladness is a part of the being of the springs of salvation, which were granted to the discerning one, and now he sees God, according to [Ps 34:8] 'Bless the Lord in the churches, O Israel, from the springs.'

[Ps 17:16bc] He acts through the building up of the inhabited world and says, and thinks of certain foundations; he is not speaking of the sins and dispositions of yours when he speaks of the foundations of the inhabited world. For if he scatters the wicked with his arrows and throws them into confusion, by the flashing of his lightning, making the hidden things of men become manifest, by the lighting of God of the secrets of darkness and by making manifest the foundations of the inhabited world, he will uncover the deep things from darkness from the rebuke of the inhabited world by him over all. And if someone says that the foundations of the inhabited world are the divine men, because of the goodness of life and the narrowness of virtue upon which those living according to Christ are built, the uncovering of these foundations too will happen, through the occurrence of a rebuke. For the uncovering and revealing of these foundations will not happen without the punishment of these [sinners].
[Ps 17:16d] God does not delay the punishments for those sinning. For if this were to happen, all would be utterly lost. But by goodness...

english: Because of great human-lovingness, even though a multitude of sins occurs constantly, He does not bring down wrath for every single day. This is what it means for Him to breathe His own spirit of wrath, because He pre-announces the punishments of wrath: 'For I will discipline them in the wrath of their affliction' (Ps 17:17).

Out of many waters—meaning the turbulent and salty matters of life, called a sea tropically, which are the poured-out and disordered opposing powers—He stands against them; and even if the doctrines of ungodliness are many, they are not able to quench love. God delivers from powerful enemies the invisible ones, as is said, and perhaps also those in high positions and those intending to deceive through pseudonymous knowledge, who are terrible in their sophistry.

No one is without their own private thoughts, and those who are dissatisfied with Providence also bring up impiety regarding others, calling them powerful enemies, and that they might be rescued from those who hate them, and that they might be strengthened above them, which is worthy, while the haters are in vain. For no one, being hated for something trivial, will have the boldness to speak this prayer to God, but rather if he is hated by sinners for Christ and for the upright life, those who loathe godliness, for they consider the conduct of the righteous to be a reproach to their own way of life.

Indeed, those who hate the righteous most vehemently attack then, when a time of affliction is present. For, being ignorant of the judgment of Providence, they suppose that the righteous is being afflicted through sin for no other reason, like those conversing with Job. For when God had subjected him to afflictions, so that he might be shown to be righteous, they said that this man had fallen into these things because of impiety and sin; but even against the one stumbling, all the predatory demons and the devil are strong, as they now think sin to be an evil.

For in the day of affliction, whoever takes refuge toward God, He becomes his support (Ps 17:19), meaning, supporting him so that he might not be shaken and fall. And concerning the perfection of the soul, those who accept the ascent and the brightening of it say marvelously: 'Who is she that ascends...'

Has she been whitened, leaning upon her brother? For the Lord becomes a support for someone, leading him out of the narrowness of afflictions, giving him breadth according to 'In affliction he enlarged me' (Ps 17:20a). But one is enlarged in affliction not by becoming outside of the affliction entirely, but by being courageously and piously stretched toward it.

He will rescue me from my strong enemies and from those hating me (Ps 17:20b–21), since they possess no power at all, for all His wills were doing me. Truly, the boldness of the pure and perfect is such that he condemns nothing of himself, even the shortest thing; therefore, those who wish to speak this psalm in the presence of the Savior, and who apply this word to Him, find Him having been tested in all things according to likeness, without sin. He speaks of righteousness as the general virtue of practice, and of cleanness of hands as the practical actions becoming pure and unstained by being fulfilled from the best of ways; for often hands are said to be upon the practical powers.

And he does not say these things arrogantly, as some are, but having placed the cause of the successes upon God. He who walks in His commandments keeps the ways of the Lord, and he who has correctly grasped the doctrines of truth does not act impiously toward his own God, conceiving blamelessly concerning God, speaking holily concerning Christ, remembering piously concerning the Holy Spirit, and glorifying in the proper manner concerning the other doctrines.

For even if His judgments are unsearchable and seem like an abyss because of the incomprehensible, it is not possible for those having them not to be displeased with Providence, nor to act impiously toward the one who provides. For even if we do not grasp, but having resolved that these things are fulfilled by God's judgment, we are well-pleased with them. And the very name 'Judgment' signifies the rectitude of the administration; for it contains and is heard to be that which has happened according to righteousness, as opposed to judgments of the unrighteous and the perverted which are performed apart from the right. Because of this, he says, a perverted judgment will come forth. 'I hold fast to the rights of God,' he says (Ps 17:23b).

english: For they depart from those things which are not contained by them. And the rights and statutes must be spoken of which have been legislated according to equality and justice, such as 'If a Hebrew acquires a child' (Deut 21:15), and the following. For all these things, the judgments are arranged as side-notes, and the following.

The judgments, being named with the rights, can signify the tested and examined words of God; for they are not called judgments because they are not being checked or being overturned. In this way even the thoughts of the righteous are judgments, that is, having been accurately examined and tested, and being this very thing similar to a rule.

Perhaps those who, not through God but through glory or something else, find fault and [call] something unblemished, are unblemished indeed, but not with God; but those who have embraced the good through God and not for the sake of anything else, are unblemished with God; for this union toward God preserves one unblemished and good. But those being uncoupled and separated from God become immediately unblemished [children], unblemished children becoming through the act of sinning.

He who has accomplished all the aforementioned things, how does he speak of his own lawlessness? It is to say that he does not wish to understand at any time; this is it: 'The mind of man leans toward evil things with care from youth' (Gen 8:21), as it flows toward sin, being enticed by pleasure. He who has given himself to the law of God protects himself from the lawlessness that overshadows men.

Perhaps also that which is called among us the mindset of the flesh, which is enmity toward God and does not submit to His law, is the lawlessness of man, from which one preserves the deeds of the body of death in the spirit and abstains from the works of the flesh. There he calls righteousness here, that which is established from the faith of Jesus Christ. For the righteousness of God has been revealed to all who believe (Rom 3:22); for to the one believing rightly, 'the faith is reckoned as righteousness' (Rom 4:3/5). And together with purity...

For you say the works of faith, which operate brightly and without stain, without which faith is dead (Ps 17:26–28). Regarding the change of face in Psalm 17:26–28, someone says these upcoming verses are to be spoken toward God, because he does not say to another, 'That you will save a humble people and humble the eyes of the proud,' but to God. Another will say that these are not spoken toward God but toward a man: that the one spending time with the holy should imitate their virtue, and the one spending time with the wicked should undergo perversion, as the divine writing of Proverbs says: 'He who walks with the wise will be wise, but he who walks with fools will be destroyed' (Prov 13:20). The interpretations are thus: 'With the holy man, O Lord, he shall be made holy,' providing him the holiness supplied from you so that, having been perfected according to it, you may bring him into the fitting promise, and the others following the one before it. He also says, 'You will pervert,' for it is possible to say, 'He perverts with a crookedness'; this is not said, but 'You will pervert.' For God perverts the one running toward evil things, blocking his way with stumbling blocks and rebuilding his paths; for to be prevented from evils is the beginning of blessing. But he who wishes to be taken toward a man says that the one associating with a holy man becomes holy from the holy things being done, as Elisha with Elijah and Timothy with Paul; and the one hastening with the innocent, having seized that one's virtue, will be innocent. Likewise, the one spending time with an elect man, but the one associating with the crooked, desiring to become like him, will pervert his own life. And he, having clarified the verses thus, turns his face toward God from 'That you will save a humble people.'
Regarding the receptive part of the soul's light, the power—that is, the mind, which some call the reasoning faculty—it is said to be its lamp, not being itself...

english: In essence it is not light, but it is capable of receiving light. But its darkness is the passionate and desiring part.

If the mind is now enlightened by the Lord, sharing with it His own rays, the victorious movements and the irrational movements of the soul are enlightened through knowledge being perfectly accomplished; not that the irrational parts themselves participate in light (for they are incapable of knowledge), but that which is under an enlightened mind is guided by knowledge and virtue without needing a way. If the mind, which is said to be a lamp, is now enlightened by the Lord, then the darkness we have spoken of must necessarily follow being enlightened.

And this is what the Savior says: 'If the light in you is darkness, how great is that darkness!' (Luke 11:35). For if the eye of the body, that is, the mind, which ought to be a lamp, is deprived of light, then the other is much more so; in this way, the body of the soul becomes darkness, but it is not a human body, rather it is that which happens according to its irrational composition.

Perhaps also those enlightened in the knowledge of the truth have the lamp exhausted, the Lord having given this to them; and having performed actions rightly from the enlightenment of the mind, they have their darkness being enlightened. And this too should not be said of the basket. Those having possessed scientific contemplation concerning intelligible and invisible things have a lamp being enlightened by the Lord, but also regarding sensible things, being well-disposed according to opinion, they have the sense perceiving things luminously, which is darkness because it is not by itself capable of being enlightened, that is, receiving knowledge; for would the senses, even if they received knowledge, receive the irrational parts?

It is not otherwise possible to be saved from the surrounding bitter things by becoming in God; for someone becomes in God partaking of Him. Just as one having come to be in knowledge is saved from ignorances, so one hastening to be in God will be saved from temptation, not by not entering into temptation, but by not being caught by its snares.

For he who confesses Jesus before men is in him; for whoever confesses me before men, I will confess him before my Father who is in the heavens (Matt 10:32-33). For one partakes of him and confesses Jesus, and is confessed by God as being in him. But the multitude of things being done toward us irrationally separates us from God and discerns [a gap], as the prophet says: Is not the hand of the Lord able to save? Did his wrath grow because they did not listen? But your sins discern [a gap] between you and God. And he who now becomes in God, clinging to him and being toward him, surpasses the wall of sins by a little and casts them before and behind, so that, not being pierced through by anything, he may face God face to face.

Perhaps also the sense of bodily and sensible things, standing between our thought and God, separates us from him. But if we now, scientifically as much as possible, through the thought concerning God, grasp him above all bodies and senses, desiring to be united with him, we withdraw from the sensible and bodies as if to leap over the world and all visible things, so that we may be able to present ourselves to God. Our God is faultless in the way toward him (Ps 17:31). And this is virtue, through which, traveling by practice and discipline, we shall be shown faultless coming toward him. But especially faultless is the way of God, he who said: I am the way and the truth and the life (John 14:6). For through this way it is possible to come to the Father.

The word of the Lord, having been made fiery, is in the one who is truthful and pure, or is a fire that consumes the weakness of the matter of those partaking. He is a defender of all who hope in him. Those who know the weakness present to them, if they make those attacking them stronger, by casting hope upon God, are worthy to have him fight for them, saying, 'Fight, those who fight against me.' And thus God fights for them with his own shield, according to: His truth shall surround you with a shield (Ps 17:30). For no one is truly and principally God except the God of the Word, who is called the only-begotten God (Ps 17:32a).

english: Because he alone is as the Father God. For all the others are made gods by the presence of the Word of God. For those are gods by participation, toward whom the Word of God came. But the Savior, not possessing divinity, is God, a maker of gods.

In Psalm 17:32b (Εἰπὼν μηδένα θεὸν κυρίως ειναι πλὴν τοῦ κυρίου), having said that no god exists in the strict sense except the Lord, he says that no god exists in any way like our God. For none of those who are gods by participation can be like the Lord Jesus Christ, or like our God as the [one] of the only-begotten Father; for to us is God the Father and is Lord Jesus the Christ. And if even the two verses can be said to be parallel, he himself will understand.

In Psalm 17:33–34 (Ἐνταῦθα Περιζωννύων με δύναμιν λέγεται), 'He girded me with strength' is said. But according to Paul, the truth is that those having put on the armor of God are girded, from which it is gathered that the Christ is the power of God; for the Savior says, 'I am the truth' (Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀλήθεια), but Paul [says], 'Christ the power of God' (Χριστὸς θεοῦ δύναμις). And he set my way blameless, that is, he demonstrated. For to demonstrate now means to have demonstrated, just as [it is said] 'He has appointed him heir of all things' (Ον εθεκεν κληρονόμον πάντων). It is also good from this verse to proclaim the whole psalm from the person of Christ.

He who says these things, having refuted the serpent-like evils and the evil powers that worked them, has the feet of his own man prepared by God (that is, the walking powers), so that he may be able to say, 'I have run without lawlessness and have directed my course' (Ἀνευ ἀνομίας ἐδραμον καὶ κατηύθυνα); and having fulfilled the course, he will be heard in the high places by God: 'You yourself also stand with me' (Σὺ δὲ αὐτὸς στῆθι μετ' ἐμοῦ). And to stand in the high places is not something one has from himself, but from God.

In Psalm 17:35a (Ωσπερ τὰ ἄλλα καλά), just as other good things, so also we are taught by God to fight against the opposing powers. For he strikes the hands of the soul (I mean the active powers of it), and teaches how to skillfully hold the mental shield and the sword of the spirit and other spiritual defenses, and how one must use such things. For even the Savior, having become man, having fought on our behalf, taught us to overcome and to fight against the opposing power; and he says that stretching out his hands in prayer: 'I am surrounded by the difficulties...'

Remaining. 139 Symbolically, he set a bow called bronze upon the arms (Ps 17:35b); for because of the bronze, it represents the unpierceable or the strong, and because of the bow, the ability to release arrows from our own arms to wound those set against us.

140 Besides these, you have given to me a shield of salvation, having sent your Son to fight for me with his own shield (Ps 17:36). But also your discipline, he says, has perfected me to the end—that is, the disciplinary teaching and the strenuous training. He has brought me to the end, that is, unto a perfect resurrection and standing. For discipline signifies the disciplinary aspect, as in 'Take my discipline, do not let go' (Prov 3:11), but also the strenuous aspect through 'Do not despise the discipline of the Lord' (Prov 3:11). And thus, in both ways, your discipline has become a teacher of good things to me.

141 Having been aided by ten thousand through God, confidence arose to pursue the enemies; and the end of the pursuit is their falling to the end (Ps 17:38). For neither toil nor fear caused me to stumble.

142 Sparing those who were envenoming, he crushes them, so that they might become unshakeable and immovable in the enmity (Ps 17:39a). For, not intending to destroy them, he surrounds them with tribulation, so that, having perceived they are evil, they might cease from the intention of hatred.

143 The falling of the enemies under the feet of the holy one signifies nothing other than the submission of the various [kinds] (Ps 17:39b). For as it is trivial to stand in the hand of the law, the beginning of salvation is to fall from it. For one falling from it does not oppose it, but lies down and submits.

144 You caused all those rising up against me to stumble, not permitting them to advance in the face of evil (Ps 17:40b.41). For, being hindered from the impulse toward evil, they will fall down beneath me, regarding me as nothing other than their ruler and head, so that, instead of hating, they might become friends; for such are they whom you have destroyed; for you do not destroy their essence, but only that which has happened to them. For it is very fitting for the goodness of God to make the evil vanish, but not the essence of that which has happened to them.
145 For he says to some: 'And if you multiply the prayer, I will not listen to you' (Ps 17:42), because of your hands—that is, your deeds—which are murderous.

Ευ δὲ καὶ τὸ εἰπεῖν Ον οὐκ ε γνων. οὐ γὰρ ει πεν· Λαὸς ο ν οὐ γινώσκω ἐδούλευσέν μοι. ὁ γὰρ ε τι τὰ τῆς κακίας ἐνεργῶν οὐ γινώσκεται· ὁ δὲ παυσάμενος τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων οὐκ ἐγνώσθη μὲν πρότερον, γινώσκεται δὲ νῦν. 39 τούτοις συνᾴδει τὸ ἀποστολικὸν φάσκον· ̓Αλλὰ τότε μὲν οὐκ εἰδότες θεὸν ἐδουλεύσατε τοῖς φύσει μὴ ου σιν θεοῖς, νῦν δὲ γνόντες θεόν, μᾶλλον δὲ γνωσθέντες ὑπὸ θεοῦ. ο τε γὰρ ἠγνόουν θεόν, ἠγνοοῦντο ὑπ' αὐτοῦ, γνόντες δὲ αὐτὸν ἐγνώσθησαν ὑπ' αὐτοῦ. Ισως δὲ δόξειέν τισιν παρέλκον ει ναι τὸ εἰρημένον Εἰς ἀκοὴν ὠτίου ὑπήκουσέν μοι, τῷ πάντα τὸν ὑπακούοντα ὠτίῳ ὑπακούειν. οὐ παρελκόντως δὲ οὐδὲ περιττῶς πρόσκειται τὸ ὠτίον τῷ πάντα τὸν ὑπακούοντα, τῷ θεῷ μὴ ἀνθρωπίνῃ καὶ θνητῇ ἀκοῇ χρᾶσθαι ἀλλ' ὠτίῳ θείῳ ἐκ προσθήκης τῷ ε χοντι παραγινομένῳ· Προσέθηκεν γάρ μοι ὠτίον ἀκούειν. english: And the eyes are full. Regarding those of whom the Word speaks, having become thickened by thinking of earthly and material things, bearing the image of the earthly, they are thinned through exhortations, admonitions, threats, and painful discipline, so that, as having become dust in the face of the Divine Spirit, which is called the tropical wind, all that is earthly, being dispersed by them by the breath of the Spirit, may become pure dust as their underlying substance, for whom it has happened to be earthly.

And if they also willingly follow this calling, the author says as if to a filthy city: 'Shake off your dust, Jerusalem' (Ps 17:43). But the Lord, or His imitator, the just, licks these even as mud in the streets. But this mud being licked will not be able to become an earthen vessel useful in the great house in which there are golden and silver and wooden and earthen vessels; but since the golden and silver are for honor and the wooden and earthen are for dishonor, the one cleansing himself from these becomes a vessel of honor, having been sanctified and made useful to the Master, prepared for every good work, while those who remain such mud in the streets—that is, the mire of pleasures and desires—are being freed from all roughness from the passions.

He who says these things, by instilling a uniformity through the licking, is now making them earthen vessels, if they should cleanse themselves by a spontaneous impulse as if to become vessels of honor, golden or silver. For just as some have become earthen vessels from golden and silver ones (For the precious sons of Zion, exalted with silver, how were they reckoned as earthen vessels of the work of hands? [Ps 51:7]), so from their own domestic choice they shall become golden or silver from earthen ones.

Regarding the second meaning of the name of knowledge, he shows both the knowing and the being known and being recognized by the one knowing the one being known. According to the former meaning, God knows all, and not only the diligent ones. For toward the lowly the Savior says: 'You justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts' (Mt 6:1); and in the prophet: 'Because I knew all your sins' (Ps 40:3). And according to the second [meaning]...

It is said that he recognizes only the righteous. For the Lord knew those who were his, but he ignored the wicked. The Savior says to them: 'Depart from me, workers of lawlessness, I never knew you' (Matt 7:23). And the people from the nations, not being known by the Savior, though he healed both demons and idols and practiced all manner of evil, having changed through repentance to serve Christ, came to him. And even the saying 'He did not know' is true. For it is not said: 'A people I do not know served me' (Matt 15:22). For he who is doing the works of wickedness is not known; but he who has ceased from sins was not known before, but is known now.

To this the apostolic word agrees, saying: 'But formerly, not knowing God, you served those which by nature are not gods; but now, having known God, and even more having been known by God' (Gal 4:8). For they did not know God, and they were unknown by him, but having known him, they were known by him. Perhaps it will seem to some that the spoken thing passes by: 'To the hearing of an ear I obeyed' (1 Sam 13:30), meaning to obey with an ear that obeys all things. But the ear is not intended to pass by or to be superfluous for the one obeying all things, so as to use a non-human and mortal hearing, but a divine ear added to the one approaching; for he added to me an ear for hearing.

'Alien sons have grown old' (Heb 1:6), and the following. God the Father, becoming the beginning and source of the good, becomes the source of those doing good works, and those who are found in doing what is necessary are truly sons of God, partakers of his only-begotten Son. But if those who did not draw near participate in the opposites (and these are the evils), they would be alienated from God, and the growing old would follow. For participating in virtue, in bright and imperishable wisdom and incorruption, they were finding constant renewal; but falling into wickedness, they would be growing old through their own corruption (if indeed it is so), being worn out.
