Τοῦ ἀκοῦσαι τῶν αἰνούντων σε ἀγγέλων καὶ ψυχῶν καὶ πνευμάτων δικαίων φωνὴν η περικύκλῳ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου γεγένημαι η ἐνιψάμην ἐν ἀθῴοις τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ πάντων τῶν προαγόντων ἀπεσχόμην, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῦ ∆ιηγήσασθαι πάντα τὰ θαυμάσιά σου α τεραστίως καὶ παραδόξως ἐπιτελεῖς. 234 Ps 25,8.9 ̔Ο τὸν κύριον ἐξ ο λης ψυχῆς ἀγαπῶν καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πάντα, ω ν ε ν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ οι κου αὐτοῦ τυγχάνει, ἀγαπᾷ· εὐπρέπεια δὲ τοῦ οι κου τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ τῶν δογμάτων ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ διαταγὴ τῶν κανόνων τῆς ἐκκλησίας οι κου νοουμένης. πρὸς τούτοις δὲ καὶ τὸ σκήνωμα τῆς δόξης τοῦ οι κου τοῦ θεοῦ ἀγαπᾶν φησιν. καὶ τάχα μὲν ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου η ν Μωυσῆς κατεσκεύασεν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τὸ σκήνωμα τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν· σύμβολον δὲ προκοπῆς τοῦτο. ο ν δὲ ᾠκοδόμησεν Σολομῶν μετὰ τὴν ὁδοιπορίαν εἰς τὴν ̔Ιερουσαλὴμ οι κός ἐστιν ου τὴν εὐπρέπειαν ἀγαπᾷ τελειότητος τύπον φέρων. Ευ χεται δὲ μὴ ὡσαύτως τοῖς ἀσεβέσι διαθεῖναι, ι να μὴ συναπόληται αὐτοῖς ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ· εὐσεβῆ γάρ τις γνώμην ε χων οὐ πείσεται τοῦτο. παρακαλεῖ δὲ μηδὲ φονικὸς γενέσθαι, ο πως ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἀνδράσιν αἱμάτων μὴ συναπόληται· ἐν πράξεσιν γὰρ τούτων ἀδικία ἐστὶν ἡ καθόλου κακία. 235 Ps 25,11b Εἰ καὶ τὰ κάλλιστα συνειδὼς αὐτῷ τὰ προειρημένα ει πεν, εὐλαβούμενος μὴ οὐκ ἐν τούτῳ δεδικαίωται λανθανόντων πολλάκις τῶν ἐν κρυπτῷ ἁμαρτημάτων, λυτρωθῆναι καὶ ἐλεηθῆναι ἀξιοῖ. 236 Ps 26,1bc Σωτὴρ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός ἐστιν ῥυόμενος ἡμᾶς ἐξ ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ τοῦ θανάτου, φωτισμὸς δὲ λύων τὴν ἀχλὺν τῆς κακίας καὶ τῆς ἀγνοίας καὶ ἐναυγάζων τῷ φωτὶ τῆς γνώσεως. ὁ ου τως ου ν ἑνωθεὶς καὶ πεφωτισμένος ὑπὸ κυρίου, Τίνα φοβηθήσεται; οὐδεὶς γὰρ οι ός τέ ἐστι βλάψαι τὸν ἀγαθῶν τοιούτων καὶ ἀσφαλείας τετυχηκότα. Κύριος ὑπερασπιστὴς τῆς ζωῆς μου· ἀπὸ τίνος δειλιάσω; θεοῦ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ζωῇ ὑπερμαχοῦντος τῆς ζωῆς ̓Απὸ τίνος δειλιάσω; τὸ ̓Απὸ τίνος ἐξευτελισμὸν δηλοῖ τοῦ ἐπανιστανομένου κατ' αὐτοῦ τοῦ ὑπὸ θεοῦ φρουρουμένου· Εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, τίς ὁ καθ' ἡμῶν; 237 Ps 26,3.4 ̔Ρηθείη ταῦτα καὶ περὶ αἰσθητῶν ἐχθρῶν καὶ περὶ φάλαγγος ἀοράτων πολεμίων· ̓Εὰν γάρ φησιν ἐπαναστῇ ἐπ' ἐμὲ πόλεμος, ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ μὴ φοβουμένῃ αὐτοὺς καρδίᾳ μου ἐλπίζω, ὑπέρμαχον θεὸν ε χειν θαρρήσας. Εστιν ο αἰτεῖται καὶ ἐκζητεῖ τὸ Κατοικεῖν ἐν οι κῳ κυρίου, τουτέστιν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ διὰ τοῦ φρονεῖν τὰ ἐκκλησιαστικὰ πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς πεφωτισμένης ζωῆς ἑαυτοῦ. δύναται δὲ τὸ Μίαν ᾐτησάμην ου τως ἀκουσθῆναι· ἐπὶ γῆς τέως διατρίβων, εἰ καὶ πολλῶν ἀγαθῶν τυχεῖν παρακαλῶ, πρὸ πάντων ταύτην ᾐτησάμην τὴν αι τησιν, τὸ ̓Εν οι κῳ κυρίου κατοικεῖν τῷ κατὰ τάξιν καὶ μὴ ἀθρόως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς οι όν τε γενέσθαι· η τάχα προσυπακουστέον τῷ Μίαν ᾐτησάμην τὸ ἐξαίρετον η μεγάλην. ̓Επεὶ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ε μπροσθέν φησιν ἠγαπηκέναι τὴν εὐπρέπειαν
english: Hoping, I shall not be weak; for I am contained by the hope toward God, being strengthened by it, I shall not be weak. Scripture is carried forth saying: 'I shall not be shaken.' And through this it is not made manifest: because the hope toward God provides for me something firm and immovable, 'Hoping in the Lord, I shall not be shaken' (Ps 25:2).

Since it is not the one recommending himself who is proven, but the Lord establishes, having testified to himself that one should walk in integrity and desiring that one should not be weak, [he] wants [one] to be tested and tried by struggles, so that the righteous may be revealed, and [one] may be tried so that, having received a trial, he might have endurance that is proven. And previously, having an analogy between the kidneys and the heart, it is said. That these two things should be purified through painful struggle, so that they might be shown as proven gold (Ps 25:3).

I would not have been worthy to suffer the aforementioned painful things, unless your mercy had considered me, coinciding with me so as to enable me to endure them. Your mercy, which has been seen by me in front of my eyes, works together to please in your truth; for God's mercy makes one please according to truth and not by affectation (Ps 25:6,7).

One washes the practical powers of the soul, called hands tropically, in innocence, doing nothing trivial but something significant in them. Perhaps also the one who stains them in the work of evils washes and cleanses them, using good works instead of water. Having become outside of all the aforementioned evils and having washed my hands in innocence, I shall surround with the justice of an innocent priest the spiritual altar of the Lord, upon which someone offers up spiritual sacrifices, namely the pure prayers or the lawful acts. To have heard the voice of angels, souls, and spirits of the righteous praising you, to have become around the altar, to have washed my hands in innocence and to have abstained from all those leading astray, but also to perform the narrating of all your wonders in a vast and paradoxical way (Ps 25:8,9).

He who loves the Lord from his whole soul and all the things of God, to whom also the decency of his house belongs, loves; and the decency of God's house is the truth of the dogmas and the command of the canons of the church, being considered his house. Toward these...

And he says that even the tabernacle of the glory of God is loved. Perhaps the tent of witness which Moses constructed in the wilderness is the tabernacle of the glory of God; this is a symbol of progress. But that which Solomon built after the journey to Jerusalem is the temple, bearing a type of the beauty of perfection.

However, he does not wish for the ungodly to possess it, lest his soul be destroyed along with them; for one possessing a pious intention will not be persuaded by this. He also exhorts [one] not to become a murderer, so that his life may not be destroyed along with men of blood; for in the practice of these things there is injustice and total wickedness.

Even if he is conscious of the most beautiful things foretold to him, fearing [to sin], he is not justified by this alone, through many hidden sins; he deserves to be redeemed and to receive mercy (Ps 25:11b). God our Savior is the one rescuing us from sins and from death, and a light that dissolves the darkness of wickedness and ignorance, and illuminating with the light of knowledge (Ps 26:1bc). He who has thus been united and enlightened by the Lord, whom shall he fear? For no one is able to harm such good ones who have attained security. The Lord is the defender of my life; from whom shall I dread? (Ps 26:3,4). These things shall be said, and concerning perceptible enemies and concerning a phalanx of invisible enemies; for if he says, 'war rises up against me,' in this heart which does not fear them, I hope, having become bold, in a God who fights for me. It is also requested and sought to dwell in the house of the Lord, that is, in the church, through thinking on ecclesiastical matters all the days of his enlightened life. 'One thing I asked, which I sought: to dwell on earth, even if I should find many good things, I beseech you, before all things I asked this one thing, to dwell in the house of the Lord (Ps 27:2) in order, and not in confusion, in all the good things that become [one];' perhaps the 'One thing I asked' is to be heard as the exceptional or the great. Since he also says in the beforehand that he has loved the beauty...

source_text: τοῦ οι κου κυρίου, ὁ ταύτην ποθῶν θεωρεῖν ευ χεται ἐν τῷ οι κῳ γενέσθαι, ι ν' ἐγγὺς αὐτῆς τυγχάνων γνησίως προβάλλων ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑπεραναβὰς ἐπισκέψηται τουτέστιν περιαθρήσῃ τὸν ναὸν αὐτοῦ, τάχα οὐδὲ ἀναχωρῆσαι αὐτοῦ ε τι θελήσας μιμούμενος 59 τὸν Σαμουήλ. καὶ ὁ μὲν ἁπλῶς περὶ τῶν ὑποβεβηκότων δογμάτων τῆς ἐκκλησίας διειληφὼς θεωρεῖ τὴν τερπνότητα κυρίου, προσβάλλων δέ τις τοῖς περὶ τῆς τριάδος περιαθρήσει τὸν ναὸν αὐτοῦ. 238 Ps 26,5.6 Πολλάκις η δη διαφορὰν σκηνῆς καὶ οι κου ο τε α μα ὀνομάζονται εἰρήκαμεν, ὡς τῆς μὲν προκοπὴν δηλούσης, τοῦ δὲ τελειότητα. ο τε τοίνυν ἐνέστηκέν τινι ε τι ἡ τῶν κακῶν ἡμέρα, οὐκ ἐν τῷ οι κῳ τοῦ θεοῦ ει ναι δύναται, ἀλλ' ἐν τῇ σκιᾷ κρύπτεται ὑπὸ κυρίου τῷ τὴν προκοπὴν σκεπάζειν τὸν κακίας ἀπαλλαττόμενον· οὐ γὰρ ὁ α ρτι μετανοῶν ἐπὶ τελειότητα ἰέναι οι ός τε. Τάχα δὲ τὸ ο νομα τῶν κακῶν σημαίνειν τὰ περιστατικὰ καὶ ἐνταῦθα δύναται. ̓Εσκέπασέν με ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ τῆς σκηνῆς αὐτοῦ, τῆς παιδεύσεως καθ' η ν προκόπτομεν. τὰ μέν ἐστι προφανῆ, τὰ δὲ ἀπόκρυφα καὶ ἀνακεχωρηκότα οι α τὰ μυστικά. ἐν τῷ προκόπτειν ου ν σκεπάζει ὁ θεὸς οὐκ ἐν τοῖς ἐπιπολαίοις ἀλλ' ̓Εν τῷ ἀποκρύφῳ τῆς σκηνῆς αὐτοῦ. πρόσκειται δὲ τὸ Αὐτοῦ πρὸς παράστασιν τοῦ μὴ πᾶσαν σκηνὴν τουτέστι προκοπὴν κατὰ θεὸν ει ναι. ̓Εν πέτρᾳ υ ψωσέν με, μετὰ τὴν προκοπὴν φθάσαντά με ἐπὶ τὸν στερρότατον καὶ ἀρραγῆ τῆς τελειώσεως λόγον πέτραν ἀλληγορικώτερον ὀνομαζόμενον· αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος υ ψωσέν με. κατάλληλον τῇ προκοπῇ τὸ Εκρυψεν, τῇ τελειότητι τὸ Υψωσεν. δυνατὸν δὲ καὶ τὴν διὰ νόμου καὶ προφητῶν ἀγωγὴν σκηνὴν λέγειν η ς ἐν τῷ ἀποκρύφῳ τουτέστιν ἐν τῷ μυστικῷ νῷ κρύπτει τὸν παιδευόμενον ὁ θεός, ὑψῶν αὐτὸν ἐν πέτρᾳ πνευματικῇ οὐκ α λλῃ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τυγχανούσῃ. Καὶ νῦν μετὰ τὸ διαβῆναι τὴν προκοπὴν καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς ἀληθείας ἐφθακέναι ὑψοῖ τὴν κεφαλήν, η τοι νοῦν τὸν ἐμὸν η Χριστὸν α ρχοντα νοῦ γεγενημένον, ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς μου, ο πως ὑπὸ πόδας καὶ ὑποτεταγμένους αὐτοὺς ε χω. ̓Εκύκλωσα καὶ ε θυσα ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ αὐτοῦ θυσίαν αἰνέσεως. Κατάλληλον τῷ Εκρυψέν με ἐν σκηνῇ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κακῶν μου καὶ τὸ προκείμενον· τότε γὰρ θυσίαν ἀλαλαγμοῦ μετὰ νίκην ἐπιτελουμένην θύσει, κυκλώσας ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ αὐτοῦ. ἀλαλάξαι δέ ἐστιν τὸ ἀθρόως ἐπὶ ἡττηθεῖσιν ἐχθροῖς βοῆσαι. ὁ ου ν τῶν ἐχθρῶν περιγινόμενος τὴν ἐπὶ νίκῃ χαριστήριον θυσίαν εἰκότως ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ, τουτέστιν ἐν τῇ προκοπῇ, προσάγει. Αισω καὶ ψαλῶ τῷ κυρίῳ. english: Regarding the dwelling of the Lord, he who desires to behold this rejoices in becoming a dwelling, approaching it closely and genuinely, not only approaching but also surpassing, as if the Lord visits and surrounds his temple, perhaps not even wishing to depart, imitating Samuel. He who simply, having grasped the established dogmas of the church, beholds the delight of the Lord, differs from one who approaches the Lord by surrounding his temple regarding the Trinity (Ps 26:5,6).

Many times the difference between the tabernacle and the dwelling is called 'we have said,' signifying indeed progress, but the latter perfection. Therefore, the day of evils that has come upon someone cannot be in the dwelling of God, but it is hidden in the shadow, the Lord covering him to shield him from evil, for the one now repenting is not yet going to perfection. Perhaps the name of evils signifies circumstances, and here it is possible.

'He covered me in the secrecy of his tabernacle' (Ps 26:5), which is the instruction by which we progress. The manifest things are the former, but the secret and withdrawn things are the mysteries. In progressing, God does not cover in the obvious things, but in the secrecy of his tabernacle. His action is set forth as a representation that not every tabernacle is, that is to say, progress according to God.

'He lifted me up on a rock' (Ps 26:6), having reached progress, me upon the narrowest and most unyielding word of perfection, a rock called allegorically; 'the Lord himself lifted me up.' It is appropriate for progress to be 'He hid [me],' and for perfection to be 'He lifted [me] up.' It is also possible to call the guidance through law and prophets a tabernacle; in the secrecy, that is, in the mystical way, God hides the one being instructed, lifting him up on a spiritual rock, not another, but one that is Christ's.

And now, after having passed through progress and having reached the goal of truth, to lift up the head, to understand my Christ having become the ruler of my mind, over my enemies, so that I may see them under my feet and having been made subject (Ps 27:6). 'I encircled and offered a sacrifice of praise in his tabernacle' (Ps 27:6). It is appropriate to 'He hid me in his tabernacle in the day of my evils' and the following: for then a sacrifice of shouting with...

A victory being completed is offered as a sacrifice, having encircled [the enemy] in his tent. To shout aloud is to cry out amidst the defeated enemies. He who, being surrounded by the enemies, rightly offers a gracious sacrifice of victory in the tent, that is to say, in progress. I will sing and I will praise the Lord. Not only will I contemplate the things of truth which are clearly manifested through the 'Singing', but also I will act according to virtue which is presented through the 'Praising', doing both in a pleasing manner to God. For this is what it means, 'I will sing and I will praise the Lord' (Ps 26:7–9a).

Knowing these things, he who says these things, hearing God through the prayers of the righteous, from the same disposition, having cried out to the righteous, deems it worthy that he will be heard. If you, Lord, were to consider according to merit, you would not hear a mortal; for no one would send up such a cry as to reach you. Having looked toward your goodness, have mercy on me; for you will also hear me. Both to be shown mercy and to be heard then happen not from the superficiality of lips, but from the heart toward you. Through this, it is presented that God hears not entirely the spoken voice, but above all the voice of the heart. 'Seek my face'; and this, if my heart is toward you, the face of my heart, which is nothing other than the mind, will seek you. And I will find, after the seeking, the face, approaching you face to face, the [vision] through a mirror and in a riddle having been done away. 'Having understood, I knew the face of your servant, imprinted according to the image and likeness of yours; therefore I seek to see your face.' For having understood it, I shall perceive a greater light. Then I am able to seek, if you appear, your face; for if this does not happen, I will not be able to approach it. Therefore I say: 'Do not turn your face away from me' (Ps 26:11).

Instruct me, Lord, so that having received such a law from you, I may walk in the word spoken (John 14:6). And guide me in the straight and unbending way of yours, escaping the enemies lying in wait, those placing stumbling blocks for me. For what is the virtue of the mean, of not being an excess or a deficiency, but keeping the proportion; you, Master, guide me, bringing me to the end of it, escaping my enemies who are working evil.

english: Acting excessively, standing by the door, they receive through deception those who do not stand by the distinction of moderation and excess. If you say that the path of true dogmas is a straight way, be careful that, not being led by God, the adjacent false dogmas are enemies of this age, who are its rulers; so that we may not fall into their deception, we pray to be led by the Lord on the straight way.

Since I have chosen to walk the straight way, all the wicked have set to trouble me (Ps 26:12); but You, Lord, my guardian, do not deliver me into their hands. He prays not to be delivered to them or to be numbered with their souls; those troubling him are witnesses that they are unrighteous. But injustice attributed it to themselves; being unstable and uncertain, it lied about itself; for it is not promised to be such, such was found. For the voice of a lie does not always signify the opposite of truth, as in the prophet Aloinos, who lied to them instead of as he promised; according to the finding of Aloinos, they lied having been diminished.

The land of promises was called the land of the living, according to eternal life (Ps 26:13), since no one in it participates in the following death of sin. But this land is in the unseen and eternal things, and upon it are the truly and properly good things of God. Therefore the saint says such a thing: I believe to participate in eternal life, so that by it, living, I may be transplanted into the land of the living, to see the Lord's good things which lie according to the promises for those living holily. And it is possible to say both to see and not to eat or taste something else; for the whole benefit is provided in contemplating the divine good things.

He says this, reasoning with himself, or to everyone hearing him (Ps 26:14). And such an exhortation may be brought to him from above by the Spirit, since, having believed to see the good things in the coming age, wait for the Lord, or wait for the descent of the Savior here; for through it he will be able to ascend to the vision of the good things. Be manly, that is, take up manliness, not by the strength of the body but...

while your heart is being held firm. For you will not be able to endure the Lord according to all the ways previously foretold (Ps 27:1c). The name of the pit and the place that guards the condemned signifies this.

Since you are not lacking in many things, that you might be able to have these things replenished toward you (Ps 27:2a), I am worthy to cry out to you, that you might hear the voice of my prayer when I am praying to no one else; for no one else is able to replenish what I lack. The temple of God is the one, and the super-heavenly space and the powers within it, hosting the presence of God as much as is possible (Ps 27:2b). And the Word of God is also the one who declares: 'The Father who dwells in me performs the works.'

He prays, not saying: 'Since destruction certainly comes to the wrongdoer (Ps 27:3b), do not let me, providing justice to me, fall into becoming an unrighteous one, lest I perish with those practicing it.'

The discerning one, approaching things with scientific knowledge, turns away from the harmful useless things, choosing the good and profitable ones (Ps 27:4). But the foolish one, being enticed by pleasure, performs evils, not seeing their harmfulness. Since he does not rationally perceive the harmful things, the saint prays that the foolish one might be repaid according to his painful works, so that through those pains he might turn away from the evils having become causes of punishment for him.

A man does, his works indeed, but they are the works of his hands; for he works according to a disposition (Ps 27:5). And the active powers, being called his hands, perform the practical aspects of sins. They deserve to receive a retribution in kind, because they did not comprehend the works of the Lord and the works of his hands; they turn out to be the visible works and the invisible works of God. For those who do not comprehend the works of God and the works of his hands, he wishes to receive the retribution of them; for they themselves having chosen the non-comprehending, the punishment followed them to fall into it.

Hoping in the Lord, the helper and defender, my heart was helped (Ps 27:7), so that there is nothing in it of a shameful remembrance or a foolish opinion. For the helping of the heart is to agree with what is necessary and to renew toward the opposites. But not like that of the...

english: My flesh has sprouted in doing these things, aiding my heart. Perhaps also the hoping heart will be aided, the flesh having risen according to the time of the resurrection, enjoying it. Near to this, even our bones sprout like herbs. For our body now holds the word of a seed toward the resurrection; for this very thing, having been sown in corruption, sprouts in incorruption, being sown. Paul also used the example of that which is sown regarding the things of the resurrection.

And I will confess to him according to my will. Many, through fear of punishment or shame, or because they are being reproached by men, forbid sins by disposition, enjoying them. But the critical man, having seen the mystery and the harm of sins, voluntarily turns away from them, confessing them to God of his own will. And if 'I will confess to him' signifies thanksgiving, someone does it according to his will, being thankful for all things that happen, even if something seems unpleasant. For those thanking only in things that please, they do not do it of their own will, but are driven to this by pleasure.

The people of God have nothing else as a stronghold except the Lord himself being their refuge and fortress (Ps 27:8). He himself is the Lord and the defender of the salvations of Christ. And every partaker of Christ is called 'Christ' homonymously with him. He who is not saved of the salvations, his Christ is not a defender; but if he is a defender of the salvations of Christ, the Son of the one who is, then salvation is heard through him by which he saves.

Save this your people, for you are a stronghold, blessing your inheritance; not like any other people (Ps 27:9). Bless it with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly things, lifting them up and suspending them through virtue, but also shepherding them into all this age. For in the future, having surpassed the state of being fed, they will be a pupil and a teacher to you.

The preceding psalm, containing greatest mysteries, is rightly arranged according to the twenty-seventh number, the power of the seven (Ps 28,1a). If indeed you combine the six numbers from unity as a seven, the twenty-seventh is composed; and it is a triangle, each of its sides being composed of seven. It is also a perfect number, second after the ten. For they say a perfect number is one composed of its own parts, so as not to exceed or fall short. And the present one is a number having parts: half, fourth, seventh, fourteenth, twenty-seventh; all being combined, it completes itself.

Protect then those who have the spirit of adoption by the angels, to bring upon the tent those things for healing (Ps 28,1b–2); and they carry [glory], and they are also sons of the lambs. Lambs ought to be considered those who return to a life of godliness according to piety, without logically contemplating the truth. Therefore they are also sufficient to rule, and sons of lambs are those born of the imitation of their way of life. Those having correctly and justly and piously received the Trinity carry glory, but those guarding the commandments of the Lord carry honor. For he who transgresses the law, by transgressing, dishonors God; honor he offers to Him, the one who is contained by the divine law. Bring glory to the Lord in His name; likewise to Him before Him. Worship the Lord in His holy court. He who worships God according to the ecclesiastical doctrines and the blameless canons of it, worships the Lord in His holy court.

Someone, imposing a more superficial interpretation, will say of John baptizing in the Jordan river, 'A voice of the Lord upon the waters' (Ps 28,3a). Yet John, having taken up a more pleasant and austere life, making the flame of the pleasures of life manageable, is a voice of the Lord cutting the flame of fire (Ps 28,7).

english: It has not become a desert the inhabited world (Ps 28:8). The previously mentioned voice of the Lord prepares the allegorically called deer. And these are souls, to kill the acts of the body by the spirit and to strip the impious one by the spirit through the lips by imitation of God.

And the voice of the Lord will work for her and a revelation of woods (Ps 28:9), so that the beasts lurking in them might be made manifest, they are lifted up as deer. And a wood is a natural place of fruitless trees; and the wood is revealed when the fruitless trees in it are being cut down by the axe of the Word and are being thrown into fire.

When that which overshadows the progress of men is removed, then everyone, having ceased from the manifold error, will speak glory in the temple of God (Ps 28:10). The sitting of God signifies his strength to remain unshakeable and incorruptible forever (Ps 28:10). For indeed he distributes it to those perishing through turning: 'You sitting for the age, and we perishing for the age.' And here the permanence of his kingdom is presented. For this reason, 'And the Lord King is established for the age' (Ps 28:10), having no end to his kingdom.

But he who speaks according to the history says that David the king, having been eager to build something tangible for the Lord, was forbidden by God speaking to him (Ps 29:1): 'Not you shall build for me something, because you are a man of war from your youth, but he who comes out of your loins shall build for me something.' Having been persuaded by the oracle, David ceased from building, but he pre-arranged the materials for the building. As he says, he prepared the materials, and also having composed the psalm, he left it as one of the necessary things, and how, after the temple having been built and dedicated, it might be struck with singing and chanting by those appointed to this.

He says that he will be saved (Ps 29:4) if God does not let him descend to him, or after descending, having brought him up. These things are said economically and as from the face of Christ, who having descended his soul on our behalf and having given it and having risen from the dead by the good pleasure of God and Father, toward whom he says humanly: '...
"For You did not abandon my soul to the pit, a pit called by name; I say with confidence: You saved me from those descending into the pit" (Ps 29:6c).

The end of the day prepares the true light; they weep in the evening—that is, having come into being at the beginning of the night—while the beginning of the day rejoices, having occurred for them with the rising of the sun of righteousness (Ps 29:6d). This applies to both: the weeping of the circumcised when the sun of righteousness rises for them, and the joy of the Gentiles when the saving word shines upon them.

One must hear prosperity through spiritual fruitfulness, so that the seed of Jesus becomes a hundredfold and the other generations of virtue are multiplied (Ps 29:7). In this prosperity, having been evidenced through these things, I will say that I remain firm and immovable, never to be shaken for ever. And one must cry out thus: "In my prosperity, I shall not be shaken for ever" (Ps 29:7); for through his works he cries out, "If I were in the aforementioned prosperity, I would be unshakeable, not being turned aside by the adversary."

Bodily beauty appears through the symmetry and proportion of the limbs (Ps 29:8a), but the beauty of the soul is in the harmony and symphony of all perfected virtues, having symmetry and proportion in all activities according to reason, and the harmony of the soul's powers in proportion. "Grant this beauty to me, O Lord, according to your will." For having done your will and that of the Father in heaven, he took it up, since everyone having become conformed to the image of the Son of God has received beauty from God, having been united with the Lord's will.

He who, through doing material things and thinking of earthly things, being as dust and persisting in sin, will not confess to God, nor announce the truth to Him, being led astray through morals and knowledge (Ps 29:10c-d).

It is to be noted that "became" does not mean "always being," but also signifies a relationship toward someone. If such a voice were ever to occur regarding the Savior, it signifies a relationship toward Him and not merely being (Ps 29:11b-13). "You turned my weeping into joy for me." The voice of weeping signifies the emotion, just as the very act of the hands placing them on the chest demonstrates it.

english: One who has not become aware in the consciousness of his own sins, and who has not actively awakened his sensation through spiritual hands, changing from being consumed by grief, will receive the fruit of the Spirit as joy. The phrase 'You have turned' signifies a change from cutting and grieving into joy; and 'I shall not be confounded' (Ps 30:2) is said instead of 'I shall not know'. He who sings glory while saying these things to God possesses a right conduct and sincere knowledge.

He who has hoped to reach the end of what is laid up for the saints, and who will not be put to shame for ever, has placed such an expectation upon the Lord. 'In your righteousness, he says, save me' (Ps 30:3) (not by any other than your only-begotten [Son]) 'from those surrounding me and bring me out from those intending to fight against me' (Ps 30:3). And since our cry may not reach your height, 'Incline your ear to me' (Ps 30:4) so that you may descend to accompany me; for the existence of this means that, having received my prayer, you will immediately deliver me by your wills.

And here 'Make me a hiding place' (Ps 30:4) signifies a protector for the one being protected. It is also worthy that those near a refuge should have God become a salvation for them, just as one is saved unharmed while remaining enclosed by an impregnable and unassailable fortress. This I have often and always attempted, as [the Psalmist says], 'You are my strength and my refuge, since your name is my stronghold; for I am your man and your servant' (Ps 30:3). Even if I am not worthy to receive what I ask, because of your goodness you will guide me toward salvation and sustain me, providing me with your heavenly bread (Ps 30:5).

Diligence belongs to the good; the body is not so much to be wounded by enemies, for the war does not seek to deceive him with phantoms and terrors, but rather it seeks not to strike the flesh but to wound the mind from before; the spirit places itself into the hands of God, being able to guard it. And the Savior, having been hung upon the stake, his hands and feet having been pierced according to the prophecy, 'Into your hands I shall commit myself' (Ps 30:6), has used the hands of God, which are none other than his providential and protective powers, to be exercised.

It should be noted that the spirit of man is spoken of in many ways. For in the [prophecy of the] Virgin, where it is said she is to be holy in spirit and body, spirit refers to the intellect. But according to James (as the body without spirit is dead), the designation of 'spirit' signifies nothing other than the soul. And in the [passage] 'For what are the things of man, except the spirit of man which is in him?', it is shown to be nothing other than the spirit joined to the soul or being part of it, which is also called conscience; for the conscience of man is the inward thoughts, which are something other than the soul; for the soul is the man, not the inward thoughts.

Regarding the [Psalm] 'the spirit of man having been set in your hands', stand firm to grasp in what way it is meant: 'Into your hands I commit my spirit' (Ps 31:5). And it pleases me that the present text is true according to the three ways. 'Having been seized by enemies, as having become a captive, I will redeem, O Lord, you who are the God of truth and of the truth shared by each of those participating in the truth of the Only-Begotten' (Ps 30:7a). In general, everyone guarding vanity for no reason does this, making the uncertain to be, or making vanity to happen emptily and superfluously. And he who hates this makes those guarding it hateful to God.

The humiliation, on one hand, shows blindness, when it calls for humility, and on the other hand, the harm by enemies. And it is good to see God in both kinds of humiliation. What follows, he considers to be the harm following the humiliation: 'For you have compressed my soul by necessity' (Ps 31:5), saying 'necessities' regarding the circumstances from which the soul, having been rescued, is not enclosed into the hands of the harming enemy. If the 'spaciousness' were to say the same regarding the wide and spacious way (which is the love of pleasure), it would thank it for its stability and for desiring a standing in this life. For it says something like this: being in the place of the earth, where living is slippery and unsafe because of the sliding pleasures, you have given a standing to my soul, so that I might not be carried away there by the passions. english: Glory comes from circumstances, I will say: 'You have set my feet in a wide place' (Ps 30:11c). Not every poor person is weak (for many poor people are strong), nor is one lacking in strength poor; but in spiritual matters, since strength is the same as wealth, the one who is wealthy has strength in good works. He does not wish to say 'I am such a thing'; since, having turned away from the visible wealth (which is not the divine), he says, 'My strength has grown weak.' It is to be noted what it means to say 'is' instead of 'has'; for it is not strength that is weak, but the one who has it, just as we do not say one is ignorant of knowledge, but that one is ignorant. This is in agreement with what was said by Paul concerning Christ: 'That we might become the righteousness of God in him' (2 Cor 5:21). For in these things, he called those having righteousness 'righteousness.'

Those enemies who are lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God, not only do not feel shame nor seem to suffer reproach for the evil they do, but on the contrary, they take pride, as it has been said concerning them: 'The glory is in their shame.' And they boast over those who become objects of reproach. Therefore, turn away from your boasting and reproach against the Lord; otherwise, they shall rise to reproach and eternal shame. But he who perceives himself to have become in the aforementioned poverty confesses that he is to be reproached. Therefore he says: 'I have become a reproach to all my enemies, but also to all those who draw near to me according to the proverb—that is, to those who hold the same opinion.'

Those who attack me with persistence, perceiving that they have fallen from wealth into poverty, fearing that they might suffer the same, hasten to be outside of my stability. But also, a vessel which formerly was precious and very useful to the master, seemed to have been lost. Because the ear hears the slander of many dwelling around. If a teacher is called a liar by those who seem to be his [disciples] because of the necessity of learning, yet they dwell around and do not remain in the lessons, they do not abide in them. And it is possible to not be so; since the ear hears the slander of many around me, because they do not abide but merely dwell around our things, for this reason I have become a lost vessel. With this, ...

Is it that someone is weak and I am not weak? Is it that someone stumbles and I am not being burned? (Ps 30:16) My lots fall into those things which are covering and guarding by your hands, being profited by them; that is, all things allotted to me according to your judgment, either to flow from them or to suffer; for it does not happen to them by chance. (Ps 30:16a)

Others clarify the word not thus: the powers given, they say, are called their lots, as if they have superiority over teachers or others. They are not in the hands of God. For just as He establishes, so also He distributes kings. Therefore, because some are coming to move this superiority which is present to me, wanting to do so, they will not be able, since all things concerning me are in your hands. (Ps 30:16)

He does not merely hide his goodness from those fearing him (for they see much of it), but the abundance, so that they may not be harmed. (Ps 30:20-21) And it is also good to say: To those fearing you, it is stored up for them. Reveal it to them, so that those having become in perfect love might cast out fear. 'You have made it known to those fearing you' means you have revealed it by energy, so that those having more hope than fear possess it.

Regarding 'Against the sons of men': You say 'men' regarding those having preserved the rational and incorruptible image, but 'their sons' regarding those having become their rational disciples and imitators. And 'hidden from the face of God' you say, meaning that which is not attainable now to knowledge, but will be revealed then, when we shall see Him as He is. With this 'hidden' thing, that which is said by Paul is contrasted: 'made known to men,' that is, His creative and providential nature. For after the 'God revealed' it is said: 'For his invisible attributes, from the creation of the world, are understood and perceived through the works.' (Rom 1:20)

Perhaps also the Savior has the face of God hidden, all that is according to the divinity, but that which is according to the economy is manifest. And since now the Word having become flesh dwells among us, we are being hidden in the mystery of His face, so that we may see Him as we shall see His glory, a glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. (John 1:14) But stand firm, if...

source_text: καὶ τὰ προφανῆ ε ργα τῆς προνοίας πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ει ναι δύναται· δι' αὐτῶν γὰρ θεὸν φανταζόμεθα· ἀπόκρυφον δὲ αὐτοῦ οἱ ἀπόρρητοι λόγοι καθ' ου ς γίνεται τὰ γινόμενα, ου ς ἐπὶ τέλει τῶν πραγμάτων εἰσόμεθα ̓Απὸ ταραχῆς ἀνθρώπων. οἱ ἀνθρώπινα δόγματα ἐπαγγελλόμενοι α νθρωποί εἰσιν ταραχὴν προβαλλόμενοι, δι' η ς ταράττουσιν τοὺς ἀνερματίστους. ταύτης τῆς ταραχῆς ἐκτὸς ποιῶν τοὺς ἐλπίζοντας ἐπ' αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς κατακρύπτει αὐτοὺς ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ κατὰ πάντας τοὺς εἰρημένους τρόπους. Σκεπάσεις αὐτοὺς ἐν σκηνῇ ἀπὸ ἀντιλογίας γλωσσῶν. ὁ τέλειος πάσης προκοπῆς ἀναχωρήσας αὐτὴν κατανοεῖ τὴν ἀλήθειαν δι' ο ἀνεξαπάτητός ἐστιν, ὁ δὲ ἐν τῷ προκόπτειν ἐπιτυγχάνων χρῄζει σκεπάζοντος θεοῦ ἐν σκηνῇ τουτέστιν τῶν διαφόρων γλωσσῶν η τοι διαφόρων ψευδοδοξιῶν. πρὸς γὰρ τὸν τέλειον λέγεται· Καὶ πᾶσα φωνὴ η ἀναστήσεται ἐπὶ σὲ εἰς κρίσιν, πάντας αὐτοὺς ἡττήσεις. πᾶς γὰρ λόγος ἑτερόδοξος ἀνίσταται κρίνεσθαι βουλόμενος μετὰ τῆς ἐκκλησιαστικῆς γνώμης. πάντας δὲ αὐτοὺς ἡττήσει ὁ τέλειος τὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας φρονῶν. 278 Ps 30,22.23 Οὐ τοσοῦτον θαύματος α ξιον ο τ' α ν ἐμφαίνηται ὁ ε λεος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ταῖς ἀνετικαῖς καὶ ἡπλωμέναις πόλεσιν, ο σον θαυμαστούμενος τότε ο τ' α ν ἐν πόλει περιοχῆς γένηται· ὡς καὶ διὰ τοῦτο εὐλογητὸν ει ναι τὸν θεὸν πάνυ εὐλογούντων τῶν ἐκ πλείονος περιστάσεως ῥερυσμένων. Τὸ δὲ τῆς ἐκστάσεως ο νομα σημαίνει τὴν παραφροσύνην, δηλοῖ δὲ καὶ τὸν θαυμασμὸν μετ' ἐκπλήξεως γινόμενον· σημαίνει ἡ παροῦσα λέξις τὸ δεύτερον τῶν σημαινομένων. ο γὰρ λέγει 66 ε στιν τοιοῦτον· ̓Εν ἐκστάσει, τουτέστιν ἐν ἐκπλήξει γεγενημένος, ει πα ̓Απέρριμμαι α ρα ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν σου, τουτέστιν μακρὰν ε δοξα ει ναι τῶν ἐποπτικῶν καὶ ἐπισκοπευτικῶν σου δυνάμεων, καὶ ἐπεὶ ου τω διατεθεὶς παρεκάλεσα μὴ ἀπερριμμένος μεῖναι ἀλλ' ἐπιφανῆναί μοι τὸ πρόσωπον τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν σου. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο εἰσήκουσας τῆς φωνῆς τῆς δεήσεώς μου ἐν τῷ κεκραγέναι με πρὸς σέ. 279 Ps 30,24ab Μιᾶς ἀληθείας ου σης τῆς εἰπούσης ̓Εγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀλήθεια, πολλαὶ συνίστανται ἐν τοῖς μετέχουσιν τῆς μιᾶς ἑκάστης ψυχῆς ἀλήθειαν ἐχούσης, ο ν ἐδέξατο τύπον ἐκ τῆς μονογενοῦς ἀληθείας. ἐπεὶ ου ν πάσας τὰς ἀληθείας ταύτας ἐκζητεῖ κύριος, τιμῆσαι ἐπ' αὐτὰς βούλεται τοὺς ε χοντας αὐτάς. τούτου χάριν, οἱ ο σιοι αὐτοῦ, ἐκζητήσατε αὐτόν, οὐκ ἀμισθὶ καταλύοντες ἐφ' ῃ ε χετε ἀληθείᾳ. 280 Ps 31,1a Καὶ ἐπεὶ πολλὰ κεκρυμμένα ὁ ψαλμὸς ε χει, συνέσεως χρεία τῷ ἐντυγχάνοντι, ι να συνιέναι δυνηθῇ ε καστα τῶν ἀσαφῶς εἰρημένων. 281 Ps 31,1bc ̓Ανομιῶν καὶ ἁμαρτιῶν διαφορὰν ει ναί φασιν τοιαύτην· αἱ ἁμαρτίαι τῶν μηδὲ ο ντιν' ου ν νόμον προσηκαμένων ἀνομίαι καλοῦνται, τῶν κατὰ παράβασιν νόμου πραττομένων ἁμαρτιῶν ὀνομαζομένων. Μακάριοι ου ν εἰσιν ω ν ἀφίενται αἱ ἀνομίαι, α ρτι τῷ θείῳ λόγῳ προσερχομένων· Μακάριοι δὲ καὶ ω ν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ο τ' α ν παρακούσαντες τοῦ νόμου υ στερον μετανοήσωσιν. α φεσις μὲν ἐπὶ τῶν ἀνομιῶν, ἐπικάλυψις δὲ ἐπὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ει ρηται τῷ τὰς ἀνομίας πάντῃ ἀφίεσθαι. συγγνωστοὶ γὰρ οἱ δίχα νόμου ἁμαρτάνοντες τῶν ἐπικρυπτομένων ἁμαρτιῶν οὐ πάντῃ ἀφιεμένων ἀλλ' ἐξ ἀγάπης ἐπισκιαζομένων· ̓Αγάπη γὰρ καλύπτει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν. Χρῶνται δέ τινες τῷ μὲν Μακάριοι ω ν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι ἐπὶ τῶν τὸ λουτρὸν εἰς α φεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν ἐσχηκότων, τῷ δὲ Καὶ ω ν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν ἐπὶ τῶν ἐκ μετανοίας ἐπικρυψάντων τὰ ἁμαρτήματα. εἰσὶν δὲ οι λαμβάνουσιν τὴν μὲν προτέραν ἐπὶ τῶν πιστευόντων ἐθνῶν, τὴν δὲ δευτέραν ἐπὶ τῶν ἐκ περιτομῆς τὸν σωτῆρα προσηκαμένων. 282 Ps 31,2 ̔Ο ἀναμάρτητος οὐχ ἁπλῶς α νθρωπος ἀλλ' ἀνὴρ διὰ τὴν τελειότητα λέγεται. ου τω γοῦν ὁ θεὸς οὐ λογίζεται ἁμαρτίαν η τοι τῷ ἀφίεσθαι αὐτὴν η τῷ μηδ' ο λως γεγονέναι. ἁρμόσει γὰρ τοῦτο
english: The manifest works of providence can serve as his face, for through them we perceive God; but his secret, private words are the basis of all things, though we do not perceive them in the perfection of reality.

From the disturbance of men—those human doctrines promising things to men while causing disturbance, through which they trouble the uninstructed—God, making those who hope in him outside of this disturbance, hides them in the secrecy of his face in all the ways mentioned. He will cover them in a tent from the opposition of tongues. He who has reached the perfection of all progress, having withdrawn from it, understands the truth through which it is un-deceivable; but he who encounters it while still progressing needs the covering of God in a tent, that is, of various tongues, or rather various false doctrines. For it is said toward the perfect: 'And every voice that shall rise up against you for judgment shall defeat them all' (Ps 30:22-23). For every heterodox word rises up desiring to be judged alongside the ecclesiastical opinion. But he who thinks the things of the church will defeat them all.

Not such a great wonder is worthy of being shown by the mercy of God in the hostile and smoothed-over cities, which would be wondered at if it occurred in a city of dominion; just as for this reason God is most blessed, being praised by those who have been rescued from greater disturbance. And the name of ecstasy signifies madness, and also denotes the wonder occurring with astonishment; the present word signifies the second of these meanings. For he says such a thing: 'In ecstasy,' that is, having occurred in astonishment, 'I have been cast away far from the presence of your eyes' (Ps 31:9), that is, far from the glory of your supervisory and inspecting powers; and since I have thus arranged, I pleaded not to remain cast away but that the face of [the Lord] might appear to me.

source_text: μάλιστα τῷ Χριστῷ κατὰ τὴν οἰκονομίαν· καὶ τὸ Οὐκ ε στιν ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ δόλος ὁμοίως ἐκδεκτέον η τῷ ἀποβεβληκέναι η τῷ μὴ ἐσχηκέναι δόλον. οὐκ ε στιν δὲ δόλος ἐν στόματι τοῦ λόγον ἀληθῆ καὶ ἀκατάγνωστον ε χοντος. 283 Ps 31,3 ̓Απὸ τοῦ ἀληθινοῦ φωτὸς καταυγαζόμενος ἐν ἡμέρᾳ διῆγον καὶ ἐν ο λῃ ταύτῃ ε κραζον ὑμνῶν εὐχόμενος. ἐπεὶ ου ν ἀπὸ ταύτης τῆς κραυγῆς ἐξ ἀπροσεξίας ἐσίγησα, ἐπαιλαιώθη τὰ ἰσχυρὰ καὶ τὰ ευ τονα τῶν δογμάτων, ὀστᾶ μου ὀνομαζόμενα. σημαίνει δὲ τὴν μετάπτωσιν τοῦ ταῦτα λέγοντος τῷ πεπαλαιῶσθαι καὶ μὴ φύσει παλαιὰ ει ναι τὰ ὀστᾶ αὐτοῦ. 284 Ps 31,4 Καὶ ἐν τοῖς προάγουσιν ει ρηται, ὡς ἐν πολλοῖς τόποις τῆς γραφῆς ἡ κολαστικὴ τοῦ θεοῦ δύναμις χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ὀνομάζεται. ταύτην ου ν βαρέως ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς τουτέστιν συνεχῶς λέγει διὰ τὴν ἐπὶ τὸ χεῖρον μεταβολήν. Τὰς βιωτικὰς μέντοι μερίμνας ἡδονάς τε καὶ ἀπάτας τούτου τοῦ αἰῶνος ἀκάνθας ἡρμήνευσεν ὁ σωτήρ. ο τ' α ν ου ν τοιαύτη α κανθα ἐμπαγῇ τινι, εὐθέως εἰς ταλαιπωρίαν στρέφεται. ἰστέον ο τι κατὰ μεταβολὴν καὶ τροπὴν ταλαίπωρός τις γίνεται μὴ φύσει ω ν τοιοῦτος. σημαίνει δὲ ἡ λέξις τὸν οἰκτρὸν καὶ ἐλεεινόν. Καὶ τὸ ἐμπαγῆναι δὲ α κανθαν τὸ μὴ φύσει δηλοῖ ἀλλ' ε ξωθεν ἐπεισιοῦσαν. νυττόμενος ου ν ὑπὸ ταύτης ̓Εστράφην εἰς ταλαιπωρίαν, τὴν διὰ τῆς μετανοίας καὶ τῆς ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου παιδευτικῆς νουθεσίας· Ον γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει, μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ο ν παραδέχεται. ε γνωμεν δὲ ἐν ταῖς Βασιλείαις ο σα ὑπέμεινεν διὰ ταύτην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ὑπὸ κυρίου παιδευόμενος διὰ τὴν προτέραν αὐτοῦ δικαιοσύνην, ι ν' ἐκείνης τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τῆς δι' αὐτὴν τιμωρίας ἀπαλλαγεὶς 67 τὴν προτέραν ὑγείαν ἀναλήψηται. 285 Ps 31,5 ̔Ο εἰς ἁμαρτίαν ἐμπεσὼν ο σον ἐνεργεῖν αὐτὴν βούλεται σκέπει καὶ κρύπτει αὐτήν, ὁ δὲ μισήσας αὐτὴν φανερὰν ποιεῖ τῷ δυναμένῳ ἰάσασθαι δι' ἐξομολογήσεως ἐξαγορεύων αὐτήν. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν ταύτῃ κατάλληλον ἀνομίαν ἀποκαλύπτει· ει δος γὰρ ἁμαρτίας ἡ ἀνομία· πᾶς γὰρ ὁ ἀνομῶν ἁμαρτάνει, οὐ παντὸς ἁμαρτάνοντος ἀνομοῦντος. δύναται ἐκ παραλλήλου εἰρῆσθαι μάλιστα διὰ τὸ Πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν καὶ τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιεῖ, καὶ ἁμαρτία ἐστὶν ἡ ἀνομία. Πραγματικῶς δὲ εἰπὼν ἐξαγορεύειν κατ' ἐμαυτοῦ η ν πεποίηκα ἀνομίαν πλέον ου ᾐτησάμην ε σχον· οὐ μόνον γὰρ ταύτην ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν τῆς καρδίας ἀσέβειαν ἀφῆκεν ὁ θεός. ἀσέβεια δὲ καρδίας ει ναι δύναται ἡ συμβαίνουσα τοῖς πολλοῖς δυσαρέστησις τῆς προνοίας ἐκ τῆς δοκούσης τῶν πραγμάτων ἀνωμαλίας. 286 Ps 31,6a Εἰ καὶ πρακτικῆς ἀνομίας καθαρεύουσιν οἱ ο σιοι, ἀλλά γε χραινομένους ε χουσι τοὺς λογισμοὺς πολλάκις ἐκ τῆς εἰρημένης καρδίας ἀσεβείας. καίτοι οὐ περὶ ἀνομίας η ς οὐκ ε χουσιν οἱ προσευχόμενοι, ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀσεβείας προσεύξονται, α φεσιν αὐτῆς αἰτούμενοι ἐν εὐθέτῳ καιρῷ. ευ θετος δὲ καιρὸς προσευχῆς περὶ τῆς εἰρημένης ἀφέσεως, ο τε τις ἀπὸ πράξεως ῥυπαρᾶς καθαρεύει. καὶ ω σπερ τις τραυματίας ο λος ω ν περὶ ἀμυχῆς οὐκ ἀπαιτήσει ἰατρὸν θεράπειαν ἀλλ' ο λον τὸ σῶμα ὁλόκληρον ε χων ἐν μόνῃ τῇ ἀμυχῇ τυγχάνων, ου τως οὐδεὶς πράξεων ἐναγῶν πεπληρωμένος περὶ καθαρότητος λογισμῶν προσεύξεται ἀλλὰ μόνος πᾶς ο σιος. 287 Ps 31,6b Οτ' α ν κατακλυσμὸς πολλῶν πνευματικῶν ὑδάτων γένηται, ἐσχηκότος τινὸς ἐν ἑαυτῷ πηγὴν υ δατος ἀλλομένου εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον τουτέστιν τῶν ὑδάτων ἐξαφανιζόντων πάντα τὰ ἁμαρτήματα καὶ τὴν ἐπ' αὐτοῖς ἀσέβειαν τῆς καρδίας, οὐκ ἐγγιοῦσιν ἡ ἀσέβεια καὶ ἡ ἀνομία τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν προσευξαμένῳ. 288 Ps 31,7 Τῆς περιεστηκυίας θλίψεως ἀπαλλαγὴν οὐκ α λλως εὑρίσκειν ὁ ταῦτα λέγων νομίζει η καταφυγὼν πρὸς Χριστόν. Ωσπερ δικαιοσύνη καὶ σοφία ου τω καὶ ἀγαλλίαμα τοῦ σπουδαίου ̓Ιησοῦς. φησὶν γοῦν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὡς ἀγαλλίαμα ἡμέτερον· Λύτρωσαί με ἀπὸ τῶν καταδιωκόντων με· καταδιώκουσι γάρ με δαίμονες ἀλιτήριοι καὶ α νθρωποι πονηροί· πείσομαι γὰρ οὐδὲν κακόν, σοῦ ῥυομένου. 289 Ps 31,9 Τουτέστιν μὴ τὸ λογικῶς ἐνεργεῖν ἀποβαλόντες εἰς α λογον πέσητε κατάστασιν, ω στε ι ππῳ διὰ τὸ θηλυμανὲς ὁμοιωθῆναι η ἡμιόνῳ διὰ τὸ ἐστερεῶσθαι πρὸς τὰ κακά· μὴ ἐχόντων γὰρ σύνεσιν ἡ τοιαύτη ὁρμή. Πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὁ προφήτης φησίν· τοὺς γενομένους ὡς ι ππους διὰ τὸ σκιρτητικὸν καὶ ἀφηνιαστικὸν καὶ ἡμίονον σκληρόστομον ἐν χαλινῷ τῷ σῷ λόγῳ καὶ κημῷ τῇ καταλλήλῳ προτροπῇ τὰς σιαγόνας αὐτῶν α γξαις δαμάζων καὶ ε λκων τῷ σῷ χαλινῷ, ῳ α ξεις ὑπὸ ζυγὸν τὸν σόν. Οἱ μὲν εὐεικτοὶ καὶ εὐήνιοι ἑκουσίᾳ ὁρμῇ ἐγγίζουσι τῷ θεῷ, οἱ δὲ προειρημένοι ὡς ι ππος καὶ ἡμίονος διὰ τὸ ἀσύνετον
english: Especially regarding Christ according to the economy; and that there is no deceit in his mouth is likewise to be understood as the fact that he has not possessed deceit. For there is no deceit in the mouth of the Word, being true and unsearchable.

Glancing from the true light in the day, I ran and in this day I cried out to you, praying [Ps 31:3]. Since I did not fall silent from this cry due to inattention, my bones were struck, both the strong and the soft of the dogmas, which are called my bones. And he means by saying these things the falling away, that his bones are becoming old, but are not old by nature.

And in those things that lead forward it is said, as in many places of the Scripture, that the punishing power of God is called his hand [Ps 31:4]. That this lies heavily upon him day and night—that is, he says continuously—is because of the change that comes upon the hand. The Savior interpreted the cares of life, both the pleasure and the thorns of deceit of this age. And if one is pierced by such a thorn, he is immediately turned into misery. It must be understood what one becomes miserable through change and turning, not being such by nature. The word means the wretched and the pitiable. And to be pierced by a thorn signifies not being such by nature, but it approaching from without. 'I was turned into misery' through repentance and through the instructive admonishment of the Lord; for the Lord loves whom he disciplines, but he scourges every son whom he does not receive [Heb 12:6]. Let us know in the Kings who endured because of this sin, being disciplined by the Lord because of his former righteousness, so that, having been freed from that sin and the punishment through it, he might take back his former health [1 Kings 15:3-5].

He who has fallen into sin, if he wishes to work it, provides a cover and hides it; but he who has hated it makes it manifest to the one who is able to heal through confession, declaring it [Ps 31:5]. But he also reveals the lawlessness appropriate to this; for the sight of sin is lawlessness; for everyone who acts lawlessly sins, though not everyone who sins acts lawlessly. It can be said by analogy, especially because everyone who does sin also does lawlessness, and lawlessness is sin. But having spoken truly, 'I confessed my sin against myself' [Ps 32:5] which I have done...

I did not ask for more lawlessness than what I had; for God has forgiven not only this but also the impiety of the heart. And impiety of the heart is able to be the dissatisfaction of providence occurring to many through the irregularity of things as they seem.

If even the righteous cleanse themselves from practical lawlessness (Ps 31:6a), they still often have impure thoughts from the aforementioned impiety of the heart. Even if those who pray do not have [thoughts] concerning lawlessness, they will pray concerning impiety, asking for its forgiveness in a favorable time. And a favorable time of prayer concerning the aforementioned forgiveness is when one cleanses himself from practical filthiness. And just as one who is wounded in a small scratch will not demand a physician's treatment, but having the whole body intact, only suffering in that single scratch, so no one filled with the guilt of actions will pray concerning the purity of thoughts, but only every righteous person.

When a flood of many spiritual waters comes (Ps 31:6b), having had a spring of water within himself changing into eternal life—that is, the waters vanishing all sins and the impiety of the heart upon them—impiety and lawlessness will not approach the one who has prayed for them.

He who says these things thinks he finds deliverance from the standing affliction in no other way than by fleeing to Christ (Ps 31:7). Just as righteousness and wisdom [are], so also is the joy of the diligent Jesus. For he says to Him as our joy: 'Deliver me from those pursuing me; for lawless demons and evil men pursue me; for I will be persuaded that nothing evil [can happen], You saving me.'

That is, not having cast away acting logically, you do not fall into an irrational state (Ps 31:9), such that through being headstrong you become like a mule because of being deficient toward evils; for such an impulse does not have understanding. The prophet says toward God: [He brings] those who have become like horses because of being skittish and unruly, and a mule, hard-mouthed, subduing their bits with nails and drawing them with Your suitable bridle, with which You lead them under Your yoke. The compliant and gentle ones approach God by a voluntary impulse, but those previously mentioned as horses and mules because of the lack of understanding...

english: Having become subject to the aforementioned necessity of the afflictions, they will be drawn toward you (Ps 32:1). Those who have accomplished an ethical life are righteous, rejoicing in the Lord, and it is necessary that those who flee from all the crookedness of false doctrine be upright. For it is fitting to praise God with these, since praise is not beautiful in the mouth of a sinner (Ps 32:2).

Confession and here thanksgiving are expressed. This ought not to be made on a lyre. And if the body is a lyre, the stretched strings are none other than the senses; for being struck by divine hearing, they perceive the hearing and the heavens and those in them, seeing them as to marvel at the Creator, and using the other senses praiseworthy, we confess to the Lord rhythmically and harmoniously with this lyre. But if one should conceive the soul as a lyre, its powers—which are the mnemonic, the assentive, the productive, and others according to reason—being struck like strings by the mind musically, will confess to the Lord. Musicians say there is a difference between the psalmtery and the lyre, such as this: they say the lyre is composed of the lower parts, while the psalmtery is from the upper parts with the strings, and it is more straight through strings. Since the soul is given as lyres, the spirit of man, which is in it, is perhaps something other than the mind, is a psalmtery, singing not to anyone else but to God. For we use right thoughts and with our own spirit we receive the Holy Spirit, and we sing victoriously in a ten-stringed psalmtery. And perhaps from the ten strings its perfection is shown. For such a number is found continually being hymned in the Scriptures. And God used only ten general terms for the high priest Moses, and the people are commanded to offer ten.

He who hastens to praise God through all things and through voice will sing to God a new song (Ps 32:3), saying an anthem kindred to the new covenant and the newness of the Spirit, so that he might praise God not only with lyre and psalmtery but also with voice. And he wishes to sing praiseworthy with a shout of triumph; for the shout is a voice. He who makes a shout without distraction and without insignificance against the conquered enemies, then he says, 'You have sung well,' while those having conquered say, 'Shout!'

Because of the enemies. The word of the Lord, which he gives to those pursuing knowledge, is straight and not a crooked deception (Ps 32:4). Moreover, the workers perform the appropriate things for this word, being fulfilled in faith; and the works which the word of God performs are in faith, that is, they are firm and unshakeable, and the word by which he governs and provides is straight.

If someone were to call the word of God a straight word, the works he performed in this word, being fulfilled in faith, would be easy; for the paradoxical works of Jesus are his works according to the faith of those, becoming [things] for them: 'Let it be done to you according to your faith' (Ps 32:5). He himself is God, or his straight word, accepting judgment in that he must avenge the virtues being insulted by the wicked, but loving mercy, helping those being led to judgment by his own goodness. For if he were to observe all their works, no one would be able to endure. Therefore, even before judgment, he loves mercy. For if it were not so, all would suddenly be lost.

The heavens were made thin, having the most corruptible nature (Ps 32:6); for such is the nature of the heavens. But when taken allegorically, of all those who think upon the image of the so-called heavenly, their firm grip and stability becomes [theirs] through the word of the Lord, and their power, by which they are able, is not produced by anything else but by the Holy Spirit. And by this spoken word, pious men discourse that the Holy Spirit is the creative [force].

Just as water held in a skin or in another vessel is not permitted to pour out outside of the container holding it, so the vastness of the sea's water is limited by a certain boundary, not being allowed to exceed the appointed rivers. For if it did not hold back by the command of God, it would have overflowed the whole earth. But stop, unless even this is made clear: since, calling the water of the sea, he pours it out upon all the earth through the rains, his command, practicing justice, makes the water ethereal, as if composing a cloud of mists to be carried over the earth. Allegorically, the life of men is often called a sea.

english: Because of the still and salty nature of the waters upon the earth, the sea, which is called the abyss, gathers them together—not as if they were scattered by a storm—as if in a skin, so that the Savior might take up the body to become calm and drinkable. He places them in the abysses of treasuries.

Nothing in creation is carried out disordered; for as a seed is held in its own treasuries by its own will, so it is released and held as it seems fit to it. It is said, moreover, that He brings the winds out of the treasuries, not by their own impulse, these being carried, but by the will of the Creator, sometimes closing them and sometimes bringing them out. But He also opens the treasury of the good heaven and gives rain to the seed of the earth, just as a seed is held, and He holds the rain by closing the heaven, as regarding the prophet Elijah. And the abysses, because they are not able to harm through the unlimited multitude of the waters, are placed in treasuries, enclosing them, so that if anyone wishes to use them, it is as is profitable according to the season (Ps 32:7).

It is also possible for the ungraspable of His thoughts and the unsearchable of His judgments, which happen to be abysses, to be placed in the hidden treasuries of knowledge and of wisdom, so that no one might attain to this from himself unless God should grant it (Ps 32:8-9). Since they came into being by His speaking and were created by His commanding, let them be shaken by Him; for it belongs to the Creator to change things toward the good (Ps 32:11a). 'They came into being' signifies the essence of those things regarded as being, and 'they were created' signifies the adornment having come into being after the essence. If all things came into being and were created by the speaking and commanding of God, then no one other than the creative Word spoke and commanded; and this is the Son of God.

And elsewhere it is said: 'For who has counseled that God the Holy should scatter?' (Ps 32:11b). Just as in other places it is said of God in a human way—as having hands and eyes and other things—so also He speaks of His heart, meaning His deliberative and intellectual energy. The thoughts of this energy, being unlifted and certain, extend from generation to generation, that is, through all the generations.

Divine thoughts remain as a conviction. Perhaps he did not cast thoughts upon the generation of the circumcised, but he casts these upon the generation from the believing Gentiles; for he has not called out against others, but against those in whom the shadows of the circumcised are hidden.

They inhabit the earth, not humans alone, but also invisible spirits and the other mortal animals (Ps 32:14b). The care of God, overseeing all, extends to everyone upon the earth, bringing them out from his aforementioned dwelling-place.
Since God understands not only the things accomplished but also the intention from which these things are activated (Ps 32:15b), it is said that he sees not, but understands all their works.

For that a king is not saved by much strength, you shall learn from history (Ps 32:16-17a); Pharaoh did not have a great array, but God cast his armor and his strength into the sea. And all history is full of such things. And he says that the one who is exceedingly strong will not be saved in the strength present to him; but having understood this, he speaks concerning Goliath. And if the allusion also indicates the god-fighter, no one shall be saved in a multitude of strengths of impious dogmas. The one called 'not strong' is to be found in Isaiah saying, 'Giant and strong,' but the god-fighter again by the same author: 'Giants come to fill my wrath, rejoicing.' And also in Genesis: 'And Nebroth was a mighty hunter before the Lord.' A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but the help is by the Lord (Prov 21:31).

Since the departing light from the eyes of God is life (Ps 32:19), the pious, participating in this and having hope upon the lion, would be saved from the death that follows wickedness, as if their souls were being made alive; but participating in the heavenly bread (and the word of God is not bread), they are nourished in famine. For famine he speaks of not the scarcity of edible foods, but the deprivation of divine teachings. Accompanying this is the saying, 'I will send famine upon the earth' (Amos 8:11), not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord.

english: We wait for a protector upon it with the soul, that is, from the depth of the intellect. Perhaps even those unable to benefit themselves before the arrival will wait with expectation for the coming helper and protector Savior. And in him our heart will rejoice.

Others are gladdened by something temporary, pouring out the soul, while others of these are absent; but we possess divine and eternal joy in the Lord, having not a bodily well-being but of mind and heart. Therefore we also hope in his holy name, praying that he might take part in sanctifying us, becoming a cause for us.

Just as those cast into the furnace in Babylon (Ps 33:4), praising God for not being burned by the fire, received all creation into this, knowing they were not sufficient for something so far off (for great is the praising of God); so also he who says 'Magnify the Lord with me' (Ps 34:3) wants all creation to join in this with the gentle ones. But to magnify God is not to increase his magnitude (for he is immeasurable; this is a matter of bodies, but God is incorporeal), but to think of the great things not as being toward him, but toward us, and to speak about him.

And those prepared with the same mind and the same purpose exalt his name. And the approach of God is exalted toward the created things, not rising from the lowly, but rather those who think of it do not fall to the ground, but contemplate high and heavenly things. For as they profane the name of God, not by the name itself becoming unholy, but by those surrounding it acting and thinking profanely, so also it is sanctified from our actions; for God the Savior says this also, teaching in the prayer 'Hallowed be thy name' (Matt 6:9), not of his name itself becoming holy by itself from being not holy. For it is necessary that it be hallowed in us by those who think and act holily. And so also the discourse concerning God...

The calling of God is a precise thing according to the thought of God. We possess it being sanctified, performing all things according to holiness. For most sons of men are in error and ignorance, the calling of God seems in a way to be pulling them in a way they should not. Some have called idols gods and their own belly.

Since 'I sought and He answered me' (Ps 33:5a) is given, it is clear what seeking and calling implies; since not only in name does one fulfill the things of a prayer, but also having sought the Lord with right mind and pure life through all these things, He found him answering. 'And from all my troubles He rescued me' (Ps 33:5b) is carried as 'And from all my wanderings He rescued me.'

Since 'The Lord is true light, he who approaches Him partakes of His light' (Ps 33:6), having been enlightened, having taken on much boldness, he possesses an unashamed face. The Spirit commands one to approach the Lord volitionally, so that having been enlightened, we may cast away all shame from the face of the soul.
Here he calls 'poor' the one not able to save himself from the present troubles (Ps 33:7). And all of us possess this poverty, so that he speaks very much about one needing salvation from God.

If he here denotes those fearing the Lord who have the spirit of slavery (Ps 33:8), we shall not say that angels are not surrounding them to rescue them from those intending to harm, just as even the little ones of those believing upon the Savior have angels, seeing the face of the Father in the heavens, having God, the perfect, in communion. If we take the perfect ones who fear God to have an angel placed around them to rescue them, we shall say nothing other than the angel of the great purpose of God the Savior. Following this is that which is said by Jacob: 'The angel who rescues me from all my evils; from all...'

english: He is not an angel sent to rescue from evils, but the indicated Savior (Ps 33:9a). Regarding God, the good means the same as the good. Since he is also the bread of life, the Spirit commands those who do not have desire for it not to be overwhelmed by it, but only to taste it. For the tasting is sufficient to make them desirous and to make them desire to experience it. And to taste signifies, as if by a little, to know and to examine concerning God. For he says that a pure tasting imparts to the souls an incomparable enjoyment of those things which are above human and wonderful (Ps 33:9b).

Blessed is the man who hopes in him (Ps 33:9b). The man who exists by hoping in God completely and without fail is blessed (Ps 33:10). We say that fear is twofold. For immediately, someone coming to God, having taken up fear toward him, makes straight all his commandments. For it is said: Fear God and keep his commandments (Ps 33:10). But in the present verse, concerning a fear that has ascended above, he speaks of that on which he calls the saints to have become; for having taken on the introductory fear, they hurried toward holiness. But now, he commands those saints not to fear God, but to have the fear that fulfills all good, so that the one having it may be unceasing (Ps 33:12b).

It is to be noted that, just as other good things are taught, so also the divine fear is taught, from which we learn not to signify a passion-driven fear; for an undidactic fear exists by nature not only in humans but also in irrational animals (Ps 33:12b). Since those looking upon the whole of God—powers called eyes in a figurative sense—look upon the righteous, but also his ears are ready to receive their petition, for this reason he says: if you wish to enjoy these, turning away from evil, do the good (Ps 33:15-16).

Those placing all this thoughtlessly and doing evils as if God were not watching, will encounter punishment, receiving a reminder that God is present to exact judgment upon them (Ps 33:17). And according to this, it is said that the face of God shines upon them, or that how their remembrance shall be destroyed not ever, but from the earth. But blessed is the one whose remembrance is destroyed from the earth; for thus the law shall be written.

His [protection] in the heavens. But the workers of iniquity do evil. The Lord will preserve the bones of the righteous (Ps 33:21), not allowing even by chance for them to be broken, nor for the doctrines of the righteous nor for his own powers to be overturned.

He who sins is deprived of life (Ps 33:22a) as he approaches the keeping of the commandments, falling into evil death. And evil death is that which is contrary to the good life, which inflicts pain upon the subject; for Job was also struck with evil, as it is evident that it was inflicting pain. Those who hate what is loved harm not others but themselves (Ps 33:22b). And indeed, the one who hates the diligent righteous man errs and falls into punishment.

It is to be noted what the redemption truly is: it frees souls from captivity; for if bodies are ever redeemed, it is not beforehand but this happens by consequence (Ps 33:23a); and souls are saved, not of others, but of his slaves. Those who hope in the Lord will not be disappointed of the things hoped for and expected (Ps 33:23b).

He also teaches in other places those who fight against him, saying, 'Many are those fighting against me from below' (Ps 34:1bc). Those who were not fighting against him were acting unjustly toward him who had done no injustice; but he does not wish for the enemies to be unpunished, but rather that they be judged by the injustice of the enemies, opposing the justice of God, being destructive against the injustice, just as the light is destructive to the darkness. For injustice, being contrary to and set against the justice of God, will be fought against from it. Therefore also the unrighteous man would be called an enemy to the righteous. But justice makes the righteous a friend to God, just as the just are friends to the just. Therefore it has been said, 'The Lord is righteous and loves righteousness' (Ps 34:1c). The righteous, trusting in his own righteousness, says, 'Judge me, Lord, and judge my case' (Ps 34:1d). The Lord is therefore judging those who do injustice, destroying the injustice within them. And he also fights against those who fight against the righteous, doing this for the good of those being fought against, as if they might at some time cease by practicing righteousness (Ps 34:1b).
The act of doing injustice signifies harm in the [words]: 'Behold, I have given you to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon...' (Ps 91:13).

english: [He will protect you from] all the power of the enemy, and he will not wrong you in any way. Since many have set out to fight me through false doctrine and other evils, fight them instead on my behalf; for they shall be irrefutably destroyed, since you are the Lord who crushes wars (Ps 34:2).

Taking hold of your companion's shield and the wealth of truth, 'Arise to my help' (Ps 34:3), that is, become my champion. In the same way, you will think of the sword. It is noteworthy that in the upcoming verses he used imperative words instead of optative ones; for 'Let their way be made' (Gen 7:21) instead of 'May their way be made,' and 'Let him come' instead of 'May he come,' and the rest similarly. And 'he shall fall in the snare' (Ps 34:8); for according to their actions, each one is punished.

When these things happen to them, my soul shall rejoice (Ps 34:9), seeing by providence the wicked being punished and the diligent being benefited; but it will also experience delights, having gained experience of his salvation, of God. Let those who desire to take everything from the bare word and nothing allegorically be rebuked, even from the context of the verse. For it is not foolish to think that the bones possess the thought of God, so as to praise him and know that no one is like him. For concerning the bones of man (and his powers and true doctrines are these), it is said, 'All my bones' (Ps 34:10); for through every thought and true doctrine, I was established that nothing of the created is like the Lord; for he himself is the image of the invisible God and the character of the divine essence.

Furthermore, whether the poor man is more [distinguished] than the laborer, and whether by essence or by thought, the one who is poor and remains poor, and the one who has fallen from wealth, and the laborer who acquires things through toil to live. Those who, rising up and stirring themselves up as witnesses of injustice rather than justice, ask sophistically, 'I do not know.' For the diligent knows nothing of the wicked, that is, he has not been mixed with any of the evil ones; and a testimony: 'He who keeps the commandment shall not know an evil word' (Prov 14:16). And in

For here the 'will not know' stands instead of 'has not trusted' or 'has not been tested' regarding an evil word. For it is a falsehood to think that one who guards the divine commandment does not know an evil word; for having a discernment of evil and good, he has turned away from all other things to keep the commandment. He does not say such a thing: 'They, interrogating me, seeking to distinguish my lack of experience or knowledge or intention regarding evils, questioned me about them, just as the Egyptians did to Joseph, and the elders to Susanna.' (Ps 34:12).

When I, desiring to perform my duties toward all people blamelessly, wishing to live in peace with all men if possible, they instead returned evil to me for these good things, enemies and ill-wishers appearing through all things; and they attempted to annul in themselves the good fruitfulness of my soul. If, indeed, being persuaded by their questions, I had become such as they wished to make me, my soul would have been rendered barren, no longer receiving the divine marriages of the Bridegroom. But if the disciples of the Teacher were to say, 'and thus the soul of the Teacher is not rendered barren, falling into errors through its own stumbling block, annulling those born from it through discipleship,' [this would be an error].

Because luxury, stirring up irrational pleasures, irrationally exalts the soul, while fasting, doing the opposite, cuts down the passions; but also praiseworthy fasting effects a cleansing of sins, truly working blindness and humbling the soul. For him who has prayed well, the prayer returns to him, bringing back the good things for his sake, and having turned back, it is drawn into the bosom of the one who sent it. And 'the bosom' signifies their ruling principle; for their humiliation was into their bosom in the land of Egypt, and all things come into the bosom of the innocent; and in this way all the righteous go into the bosom of Abraham, that is, into the same mind and promise as he. (Ps 34:13).

I did not lie so pleasingly toward those wishing to harm the things previously mentioned, as if one were pleasing to a neighbor and a closer brother; but not so, as they were not pleasing to me as a neighbor and a closer brother. (Ps 34:14). Since I lied as if concerning genuine brothers...

english: Seeing them through whom they act as if dying, I humbled myself by mourning them and frowning upon them, seeking to preserve the one able to keep me harmless from them (Ps 34:15ab).

The present [text] is explanatory if it is possible for [God] to repay me evil for good. For while I mourn and frown over them, through which they possess death, they gather together in joy against me, as if they were to take me by the hand; and they have plotted against me, so that they might gather and rejoice (Ps 34:15c).

Because of those who attempted against me, I was logically scourged in my soul; but I remain harmless, neither perceiving nor knowing those approaching them. If ever, when the enemies were dividing, a disturbance in the thoughts occurred toward sin, so that I was to be scourged by sensations from the thoughts, I did not reveal these lashes to those opposing me, lest they, not taking a starting point from the branch of the soul, should rather attack me (Ps 34:15c-16).

Having gathered and rejoiced against me, they were split apart by divine providence; having been dissolved and scattered in such a way, they did not repent, that is, they did not recognize for whom they had advised wickedly, but instead they attempted the same against others. Because of all those who were striving to make an attempt upon me, they were not able to see or take hold of me; therefore, they turned to mocking and sneering at me. Watching like wild beasts, they bared their teeth, that is, their angry and wrathful power, against me; for wanting to devour me, they failed (Ps 34:16-17).

The holy one says: 'Lord, how long will you look?' (Ps 34:17). For when you look, all the aforementioned things will be gathered together with those doing them. And he says 'only begotten' because his soul has it alone; for one must not pay attention to the myth-making regarding metempsychosis. Perhaps the only begotten besides his soul is the essence of the spirit joined to the soul; for it is only begotten in its separation from all those in us according to divinity (Ps 34:18).

A great assembly is gathered from many saints, a heavy people, the steadfast and solid, praying and interceding (Ps 34:22b). Since you are present with me, the enemies are far; do not depart from me, lest they come upon me alone (Ps 34:22b).

Because God's long-suffering is often called his breath (Ps 34:23), the Lord is driven to indignation by the pressing of enemies, saying: 'Arise, Lord, and take up my judgment,' that is, stand up with the power of your strength, so that the things concerning me against my enemies may be examined. For this is for good, since they hate me unjustly and those who hate me without cause shall certainly be condemned (Ps 34:27-28).

And not everyone, the writer, took the psalm toward David and toward Christ, but rather toward Christ; another [took it] indistinctly toward the righteous; and the third toward David alone. Regarding the overcoming of enemies, one says it is spoken prophetically of things that will happen, while the other says it is for the benefit of the enemies, that these things be said so that they might be ashamed, be trapped, and receive sensation of their own sins and retreat from the way they feared. The third says that David lives a legalistic and not an evangelical life; for the law, he says, forbids loving the neighbor and hating the enemy, and speaking badly; for David, living evangelically, says, 'If I repaid evil to those repaying evil to me' (Ps 35:2). Finally, not everyone says these things were spoken prophetically as that he would certainly be.

He who considers himself lawless in himself says nothing other than that he sins. For someone, having first agreed in thought, proceeds to sin in practice. He can also say in himself that he sins, which is 'But if all in your mind...' 'I will ascend into heaven,' and the following. 'If fear is held before the eyes of a man, he abstained from every sin,' but since he does not have it in himself, he says, 'to sin.' A testimony of not sinning for one who has fear is 'That how your fear may come upon you, so that you may not sin' (Ps 35:3).

He who has become lawless, knowing his lawlessness to be hateful; if he were to be observed, he would deceive before Him, so that the shame of the lawlessness might not be found, lest he should hate it. This is what those who reason sophistically do, agreeing with sin as if it were a duty and not something contrary to reason. There is another scripture (Ps 35:4-5).
