english: Suffering on our behalf (Ps 68:28). By their own desires and by being handed over to passions, they are the cause of enduring these things, not having God as the cause, since they are handed over to those whom they loved. For He sent them away according to the desires of their hearts, so that they might walk in their own desires, an addition of lawlessness upon their lawlessness.

Since, therefore, they did not receive the truth when it came, but wished to live lawlessly within the shadow of the law, they were also driven out from the place of typical worship, so that I might add to the former lawlessness another, by wanting to keep this outside of Judea. Therefore they do not enter into the righteousness which is through the faith of Jesus Christ, concerning which it is written: 'But now the righteousness of God without law has been revealed, being witnessed by the law and the prophets' (Rom 3:21). For how could those who were always about external things and possessing the shadow, enter into the righteousness which they did not know as God, in order to establish their own? For he says that, not knowing the righteousness of God and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to the righteousness of God; to submit to righteousness and to enter into it are the same thing.

For those having virtue and faith and knowledge of God live: 'Hear, O my life, your life and the length of your days, to love you, Lord your God, with all your heart and with all your soul' (Deut 6:5); but also, 'he who believes in me has eternal life' (John 3:36). It is a book in which those living thus are written: it is the knowledge of God, of him who knows those who are His, to whom it is promised that those not falling under the remembrance of God shall be blotted out.

Rich and being outside of wounds, I have become poor, so that the poor might become rich through my poverty, and having grieved, having been wounded on behalf of wounds made by the burning arrows of the evil one (Ps 69:29). If my being [indifferent]...

A poor and suffering one, as if a reproach were added to my wounds, and I am by nature a poor man, but salvation from the face of God has taken hold of me (Ps 68:34). For having risen from the dead and having been taken up, he cast away the wounds and the poverty which he had on behalf of men. And when the enemies had been destroyed, and especially the devil, it followed that a triumphal song should be shouted by him, having conquered in the name of [Christ].

I came in the name of my Father, and having surpassed by thought him who does not magnify the name, in praise saying great things, not only praising and glorifying him but also contemplating highly the things concerning him; for those who do not magnify God in this way do not find all perceptible magnitude to be far from him being incorporeal. And since to praise God is a sacrifice, according to 'Sacrifice of praise, you will glorify him' (Ps 68:31), having praised the name of God with song and having magnified him in praise, he is encouraged as 'It pleases God [that one] brings a young bull with horns and weapons, being brought for a sacrifice.' Therefore also, to those who do not sacrifice thus, he says, 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice, a knowledge of God or burnt offerings' (Ps 50:8).

Let these things be seen by the poor in spirit, whom Jesus strengthened against every evil phalanx; for seeing such courage in them, to be rejoiced eternally according to 'Eternal joy shall take hold of them.' For he is not the one loosing those who are fallen and bringing out from bonds those who are bound and from the prison (Ps 68:35-36). Those formerly called prophets and God-beloved men, and after these, servants and ministers of the gospel (Ps 68:37).

english: It is possible to fail to remember those things which were previously described as having precise and complete knowledge, following the command: 'To the end, into remembrance, to save me, Lord, you are' (Ps 69:3-4). This is the saving of everyone who has cast away the use and knowledge of the good through forgetfulness.

For all, having been made straight according to the image and likeness of God, have the thoughts concerning God scattered within them. For sin always enters through negligence; if it happens that after its practice one repents, he remembers the good, for his thought is rational and having become according to the image of God.

Since sin is led by insensitivity and ignorance of the good, and because of this one acts with pleasure and boldness, it is said concerning some that they have glory upon which they ought to be ashamed; for he says, 'The glory is in their shame' (Ps 69:3). And the prophet says, 'Be ashamed of your boasting' (Ps 69:3), for it brings mockery and destruction.

Those running toward evil without feeling, if they were to receive feeling and thought of it, would cease to desire to do it; the good turns them from the evil to do the good. He says that this very thing happens to those destined for various things: 'They would have been ashamed, knowing they are evil, having been ensnared and having failed to remember what they did; for they sought to lead my soul into the same wickedness as theirs, or to kill me, because I do not run with them into the apostasy in which they are outside of God' (Ps 51:13).

Saying this, he reproaches them, saying, 'They would have turned back, no longer desiring to hasten toward evil, and they would have been ashamed, regarding those things on which they acted wickedly, desiring that which harms me to be for me' (Ps 51:14). The one repenting turns back, running again toward what he left, desiring to be with the good and to be ashamed, even though before the repentance he spoke arrogantly against the one being persecuted, saying, 'Well done, well done,' that is, 'Let us prevail, as you flee from us' (Ps 51:15).

One must watch those who desire evil toward me; until they have the power to intend to do evil and harm, they will not be able to bring about evil, unless God delivers them (Ps 51:16). Not those who plot against money, but those who plot against the soul.
But the assault on the soul from God is alienation.

english: Hope is held toward a person. One must strive, for the Lord holds hope; for blessed is the man who has trusted in the Lord (Ps 40:4), and he will be the Lord's hope. For this hope is living; therefore it is written, 'Born again into a living hope' (1 Pet 1:3). It has been said by the one possessing it, 'Not to be put to shame through the ages; and in your righteousness save me and bring me out' (Ps 7:10). God saves in righteousness those who hasten to be outside of iniquities, just as in wisdom He takes to Himself those who desire to possess it. And he who says the things set forth prays to be saved and to be set apart even from those who do wrong, 'Stand fast.' For it seems to follow to submit this to those spoken of in the prophecy 'For the sake of other captives' (Ps 141:7); for they do not justly demand to be saved and set apart. For some were doing wrong, but the Israelites did no wrong. It shall also be said thus: since practical virtue is named righteousness, and every sin in practice is injustice from the opposite, he who loves [God] deserves to be saved from injustice, [whereas he] who hates his own soul. And the testimony of saying thus of universal virtue, 'Walking blamelessly and working righteousness,' and the testimony of calling universal sin 'injustice,' is found in: 'I hated and detested injustice' (Ps 52:9), and 'The blood of Jesus Christ will cleanse us from all injustice' (1 John 1:7). He who wishes to surpass the shadow according to the law says this, believing in Jesus Christ, so that he might be found not having in himself his own righteousness from the law, but the righteousness of God, reckoned toward righteousness. O Lord, [not] of much superiority toward the creatures, but especially toward us humans, to cry out so much, we are not strong enough to reach your ears with the prayer which we offer up; therefore I entreat you by much goodness to incline your way of condescension toward me, so that you might save me, receiving the prayer concerning salvation. Of many desiring to fight me, become my defender; cover me with your shield, concerning which it is said, 'His truth shall surround you with a shield' (Ps 5:12). And since I want you to be for me all things, to become for me an invincible fortress and an unshakeable bulwark, most fortified.

You are a place where I remain outside of all fear from enemies, my refuge and my stronghold. Regarding Ps 70:4, the hand of a sinner is a sinful practice from which it is worthy to be rescued, so that he may not act according to it to any extent. Likewise, when one transgresses and acts wickedly, the effective energies of his actions are placed outside of him, having been rescued by God. Whether the sinner himself or another is the subject of the transgressing and acting wickedly, examine this. For it seems to incline toward the two, if a sinner who transgresses and acts wickedly exists. But if the devil is meant by these names, his hand must be seized and his military-like power must be arranged against every evil and unclean spirit. He who is rescued from the hand of those things, having become under the mighty hand of God, is snatched by nothing from it.

Just as God is the wisdom and power of the holy one, so also He is the endurance and hope of the one enduring unto salvation and hoping in Him. For it is said about these things in the 70th Psalm, 'But now where is my hope? Is it not the Lord?' (Ps 70:5) and in the 71st, 'My hope is in God, the hope of all the ends of the earth' (Ps 71:5). One must oversee 'My hope' from youth, being able to demonstrate how one, having been brought up according to God from infancy, has never possessed any hope other than God. And in addition to this, you will say that from youth there is some hope in God, from which, having stripped off the old man, you put on the new and fresh [man], created according to God in holiness and knowledge of the truth.

Regarding Ps 70:6ab, 'From the womb from my mother's belly' must be understood wisely, not meaning from the time of birth, but rather then moving logically and God-fearingly regarding the one being born; for it is written, 'Even Samuel, before knowing God' (1 Sam 3:7), although he was brought up God-fearingly from tender nails by God-fearing parents. For the children of men have a time from which they are able to move logically. The great Moses says in the wilderness, 'And all the children with us today will not enter into the land of promise, if indeed they do not enter good or evil' (Num 14:29-30). The children do not know good or evil before the fulfillment of the decisive word, how those who know God in this age [do so], just as...

english: To be supported upon Him by choice?

While others are praising rulers, teachers of human lessons, and those very lessons which are indeed glorious and constitute an honorable wealth, our remembrance is in you and not in any other. A scripture is brought forward saying: 'My remembrance is in you always' (Ps 70:5). Regarding both types of scriptures, one must choose 'always' over 'throughout,' to have the remembrance and the recollection continually and without interruption in God.

Those who despise virtue and consider piety an abomination, sinners, are defiling the diligent and the lowly, calling it a terror. For they say among themselves, 'Let us give up the righteous one, since he is troublesome to us.' And since those who think and speak such things are vile to us, they say, 'It is not at all a terror, but it has happened to the many, that is, to the most vulgar,' and they flee from virtue. But even if they speak to me in that same manner, you, being stronger, protect me without harm from them. With this same thought the apostle also says that we have become a cleansing for the world and a reproach to all men (1 Cor 4:10-13). In agreement with this is also: 'We are fools for Christ, but you are wise' (1 Cor 4:10). From the same disposition is also written: 'For I think that what God has shown us the apostles to be, we are last, as if marked for execution' (1 Cor 4:13), and 'That we became a spectacle to the world' (1 Cor 4:9). Such also is what was said to the sinners by God: 'And I will be a terror to Ezekiel' (Ezek 4:14), as the prophet himself says, because of what happens most symbolically through him, to lay this one down for so many days on the right side, and so many again on the left, and the shaving of the hairs of the body. And if even these things are referred to the Savior, appearing to the many as if a terror had happened because of the cross, to visit [them]... And even the appearing as if a terror: for none of the aforementioned was such as the many supposed.

Worthy is his word, the mouth having been named, to be filled with praise (Ps 70:8). But the glory of God is the discourse concerning him, his only-begotten Son; for it is said concerning Christ, as the glory of God was to be revealed upon his appearing. For the glory of God shall be revealed, in majesty...

source_text: αὐτοῦ νοουμένης τῆς ἐν προνοίᾳ καὶ δημιουργίᾳ τάξεως ὡς πολὺ τὸ πρέπον ἐμφαινούσης, μόνῳ γινομένης κελεύματι. τοιαύτη γὰρ καὶ ἡ προνοητικὴ τῷ δυναμένῳ λέγειν Κατενόησα τὰ ε ργα σου καὶ ἐξέστην· σύμφωνον δὲ τῷ παρόντι τὸ ̓Ενέβαλεν εἰς τὸ στόμα μου ᾳ σμα καινόν, υ μνον τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν. 741a Ps 70,9a ̓Επὶ σοὶ ἡ ἐλπίς μου ἐκ νεότητός μου. παρακαλῶ ἐν τῇ καταστάσει ταύτῃ μέχρι γήρως διαμεῖναι οὐκ ἀπορριπτόμενος ἀπὸ σοῦ, παντὸς τοῦ φαῦλα πράσσοντος καὶ ἀνομοῦντος ἀπορριπτομένου. Θεωρηθείη δὲ καὶ πρὸς διάνοιαν· ἐπεὶ γῆρας τίμιον οὐ τὸ πολυχρόνιον, πολιᾶς ου σης τοῦ ε νδον ἀνθρώπου τῆς θείας φρονήσεως καὶ γήρως τοῦ δι' ἀκροτάτην ἀρετὴν ἀκηλιδώτου βίου· ἐπεὶ ἀκμὴν ἐν τῷ προκόπτειν εἰμί, παρακαλῶ μὴ ἀπορριφῆναι ἀλλὰ συνεργεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῆς ἀγαθότητός σου, ε ως φθάσω ἐπὶ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦ ἀκηλιδώτου βίου. 742a Ps 70,10.11 Εἰ γὰρ Χριστὸς ὁ λέγων, ε πεται τῷ Εἰ ἐχθρὸς ὠνείδισέ με, ὑπήνεγκα α ν. τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ τὰ ἐπὶ τούτων περὶ τοῦ ̓Ιούδα φησίν. 743a Ps 70,14–16 Τῶν ἐμῶν αἰσχυνομένων ἐχθρῶν τῷ κατ' ἐμοῦ μάτην ἐσπουδακέναι, προστίθημι καὶ νῦν ἐπινικίως αἰνῶν σε τῇ προλαβούσῃ αἰνέσει περὶ η ς ε φην ̓Εν σοὶ ἡ υ μνησίς μου διαπαντός. ἐνδιέβαλλον δὲ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ οἱ λέγοντες ̔Ο θεὸς ἐγκατέλιπεν αὐτόν. μεγίστη γὰρ δηλοῦται κατὰ τοῦ ἐγκαταλειπομένου διαβολὴ πρὸς ο τὸ ̓Εγὼ δὲ διὰ παντὸς ἐλπιῶ φησίν, δεικνὺς ὡς οὐδεμίαν ἐγκαταλείψει παρέσχετο χώραν. Πρὸς τὸ ̔Ο θεὸς ἐγκατέλιπεν αὐτὸν τὸ ̓Εγὼ δὲ διαπαντὸς ἐλπιῶ ει πεν. καὶ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ἀδίκως φονώντων ὡς ἀπωλείᾳ περιβαλεῖν αὐτὸν θέλειν, ἀβλαβὴς διαμείνας ἀπ' αὐτῶν ἐξαγγέλλει παρ' ο λον αὐτοῦ τὸν βίον (ἡμέραν ὀνομαζόμενον) τὴν δικαιοσύνην καὶ σωτηρίαν τοῦ κυρίου. Καὶ ἐπεὶ μὴ ε γνων, φησί, γραμματείας τι τοῦ νόμου, τούτου χάριν οὐκ ε ξω μένων ἐπὶ τῆς λέξεως καὶ τῆς σκιᾶς εἰσελεύσομαι, κατὰ τὸ ζωοποιοῦν πνεῦμα καὶ τὸν θεῖον τῶν γεγραμμένων νοῦν δυναστεύων βασιλικῶς, θεοῦ δεδωκότος. διό φημι Μνησθήσομαι τῆς δικαιοσύνης σου μόνου, οὐκ ε τι φροντίζων τὴν κατὰ σκιὰν τοῦ νόμου δικαιοσύνην, περὶ η ς γενόμενος κατὰ τὴν ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοσύνην α μεμπτος Παῦλος γράφει πάντα τὰ σκιώδη α η ν αὐτοῦ πρότερον κέρδη ἐζημιῶσθαι καὶ σκύβαλον ἡγεῖσθαι διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως. 744a Ps 70,19a Ταῦτα ε ως ὑψίστων μεγαλεῖα καὶ σὺν αὐτοῖς τὰ θαυμάσια ὑπῆρκται, τοῦ σωτῆρος ἀνθρώπου γεγενημένου. τεχθέντος γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῆς παρθένου, πλῆθος οὐρανίου στρατιᾶς ∆όξα ἐν ὑψίστοις θεῷ, ε λεγε, καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη, ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία. τῆς γὰρ γενομένης εὐδοκίας ἐν ἀνθρώποις εἰρήνη πολλὴ ἐκράτησεν, τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς πάντων πολεμίων καταλυθέντων· ἀλλὰ καὶ δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις γέγονεν, τῶν σῳζομένων ἀνθρώπων μέχρι τῶν ὑψίστων τὴν ἀνάβασιν ἐχόντων. πῶς γὰρ οὐκ ε μελλον οἱ γενόμενοι τέλειοι, ὡς ὁ πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν, ἐν ἀνυπερβλήτῳ ἁγιότητι γενόμενοι, ε χειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς τὸν θεὸν πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν γενόμενον; καὶ αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ κύριος ἐν Εὐαγγελίοις ε φη πρὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ πατέρα Θέλω, πάτερ, ι να ο που εἰμὶ ἐγὼ καὶ ου τοι ω σιν μετ' ἐμοῦ, ι να θεωρῶσι τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἐμήν. 745 Ps 70,20 ̓Επεὶ ἀγαθότητι ὁ θεὸς πειραθῆναι θλιβερῶν καὶ κακωτικῶν πρὸς σύμφορόν τι συνεχώρησεν, πάλιν ἐπιστρέψας πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ζωοποιεῖ, μεταδιδοὺς ζωῆς τοῖς ἑωρακόσι διὰ πείρας θλίψεις καὶ κακά, ὡς καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν τῶν ἀβύσσων τουτέστι τοῦ βάθους τῶν περιστατικῶν ἀνιμήσασθαι τὸν κατενεχθέντα. καὶ ἐπειδὴ τὰ κακὰ κατάλληλα ταῖς θλίψεσι τὰ ἐπίπονα καὶ κακωτικὰ ἐξειλήφαμεν, ἀκολούθως ἡ 141 ζωοποίησις κατὰ τὴν κοινὴν ζωὴν ἐκληφθήσεται καὶ ἡ ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου α νοδος· ἐπεὶ γὰρ τὰ κακωτικὰ ἐκταθέντα θανατοῦν δοκεῖ καὶ καταβιβάζειν εἰς ᾳ δην, ο ταν τέλος λάβῃ τὰ αι τια, ζωοποιεῖταί τις ὑπὸ θεοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἀβύσσων τῆς γῆς ἀναβιβάζεται.
english: When his providence and creative order are understood as manifesting much propriety, it happens only by command. For such is also the providential [order] to the one capable of saying, 'I understood your works and was astounded' (Ps 70:9a); and it is consistent with the present [context], 'He cast a new song into my mouth, a hymn to our God' (Ps 70:9a). 'Upon you is my hope from my youth' (Ps 70:9a). I beseech [you] in this state to remain until old age, not being rejected from you, [but] one who does all vain things and acts lawlessly being rejected.

And let it be considered also toward thought; since old age is precious not because of long duration, but because of much divine wisdom of the inward man and old age of an unblemished life through supreme virtue; since I am at the peak of progressing, I beseech [you] not to reject [me] but to cooperate by your goodness, so that I may reach the time of unblemished life. For if Christ is the one saying, 'If being an enemy, let them shame me, I have lifted up [my head]' (Ps 70:10-11); for this is also what is said regarding these things about Judas.

Of my shameful enemies who hastened to my ruin (Ps 70:14-16), I add even now to triumphantly praise you with the praise that preceded me: 'In you is my memory forever' (Ps 70:14-16). And those saying, 'God has forsaken him,' were casting into his soul. For the greatest slander against the one forsaken is declared by [the phrase] 'God has forsaken him,' but 'I, however, through all things, hope,' he says, showing that he will not leave any place available. Toward 'God has forsaken him' and 'I, however, through all things, hope' [is the contrast]. And regarding the enemies unjustly killing, wanting to surround him as a destruction, remaining unharmed from them, he announces the life (the day called) the righteousness and salvation of the Lord. And since he did not know, he says, some writing of the law, for this reason not knowing, I will not enter upon the word and the shadow, according to the life-giving spirit and...

God has given the power to rule the mind of the written scriptures in a kingly way. Therefore I say, I will remember your righteousness alone, not being one who cares for the righteousness according to the shadow of the law, having become according to the righteousness in the law; Paul, blameless, writes that all those shadowy things, which previously were his gains, are to be counted as refuse because of the excellence of knowledge.

These things, as the great works of the Most High, and with them the wonders, have been lifted up, because a Savior man has come into being. For having been born of the virgin, a multitude of the heavenly host [cried out], 'Glory to God in the highest,' say, 'and peace on earth, in men goodwill' (Luke 2:14). For because of the goodwill having come into being in men, much peace prevailed, the enemies of all those on earth having been destroyed; but also glory has become in the highest, of the saved men having the ascent unto the highest. For how will not those having become perfect, just as the heavenly Father is perfect, having become in unsurpassable holiness, have God within themselves, all in all becoming? And the Lord himself says in the Gospels to his own Father, 'I will, Father, that where I am, they also may be with me, so that they may see my glory' (John 14:3).

Since God, through goodness, permitted to be tested by afflictions and evil things for the sake of some benefit, turning back again to himself, he gives life, imparting life to those who have seen through trials and evils, just as one is lifted up from the abysses, that is, from the depth of circumstances, the one being driven down. And since we have received the evil things, the painful and evil ones, as appropriate to the afflictions, following this, life-giving will be called according to the common life, and the ascent from the abyss; for since the evil things, having been stretched out, seem to kill and to bring down into Hades, if one receives the end of these things, he is being made alive by God and is brought up from the abysses of the earth.

source_text: Ταῦτα δὲ οὐκ ἀπὸ ἰδίου προσώπου ὁ α γιος λέγει ἀλλὰ τοῦ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένους πειραθέντος πλείστων ο σων κακῶν καὶ θλίψεως πρὸ τῆς τοῦ σωτῆρος ἐπιδημίας· μεθ' η ν πεῖραν ἐπιστρέψας ὁ κύριος πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἐλήλυθεν καὶ ἐζωοποίησεν δοὺς ἀνθ' ἡμῶν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν λύτρον ω στε πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτὸν καὶ δεχόμενον τὴν διδασκαλίαν αὐτοῦ ε χειν ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἀνήγαγεν δὲ ἐκ τῶν ἀβύσσων τῆς γῆς τουτέστι τοῦ ᾳ δου γενόμενος ἐκεῖ μετὰ ἀπόθεσιν ου ει χεν σώματος οὐκ α λλου ε νεκα η τοῦ ἀναγαγεῖν τοὺς ἐκεῖ καταχθέντας δι' ἁμαρτίας ἰδίας. 746 Ps 70,21 Προσκειμένου τῷ ̓Εκ τῶν ἀβύσσων τῆς γῆς ἀνήγαγές με τοῦ πάλιν–εἰ μὲν ἡ α βυσσος σημαίνοι τὸν ἐν τοῖς περιστατικοῖς βυθισμόν (ὡς ἑρμηνεύεται), ἀκόλουθον ἐκλαβεῖν ὡς πολλάκις ε στιν ὑπὸ θεοῦ ἐκεῖθεν ἀναχθῆναι ἀεὶ εὐεργετοῦντος (μαρτύριον τούτου τὸ φερόμενον ου τως· Πολλαὶ αἱ θλίψεις τῶν δικαίων καὶ ἐκ πασῶν αὐτῶν ῥύσεται αὐτοὺς ὁ κύριος)· εἰ δὲ ἀντὶ τοῦ ᾳ δου ἡ α βυσσος παραληφθῇ, ε ργον εἰπεῖν πῶς πάλιν ἐκεῖθέν τις ἀνάγεται· ὡς γὰρ μία ει σοδος εἰς τὸν βίον καὶ ε ξοδος ἀπ' αὐτοῦ μία, ἀνάγκη καὶ τοὺς χωριζομένους τοῦ σώματος ου ε σχον ἐν τῷ ᾳ δῃ α παξ γίνεσθαι. Ητοι ου ν παρέλκει τὸ πάλιν η παραμυθίας τεύξεται, ἀλλὰ μὴν οὐδὲν τοῖς θείοις παρέλκον καὶ περιττόν. ε σται αὐτοῦ α ρα νόησις τοιαύτη· ζωοποιήσας με εὐεργεσίᾳ τῇ σῇ, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην σου πλεονάσας ἐπ' ἐμέ, πάλιν εὐεργετῶν ἀνήγαγές με ἐκ τῶν ἀβύσσων τῆς γῆς τῷ μὴ μόνον ἐζωοποιηκέναι με καὶ πεπλεονακέναι σου τὴν δικαιοσύνην ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐκ τῶν κάτω ἀναγαγεῖν με. 747 Ps 70,22.23 Σκεῦος ψαλμοῦ τὸ ψαλτήριον, δι' ου λέγει ̓Εξομολογήσομαί σοι, εὐχαριστικῶς προφέρων τὴν ἀλήθειαν καὶ καθ' η ν οὐδεὶς ο μοιος θεοῦ μετὰ τὰ κακὰ ζωοποιοῦντος καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν ἑπομένην εὐεργεσίαν τελοῦντος. πρὸς τὸ ἐξομολογήσασθαι τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν σκεύει ψαλμοῦ καὶ ἐν κιθάρᾳ ψάλαι ὑπισχνεῖται τῷ θεῷ ὑπάρχοντι ἁγίῳ τοῦ ̓Ισραήλ. α γιος δὲ τοῦ ̓Ισραὴλ λέγεται ὡς ἁγιάζων αὐτόν· ω σπερ γὰρ ἐὰν λέγωμεν θεοῦ ἁγίους ει ναι παριστῶμεν τοὺς πρὸς αὐτοῦ ἁγιαζομένους, ου τως α γιον αὐτὸν λέγοντες τίνος τὸ ἁγιαζόμενον σημαίνομεν. καὶ ο τι τοῦθ' ου τως ε χει, ἐπίστησον τῷ περὶ Χριστοῦ λεγομένῳ Ος ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν σοφία ἀπὸ θεοῦ, δικαιοσύνη καὶ ἁγιασμὸς καὶ ἀπολύτρωσις· γέγονε γὰρ σοφία τοῖς σοφοῖς, δικαιοσύνη τοῖς δικαιουμένοις, ἁγιασμὸς καὶ ἀπολύτρωσις τοῖς ἁγιαζομένοις καὶ ἀπολυτρουμένοις. οὐκ ἐνταῦθα μόνον α γιος τοῦ ̓Ισραὴλ ὁ θεὸς ει ρηται ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ Παρωξύνατε τὸν α γιον τοῦ ̓Ισραήλ, δῆλον ο τι οἱ ἁμαρτάνοντες. Λυτροῦται ἡ λογικὴ ψυχή, λύτρον δεδωκότος τοῦ ̓Ιησοῦ ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν καὶ αὐτὴν δηλονότι λογικὴν ου σαν. ο νπερ γὰρ τρόπον λυτρούμενος τὰ σώματα τῶν ἀνθρώπων σῶμα ὁμοούσιον αὐτὸς ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν δέδωκεν, ου τως λυτρούμενος λογικὰς ψυχὰς λογικὴν ψυχὴν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ε θηκεν. 748 Ps 71 αργ Ου τος ὁ ψαλμὸς οὐ διενέγκοι τῷ πατρὶ τοῦ ̔Ροβοὰμ Σολομῶνι ἀλλὰ τῷ πνευματικῷ ου τω καλουμένῳ διὰ τὴν τοῦ ὀνόματος μετάληψιν· ἑρμηνεύεται γὰρ ̔Ελλήνων φωνῇ εἰρηνικός. τίς δὲ ου τος ὑπάρχει η ὁ λέγων ̓Ιησοῦς Εἰρήνην τὴν ἐμὴν δίδωμι ὑμῖν; περὶ τούτου ὁ θεολόγος γράφει Αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, καὶ τὸ Εὐηγγελίσατο εἰρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς μακρὰν καὶ εἰρήνην τοῖς ἐγγύς, λύσας τὴν ε χθραν τὴν διαιροῦσαν Ελληνας ἀπὸ τῶν ̔Εβραίων ω στε μίαν ποίμνην καὶ ε να λαὸν ἐξ ἐθνῶν καὶ ̓Ιουδαίων συστῆναι. ου τως εἰρηνικὸς δεικνύμενος διὰ τῶν ε ργων ω ν ἐτέλεσεν ἐκ τοῦ ∆αυίδ ἐστιν ὁ κατὰ σάρκα γεννηθεὶς ἐκ παρθένου. 142 γέγραπται γοῦν περὶ αὐτοῦ Βίβλος γενέσεως ̓Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ υἱοῦ ∆αυίδ. 749a Ps 71,2 Κρίνειν δὲ τὸν λαόν σου ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ (τὸν ἐκ περιτομῆς δηλονότι) καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς σου ἐν κρίσει· ου τοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ ἀπὸ ἐθνῶν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ προσερχόμενοι πτωχοὶ ὠνομασμένοι διὰ τὴν ἐξ ἀπιστίας καὶ κακίας πενίαν. εἰ δὲ δύνανται πτωχοὶ ει ναι θεοῦ οἱ μέτριοι τὴν γνώμην κατὰ τὸ Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, συνεπίσκεψαι. 750 Ps 71,3 Προστάττει τοῖς μεγαλοφυεστέροις δι' ἀρετῆς υ ψος ο ρεσι καὶ βουνοῖς καλουμένοις πρὸς τὸν λαὸν εἰρήνην ἀναλαβεῖν. καὶ εἰ μὲν ο ρη καὶ βουνοὶ ἀρχάγγελοι καὶ α γγελοι τυγχάνουσι, πᾶν τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος λαός ἐστι πρὸς ου ς εἰρηνεῦσαι καλοῦνται, ἐπείπερ ̓Ιησοῦς διὰ τοῦ αι ματος τοῦ σταυροῦ εἰρηνοποίησε τὰ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς πρότερον διαστασιαζόντων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς διὰ κακίαν πρὸς τοὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ὁ σταυρωθεὶς ῃ
english: The holy one does not speak these things from his own person, but concerning the human race having been tested by many evils and tribulation before the arrival of the Savior. After the trial, the Lord, having turned back toward us, came and gave life, having given instead of us his own soul as a ransom; so that everyone believing in him and receiving his teaching possesses eternal life. He brought up [me] from the abysses of the earth, that is, from Hades, having become there after the shedding of the body, and no one else resurrected [me] except him, to bring up those having been cast down there through their own sin.

Regarding 'You have brought me up again from the abysses of the earth' (Ps 70:21): if the abyss signifies a sinking in circumstantial matters (as it is interpreted), it follows to take it as being often raised up from there by God, always doing good (the testimony of this is the saying: 'Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and from all of them the Lord will rescue them'); but if instead of Hades the abyss is understood, it is difficult to say how someone is raised up there again; for just as there is one entrance into life and one exit from it, it is necessary that those being separated from the body also become one in Hades. Therefore, the 'again' does not pass by, but will find consolation; yet it is not passing by the divine and is not superfluous. His thought will be such: 'Having given me life by your goodness, and also having increased your righteousness upon me, you have brought me up again from the abysses of the earth, not only by having given me life and having increased your righteousness upon me, but also by bringing me up from the lower parts.'

The Psalter is a vessel of the psalm, through which he says 'I will confess to you,' bringing forth the truth thankfully, according to which no one is like God after having made bad things life-giving and having completed every following goodness. Regarding the confessing of the truth in a vessel of a psalm and in a harp, he promises to the God existing, the Holy of Israel. And 'Holy of Israel' is said as one sanctifying him; for just as if we say 'they are holy of God' we present those being sanctified by him, so we do not say 'Holy of him' without signifying what is being sanctified. And if it is not so, attend to what is said concerning Christ, who...

Wisdom was revealed to us from God, along with righteousness, sanctification, and redemption; for wisdom became for the wise, righteousness for those being justified, and sanctification and redemption for those being sanctified and redeemed. It is not only said that the Holy One of Israel is God, but also in the Parousia, the Holy One of Israel [is revealed], making manifest what the sinners [do]. The rational soul is redeemed, because Jesus gave his own soul as a ransom for it, and it is clearly a rational soul. For just as he redeemed the bodies of men by giving a body of the same essence for them, so he redeemed rational souls by placing a rational soul for them.

Regarding Psalm 71, the psalm does not pertain to the father of Rehoboam, Solomon, but to the one called spiritual, through the participation in the name; for it is interpreted with a Greek voice of peace. For who is he who says, 'Jesus, I give you my peace'? Concerning this, the theologian writes: 'For He is our peace' (Eph 2:14), and 'He preached peace to you who are far off, and peace to those who are near' (Eph 2:17), having dissolved the enmity that divided Greeks from Hebrews, as one flock and establishing one people from the nations and Jews. Thus, being shown to be peaceful through his works, he who was born according to the flesh from a virgin is from David. Indeed, it is written concerning him, 'The Book of the generation of Jesus Christ, Son of David' (Matt 1:1).

Regarding Psalm 71:2, 'To judge your people in righteousness (clearly those of the circumcision) and your poor in judgment' (Ps 72:2); for those coming to the gospel from the nations are not called poor because of a poverty of unbelief and wickedness. But if the poor of God can be the moderate in mind, according to 'Blessed are the poor in spirit' (Matt 5:3), [then He] visits them. Regarding Psalm 71:3, [He] protects the great-minded through virtue, the high-born and those called princes, to take up peace toward the people. And even if the high-born and princes turn out to be archangels and angels, the whole human race is a people toward whom they are called to bring peace, since Jesus, through the blood of the cross, made peace between those in the heavens and those on the earth, who previously were at odds on the earth because of wickedness toward those in the heavens. Since, therefore, the one crucified...

source_text: ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τέθυται, ι ν' αι ρῃ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου λυθείσης τῆς ἁμαρτίας τῶν ἐπὶ γῆς, εἰρηνοποιεῖται τὰ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, γινομένης χαρᾶς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ε μπροσθεν ἀγγέλων ἐπὶ τοῖς μετανοοῦσιν ἀπὸ ἁμαρτίας. εἰ δὲ Μωυσῆς καὶ οἱ προφῆται σημαίνονται διὰ τῶν ὀρῶν καὶ βουνῶν, πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τὸν ἀπὸ ἐθνῶν ἀπιστεύσαντα εἰρήνην ἀναλαβέτωσαν εἰδότες ο τι αὐτοὶ περὶ τῆς κλήσεως ταύτης προανεφώνησαν. Ει τ' ἐπεὶ καὶ τῶν ἀρετὴν ἐχόντων οἱ μὲν μᾶλλον, οἱ δ' η ττον αὐτὴν ε χουσιν, τοὺς μᾶλλον ε χοντας ὡς ἐπὶ πλεῖον διαρθέντας πράξει καὶ γνώσει τῆς ἀληθείας ο ρη λεκτέον τῶν ὑποδεεστέρων χρηματιζόντων βουνῶν. 751 Ps 71,4 Εργον δὲ τοῦ λαβόντος τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ κρίμα καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὸ κρίνειν τοὺς πτωχοὺς τοῦ λαοῦ. english: The Lamb of God is sacrificed, and by this the sin of the world is released, the sin of those upon the earth; peace is being made between those in the heavens and those upon the earth, joy being made in the heavens before the angels for those repenting from sin. And if Moses and the prophets are signified by mountains and hills, let them take up peace toward the people from the nations who disbelieved, knowing what they themselves had previously spoken concerning this calling. And since even among those possessing virtue, some more so and others having it less, it must be said of those possessing it more as being increased in greater measure by practice and knowledge of the truth, that they are the higher mountains compared to the lower hills. [Ps 71:4] For it is the work of him who received from God judgment and righteousness, to judge the poor of the people.

Not such are those clinging to the letter and the shadow of the law, always named poor, seeing sharply the wealth of not having possessed the spiritual law, having that which the ones from the Jews who believed have, and the apostles also are such. Toward this also he brings salvation to the sons of the penitent. Not such are those who have come from idolatry to the faith of Jesus, those who were born of them according to the superstition of the penitent. Therefore, he will not leave them remaining in many-sided error, but will save their sons having recognized [the truth]. These having been rescued and saved, in order to judge and having come to save, he humbles the one who tyrannizes all in slander, so that he might be crushed as under the feet of the saints. For toward the righteous it is said, 'And you shall tread upon the lion and the dragon,' [Ps 71:5] and toward a man (and toward every slanderer), if he were to say, 'He will turn away slander.'

The same is said to the one remaining with the anointed, what was said to him: 'You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek,' [Ps 110:4] and 'Before the moon, generations of generations, the same one established me before the age.' [Ps 89:2] It is said 'He remains with the anointed' concerning the flesh which he clothed himself with, the soul being breathed into it, being both rational and spiritual; for he remains with the anointed of righteousness because of the indivisible union. But even before the moon, which has the analogy to the sun, there exists a generation of generations, for the church is established through him and in him, composed of all the generations.

They have it from generation to generation in succession. It is presented from the cloud of the waters as the moon is the church; but not thus: Who is she, emerging like the dew, beautiful as the moon, chosen? (Ps 71:6) Just as the rain comes upon the earth bringing fertility, so the visitation of the Savior to men has become the generation of righteousness.

It must be said that the cloud signifies Israel, and the earth signifies the Gentiles. Since previously it descended upon the cloud, and then from there upon the earth. For because Israel disobeyed and did not receive the one who had come, there was a transition to the rain upon the earth, so that all the men upon it might be moistened, rather being watered from the drops to bear spiritual fruits. (Ps 71:7) In the days of the Savior's visitation, the light of practical virtue of righteousness rises, and with it the evangelical standing through the faith of Jesus among the living, and the appropriate peace, possessing a great multitude, so as to extend until the completion of the world. For this is what the reflection of the moon signifies. (Ps 71:7b)

We say that the moon signifies the church. For the moon receives light as a derivative from the sun and does not possess it from itself; so the church, being upon the earth, knows in part and has not been truly illuminated, destined one day to be according to the sun, the perfect one... [gap] ...destined not to have been truly illuminated by appearance, then this happening according to the sun, so that it may receive the perfect [light] and face to face. For by the Word, knowing in part is abolished, and the surpassing knowledge will be established. Thus the lunar condition of the church will be abolished when the sun of righteousness comes, shining like the sun, completing the church of the righteous in the kingdom of their own Father. [gap] ...in the cloud of the waters is the perfection of the bride; and the church itself, after much progress, will be according to the sun. For who is she, he says, emerging like the dew, possessing the beginning of illumination, with which the beginning will be, as the moon, approaching? For she... [gap] ...with which there will be wonder like the sun. (Ps 71:9-11a) Understandings [are] not thus: of those from the nations, the Ethiopians.

english: Regarding those called through their existence out of impiety, falling down before the king in a manner of recognition, the Jews, who are the king's enemies, will indeed be lacking. And it also seems that the Ethiopians fall down before him; the falling down before the king, who sees the hidden things, demonstrates genuine submission.

It is also possible for the enemies of God to appear to have the sensation of repentance through the fact that they lack; for they are bowing down. Tharsis takes hold of the opportunity to spy out joys, spying out the joy of the friends of virtue and piety, if one might ever be able to hear: 'Come into the joy of your Lord' (Matt 25:21).

Those not having a contemplative gaze toward the joy, the kings who hold [their power] bring their gifts to those who are beginning. And islands are brought forward. But these are souls, possessing themselves firmly and unmovably, even when the sea stirs up a gale and a storm. To these, the Savior says: 'Dedicate yourselves, islands, to me, being renewed by the newness of the Spirit, bearing the new human being created according to God.'

Along with these kings, also the Arabs and Saba will bring gifts, those coming toward the evening of the faulty life, so that the light of the impious might be darkened by them. And it is possible for one to be falsely transformed into an angel of light until he deceives even the elect; for Arabs are interpreted as morning and evening. After these Arabs and many others, repentance is offered by Saba; and the name is taken for the return.

It is possible to take as those worshiping him and offering gifts the teachers of all the nations, the apostles and disciples and the successors of these; for they offer gifts to God from the men who are profited by them. And if even one of the faithful brings gifts of praiseworthy deeds and true mindset, it is as if kings bring their own gifts to the only and one All-King. It is also written that his name is honored, having delivered them from so many evils (Ps 72:14). Having learned, the holy men, that no one of the born [humanity] will deliver men from the prevailing wickedness, all turned away and were made blameless concerning the [unclear]...

Wishing to be saved from the hand of the powerful and becoming a cause of eternal salvation, they were continually and unceasingly sending prayer to the Father, at times saying, 'Show us, Lord, your mercy and grant us your salvation,' and at other times, 'Send out your light and your truth.' Concerning his sending and at the beginning of the present Psalm 71, they prayed saying, 'O God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the son of the king' (Ps 71:15c).

They glorify him through all the days of this present age or of the enlightened life of those blessing (Ps 71:16a). The outcomes of the anticipatory proclamations are more extreme than these mountains, for the one prophesied has become a support in the land (Ps 71:16a).

For Jesus did not bear fruit through the arrival of faithful men, and they possess a multitude and greatness of deeds and theorems; but a witness to this is [the promise] that 'the righteous shall flourish like a palm tree, and like a cedar in Lebanon he shall multiply' (Ps 71:16bc). For when the fruit of the support has been multiplied and exceeded, the Jews who were unfaithful to the Savior shall spring up from the city of Jerusalem like grass from the earth, because of the parched state and the rapid drying up, so named and most justly.

Since they have become flesh in their wisdom, having been unfaithful to the Savior and seeking glory from one another rather than that which is given by God alone, they shall spring up from the earth as grass; for all flesh is grass and all the glory of man is like the flower of the grass. For they shall not merely bloom, but shall spring up [and wither].

And also those of the grass, whether out of the city or not in the city, shall spring up, those of whom the word is. For those who hastened toward life and wisdom outside the spiritual city, Jerusalem, were dried up like the parched and rapidly drying grass; but of the one remaining within the city, nothing of this sort was experienced; for 'he who dwells in Jerusalem shall never be shaken' (Ps 71:17c–19a).

The nations, which are to be blessed in him, make happy the one who blessed them, saying, 'Blessed is the Lord, the God of the discerning race, who alone has done wondrous things, having freed us from idolatry and the treatment of wandering demons; for truly it is a wonder.'

english: Regarding what concerns the calling of the Gentiles. The 'Only One' should not be troubled, for the Son cannot do anything contrary to the Father, unless he sees the Father doing it; for whatever the Father does, the Son likewise does. For the 'Only One' and such things taken regarding divinity declare a Father and a Son, as it is presented from the prophet; for it is said to the Father: 'And the Sabaean men shall pass over high upon you and shall worship you and shall pray to you, that what is in you is God and is not God except you; for you are God, and not to be feared, God of Israel, Savior' (Ps 72:1,2). Who is the glory whose name is blessed, who having arrived has made glorious and honorable those from the worthless and gloryless who are the repentant men? It is possible to call his glory and he did not receive an unsung death for the sake of the salvation of the world; for Jesus was not yet glorified, and the Jesus whom we see being humbled through the suffering of death is being crowned with glory and honor.

If indeed his glory is that which his name is blessed for unto the age, concerning which Paul writes: 'Not worthy are the sufferings of the present time compared to the glory that is about to be revealed to us, stand fast' (Rom 8:18). For especially this and the proclamation concerning it we find to be eternally hymned, as Peter said; thus says the witness of his sufferings and of the glory about to be revealed: 'And a companion of that glory' (2 Pet 1:11). And Israel seeing God is interpreted. Therefore also, those not seeing him, they perceive what is good (Ps 72:6b-9). For indeed, although it provides something dark and unpleasant to men, they perceive how it also works advantageously toward salvation, and their steps are not shaken having crossed over and having advanced. Since those about whom the word is, are held not by practical wickedness alone but also by impiety, followingly they are clothed in injustice.

And [there is] the moral wickedness according to the soul, and with this impiety, they think impiously concerning all dogmas. And also to say that their injustice will come forth as from a cloud; then, when it comes forth, the sin is practically fulfilled, no longer remaining only in the thoughts. It has passed into a disposition of the heart.

Having previously disposed themselves according to wickedness, they not only established the evil to themselves but also desired to be harmful to others. Then, after passing into a disposition of wickedness, having thought in malice, they spoke deceitfully as if of good things. They were lifted up, he says, as if to speak even against God, slandering His justice, His creation, and His providence; such as are those who, at the time of the stars, having set their preconceptions, and those who, making the heavens and the creation [themselves] instead of the Creator, lift up their mouth to heaven. They were torn apart, rather they were consumed, as if their tongue had passed through the earth against the Most High, so that all who hear might know what vain and impious things are being philosophized against God and His providence (Ps 72:10).

Of the impious boasting loudly (Ps 72:10), the people of God calls as a starting point for a good return, desiring to enjoy the contemplations of the light of day. And the 'Here' [referring to] the one saying this is God, such as what was said to Moses: 'And you shall stand with me' (Ex 33:33).

Those wanting to cast out providence and injustice, having spoken toward the height (Ps 72:11-13), bring forth such words; how can one know God through human things? For does [the intellect] not have a sensory, organic power? For his understanding does not receive the forms of the seen and the heard, so that, having known, he might also know providential and royal things as he wishes? And having said before, 'How will God be known?', they confess to knowing God, but they are ignorant of the manner of knowing. He turns toward other things. Ps 72:22b, 23a: 'I have become like a beast in your sight.' For just as all creatures are ignorant toward the Father of wisdom and the God of knowledge, according to what was said by Moses, he who does not know the God of the Word—'I am the Word'; for how would one not compare the Word and the most wise Word? In this way it is said again by Moses: 'I am not able to speak from before I began to speak to your servant; heavy of mouth and slow of tongue am I.' For it is not simply being heavy of mouth and slow of tongue and not being able for oneself, but rather after [having begun] to speak to your servant. In this way also Abraham [spoke] to the Creator: 'Since I began to speak to the Lord, I myself am earth and ashes,' he who was ignorant before speaking to God. And he stands forth through the [fact that he] was born, as if he were not being troubled by sin among men, but rather he perceives things not by chance, but as bringing them about by his own wise providence. And it is not by chance to say, 'I am always with you,' but only to the one possessing virtue and piety in an orderly and consistent manner, which is made straight through the intervals.

Ps 72:27, 28: 'Since God is not in a place, locally no one is separated from him, but he is far from the thought of the unrighteous and evil, and near to the righteous and good and the cause of all things; and since the approaching of virtue takes hold of him and saves, the standing away from him having badness and impiety brings destruction.' The same applies to the distancing of God through sin. It is fitting that it is said: 'Behold, those who distance themselves shall perish,' not that those who distance [themselves] should cause those who have sinned to perish by imposing an end to sin through repentance. In this way also, he who does [the sin] but not he who made the sin is a slave to it. Having moved many to long [distances] and many words concerning the essence of the good, the wise man presented his presence to him through brevity, saying that the good is strictly to be joined to God and to place hope upon him. And it is said that the gates of Zion are virtues and introductions into perfection, and all the daughter of Zion becomes she who is born according to her and a soul profiting toward her. english: They stand around, preventing her from approaching and making her stay, and her things are present. God rejects the sinner, after he has first distanced himself. For he says, 'He who comes to me I will by no means cast out' (John 6:37). Do not think the wrath and anger of God is against us; it is far from senselessness. For regarding God, no human passion is indicated, but rather the exceeding turning away through the words spoken, for he says he endures the sheep of his pasture. The pasture of God is the words of the Spirit, the law and the prophets, in which as a shepherd pastures the righteous sheep.

The whole life of man is taken as a sea raised for contemplation. God strengthened this by his power to lead it from more abundant snow and more intense storm into happiness and serenity, as it is said, 'He who turns the sea into dry land' (Ps 74:13). The Savior crushed not the many heads of many dragons, but also the many heads of one upon the water, the water being understood as the wickedness of the unstable and disordered affairs of life. For in such water the dragons work harmfully, and he who excels them is written about as king over all those in the waters and how he dwells in the sea.

For this great and spacious sea shows the turbulence of affairs and the wickedness, saying, 'In this small animals are tossed with large ones, and ships are driven about by playing with the dragon within it' (Ps 74:14). Many heads of dragons are crushed; these are the rulers of this age who promise wisdom, and with them principalities and powers, cosmic rulers of this world, and also spiritual evils and the whole host of demons and opposing powers. And the heads of these dragons are divinations, sorceries, superstitions, and all that contributes to idolatry, but also false doctrines and deceptive practices. The work of the Savior alone is to crush the heads of the said dragons. It did not seem to be possible from any other than him to be strong. Since, however, he did not crush the heads of the dragon alone, al-

And he provided all of it, this food, for the Ethiopian peoples. For he did not need others to be carried away by the flesh and parts of it, nor the Ethiopian peoples, being sons of darkness and night through ignorance. Just as the flesh of Jesus is true food, since all the sons of light are nourished from its use and eating, being enlightened beyond a white snow, so the Ethiopian children of the inner man will be fed with the fleshly [parts] (that is, the things of wickedness and false glory), which will be handed over to the desires of their hearts into uncleanness, and additionally into passions of dishonor and an unproven mind.

He began from the flesh of the numbering to show that the year begins from the flesh, starting from the spring equinox, the beginning of the months and the first in the months of the year, which Moses announced (Ps 73:17b). An enemy mocking the Lord, the devil, but the people is a flock of the other invisible and evil powers (Ps 73:18). The high priest Caiaphas, the enemy, mocked the Savior Christ, and the people, having cried out the Jews, provoked his name: 'Aaron, Aaron, crucify him' (Ps 73:18–21). It is not true the preceding [text] regarding the taking of sensible beasts. For many perfect men, witnesses of the truth, were eaten by beasts. Let it be said, therefore, that a soul confessing [its faith] will not be handed over to those beasts, concerning whom it is written, 'A wandering sheep of Israel; lions drove him out.' The Lord crushed the teeth of these lions. Satan is among these, as the apostle Peter writes, 'Your adversary the devil walks like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour' (1 Peter 5:8). But the poor of God are those who are able, having left his [possessions] having been deprived of wealth, according to those saying, 'Behold, we have left all and have followed you,' whereas others become differently poor, having cast away the wealth of wickedness in false glory. But if those named now the poor of God possess [nothing] even to the poor in spirit, consider this. After these things, he entreats God to look upon the covenant which he established with the fathers around Abraham, so that he may not leave the ones from his seed incomplete.

english: It must be said that the clouds of iniquity have filled those who are darkened in the earth; for they do not walk upon the earth [as citizens of heaven], but because of this they have an earthly veil of life, their intellect being darkened by ignorance. (Ps 74:1)

If to corrupt and to be corrupted is often, according to the Divine Scripture, to sin, then incorruption and to possess it signifies virtue; for it is said, 'The grace is with those who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption.' And since it is necessary for Him who began the good work to bring it to completion, that is to say, to lead it to an end, 'Lest you be corrupted' is said, fleeing corruption until the end, so that no one remains in it but remains in incorruption. And this achievement is great, so a Psalm of song is sent up regarding its fulfillment. Having reached the end so as not to be corrupted, with incorruption having been achieved, we shall thankfully confess to you, God, as the cause of the good things that have existed and are being achieved; for with you and from you these are made firm. And we desire to receive even more upon the good things having been achieved; for we are not yet perfect. We shall indeed confess concerning the things that have existed, but we shall call upon your favor in order to receive more. And if those who confess and call upon [you] are perfect, they confess on behalf of those who have received in fullness, calling upon [you] for their protection, so that what was given by the heavenly Father might remain with those asking for it. (Ps 74:4b)
And Didymus similarly explained this. (Ps 74:4,5a)

To dwell in the earth as a resident instead of a speck is taken as being a sojourner upon praise; for it is said, 'Woe to all those who dwell in the earth,' (Ps 74:4) and 'From the face of the north shall the evils be burned upon those who dwell in the earth.' (Isa 15:2) Truly, being one who dwells in the earth, it happens to become fat from thinking of earthly things and doing the works prescribed of the flesh, and to be subject to its intellect happens to become filth toward God because of dwelling in the earth. This thickness coming from evil, through which the heart of the burning people was thickened, the piercing teaching of the Savior stretched out, concerning which it is said, 'What Fire came to be cast upon the earth.' (Luke 12:49) And since it is necessary not only to be consumed from the thing falling away, but the evil...

Because of the predetermination of those being held, the spirit commands the deeds of the body to die and the spirit to walk, so that we do not fulfill the desire of the flesh. Regarding the pillars of this ordered earth, those having a well-tuned and true mindset, the heralds of truth say, the Savior, establishing them in the house of God, does not make them unsteady (Ps 74:4,5a).

Having strengthened the pillars of the church, he grants to the rest not to deviate. He says this regarding the established order and the completed work of Christ, through whom the earth and all who dwell in it were ordered. Furthermore, to the inhabitants of the whole inhabited world, it was testified through the apostles not to deviate nor to speak injustice against God, paying heed to the many errors. But to dwell on the earth is from above as if being received in praise, whereas to reside as a sojourner is as if being received in mockery. For he says, 'Woe to all those dwelling on the earth' (Luke 12:53), and 'From the face of the north shall the evils be burned upon those dwelling on the earth' (Isa 7:4).

For the one thinking of the things on the earth and doing the works of the flesh, his mindset is made fat toward God because of dwelling on the earth, according to [the saying]: 'He was made fat, enlarged, and left [empty].' Such were those whose covering they closed up in the earth, concerning whom it has been said, 'Their iniquity shall come out like the scent of a covering.' The piercing teaching of the Savior, having said, 'Fire has come to be cast upon the earth' (Luke 12:49), has stretched out such a fatness of wickedness.

But since even by predetermination wickedness must be consumed, and not by the one commanding alone, we are commanded to let the deeds of the body die and to walk by the spirit, so that we may not fulfill the desire of the flesh. The Savior strengthens the pillars of this ordered earth, those having a well-tuned life and a true mindset; rather, regarding the heralds of truth, it has been said, 'Pillars of heaven were stretched out,' having been winged with heavenly wings, as it is said concerning them, 'He who is heavenly, such also are the heavenly ones.' It has also been written concerning all of the glorious church, to which Christ presented himself as a 'pillar and foundation of the truth' (1 Tim 3:15). The Savior, establishing all these pillars in the house of God, does not make them unsteady, saying, 'I will lay the foundation of my holy house' (Ps 74:7b).

english: They say [it is a sign] of virtue and piety. But a sign of their wickedness is that they turn away from sacrifices as if they were harmful, unless they receive residue, smoke, and ash; but the pious, knowing God, are free from the thinking of fate and sorcery.

Similarly Didymus says. The faithful, being pious, are such that the works of providence come not from the east or the west, nor from wicked caretakers, but from God. He himself establishes kings and removes them; he raises the poor from the earth and from poverty lifts up the needy (Ps 74:7-8). Regarding the verse about receiving from the Gentiles and from the circumcised people, one must also stand regarding the humbling of the circumcised and the lifting up of the Gentiles (Ps 74:9).

An opposition seems to be signified from the being full of the cup of mixture, with the mind being uncontrolled in it. But the uncontrolled does not oppose the mixture; for the uncontrolled [voice] is homonymous, sometimes signifying that the mind does not differ from the uncontrolled, and at other times presenting the one who is pure as being toward a liquid. It also presents a third meaning: that when a mixture has become, from mind and water, with the mind prevailing, we call the mixture 'the mixture'.

The third thing, therefore, signifies what is about to be said: God mixing into the mixture for those being judged a good intention, so that the one being punished might not be punished unworthily, having done [this] without anyone standing over him, observing the sins that occurred; God brought the judgment according to which the lawless one is punished. This cup in the hand of God is tilted from one to another, many a time for the one being punished, so that through the evils he did, he might be justified by repentance, and the one who was glorifying himself for a little while might fall into being good. However, even if it tilts from this to that, the reaper does not pour out upon men, but upon the sinners of the earth, and upon the devil and the robbers.

[Ps 74:10-11] When the righteous ones speaking against God are reproved and those following them are finished, I give thanks that I am not found responsible for any of those accused; I rejoice and sing for ever to the God of the patriarch Jacob, who has given me strength, as if to break all the horns of the sinners, which they used against the weaker ones, being like horned bulls. Who are these? It was shown in the assembly of the bulls among the cows of the peoples.

Having said this, he did not bring forth 'And my horns shall be exalted,' but 'of the righteous.' This is customary for the saints through approaching blindness; and they teach that it is for every man to exist in Christ, so that the righteous, having broken the horns of the sinners, may have his horn exalted. And also to say it in a plural way: the horns of the sinners are being broken, but in a singular way: the horn of the righteous is exalted. For every sinner is a multitude, because they are found not to coexist with one another, but evils following virtues like seeds, because of being a middle state. Therefore, let many men have righteousness (which is virtue in general), and they are called righteous in the singular.

[Ps 75:2] It is not the same to be the knowing and the known, so that the known, being known, might be able to be known even of the unknown. For in this way, according to what was said in Judea, that God is known, and following that, in the one inhabiting Judea, Israel, great is His name, I say, of the known.

[Ps 75:3-4] In every way the disturbance of passions and the war of evils must be driven away, so that having the peace which surpasses all understanding, we may become a place of God. english: His dwelling-place. For he says, 'Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion.' And since these things are established not by our power but by the grace of God, the word attributes to Him the cause of peace, saying: 'There He crushed the powers of bows, the shield and the sword and war' (Ps 75:5-7). For peace prevails in the place of God once the rulers of bows are crushed, from whom the evil one, sending his flaming arrows, was making afflictions and disordered movements, of which he was the cause. Along with the aforementioned bows, the related shield and sword are also crushed, and along with them, those called war are crushed; for the Lord is the one crushing wars (Ps 75:5-7).

And the holy men, looking ahead eternally, namely the unseen and eternal things, from which God illuminates differently the light of the knowledge of Christ—first before the manifestation through prophets and Moses, and after this through apostles and evangelists, so that those being illuminated become light, as Paul says: 'The God who said, Let light shine out of darkness, has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God' (2 Cor 4:6). And He marvelously added to the illuminating, that which He promises as knowledge to others, and by this God illuminates more paradoxically into knowledge and wisdom for the holy ones through both revelations and visions, seeing marvelously from the things mentioned. And even if it is not in Judea, as the Scripture says, these high contemplations and the doctrines of godliness are seen, and from these God marvelously illuminates those coming into the knowledge of truth. Often in the Scripture, intelligible things and angels are seen, from which God again illuminates, sending them into service for those about to inherit salvation. And to each of the editions it will be fitting [to say]: 'Draw near to the eternal things, protected by God for those who desire godliness, benefiting the prudent through the virtue of the present.' For understanding is a good thing for all who practice it. The senseless are troubled by both afflictions and wickedness; they are also troubled by both sensible and invisible deceivers, according to the [scripture]: 'Their senseless heart was darkened.' For to be darkened and to be troubled are the same; for each denotes ignorance, with the mind being darkened in both cases. And God is called the Jacob of the ascetic and man...

A good and righteous [state] is maintained against the reproach of one falling from these through personal laziness, being established by reproof. For some say that bodies are like vehicles and horses of the souls. In these horses, those riding themingly desire the beginning of sleep, being drawn into a false breath of those who inhale the body and enslave it with skill, those sitting upon the horses.

Indeed, one sees in the Scripture the rider as being mostly falsely named, as also in Zechariah the prophet there is a threat of God: 'And I will strike every horse in ecstasy and the rider in thoughtlessness' (Zechariah 11:7); and according to Moses, a horse and a rider was thrown into the sea—and riders being praised. For instance, toward Elijah, Father Elisha, the army of Israel and his rider; and toward the Savior it is announced: 'Ride upon your horses, and your riding is salvation' (Psalm 75:8).

No one among the wretched is able to stand against God when He is angry, creating fear for those being judged, so that they might not overlook the One who knows the heart (Psalm 75:7). For those having the word toward Him as toward a judge say: 'Lord, Lord, if He observes iniquity, who will stand?' Moreover, even if no one will be able to stand against His wrath, being terrible, yet He Himself, through the coming goodness with mercy, judges. For mercy and judgment are yours, Lord.

Judgment listens from heaven, making everything happen according to the word of providence for the benefit of each. This agrees with what is in the prophecy of Amos: 'The Lord doing judgment, He has set high judgment and righteousness in the earth' (Amos 5:24). For as it is in heaven, He does all judgment in the high place; and as He listens from heaven, sending judgment from it to those on earth, He has set righteousness in the earth as the end of judgments (Psalm 75:11).

The hidden thing of man is in the mind. He who cleanses this will confess to God with gladness. Then he will celebrate in doing what is profitable, and he will be able to think the truths. english: He is able to be made manifest from [the prayer], 'Cleanse me from my secret sins.' If one does not even imply something regarding the non-existence [of sin], a confession might not occur; consequently, the remnant of the man's inner mind is celebrated having been found outside of all evil. Or, when the doubt concerning him is taken away by the manifestation of purity, the saint celebrates—not sometimes and sometimes not, but steadily and always knowing the truth and acting according to righteousness. For this is truly the feast according to the apostle who said, 'Let us celebrate, not in leaven of malice and wickedness, but in unleavened bread of sincerity and truth' (1 Cor 5:8).

He is terrible before the kings of the earth, who struck down Pharaoh, and pursued Nebuchadnezzar of men, altering his thinking as if his life were among beasts (Ps 76:13); he deprived Saul of the spirit, who, despising the covenant of God, [was rejected by] Samuel; for it is said, 'The Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul' (1 Sam 16:14), and he was oppressed by an evil spirit from the Lord, sent upon him by judgment and vote. And if even concerning ecclesiastical leaders these things are to be considered, hold fast to the God-breathed Scripture. For Paul, having called the elders of Miletus, says to them, 'Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock in which the Holy Spirit of God has made you overseers, and with Him, and also from among yourselves some will arise speaking twisted things, that is, the divine Spirit of the terrible ones being taken away' (Acts 20:28-30).

When the one speaking has departed far off, with a strained voice (Ps 76:2). Since, therefore, the begotten essence is separated from the One who made [all], a cry according to the intellect is necessary. He is called God because He made all things, and Lord because He rules over those things which come from Him. And it is said, God indeed the Father, and Lord the Son. But to the one speaking, the day is one of affliction, his whole life, indeed, the age which has come upon him, in which he seeks God as one would seek a physician for a disease, calling out. According to Isaiah, my soul became attached to a mortal, not being self-sufficient for all the consolation of the memory concerning God. To this, what is in Isaiah also applies: 'In trouble of the Lord I remembered' (Isa 26:3). According to the common habit of many, a wandering voice indicates something superficial, but according to the Scripture and being placed upon one who is praised, it is [authentic].

For Anna, praying genuinely toward God, being called by the priest's child to persist in prayer, answers: 'From a multitude of wanderings I have wasted away until now.' And concerning Isaac, that which says: 'He went out to wander in the field.' But you will receive something superficial if you receive the one who explained to me unlawful wanderings.

If indeed the word were ever said by the divine scholars, having understood the sequence and the speaking person, we would receive the voice either for the better or for the evil. Now, therefore, both the person and the word are praised; the spirit did not faint, which indicates the soul. For even Stephen did not say, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' (Luke 22:43), but, having been faint-souled because of the enemies lying in wait, he gave himself to God.

My eyes preceded the guards (Ps 76:5). Another scripture is brought forward, not saying: 'I have preceded the guards,' but: 'All my enemies preceded the guards.' Concerning many guards happening against me, he was guarding the saying: 'With all vigilance, keep your heart.' They preceded them, those which were about to make me faint-souled, all my enemies; for they were not few, but rather all, and they were filled against me.

Therefore, also, they having become more dominant, I have seen in a certain foreknowledge that I would undergo trouble, but I did not utter anything troubling, nor in any disposition have I become disturbed; for the things of judgment and foreknowledge were not at all heavy upon me, nor had I been made in a passionate fear. For indeed I uttered nothing, whereas those who have shrunk in courage love to speak.

english: Regarding Ephraim, all enemies will lay hold of these strongholds, anticipating them; for they will not sleep unless they have afflicted [him] (Ps 76:6).

Having these things happen to me, he says, I awoke myself to remember the former and many anticipating circumstances (not only me but also my virtuous fathers) from which all the Lord rescued me and them; by which reason I have become more cheerful to endure unto the end, so that I might happen to have salvation from the struggles of such things; for he who endures unto the end, he shall be saved. For having conversed with the ancient days and the eternal ages, having remembered and having meditated, I found many times both myself and the rest of men falling into such a state of helplessness, as to leave behind salvation and all hope; but, having been established in confidence toward God, every helplessness in those who grasp [the truth] is overcome. You shall remember when the Hebrew multitude comes toward the things laid before you by the valleys of the sea; for no good hope remaining there, suddenly God provided abundance in narrowness and in remote helplessness (Ps 76:7).

Throughout all this life, because of the encroaching ignorance of things, being called night, I did not deliver myself to sleep and heart like other men, but toward sobriety and alertness I stirred myself up; for those sleeping at night sleep and at night they get drunk. With my heart, that is, with my mind, I was conversing with myself about the actions and natures of things (for know what the present things are approaching), I learned what the end of the surrounding evils will be. And I was tilling my spirit with the art of farming, desiring to sow into it, so that from it I might reap eternal life; for he who sows into the spirit, from the spirit he will reap eternal life (2 Cor 9:6). And it is not to be thought that to say 'spirit' is to speak synonymously, but rather homonymously regarding the present word and that which was previously set forth; for there the soul was called spirit, but here the spirit of the man is that which is in him. For if even here the spirit is said instead of the soul, who is the one tilling his spirit and idling with his heart? For it is not the body that does these things.

For the soul is not strictly a human being when it is wandering aimlessly apart from the mind and unsettling the spirit joined to the mind. I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray also with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing also with the mind. Corruption is the departure from natural goodness, which occurs not while the essence remains, but if something belonging to the natural state is taken away from it. Previously, he was willing to help and was favorable to those asking of him, as I reasoned: 'I remembered the days of old.' Was his goodness not present until those times, and no longer being added to, he was willing to be favorable? No, by no means. For his mercy is not cut off from the former generation, nor does it fail regarding the coming one. For they think that the end of his mercy is this: that he might do good and show mercy to one generation, and not to another. Nor will he fail to have compassion, just as neither fire nor light fails to shine and to warm. For his mercies are held in check by a temporary anger arising from sin, but they are not joined in a way that lasts forever.

Even though many troubles have come upon me, they cast a disturbance into me (Ps 76:8-10). What has been recounted followed in all the appointed words, but also, having understood things, I observed that God is not being thrust away for the ages, nor has He chosen to do other things, as if in some way to cast down a different beginning of a kind of life. For through all those things I have passed through, I have begun the Now, changing all those things that disturbed and frightened me, so that I might become courageous for the rest. This change is not a change of quality (for I have passed from one disposition to another), but an alteration, not caused by another, but by the right hand of the Most High. For He also provided these thoughts and brought them together so that I might be altered.

This aimless wandering is like the one from above is good; for it is a good thing to speak often of the wonders of God. english: But His word is in nothing trivial, for it is a way; rather, it is rightly said that the indwelling voice is in the saints alone. Regarding Psalm 76:14b, greatness is said of the intelligible substance by excellence of power, not by quantity. No god is found as great as ours.

He does not say that the gods are the idols or the demons (for these are called gods), but rather those who, having become toward us through the word of God, were made divine. For they are not partakers of divinity, but merely partakers. The present word is said of the Savior, as he will declare the following, being a great God and Father, since he is the Son of the great God.

Regarding Psalm 76:15a, after the article, the Savior is called God, so that he might be shown as different from those to whom it is said, 'You are gods' (Ps 82:6). None of them is as one who excels. After the article, it is said, 'God.' Such is also the Only-begotten God who is in the bosom of the Father, to be God by being alone in essence; for none of the others is only-begotten, but with the only-begotten is God. According to the same divinity, the only-begotten God and the Father God are.

Indeed, it is said of the Savior (of his one divinity and that of the Father), 'God is in you, and there is no god besides you; for you are God, and we shall not fear' (Ps 86:5). For how can it be that if God is in him, there is no god besides him, and he himself is God, unless we understand that the Father and the Son have the same divinity, so as to be one God, Father and Son, and not a Son and a Father? For the Father is the Father of the Son, and the Son is the Son of the Father. Therefore, the 'I and the Father are one' follows the 'I and the Father are one' being said, not the Son saying 'I and the God.' For the Father is not another Son, nor is God another, by the being of the same divinity of the offspring and of the begetter.

He performed many paradoxical wonders among the nations and the circumcised; for power went out from him and healed everyone. But also by his arm (I mean by his energy and action) he redeemed his people, the two united, having tasted death above all things by the grace of God, giving his soul as a ransom for many; for by his precious blood we were redeemed from our vain, ancestral conduct. The peoples are those in whom he made his power known, whom he also joined together into one people, whom he redeemed: the sons of Jacob and Joseph, the sons of Jacob who are circumcised and believe, and the sons of Joseph who are from the nations. For Joseph is interpreted as 'Addition of the Lord'; for God truly added to those being saved from the circumcised, those from the nations who believe. And 'He made known' does not signify the beginning of knowing, but that which is come to be known and recognized; for saying 'He who works wonders,' he recognizes these things through these words.

When the Savior appeared on earth, the earth endured confusion and trembling (Ps 76:19-21)—that is, the things on earth, which are above all laws and are fearful of all gods, through whose ordinances the demons are overturned; but also the earth endured confusion and trembling because of men, who are bound by passions and are being turned toward the Word of Christ. And the sea, the present life, Jesus God alone bound, so as to leave behind traces and proofs of the way, so that those wishing to follow him might follow; for he says, 'Your paths are in many waters, and your tracks shall not be known' (Ps 77:20), because the word of his journey is incomprehensible. And the sheep of Christ were led by God in practice (symbolically called by the hand) of the spiritual law and the priestly word.
