english: He is the initiator and high priest of the spiritual rite of God, having traversed the heavens. He signifies Moses as the law, and Aaron as the high priest; therefore they are brothers, being sons of the divine providence which brought forth this law and the appropriate high-priestly word for it; for by its will these good things have been raised up to men (Ps 77:1a).

He is able to call all the old scripture 'the law' present here. If the commanding and forbidding word were to signify the voice of the law according to the preceding verse, it commands the law to take heed how those having received the command, choosing the good and fleeing the bad, might act rightly (Ps 77:3).

These things those having the mind of Christ understood and perceived spiritually; for it was not hidden from them, having been explained to them according to knowledge. And they themselves did not reveal to their own children born of them through instruction the matters from the beginning, so that they might be known and not hidden even to their next generation.

For he who becomes with God in spirit, coming from Him, is trusted to understand and is confirmed according to the spirit (Ps 77:8d). It is to be thought that 'spirit' here refers to the intellect, according to what was said concerning the Virgin, how she [conceived] by the Holy Spirit and body; for in these things 'spirit' calls her opinion and her disposition, and from which having been sanctified, the body also comes to be sanctified, being served by sanctifying energies. And if the soul itself is spirit and is called so here, it is to be noted.

Regarding the manna given before the rebellion, the psalm says after the rebellion that both the manna and the meat were given (Ps 77:17–22). But this is not the question. For the psalm joins together things in different times, bringing together one rebellion having occurred in different times under one cause. For if someone should interpret the first rebellion as that before the making of the Tabernacle in the second month of the Exodus, he does not place that history in its proper time in the psalm; for not then did the water from the rock happen to be given, nor did the punishment of fire follow, and indeed the firstlings were not [slain] and they did not unrighteously disbelieve regarding the paradoxical gift of food...

You act with small-spiritedness because you do not immediately find abundance. Therefore, even Moses did not yield to the small-spiritedness of the people. In the second dispute concerning meats, Moses also bears it with difficulty; and it is fitting that the punishment from God was somewhat sent to them, and they were being consumed by fire. It is necessary to believe from those who were previously warned, not believing in the divine power, and it is necessary to hope for salvation from Him, not hoping.

It must also be said by way of upward leading: in the wilderness of the Son, much ignorance of things prevails. Having passed through and having divided his most meager word, a rock called [it], a great watering has become for those being benefited, as if the flowing water were cast alongside an indescribable abyss in depth and breadth. For the water sent forth from this rock flowed like rivers (Ps 77:17–25a). And regarding these rivers, the Savior says: 'He who believes in me, as the Scripture says, from his spiritual belly (that which is according to the inner man) will flow rivers of living water' (John 7:38). And he says, the writer says, that those who believe will not receive this concerning the Spirit. For the water of these rivers is drawn out from a rock, about which Paul says: 'From a spiritual [rock] that follows' (1 Cor 10:4); and the rock is Christ. Christ himself, since he is a rock, says concerning the water of the rivers: 'For from me he will take and will declare to you all things' (John 14:26).

And they added to this: sinning against him—not all who sin against God are sinning against him, but only those who have known his will and are not doing it. Certainly even David, not being ignorant of God's will, says: 'Against you only have I sinned' (Ps 51:4). Perhaps for those sinning in ethical matters, the sin becomes toward men; but for those blaspheming God and providence, the sin, being a certain impiety, rises up against God. For if someone sins against a man, and prays for him; but if he sins against the Lord God, who will pray for him? Certainly, what they overthrew the Most High with, they were lacking in a dry place, being deprived of the spiritual waters; for they turned away from the water from the aforementioned rock. And finding themselves in a dry place, they did not experience the goodness of God which is sweet. But that which is according to virtue and wisdom makes it sweet.

Καὶ ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν τῷ θεῷ, ου τε 156 η λπισαν ἐπὶ τὸ σωτήριον αὐτοῦ. οἱ γὰρ μὴ ἐλπίσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν ̓Ιησοῦν ο ντα θεοῦ σωτήριον οὐδὲ αὐτῷ τῷ θεῷ ἐπίστευσαν. τοῖς γοῦν ἀποστόλοις ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ ει ρηται Πιστεύετε εἰς ἐμέ, καὶ εἰς τὸν θεὸν πιστεύετε. δυνατὸν δ' ἐπὶ τὸν ̓Ισραὴλ μὴ πιστεύσαντα εἰς τὸν θεὸν μηδ' ἐλπίσαντα ἐπὶ τὸ σωτήριον αὐτοῦ ἀναβεβηκέναι νομίζειν τὴν ὀργὴν η ν ὑπομένουσιν ἁλόντες ὑπὸ ῥώμης, περὶ η ς ὁ Παῦλος ε φη Εφθασε δ' αὐτοὺς ἡ ὀργὴ εἰς τέλος. Καὶ α ρτον οὐρανοῦ ε δωκεν αὐτοῖς. ἡ οὐρανὸς φωνὴ σημαίνει τὴν τῶν νοητῶν οὐσίαν καθὰ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ε μπροσθεν διειλήφαμεν, αἱ δὲ ἀνοιγόμεναι θυρίδες τῶν οὐρανῶν αἱ ἐξαπλώσεις καὶ φανερώσεις τῶν πατρικῶν εἰσιν, ῥέοντος τοῦ θεοῦ τὰς αὐτοῦ δωρεὰς διὰ τούτων τῶν θυρίδων. Αρτον ἀγγέλων ε φαγεν α νθρωπος· ι να ει πῃ τὸν ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ τῆς καρδίας α νθρωπον. διὸ καὶ πάντα τὰ α λλα ὀνόματα παρεὶς καίτοι πολλάκις αὐτῶν μνημονεύσας, τοῦ ̓Ιακὼβ καὶ τοῦ ̓Ισραὴλ καὶ τοῦ ̓Εφραίμ, τῆς ἀνθρώπουπροσηγορίας ἐνταῦθα μνημονεύει πρὸς δεῖξιν τοῦ τὸν ἀληθῶς α νθρωπον τὸν κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ γεγενημένον ὁμοτράπεζον καὶ ὁμέστιον ἀγγέλοις γεγονέναι μεταλαμβάνοντα τοῦ ἀληθινοῦ μάννα. 809 Ps 77,38b Τὸ διαφθεῖραι σημαίνει ποτὲ τὸ κολάσει περιπεσεῖν καθάπερ Ει τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φθείρει, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ θεός, ἀντὶ τοῦ κολάσει. ἀλλ' ἐπεὶ δηλοῖ τὸ διαφθεῖραι καὶ τὸ παραδοθῆναι πάθεσιν ἀτιμίας κατὰ ἀντιμισθίαν πλάνης καὶ α λλων ἁμαρτημάτων γινομένων, οὐ διαφθείρει ὁ θεὸς κατὰ τοῦτο τὸ σημαινόμενον τοὺς ἀξίους τοῦ ι λεω εὑρεῖν αὐτόν, ὡς ἐλέῳ πολλῷ καὶ οἰκτιρμῷ ἱλάσασθαι ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῶν. 810 Ps 77,49c–51 ̓Αγγέλους πονηροὺς οὐ φύσει ο ντας τοιούτους φησὶν ἀλλὰ τοὺς πόνων κάκωσιν ἐπιφέροντας. Οὐκ ἐφείσατο ἀπὸ θανάτου τῶν ψυχῶν αὐτῶν, ἐπαγαγὼν αὐτοῦ τὸν ἐπὶ καταλύσει τῆς μοχθηρᾶς ζωῆς
english: Being put into action and being contemplated. They tested Him not in their hearts superficially, but from the depth of their own ruling principle, thinking against God and doubting His power to request food for their souls—not the souls made in the image and likeness of God (for they feed on the bread of life and the fruit of the tree of life), but the souls being transformed into flesh because they have succumbed to material things, desiring not beneficial and healthy foods, but pleasant and disease-causing ones.

The soul that desires food, the desiring and appetitive one, is a rational power in us. For concerning this, it is said, 'And let your soul desire meat' (Psalm 34:8). The irrational animals also participate in this, desiring and being appetitive for food. And they spoke against God, saying, 'Will God not be able to prepare a table in the wilderness?' and the following things; but He has indeed given bread having come down from heaven and prepared a table before His people. Wisdom says, 'She has laid her victims and mixed her wine in the vessel; and none of the unbelieving shall taste them' (Wisdom 18:6). To this, you will receive the 'For I say to you, none of those men shall taste my supper' (Luke 22:27).

Because of this, the Lord was angry and cast down, as if to pay attention to them. This was followed by the fire of desires being kindled upon Jacob; or rather, the [fire] decided and laboring for the sake of virtue, or the fire kindled from God, which is able to consume by their blessing their material choice and their disposition. Consequently, by this fire, wrath ascended upon Israel. For from when they were practicing lower things, the wrath, having perceived, ascended upon Israel. And perhaps wrath descends upon those lying below the strangers of godliness, according to what is said: 'For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven upon all ungodliness and injustice of men' (Romans 1:18). And wrath ascends upon those called to do what God wills, through having been called from above. Therefore, the care for Israel, who ought to look above, has ascended, as it is said: 'the wrath has ascended.' 'Stop, if those serving [God] happen to be vessels of wrath through the punishments from God,' [they] serve similarly as vessels of wrath.

They are called. And the wrath, which is not said to be below, ascends upon the former Israel. This accords with: 'If the spirit of the ruler ascends upon you, let him not leave your place' (1 Sam 2:9). For in these things the unclean spirit is said to be below, which ascends toward. Therefore it is able to ascend upon Israel.

And since they did not believe in God, they did not hope for His salvation. For those who did not hope in Jesus Christ, the salvation of God, did not even believe in God Himself. To the apostles, it was said by Christ: 'Believe in me, and believe in God' (cf. John 14:1). It is possible, then, for wrath to have ascended upon Israel because they did not believe in God nor hope for His salvation, being overtaken by a force, concerning which Paul said: 'And wrath reached them to the end' (Eph 4:30).

And bread of heaven He gave them (Ps 77:38b). The voice of heaven signifies the essence of the intelligible [realms], just as we have also learned in the [previous] passages; and the opening doors of the heavens are the outpourings and manifestations of the patriarchs, through these doors the gifts of God flow. Bread of angels man has eaten, to signify how a man is in the hiddenness of the heart. Therefore, having passed over all the other names, even though he frequently remembered them—of Jacob and of Israel and of Ephraim—he remembers the human appellation here to show the man who is truly made according to the image and likeness of God, having become a fellow-table-guest and a host to angels, receiving the true manna (Ps 77:38b).

To corrupt signifies sometimes to fall into punishment, just as 'If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will corrupt him' (1 Cor 3:17), instead of punishment. But since to corrupt also signifies being handed over to a condition of dishonor as a recompense for error and other sins being committed, God does not corrupt in this sense; rather, He finds those worthy of being seen by Him, so that they might be propitiated for their sins by much mercy and compassion. He does not say He will produce evil angels such as these, but those who bring harm through their labors. He did not spare their souls from death, bringing them to the dissolution of a weary life (Ps 77:49c–51).

source_text: θάνατον· εἰς τοῦτον τὸν θάνατον συγκλείσας καὶ τὰς ἀλόγους αὐτῶν δυνάμεις κτήνη τροπικῶς ὀνομαζομένας. πρὸς ἀγαθοῦ γὰρ αὐτοῖς ε σται ἀποβαλεῖν καὶ τὰ κτήνη αὐτῶν τὴν φαύλην ζωήν, τουτέστι τὴν ἐμπαθῆ κίνησιν. Καὶ βαθύτερον δὲ νοήσεις· ἐπεὶ γὰρ ὁ ψυχικὸς α νθρωπος κατὰ ψυχὴν ἀλλ' οὐ κατὰ πνεῦμα ζῇ, οὐ φείδεται τῶν ου τω λεγομένων ψυχῶν αὐτῶν, ι ν' ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχικὴν κατάστασιν αὐτῶν εἰς πνευματικὴν ε ξιν αὐτοὺς ἀγάγῃ. ο τι δὲ οὐκ ἀεὶ τὸ ο νομα τῆς ψυχῆς οὐσίαν σημαίνει, σαφῶς παρίσταται ἐκ τοῦ Ψυχὴ πονηρὰ ἀπολεῖ τὸν κτησάμενον αὐτήν. οὐ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα κτησάμενον ψυχὴν λέγει πονηρὰν ἀλλὰ τὴν οὐσίαν ῃ συμβέβηκε τὸ πρᾶγμα καθ' ου κεῖται νῦν ἡ ψυχὴ λέξις. καὶ ἡ συνήθεια δὲ ψυχὴν καλὴν καὶ φαύλην ε χειν τινὰς λέγουσα συμφέρεται τῷ προκειμένῳ σημαινομένῳ. ̔Η δεκάτη δὲ πληγὴ τοῖς Αἰγυπτίοις ἐπαχθεῖσα θάνατος η ν τῶν παρ' αὐτοῖς πρωτοτόκων ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπου ε ως κτήνους. τάχα ου ν ἐπὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τῶν πρῶτον τεχθέντων κυριολεκτοῦσαν τὴν πρωτότοκον φωνὴν ἐπὶ τῶν ἀλόγων ζῴων ἀπαρχὴν πόνων τὴν πρωτότοκον ει πε. ἀπαρχὴ γὰρ πόνων τῶν ζῳοτροφούντων τὰ πρωτότοκα. συμφέρομαι δὲ εἰς τοῦτο ει ναι τὸ δηλούμενον· ἐκ προσθήκης τῆς λεγούσης ἐν τοῖς σκηνώμασιν αὐτῶν τὰ πρωτότοκα τῶν ἀλόγων ἀνῃρέθη, ο πως ζημίᾳ ὑποπέσωσιν οἱ κεκτημένοι, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ἀνθρώπων πρωτότοκα ὑπεβλήθη θανάτῳ ἐπὶ τῷ πειραθῆναι συμφορᾶς τοὺς τούτων γονέας. πρὸς γοῦν τοὺς μὴ παιδευομένους μηδ' αυ μετανοοῦντας ἐπὶ τοιούτοις θεηλάτοις Μάτην ἐπάταξα τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν, ει ρηται, παιδείαν οὐκ ἐδέξασθε. καὶ ου τοι δὲ οἱ πρωτότοκοι η τοι ἐπιτιμίαν ε σχον τὸ θανεῖν τῶν σφῶν ἁμαρτιῶν η οὐδὲν ἐβλάβησαν, εἰ παιδεύσεως α λλων ε νεκα ὑπέπεσον θανάτῳ· ἀδιάφορον γὰρ τὸ τεθνάναι καὶ ἐξ ἀνάγκης συμβαῖνον, πρὸς δ' ἀλήθειαν ἀνεξερεύνητα τὰ κρίματα τοῦ θεοῦ. Πρὸς ἀναγωγήν· ἐπεὶ πνευματικῶς Αι γυπτος καλεῖται πᾶς ὁ περὶ γῆν τόπος, οἱ ἐν τούτῳ διατρίβοντες Αἰγύπτιοι προσαγορεύονται. χάριτι θεοῦ τοίνυν τούτων τῶν Αἰγυπτίων τὰ πρῶτα γεννήματα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτῶν ἀναιρεῖται, α γνοια καὶ κακία τυγχάνοντα. πρὸ γὰρ τῶν 157 ἀρετῶν καὶ ἐπιστημῶν τῶν ὠφελίμων τέκνων τῶν διανοιῶν κακία καὶ α γνοια ὑφίσταται· διὸ καὶ πρωτότοκά τις ταῦτα ὀνομάζων οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει. ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιτηδεύσεις τῶν κατὰ ἀρετὴν ἐπιστήμην ἐνεργειῶν φαῦλα τυγχάνοντα ε στιν ἀναιρετέα. παντὶ γὰρ τῷ κατὰ τέχνην καὶ ἐπιστήμην ἐνεργοῦντι οὐκ εὐθὺς τὸ ευ ποιῆσαι η πρᾶξαι παραγίνεται, ἀλλὰ μετὰ τὸ ἀνεπιλήπτως ἐνεργῆσαι τὸ ἀμέμπτως ἐνεργῆσαι παραγίνεται. Τὸ δ' ἐν τοῖς σκηνώμασιν αὐτῶν προσκείμενον δηλοῖ περὶ ψυχῶν τὰ προκείμενα λέγεσθαι ε τι τοῖς σώμασι συμπεπλεγμένων· σκηνώματα γὰρ ψυχῶν τὰ σώματα. 811 Ps 77,54 ̔Αγιάσματος ο ρος ἡ διῃρημένη καὶ ὑψηλοτάτη ἀρετή ἐστιν, οὐχ ἡ διανοητικὴ μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡ πρακτική. μόνος δὲ εἰς ταύτην γνησίως εἰσάγει ὁ μόνος τέλειος διδάσκαλος ̓Ιησοῦς. τότε ου ν ἁγιάζονται οἱ ἐν τῷ ο ρει γινόμενοι, ο ταν ὑπὸ κυρίου ἀχθῶσιν εἰς αὐτό. τοῦτο δὴ τὸ ο ρος οὐχ ἡ τυχοῦσα ἀλλ' ἡ δεξιὰ τοῦ θεοῦ δύναμις οὐκ α λλη τοῦ μονογενοῦς ̓Ιησοῦ τυγχάνουσα κέκληται αὐτό. κτῆμα γὰρ ἀληθῶς ̓Ιησοῦ πᾶσα ἀρίστη γνώμη καὶ θεωρητικὴ τῆς ἀληθείας ε ξις, ο θεν καὶ οἱ ταύτας τὰς διαθέσεις κτώμενοι κτήματα τοῦ κυρίου καλοῦνται. 812 Ps 77,61 Τάχα δὲ καὶ τεθνηκυίας αὐτὰς ἐν τοσαύτῃ φορᾷ θεηλάτων κακῶν ἐμακάρισαν μᾶλλον η ε κλαυσαν. 813 Ps 77,66 Εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω αὐτοὺς ἐπάταξεν, ο πως μὴ ε μπροσθεν καὶ πρόσω ὠμότητος ἐλάσσωσιν ἀλλ' ἀναχαιτίσωσιν ἀπὸ τῆς ἀπανθρώπου καὶ πονηρᾶς ε ξεως αὐτῶν· οὐδένα γὰρ βούλεται ὁ θεὸς ἐν κακοῖς προκόπτειν, κηδόμενος δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ ο νειδος αἰώνιον παρέσχεν αὐτοῖς. ὀνειδίζονται δὲ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ καὶ οὐ πρὸς α λλων μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑφ' αὑτῶν, ο ταν αι σθωνται ω ν δεδράκασι κακῶν. λέγει γοῦν πρός τινας ὁ θεὸς Αἰσχύνθητε ἀπὸ καυχήσεως ὑμῶν καὶ ἀπὸ ὀνειδισμοῦ ο λην τὴν ἡμέραν. οἱ γὰρ ἐπὶ τοῖς χειρίστοις καυχώμενοι εὐεργετοῦνται, ο ταν αἰσχυνθῶσι καὶ ὀνειδισθῶσιν ἐφ' οι ς ἐσεμνύνοντο. 814 Ps 77,72 Τὸ τῆς ἀκακίας ο νομα οὐκ εὐήθειαν ἐνταῦθα σημαίνει ἀλλὰ στέρησιν κακίας καὶ τὸ α δολον. ο σοι ου ν τῶν ἀρχομένων μιμοῦνται ἀκακίαν τοῦ διδασκάλου, ποιμαίνονται ὑπ' αὐτῆς. ο πως δὲ μὴ ἐπιπλάστως τὸ α κακον ἐπιτηδεύων νομισθῇ ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ βελτίστης ε ξεως, ἐπιτελούμενον καρδίας ἀκακίαν ε χειν αὐτὸν ε φη. ̔Ωδήγησε δὲ καὶ α λλους τῇ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ συνέσει.
english: Death; having enclosed into this death and their irrational powers, which are tropically named cattle. For it will be for their good to cast away both themselves and their cattle, that is, their base life, namely, the passionate movement.

And understand more deeply: since the psychic man lives according to soul but not according to spirit, he does not spare these so-called souls of theirs, in order to, having destroyed their psychic state, lead them into a spiritual one. And since the name of the soul does not always signify its essence, it is clearly shown by 'the evil soul will destroy the one who has acquired it.' For it does not say the one having acquired a body calls the soul evil, but the essence of the matter has happened to which the word soul now lies. And the habit of calling some soul beautiful or base is consistent with what is being signified here.

And the tenth plague brought upon the Egyptians was death, the death of the firstborn among them from man to cattle. Perhaps it does not literally speak of the firstborn among men first born, but literally speaks of the firstborn voice upon the irrational animals as the firstfruits of pains. For the firstfruits of pains are the firstborn of those who are beast-fed. I agree to this being what is signified: that by the addition of what is said in their dwellings, the firstborn of the irrational ones were taken away, so that those having them might fall into loss, but also the firstborn of men were struck by death because their parents were tested by calamity.

Toward those not being disciplined nor repenting of such god-fearing things, 'I struck your children,' it is said (Exodus 12:12), 'because you did not receive discipline.' And so the firstborn either suffered the penalty of dying because of their own sins or they were not harmed at all, if they fell into death by the winning of others' discipline; for it is no difference to die and it happens by necessity, but toward the truth, the judgments of God are unsearchable. For the purpose of leading upward: since every place concerning the earth is called Egypt spiritually, those dwelling in it are called Egyptians. Therefore, by the grace of God, the firstborn offspring of their souls among these Egyptians is taken away, being ignorance and malice. For before the 157 virtues and sciences of the beneficial children of the intellects, malice and ignorance exist; therefore...

One does not err by calling these things 'firstfruits'. But even regarding those things which appear to be trivial in the exercise of knowledge according to virtue, they are to be rejected. For for everyone acting according to art and knowledge, the doing or acting well does not immediately occur, but it occurs after acting unassailably and acting blamelessly.

And that which lies in their tabernacles reveals what is to be said concerning souls when they are entwined with bodies; for bodies are tabernacles of souls (Ps 77:54). Holiness is the divided and most high virtue, not the intellectual alone but also the practical. And only the one perfect Teacher, Jesus, introduces one genuinely into this. Then those who are in heaven are not sanctified, but they are carried into it by the Lord. This very holiness is not a matter of chance, but it is called the right hand of God's power, not being anything other than the only-begotten Jesus. For every excellence and theoretical vision of the truth is truly a possession of Jesus, and therefore those acquiring these dispositions are called possessions of the Lord (Ps 77:61).

Perhaps they even blessed those having died in such a way, rather than weeping over the evils they had seen (Ps 77:66). He struck them from behind, so that they might not be diminished by a face of coarseness in front, but might be severed from their inhuman and evil state; for God does not desire anyone to progress in evils, but, caring for them, provided them with eternal reproach. And sinners are reproached, not only by others but also by themselves, when they are ashamed of the evils they have committed. For God says to certain ones: 'Be ashamed of your boasting and from reproach, mourn the day.' For those boasting over trivial things are benefited, if they are ashamed and reproached for the things they were vaunting of (Ps 77:72).

The name of 'innocence' does not signify gentleness here, but the absence of evil and simplicity. The sheep do not imitate the innocence of the Teacher, but are shepherded by it. And lest the one practicing evil be thought to be doing so deceptively, but rather from the best state, it is said of him that he is completing the innocence of the heart. And he also guided others by the wisdom of his hands.

english: For the nature of understanding is twofold: one is of the hands, the other of mind and hand; for understanding, which is called along with wisdom, comes into being through the mind. Concerning this it is said, 'The Lord gives wisdom, and from his face knowledge and understanding' (Ps 78:6). But the one of the hands, being practical and productive, is shown in the understanding of the good in all those who practice it. For the understanding being practiced is an understanding of the hands; and by this the teacher guides certain ones who are not so much benefited by word. Let the understanding of the hands and the discourse of practical things be understood, so that we may logically know for each of those practicing according to virtue.

Toward the intellect: once having become the lot of God, the soul, having enriched the temple, having fallen into the experience of those dwelling within, received it. For they came upon it, not as the inheritance of God, the invisible enemies of old, being unable to approach it even in measure, being mortal because of the foreignness of the indwelling of God. Having not approached these, they entered into the temple of God which is in it, corrupting it through which they entered into sins. Lest this should happen, it is written to some, 'Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?' (1 Cor 3:16). If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God corrupts him; for the temple of God is holy, and you are some of them. It is also possible to call the unclean and uncircumcised thoughts mortal, having come into the inheritance once inhabited by God as a soul, which also once entered into the holy. But if the things happening at certain times in Christianity, having been worked by the Gentiles in the holy places, signify the things dwelling within, let the one encountering them judge. For the invisible enemies, called mortal, were not so powerful as to lay waste the once-become city of God, as if no fruit of anything remained in it, to place it in a state of desolation. And the desolation...

A small thing, as it is written in Isaiah (Isa 55:1), is a fig-bearing tree; and the fruits of this are figs and gourds. These are Egyptian foods which the people desired when sinning, even though they had the manna and the heavenly food from God, but also the mortal foods of God's servants and food to be eaten by the winged ones of heaven.

For the sinning soul, seeing the peace of God, [is lost]; Jerusalem, which passed well, had certain thoughts, because the diligent and virtuous servants happened to be of God. But they did not entirely remain, instead of seeking the incorruptible life, but they received something mortal in doing something passionately.

This is not the mortal food becoming of the winged ones who snatch what was sown by the roadside, which the Savior interpreted as the evil one (Matt 7:15) and those being sickened by this. For indeed vultures and young vultures, profiting from the beasts of the earth, do not eat the holy ones but their flesh. For whatever is found to be fleshy and passionate is nourished.

If it is possible to raise these things up to the witnesses of Christ, he himself will understand; many in persecutions, having become food for birds and beasts, yet their souls were not able to be devoured by the spiritual winged ones of heaven nor by the beasts themselves, because God did not hand over a soul confessing Him.

But the blood, which becomes the removal of the soul, instead of its life-giving power, which is called 'turning,' is poured out not far from or far from Jerusalem but around it. And this is the boundary of peace. Since the one stumbling goes outside of Jerusalem, of the correctness of the dogmas, the aforementioned blood is poured out about it and around it, not even worthy of a burial because of his exalting his sins; such are the things falling away after the knowledge of the truth (1 Tim 4:2). english: If it is a bath, it is fitting that those who have acted impiously after the bath are not buried (Ps 78:4).

By analogy, you call the heretics neighbors; for their dwellings are near us because they hold to the same writings. They do not reproach us, saying we are heretics, but they call us as slaves, well-behaved and foolish. Around us, if there are wise men among the Greeks, they sneer and mock us as believing without examination and foolishly (Ps 78:5–6).
'You have disciplined the Jews sufficiently,' they say; 'surely, at some time, turn your wrath upon the impious mortals and upon the kingdom of your reverence that is alien' (Ps 78:7, 8a).

By analogy: if the word is about invisible enemies, we did not consume the one who once became a wing for the wicked, and their place was laid waste. The place of each is his own station of life; for the prudent man in some way inhabits prudence. We say that the prudent man inhabits the place of the prudent, and others the order of the righteous. If it happens that those possessing these things of yours are devoured by enemies, their order and their place will be laid waste. We say, for example, the place of a bishop and a presbyter. As the saved are food for Jesus, the perishing are not by the eating of the wicked.

'Do not remember our ancient iniquities' (Ps 51:3). And in other places, if no one confesses what he does evilly, but rather what he acted upon of old, 'Do not remember the sin of my youth and my ignorance' (Ps 25:7). And now, those who repent of their ceased iniquities are not worthy that their ancient [sins] not be remembered by God. For indeed, the sensual ones always call upon God not concerning youthful [sins] but concerning past deeds, saying: 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have transgressed' (Ps 51:1-3). For it is contrary to the one repenting to be sinning.

'We have become exceedingly impoverished, having fallen from the wealth of virtue and knowledge, Lord; therefore we beseech you to grant us mercy, not in the future, but surely even now and quickly (Ps 51:7). For you are the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, and your mercies are sufficient to make us rich again.' And this will be easy for us, with your helping and saving; for many times, with your helping...

We experience the salvation of the Lord. Even if we are not worthy to suffer well because of the sins that are among us, but since your name has been called upon us (for we are your inheritance and your people), be propitiated toward our sins, so that your name may be glorified. For we do not bear the reproach of the nations saying, 'Where is their God?' (Ps 78:10). For they hold us in subjection because we have sinned, and they reproach even your name, thinking that you have been defeated by those who are beneath us.

And toward a turning point of discourse: those being squeezed by the chains of their own sins have been brought low, but having become aware of the weight, they are overcome by the plains, through which they are hindered from running toward salvation and from working out those things that contribute to happiness, groaning thus, being utterly exhausted. Therefore they also pray that their groan may be known to God and enter before him. For he will move his own goodness to intervene to break their bonds; for the Lord looses the bound (Ps 78:12). And he will set them apart for blessed life, according to the greatness of the God Word, his arm, so that, even if they appeared as sons of men having been dead, they might be shown to be children becoming living ones. For their fathers, having been killed by the enemies, are living before the Lord, and they are found to be his sons and his servants.

Since the number seven holds a symbol of rest, they desire the retribution to be upon the description of their impiety, through which they reproached God and were roughly brought to his servants, to be led away. For those knowing the good God will not lift up the reproaches of the scourged, but they want the scourgings to be brought upon them, so that the workers of that laziness, to whom punishment follows by necessity, may be idle. But the Sabbath number is a symbol of laziness. Since we are being enriched as your people and sheep grazing your pasture, concerning which it has been said, 'He shall enter and go out and shall find pasture' (Ps 78:13) (clearly meaning the sheep of Christ), we asked for blessings; do according to your greatness, so that, as you are clearly present, we may gratefully acknowledge you throughout life; for this clearly signifies 'unto the age' regarding the present. english: But also in the coming life, thanks be to God. The phrase 'unto generation and generation' can be said more simply instead of 'and unto the generations and the many successors of men.' Or you may say more mystically, 'in the present and in the coming life,' or 'in both generations, the one of circumcision and the one of the calling of the Gentiles,' so that they may learn to praise God.

The Shepherd of Israel is none other than the one who said, 'I am the good shepherd' (John 10:11), who grazes those who have understanding and see God. He also guides those being added from the Gentiles like sheep, that is, as his own sheep, the Israelites; for Joseph, being interpreted as 'addition of the Lord,' signifies those from the Gentiles being added to those of the circumcision. It is the custom for the shepherd's voice to be placed instead of the approach of kings only in the ancient days. For indeed, even shepherds, as far as possible, set themselves out to rule and to lead among the flocks of the simpler animals, so that having progressed, they might consider themselves to rule over even peoples.

The Lord is seated upon the cherubim, as he is presented in Ezekiel (Ezek. 10). But he breathes upon the animals who have not attained this leadership from the wisdom present to them (for a multitude of knowledge is interpreted by the cherubim), which is established by virtue itself and is found by chance; but there exists in all those who have lit themselves with the light of knowledge which God has shone in the hearts for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of Christ. This one, being royally established upon the cherubim, the choir of the saints entreats to appear and to shine before those bearing fruit in virtue and the sons of the right hand of God through the right-hand works, thoughts, and words having been performed, and those who have departed from the form of evils by their actions. For they have not truly taken forgetfulness of evils in the remembrance of good things. For Ephraim is fruitfulness, Benjamin is the son of the right hand, and Manasseh is interpreted from forgetfulness. They say therefore: 'Since you are a king, having awakened a greatest power and having roused it, O Lord, so as to save us; for there is no other way to attain salvation than for you, having come to us, to turn us back from sins.'

And of the captivity, the Lord of powers, as follows, bringing it upon us. Ps 79:5-6: 'O Master, All-King, ruling over the heavenly hosts, when will you shine for me, so that I may desire to see your face? For you are angry with me, your servant.' Therefore I beseech you: having been reconciled to your servant, who ruled, that I might not be in need. For I thirst for him exceedingly and without restraint.

And because you are angry at the prayer which we sent up, having turned it into weeping and lamentation, we bear such a multitude of tears at the time of food, as if to eat bread of tears and to drink with tears a little and measured drink. Ps 79:6-8: Since the toil and weeping for the sake of virtue is nourishment, we eat the tears of this very weeping as bread, and also drink them in measure. And the 'in measure' prevents one from always weeping and weeping through trial. For he will receive as rest and a propitiatory state those who undergo labors for the sake of good things. To this end, 'Blessed are those who weep now, they shall laugh' [Matt 5:4], and 'Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy' [Ps 126:5]. For those who sow virtue with sweat and tears, they are able to measure the weeping, reaping in joy; for with it they shall laugh.

Let us be set for contention against our neighbors. It is said, 'Every evil man raises contention'; and the Savior has cast down his hands toward the sinning people who disobey and contradict him. For the neighbors are enemies; they mock them, sneering and dragging away their wise words. The wise man, however, has taken a command for his mind not to say anything, lest the fool should mock the wise man's wise words. But they will also mock those crying out to God. But they themselves, rather, say they are entreating: 'Lord God of powers, turn back now, redeeming our captivity from those who tyrannize.' And we shall desire this good thing: if you show your eternal face to us, you will grant us salvation. Ps 79:6-14
For allegory: the soul is then said to dwell in Egypt, as it spends time with the sensible things and the works of the flesh. But God moves it from Egypt, tearing it away from material things.

english: For all, even he who will transplant it from the former bad planting into a better land. And that land is the state according to virtue.

And he sang before it, having given a saving law and luminous commands before it, in order to travel to the good land; and that land is perfect virtue. If it seems well to you, Egypt, to take the land as a spiritual world in which the soul, struggling with the sensible and temporal things, is planted, you would take a transplantation into the heavenly and intelligible realms of it, with God being the cause of this so great good for it, because he has prepared the way before it by giving the spiritual discourse of the God-breathed Scriptures (2 Tim 3:16). Its shadow covered them. For those called the righteous, who were high and possessed a lasting citizenship, were sheltered by what was well spread out under it. But also those who have become wealthy and well-toned through a more prosperous life, as if to profit from God's gain, were covered by its leafy branches in a certain way, being supported by them. And the vine extends its branches to the greatest extent, as if approaching the seas without suffering harm from the trials and surges of life called seas, to bear fruit metaphorically. And it also extends its shoots, just as the rivers that water it, in order to yield the proper fruit. And its branches are those joined to the Jewish worship, who, because of remaining in the law, happen to bear fruit like the shoots of those proselytizing.

If the vine is such a soul cultivated by God, having its beginning and its root in the Word, according to which it is logical for the one saying, 'I am the true vine' (John 15:1), God will transplant its various branches and powers, its roots metaphorically being shoots, into the various thoughts of the Only-begotten. For the vine, being raised up because it is well cultivated, will cover the high doctrines of truth, called shadows, with itself. And this citizenship and knowledge existing here are able to bear a shadow and a type of its true state hereafter.

And its side-shoots, which have branched out from its powers and virtues, are also extended, being called rivers as they are the drinkable waters of the divine words. And in another way, its side-shoots may be called such, as that which branches out from it for the benefit of the other instruction. For just as the side-shoots drink and are transformed into drinkability from the plant upon which they have branched, so also those branching out from the other learning drink from its preceding teaching, with every name being taken captive into the obedience of Christ.

Why would you remove its hedge? For if the vine does not bear fruit, the keeper of the cluster is found in the tent. But when fruitlessness exists, he abandons the tent. And those passing by the road trample it, not those walking [the path]. But these are false teachers and the spirits of error. They trample it, possessing a cluster of gall and a grape of bitterness; for such a settlement has become. And one bears passions instead of moral virtues, having produced thorns instead of grapes; and another errs concerning knowledge, bearing a cluster of gall and a grape of bitterness.

God desolated it from the thicket. Those desolating it are either the irrational [passions] and its wild passions, or the exposed and most evil powers. And perhaps God is able to be the shameful desires and unbridled pleasures, and because of the uncleanness in the thicket—that is, in the fruitless plants—they will be surrounded; for these passions are hidden regarding irrational impulses and fantasies, but the description of the more savage beast may signify even as if they had come to be, the heart and the angers. But the savage beast is the irrational mind, as if someone were to mount its passion (Ps 79:18-19).

A man, who has become like us individually and has not cast away his being, has been foretold by the Divine Scripture: 'Behold, his name is Orient, and a man comes after me' (Ps 79:18-19). If, regarding this man, the creative sign and wonders of God's hand were not to become the right hand (and this is the Divine Word), instead of the logical soul having been united to flesh according to subsistence and through it having blessed the God-marked things, such an improvement would be for us as not...

english: To depart from you. For if we are not partakers of you, we shall not be made alive, and we shall not call upon your name. For from this salvation will also follow us; for everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved (Ps 80:2).

Since the commands of those being improved by Christ are many, and his stages have been spoken of as the true vine, there are various presses—that is, promises—in which the fruit is being pressed out, making the name [of God] and gladdening the heart of man. And since all the God-breathed Scripture speaks of vines (for concerning it, after it was taken away from the Hebrews and given to those believing from the Gentiles, it was said to the Jews, 'The kingdom of heaven shall be taken from you'—'the vine in the parable had grown'—'and it shall be given to a nation producing its fruits'; the fruit and clusters of this vine are the bearing of thoughts; the minds of the believers, having received divine presses, will not receive seeds as fruit, but will press out the Name, from which the one able to say to God, 'Joy has come into my heart' (Ps 80:2), drinks.

Fittingly, the eighty-first psalm is arranged according to its title, this number containing eights and tens as a symbol of the resurrection of the Lord being accomplished on the eighth Lord's day. And it is not the first that is written concerning the presses, but also the eightieth. And it himself, because of the aforementioned thought, is arranged in the order of the number eight.

Since Jesus, helping us through his death, dissolved the one having dominion over death, the devil, we shout aloud, triumphing against the abolished tyrant, rejoicing in the one providing the help (Ps 80:2).

Since the timbrel is made of the skin of a dead animal, he wants us, having killed the members upon the earth and carrying the death of Jesus in the body, to construct a timbrel for ourselves, which we shall give instead of a psalm. We do not take by the present...

The word commands not only to strike a timbrel for the psalm, but also a harp and a lyre. As it is said in other psalms, the harp is [called so] because it is straight and unbending, and because it gives back the sound from above; the spirit is the human spirit within him, the soul being signified by the lyre, with the senses stretched out and the powers of the soul composing the sound through well-ordered and musical activities.

If, then, the harp is the spirit, the lyre the soul, and the body the timbrel, it is being allegorized: we take the divine word [as] a psalm, in order to make the spirit, the soul, and the body active through the contemplation and actions according to virtue. According to an upward leading, it is thus: the command which declares the spiritual will of the shadowy feast is set as a testimony by the Lord to those who were added to the Gentiles by the Gospel. For the name of Joseph and what was said before signify these. For they did not leave behind the passions and the evils and the very place of the earth by wisdom, fleeing out of tropical Egypt, but in leaving it, they previously did not know the language, that is, the dialect they heard. The symbols of this paradox are carried into the Acts of the Apostles, where, having appeared as tongues of fire, they sat upon each of the believers, so that each one might suddenly speak the greatness of God in his own dialect heard in various voices. But those receiving this gift turned away from lifting up the sense of their souls, no longer enduring to lift up the material and muddy things of tropical Egypt. For they served, but they shall not serve with their hands in the basket; their hands in their actions are no longer touching wheat and brick, but are lifting up gracefully and freely some of the baskets, of which Jesus filled, from which he broke.

english: For the fragments left behind have become full baskets since those who feed the disciples carry these spiritual baskets. A storm is often taken for a trial. Since God is not present with those being tempted openly but rather hiddenly, it is necessary for the one being tempted to call upon Him, [so that] how having heard him, God will rescue him from his present distress.

'And my people will not hear my voice' (Ps 80:12). To hear signifies not only the sensing of a voice, but also to be persuaded by the one speaking, according to [the Psalm]: 'You do not heed the voice of my disciplining,' that is, I did not consent to the commands of the discipliner. And hearing the voice signifies also to understand and to think. For he says, 'Whoever has ears, let him hear'; that is, whoever has understanding, let him understand. And he says of his people that he awakens them to goodwill, while weighing down and increasing their transgression; saying only once, 'If he had encountered a nation [that would forgive],' [but] not hearing our voice, being uninitiated, now they shall be punished without forgiveness.

And not only 'my people will not hear my voice,' but also 'they will not pay attention to me,' even though [they are] capable of understanding, seeing me. For even if he despises the voice, it is good to make clear through the one approaching me with my authority, that the timely evangelical word is not understood by the heterodox, who are interrupting these things, as seen in the Savior saying to the Jews concerning the Father, 'Nor have you ever heard his voice, nor have you seen his form' (John 12:49). The heretics, not having understood what was said, say that the Jews, having heard the voice of God and having seen his form, according to the appearances written by them. But the Savior rebukes them, showing that they have never heard the voice of God nor seen his form, and that to pay attention to God involves both hearing the voice and seeing the form. And those of differing opinions were deceived, having ignored the great significance of hearing the voice. For if even the Jews, having heard the voice of God and having received the law from him, did not understand it nor were persuaded by it, they are justly rebuked for not hearing his voice; but they also did not see his form, not having conformed to the character.

Regarding his substance, saying, 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9). Not so; it is said, meaning they have never heard the voice of God, and likewise here they are struck by the spoken word and the word that will be declared hereafter.

In 'the nothing' of Psalm 80:15a, it signifies that they humbled their enemies through lowly things, just as even the greatest tyrant of Egypt was not opposed by great and strong armed men, but by lowly and small creatures. In Psalm 81:2–4, they say that men set over the judging of the people are called gods, as Moses himself demonstrates, saying, 'You shall not do evil to gods, nor shall you speak evil of rulers of your people' (Exodus 22:28). For those being appointed as gods to the people of God are not further from the judges. But since hereafter in this same Psalm God says, 'I said, You are gods, and all of you are sons of the Most High' (Psalm 81:6) (not having been placed there, but because the word of God came to them), it is evident that even now 'God stands in the assembly of gods' (Psalm 82:1) will be brought against them. For all those who are such gods—men and angels—are divine in the same way, for God stands in their midst, unmoving and not abandoning them; such are they. For he stands away from those who fall, leaving them behind. Therefore also Adam, after the transgression, was standing before God who was with him before the sin; and it is said in the prophet, 'And the Lord God will go in the fury of his wrath' (Isaiah 33:19). But God, standing in the assembly of the gods, preserves their divinity, rather nourishing and increasing it through the participation they have in him. But even being in their midst, he distinguishes them in the manner spoken: 'How long will you judge injustice and accept the faces of sinners?' (Psalm 82:2). If the judges of Israel are gods, what is written will fall upon them. For it is a perversion of a judge to judge injustice and to accept the faces of sinners. Just as they corrupt the right through the greed for gifts, so too they judge contrary to the law by accepting faces. It is fitting, then, that the judgment falls upon sinners. For it is not right to give the right to the rich and to another who excels in the sequence of equality. For it is said, 'And you shall not show mercy to the poor in judgment' (Psalm 82:8); and it is also said, 'Not...'

english: He will show no partiality in judgment; you will judge both the great and the small (Ps 81:5); one will not show partiality, for such is the judgment of God. For it is necessary for the judge to know what he serves in the judgment of God. Therefore it is also well said, that God stands in the assembly of these gods and judges them in their midst (Ps 81:5), as those knowing Him in them and in their midst, according to His own purpose.

If indeed they are gods who change their divinity, since they prove to be turnable, how can one judge injustice? For having an intermediate law by which it is possible to know the good to be chosen and the evil to be avoided, if they come to things in a way that turns away from the good and embraces the evil, you judge injustice; therefore you also take the faces of sinners, hiding your own faces which are according to the image of God. Judge the orphan, who has been left desolate by the father entrusted to guardianship, but also the poor man who does not wish to contend with his own righteous ones; but also bring out the laborer and the poor, being oppressed, rescuing them from the grasping sinners.

But it is also said to those who have been made divine according to virtue, how they judge worthily the one who has cast off the worthless father and the wealth of wickedness, in protection through discipline toward them. And let them also justify the one made lowly and poor through blindness, because he has come to toil for the sake of piety, excluding those who are not truly poor and needy, on account of making them do the work of a sinner by a hand outside of them.

The divine knowledge, being wisdom of God, shines and enlightens the one having it; for the wisdom of man enlightens his face (Prov 1:5), and those called toward divine knowledge have the command to enlighten for themselves the light of knowledge. If then the wise according to God happen to be enlightened, those who are contrary, being filled with ignorance and unreasonableness, wander in darkness, always progressing in evils.

But since, having become accustomed to evils and having embedded the first things of wickedness, they have not only become earthly due to their material existence, but they also wished the foundations of the earth to be, remaining firmly and immovably in the worthless opinion. But if they themselves are of such a kind...

They did not love, but rather the human-loving word causes them to be shaken and moved from the very bad position they hold, and to fall from the position they built with a clumsy hand (Ps 81:6-7). The good God is not all envious of his own, giving to men what he is, just as he accepted the word of the gods. But the God who makes them gods is God, and he will make them sons of the Most High, participating with them, the only-begotten Son of the Most High. But although God granted to them the being to be gods and sons of the Most High, they ran toward the opposite, to become humans and to die the death that follows humans.

For they did not become humans by falling from divinity (for this is how both gods and sons of the Most High happened), but according to how they loved, mortal and human. And they die not as humans do, not the common death, but the death that follows sin, falling similarly to the one who fell among the rulers. For such is the devil; for he himself was a ruler and fell in the heavens. For it is said concerning him, 'How did the Morning Star, rising in the morning, fall from heaven?' (Luke 10:18). In this way also Adam, sinning, did not as a god but as one of God's fell, clearly showing that he became [human]; for God did not say concerning him, 'Behold, Adam has become like us,' but 'As one of us' or 'As one of ours'—as many things are contained in the copies (Ps 81:8).

He said another scripture has, 'Rise, O God, judge the earth; you shall destroy all the nations' (Ps 81:8). God will judge all those on the earth, for the earth was made because of those who think of earthly things. And God will judge the earth, destroying all the nations, but not all the mortals. For the superstitious and the other curiosity, along with those who have worked them, the mortals were destroyed by God, so that the mortals might become pure for the acceptance of the word of salvation. And that disposition in the nations, through which the mortals were diverse, God, by destroying them, will show that they, having cast away what had happened to them, will prove to be in the image of himself, just as mortals have become.

english: Likeness is understood in two ways. For when there is identity in essence, it is called similarity and even strictly identity; but when it is according to quality, it is called simply similarity. According to the second meaning, those becoming perfect are said to be made like God, just as the heavenly Father is perfect; therefore it is said, 'When he is revealed, we shall be like him' (1 John 3:2), meaning, like God. And the Creator of all, according to the first meaning, which I say is according to essence, fashioned man not according to an image and his own likeness, for no one is becoming like God. For 'Who shall be like [God]?' (Ps 82:2) does not declare something rare but rather something impossible, that no one is able to be like God in essence. But do not err, thinking that yourself and the Son are subject to the things being said. For it is not 'Who is like you?' but 'Who shall be made like you?'; for the Son is not about to undergo being made like God, being of His own essence and therefore being the same as Him, not in number but in the sameness of essence.

He wills them to be placed by God like an unstable and unwatered wheel (Ps 82:14). For it will be a misfortune to them not to be made stable and to remain motionless, having pursued wickedness. Therefore also He wills them to be placed like a reed being scattered and being driven about by a fierce wind before the face of the one pursuing them, a punishing spirit, allegorically a wind (Ps 82:15). And the fire of punishments shall consume them, having cut off the grove which had become fruit. And using another punishment against them, He will pursue them with His own storm, from which there is no escape; therefore they shall be troubled in the wrath of God being brought upon them. Since indeed their sins were diverse, a multi-faceted punishment has necessarily risen over them. It should be noted, however, that He loved them, though they were a good planting, becoming unfruitful. For the reed has its beginning from a good seed, not beforehand, but deviating by accident. For if they had borne fruit beforehand, it was necessary for them to become wheat, if they were to be brought into the granaries of the Word. But not desiring this, they have become a reed and a wasteland, which the tyrant of the spiritual Egypt shall use for the construction of...
They shall burn in the fire of destructive cities, and they shall be consumed by the unquenchable fire (Ps 82:19b).

For even if others are high and have become Most High through virtue, being lifted up, none of them is such from himself or in essence. For God alone is Most High, making [others] Most High but not becoming [so] himself; just as He alone is wise and alone is true, providing wisdom and truth but not participating [in them as a recipient], so the Most High is unique, according to this being the Most High and the Only-begotten Most High. For the power of the Most High overshadowed Mary; and the Holy Spirit, being sent from the Most High, is Most High. The only Most High is fitting to the Trinity. For he who spoke the Most High Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit declares [them]; likewise, he who called the Son also declares the Father and the Holy Spirit. For as there is one deity, so is the Most High in it, so that there might be no difference regarding the Trinity, just as we theologize correctly in other matters.

Regarding the word 'As' (Ps 83:2,3a), it does not signify a likeness or a parable here, but the beloved thing itself, just as in Moses, where he is 'as' a servant, and Christ is 'as' a son. For 'as a son' signifies a true Son and not a likeness; and Moses was not a likeness of a servant of God, but was a servant of Him. Therefore, regarding the word present, the beloved dwellings of God are not according to a parable but according to truth. And if we have meditated on what kind of things they are, we will more certainly understand them as beloved things, rather than finding them to be merely like beloved things. These things are therefore eternal and heavenly, concerning which the Savior says to those present, 'Make friends for yourselves from the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when it fails, they may receive you into the eternal dwellings' (Luke 16:9). My soul longs and faints, to cast off the psychic state and become spiritual, as is appropriate for the dwelling in the heavenly courts, as they have been spoken of in parallel.
The altars are not perceptible. For the altar was not a multitude, according to the history. Unless even the altar is called so, Lord of hosts of the heavens (Ps 83:8).

english: The altars upon which [sacrifices] are brought up are better than the sacrifices of shadow and type. The apostle says that the types of those in the heavens are [linked] to these sacrifices, but the heavenly things are better sacrifices than these. For the sacrifices of praise and righteousness are brought up upon these altars, and those offering the living sacrifice, presenting their own bodies pleasing to God, they offer them not upon something else but upon these altars.

For the dwelling of God is perfect virtue and the highest knowledge of the truth (Ps 83:5). It is said that in the presence [of God] the tent is a symbol of progress; for those traveling, it is a home. But the end of blessedness is made manifest by the dwelling of God's voice. And according to the history, the people traveling had a tent of witness (the dwelling of theology) and they had various tents for their own virtues in which all the people dwelt. Having reached the holy land, they had the dwelling in houses, no longer progressing; for they had reached the end of virtue and knowledge. But they were no longer approaching the tent of witness but the dwelling established, completing the things of worship. And there, therefore, after desiring and loving their progresses through the tabernacles, he began, saying, 'How lovely are your tabernacles, O Lord' (Ps 83:7), blessing those who have ascended through the progresses to the summit, as dwelling while bearing the state according to God, when the fullness is fulfilled upon them and the Son is revealed, we shall be like him, seeing him as he is (Ps 83:7-8a).

'The one set' signifies 'to do then,' as 'I set a guard with my mouth' instead of 'I did' (Ps 83:8a); and 'He who sets the inhabited world desolate' is the same as 'He who will make the inhabited world desolate.' And here 'the one set in a place' does not present 'He made a place.' For the surrounding place is not this. For in this God disposed of the [things] before...

He makes covenants for men. Let us not weep, nor let us praise the blameless weeping, learning from the fact that God established covenants for those who are here. For we shall also receive the blessings, living according to the will of the covenant given here. And we shall know the magnitude of the blessings given, understanding who the possessors of them are. And not such is the God who legislated. And they shall proceed from power to power. The virtues and contemplations of the truth are powers. Therefore, those having these are also more able.

Those having proceeded will not hasten according to the progress of the introductory power to become the more perfect, and those living according to the law toward the evangelical way—those knowing Christ according to the flesh to behold his glory, glory as unique from the Father; those knowing in part that he is on earth and that the most sharp knowledge does not fit—upon the coming of the perfect vision of contemplation to know as it is necessary to know, proceeding from a lower power of the intellect to a greater and more perfect power. [Psalm 83:10b] And more pure and more holy of the saints, but rather also of priests and kings, he is able to bring this merit to, Christ, the Son of God. For it is said, 'Do not be afraid of my Christs concerning all the saints,' and priests and kings were approaching as Christs in Hebrew. [Psalm 83:11a] Better it is to be in your courts for one day than a multitude of thousands of days outside your courts. For the perfection among men exceeds that which seems little in the courts of God. Such also is that which was said concerning John by the Savior: 'Among those born of women no one is greater than John, but the least in the kingdom is greater than him.' [Matthew 11:11] Let it also be said thus here: men living are under time, but those in [eternity] are time unto a multitude.

source_text: ἡμερῶν μερίζεται, μίαν ἡμέραν ε χοντος αἰώνιον καὶ ἀδιάκοπον τοῦ ἐν ταῖς θείαις αὐλαῖς τοῦ κυρίου γεγενημένου. γέγονε γὰρ αὐτῷ κύριος φῶς αἰώνιον τοῦ ἡλίου τῆς δικαιοσύνης οὐ δύνοντος ἐπ' αὐτῷ. αυ τη ου ν ἡ ἀδιάστατος καὶ ἀδιάκοπος ἡμέρα κρείσσων ει η τῆς πολυημέρου ἐνταῦθα γινομένης ζωῆς. 849 Ps 83,12b–13 ∆ίδωσιν ὁ θεὸς χάριν τοῖς σῳζομένοις χάριτι κατὰ τὸ Χάριτί ἐστε σεσῳσμένοι, ι σον δωρεᾶς δυναμένης ἐνταῦθα τῆς χάριτος. ε στι γὰρ καὶ ε τερον τῆς χάριτος σημαινόμενον καθὸ κεχαριτωμένος τις εὑρίσκεται. κατὰ τοῦτο γὰρ λέγεταί τις εὑρηκέναι χάριν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ. ταύτην τὴν χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος προτέρας δίδωσιν, η ς ἐκ τοῦ ἐφ' ἡμῖν κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν ἀναλαβεῖν ἐσπεύσαμεν. ∆ίδωσι δὲ καὶ δόξαν τοῖς ἀξίοις τοῦ τυχεῖν ταύτης διὰ τὸ προδεδοξακέναι τὸν λέγοντα Τοὺς δοξάζοντάς με δοξάσω, δηλονότι δι' ἀγαθῶν ε ργων καὶ ἀληθινῶν δογμάτων. Πορεύονται δ' ἐν ἀκακίᾳ οἱ α νευ χειρίστης ε ξεως διὰ πάντων κινούμενοι. εἰ δὲ καὶ τὴν ἁπλότητα σημαίνει ἡ ἀκακία, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπίστησον. Καὶ ἐπεὶ προσδοκία ἐστὶν ἀγαθῶν ἡ ἐλπίς, μόνον δὲ τὸ λογικὸν ὀρεκτικὸν τῶν κυρίως ἀγαθῶν, μόνου ἀνθρώπου οἰκεία ἀρετὴ τὸ ἐλπίζειν, μάλιστα ο ταν εὐσεβείας ἀντιποιῆται· γέγραπται γὰρ ̓Ελπὶς τῷ εὐσεβεῖ. ἀναγεννῶνται γὰρ οἱ πιστοὶ εἰς ἐλπίδα ζῶσαν καὶ μένουσαν διὰ τὸ ἀκήρατον ει ναι τὴν τῶν ἀγαθῶν προσδοκίαν. 850 Ps 84,2–4 Πρὸς δὲ διάνοιαν· εὐδοκεῖ κύριος τὴν ἀγαθὴν καὶ σπουδαίαν καρδίαν γῆν αὐτοῦ τυγχάνουσαν διὰ τὸ δέχεσθαι τὸν σπόρον τὸν παρ' αὐτοῦ καὶ ἑκατονταπλασίονα καρποφορεῖν. ἀποστρέφει δ' εἰς αὐτὴν καὶ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν αἰχμαλώτων ἀχθέντων ὑπὸ πονηρῶν δυνάμεων, λογισμῶν ̓Ιακὼβ ο ντας διὰ τὸ ι στασθαι κατὰ τῶν παθῶν. Ταῦτα δ' ἐνέργησας α φεσιν ἀνομημάτων χαρίζεται πᾶσιν, ἐξαίρων καὶ λύων τὰς ἀνομίας αὐτῶν. ει ποτε δὲ καὶ μετὰ α φεσιν η μαρτον, καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ἁμαρτήματα ἐπικαλύπτει ἐνδοὺς τὴν ἀρετήν· καλύπτει γὰρ ἡ ἀρετὴ τὰς ἁμαρτίας, οὐκ ἐγκρύπτουσα αὐτὰς ἀλλ' ἐξ ο λων ἀναιροῦσα καὶ ἀφανίζουσα. ου τω γὰρ ἀγάπη καλύπτει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν. ὡς γὰρ ἡ ἐπιστήμη καλύπτει τὴν α γνοιαν ἐξ ο λων ἀναιροῦσα αὐτὴν τῆς ψυχῆς ῃ α ν παραγένηται, ου τω καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ αὐτὴ ου σα τῇ ἀρετῇ καλύπτει τὰς ἁμαρτίας ω ν α ν εὐεργετεῖν κρίνῃ. Εὐδόκησεν δὲ τὴν γῆν αὐτοῦ ὁ θεός, ἀποστείλας τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ὀφθῆναι ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις συναναστραφῆναι· ο θεν ἐπὶ τῷ τοκετῷ τῆς Μαρίας ∆όξα ἐν ὑψίστοις θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία ει ρηται. Μανθάνομεν δὲ ἐκ τῶν εἰρημένων ἐντεῦθεν μὴ πάθος ει ναι θεοῦ τὴν λεγομένην αὐτοῦ ὀργήν. διὰ γὰρ τὰ 168 ἁμαρτήματα ὑποστῆναι οἰκονομεῖται ω ν καταλυθέντων καὶ ἠφανισμένων καὶ αὐτὴ αὐτοῖς συναπέρχεται. εἰ δὲ φαίνονται οἱ τῇ ὀργῇ ὑπηρετούμενοι σκεύη ὀργῆς καλούμενοι ὁμωνύμως αὐτῇ θυμὸς καὶ ὀργὴ προσαγορευόμενα, βέλτιον ἐπισκέψῃ. 851 Ps 84,5–7 ̓Επεὶ τῶν σωτηρίων ω ν δίδως ἡμῖν θεὸς ὑπάρχεις, ἐπίστρεψον ἡμᾶς, ἀφορμὰς μετανοίας ἡμῖν παρασχὼν καὶ δεχόμενος ἡμᾶς ἀνακάμπτοντας πρὸς σέ. ε ψεται γὰρ τὸ καὶ τὸν θυμόν σου ἀποστραφῆναι ἀφ' ἡμῶν. ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἐξήψαμεν αὐτὸν δι' ω ν ἡμαρτήκαμεν, μεταγνόντων καὶ ἐπιστρεψάντων ἡμῶν, οὐκέτ' ἐνεργήσει καθ' ἡμῶν ἀφανιζόμενος. ὡς γὰρ πῦρ, ἐπιλειπούσης τῆς καυστῆς υ λης καθ' η ν ἐνεργεῖ, οὐκέτ' ἐστιν, ου τως ἠφανισμένων τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἡμῶν οὐκέτι ὑποστήσεται θυμός σου καθ' ἡμῶν. Ζωοῖ ὁ θεὸς ζωὴν παρέχων τούτοις, οι πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπέστρεφον ἀποστάντες αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀποστραφέντες αὐτόν· η αὐτὸς ἐπιστρέψας τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ο ἀπέστρεψεν ἀπ' αὐτῶν δι' η ν ε πραττον κακίαν. ἑκατέρως γὰρ τὸ ̓Επιστρέψας νοεῖν δυνατὸν ἀπαρεμφάτως εἰρημένον. οὐ γὰρ ἐμφαίνει τὸ πότερον αὐτὸς ἐπ' αὐτοὺς η αὐτοὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπέστρεψαν. ζωῆς ἐνδοθείσης τοῖς ζωωθεῖσιν, εὐφράνθη ὁ λαὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπ' αὐτῷ τῷ τὴν ζωὴν δεδωκότι θεῷ. 852 Ps 84,8 ̓Επεὶ οὐκ ἐξ ε ργων ἀλλὰ χάριτι καὶ ἐλέῳ θεοῦ ἀπαιτοῦσι τὴν σωτηρίαν, φασὶν Ω κύριε, δεῖξον ἡμῖν δι' ω ν ἐλεεῖς καὶ οἰκτείρεις τὸν λαόν σου· ου τω γὰρ καὶ τὸ σωτήριόν σου, τουτέστιν ἡ παρὰ σοῦ σωτηρία, δοθείη ἡμῖν. ∆υνατὸν ε λεος καὶ σωτήριον εἰπεῖν τὸν αι τιον τῆς ἐλεημοσύνης καὶ σωτηρίας ̓Ιησοῦν. αὐτὸς γὰρ τὸ ε λεος καὶ τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστι καθὸ ἐλεεῖ καὶ σῴζει. 853 Ps 84,9 Οὐκ ε ξωθεν κρούων τὴν ἀκοὴν τῶν ἀκουόντων λαλεῖ θεὸς ἀλλ' ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ διανοίᾳ ἐναποτιθέμενος α περ βούλεται δηλῶσαι τῷ νῷ α νευ προφορᾶς, ο θεν ει ρηται τὸ ̓Ακούσομαι τί λαλήσει ἐν ἐμοί. συνᾴδει τούτῳ καὶ τὸ τοῦ ̓Αμβακοὺμ ε χον ου τως· Καὶ
english: The days are divided, one day being an eternal and unceasing one, because of having been created in the divine courts of the Lord. For the Lord has become to him an eternal light, like the sun of righteousness, which is not able to be overcome by it. The unceasing and unceasing day is greater than the life of many days occurring here.

Ps 83:12b–13: God gives grace to those being saved by grace, according to 'By grace you have been saved' (Eph 2:8), a gift of the grace able to be given here. For 'grace' and 'gift' signify the same thing, as one is found to be 'having been graced.' For this reason, it is said that someone has found grace in the sight of God. He gives this grace instead of a former grace, which we hastened to take from ourselves as much as possible. And He also gives glory to those worthy of receiving this, because He has promised the one saying, 'Those who glorify me I will glorify' (John 12:26), clearly through good works and true dogmas. And those moving through all things, unhindered by any hand, go about in innocence. If innocence also signifies simplicity, let Him also establish it.

And since hope is the expectation of good things, and only the rational appetite for truly good things is the proper virtue of man, to hope is especially the substitute for piety; for it is written, 'Hope [is] to the pious one.' For the faithful are reborn into a living and abiding hope because the expectation of good things is pure.

Ps 84:2–4: For contemplation: the Lord is pleased with a good and eager heart becoming His land, because it receives the seed from Him and bears fruit a hundredfold. But He turns away from it also the multitude of captives brought by evil powers, the thoughts of Jacob, because of standing against the passions. These things, having worked them, He grants as a remission of transgressions, removing and loosening their lawlessness. And if even after a remission there is error, He covers these sins, entering into virtue; for virtue covers sins, not hiding them, but utterly destroying and making them vanish. For in this way love covers a multitude of sins. Just as knowledge covers ignorance, utterly destroying it in the soul that it was generated in, so also the love of God, being the same as virtue, covers the sins of those it benefits.

God was pleased with his earth, having sent his Son to appear on the earth and to associate with men; thus it is said, 'Glory in the highest to God, and on earth peace among men of good pleasure' (Luke 2:14). From these things said, we learn that what is called God's wrath is not a passion. For because of sins, wrath is sustained, but it is managed such that they are destroyed and vanished, and it approaches them as a consequence.

If those serving wrath appear to be called vessels of wrath, being homonymous with it—fury and wrath being addressed—it is better that he visits. Since you are God, who gives us the salvations, turn us back, providing us opportunities for repentance and receiving us as we turn toward you (Ps 84:5–7). For it will be possible for your fury to turn away from us. Since we have removed that [wrath] through which we sinned, once we have recognized and turned back, it will no longer act against us, vanishing. Just as fire, when the combustible fuel through which it acts is failing, is no longer, so too, once our sins are vanished, your fury will no longer be sustained against us.

God lives, providing life to those who turn to him, having departed from him and turned away from him; he himself, having turned his face, turned away from them through which they practiced evil. It is possible to understand 'having turned' in both ways, most certainly said. For it is not made clear whether he himself turned toward them or they themselves turned toward him. When life was granted to the living ones, the people of God rejoiced over him, the God who granted life.

Since they require salvation not from works but by the grace and mercy of God, they say, 'O Lord, show us through whom you show mercy and compassion to your people' (Ps 84:8); for so also your salvation, that is, the salvation from you, might be given to us. It is possible to call Jesus the cause of mercy and salvation. For he is the mercy and the salvation of God, according to how he shows mercy and saves.

God does not speak striking the hearing of those listening from the outside, but placing [his will] within that mind, he desires to reveal to the intellect without utterance, which is why it is said, 'I will listen to what he speaks in me' (Hab 2:20). Agree with this also the words of Habakkuk, which say: 'And...'

source_text: ἀποσκοπεύσω τοῦ ἰδεῖν τί λαλήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ κύριος ὁ θεός. κατὰ ταῦτα καὶ ὁ Παῦλός φησιν Εἰ δοκιμὴν ζητεῖτε τοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ· ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ἀλλ' οὐχ ἁπλῶς αὐτῷ ἐλάλει Χριστός. λαλεῖ γὰρ ἐκείνῳ ἐν ῳ λαλεῖ, οὐ πάντως δὲ ῳ λαλεῖ τις καὶ ἐκείνῳ λαλεῖ, ο ταν ε ξωθεν μόνον πλήττηται ἡ ἀκοή. πλὴν ο λαλήσει ἐν αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἑρμηνεύων, ει πεν εἰρήνην ει ναι ἐπὶ τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ πάντων πολεμίων τῶν κατὰ τοῦ λαοῦ δηλονότι ἀνατρεπόντων, η εἰρήνην τὴν ὑπερέχουσαν πάντα νοῦν ἐσχηκότος τοῦ λαοῦ δι' η ς πάσης ταραχῆς καὶ θορύβου ἐκτὸς ει η γαλήνην ἀγόντων τῶν λογισμῶν. αυ english: I will aim to see what the Lord God will speak in me. According to these things also Paul says: 'If you seek a test of the Christ speaking in me; for in him indeed Christ does not speak simply to him' (2 Cor 13:5). For he speaks through that [person] in whom he speaks; and not everyone who speaks speaks through him, but only the hearing from the outside is struck. But the Lord God will speak in him, interpreting, whether it be peace or whether it be upon his people, the God of all, against all enemies of the people, clearly those subverting [them], or the peace having possessed a mind surpassing all things of the people, by which all disturbance and noise are excluded, bringing tranquility. This peace is given from God and Father and Lord Jesus by grace, as the Savior says concerning it: 'My peace I give to you' (John 14:27). And this peace is given also to those who give back the things of God to God, guarding the righteousness toward him, who are rightly called his own. And he gives it also to those who through repentance turn their heart toward him, making the turning not crooked toward him nor superficial, but from the depth of the mind.

Then indeed he truly dwelt and brought glory in the earth, performing many and great things paradoxically: the Savior's resurrections of the dead, sight to the blind, cleansings of the lepers, and other wondrous things he did (Ps 84:10). And as toward a more mystical word for those fearing God, he did not leave them wanting (For there is no lack to those fearing him), he drew near to the God-participating salvation which they partake in through which they act salvifically. For just as salvation is far from sinners, working the things of destruction, so the salvation of God is near to the opposite, to those fearing him. Therefore also he dwells, glory in the earth, of those saying these things. And you will say their earth: the good heart of theirs which has yielded a hundredfold fruit of the seed cast upon it. But what dwells in the heart as the glory of God, the word establishes, which says: 'The God who said light should shine out of darkness' (2 Cor 4:6); He shone in our hearts for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of Christ. And it dwells also in the body of those persuaded by the exhortation being said: 'Glorify then God in the body' (1 Cor 6:20).

Regarding those who achieve perfect prudence (Ps 84:11-12). From this, the following of virtues can be shown: that the merciful is true and the true is merciful, and that the just is peaceful and the peaceful is just.

In other words, truth is named along with mercy, as it is said in the Psalm: 'Thy mercy and thy truth have encompassed me' (Ps 84:11), and 'God sent His mercy and His truth' (Ps 84:12). I stand by saying these things because the truth of matters is difficult for men, and even more unreachable unless they happen to be granted it by the grace of God. Perhaps one cannot receive true salvation without the mercy of God, and thus they were named by righteousness. He says that mercy has met with truth. For if mercy and truth come to the same place, we shall know it and be in it.

Moreover, justice loves peace and peace loves justice. For where there is justice, there is certainly peace, without it being a mere sprout. You can also grasp these things regarding the Savior, spoken through His various thoughts, as has been clearly stated before. The truth of the Savior, having become man, has risen from the earth. For there is much deception and much falsehood among men. For there is no truth and mercy nor knowledge of God upon the earth; therefore, falsehood, murder, and adultery are poured out upon the earth, says the prophet (Ps 84:13). This is not the falsehood of the whole earth that prevailed, but the one overcome by Him who said, 'I am the truth' (John 14:6), having caused the truth from the earth (that is, from men) to rise. But also, becoming justice according to the Word of God and Wisdom, He descended from heaven, bowing the heavens and coming down. He brought to us peace according to justice and mercy according to truth; for all these things are thought of in Him, as has been clearly said.

As the manner of rain being given, the soil bears the goodness of the Lord's gift; the intelligent earth gives fruit, having been moistened by the goodness from God. And the fruit of it is the general virtue, whereby the soul, being as a fruit-bearing earth, happens to be presented as described. english: Something like this is said. Since the Lord spoke peace upon his people, the justice of the people going before him will set his steps upon the way leading to blessedness; and the Lord himself, who is justice, goes before the people and will set his steps into a way. To whom, indeed, is it said, 'Before you I will go and I will make the level places'?

And likewise: the justice operating according to the law in Moses and the prophets, having come forward before the end of John from the Savior, having been placed into the way of his crossings in us, to dwell and walk among us, has cried out: 'Prepare the ways of the Lord straight, make his paths'; for he alone cries: 'Make straight for him who is stepping upon the mountains, the Lord, his name.' Care also regarding John, it is said: 'He will go before the Lord in spirit and in power like Elijah,' and 'Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.'

If even the Savior is justice going before the Father into the minds of the God-bearers, consider with understanding in what way it was said: 'He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me' (Matt 10:40). Psalm 85:2b,3: 'All the saints cry out as if upon a great command concerning the servant of God.' Jonah, indeed, when asked from what land he is and from what people, said: 'I am a servant of God, and I fear the God of heaven.'

And the apostles, indeed, are testified by the Savior well through works and words, confessing him as Lord: 'For you call me Lord and Teacher, and you say well: for I am both your Lord and Teacher always, learning from me and serving me sincerely' (Matt 23:36). And concerning their own letters, they set forward this significance, as if being refreshed by a greatest command: 'James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ,' and 'Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ.' Just as the men of the world in the writings of life-transactions wish to be designated by the honors concerning them, so the apostles in the beginnings of their writings are worthy to be designated servants of God and of Christ. David, doing the similar, [and]...

To the King, he says, 'Save, O God, your servant who hopes in you; save me in your abundant mercy, because as I say all the time of my life, I cry out to you' (Ps 85:5a). But leniency is not spoken of as being upon God; for leniency is a human virtue. If it is said about it to be more human, as are the other things, such as rejoicing, being glad, or remembering.

And 'gods' is said not only there to be taken for idols and demons, but also for the saints (Ps 85:8). For in these no one is entirely and unchangeably the equal of the Lord. For He himself alone is likewise God to the Father; but each of these has become a god by participation, having received the Word of God according to 'They shall be gods' (Ps 82:6) and 'The Word of God became' (Jn 1:1). For even if they have become the image and likeness of God, none of them is in essence the equal of the Lord, being those who shall be made like Him but not being Him. 'You shall be holy because I am holy' (Lev 11:44), He who is holy, so that they may become [holy]. To speak the truth concerning those who shall become [holy]: 'Who is holy like you, Lord?' (Ps 86:15). For it has not been written, 'Who shall be equal to you among the gods, Lord?', but 'Who is your equal?'. For they shall be like, according to what was said: 'We shall be like him, what we shall see him to be.' No one is the equal of the Lord among the gods mentioned, nor does anyone among them attain [it] according to His works. Therefore also in the Gospel it is said, 'If I have not done the works which I did in them, no other man has done; he has no sin' (Jn 10:38). For even if the saints once did the same things as the Savior, it differs greatly in the manner: some working by prayer and faith toward God, others by exercising authority; therefore it is said that none of the gods are [gods] according to the works of the Savior. And it is said to us also in the beginning of the Second Book how it was said, 'Lord God, who shall be equal to you?', which we also ought to apply to the one encountering the prescribed word.

To partake blamelessly of the knowledge of the truth is impossible not through moral instruction and active deeds having been passed through (Ps 85:11ab). For one is first led by God through prayer in the way; but this second way is that of practical progress. For the beginning of a good way is doing what is just, and so on.
