Εἰ δὲ προφητεία ει η περὶ Χριστοῦ τὰ ἐπαγγελλόμενα, τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον ἐξομαλισθείη τὰ προκείμενα· φησὶν ὁ ∆αυίδ· ἐπιβλέψας ὡς θεὸς ἐλέησόν με. ὑπάρξει δὲ τοῦ διδόντος σοῦ τὸ κράτος σου τῷ παιδί σου ἐν τῷ ἐνανθρωπεῖν καὶ λαμβάνειν τὴν τοῦ δούλου μορφήν. καὶ ἐπεὶ ἀκολουθεῖ τῷ γενομένῳ ἀνθρώπῳ καὶ τεθνάναι, ἀνιστῶν αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς σώσει αὐτὸν ο ντα υἱὸν τῆς παιδίσκης αὐτοῦ τῆς εἰπούσης ὁπηνίκα η κουσεν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγγέλου ∆ιὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἐκ σοῦ α γιον κληθήσεται υἱὸς θεοῦ· ̓Ιδοὺ ἡ δούλη κυρίου· γένοιτό μοι κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου. ἀληθῶς γὰρ δούλη καὶ μήτηρ τοῦ κυρίου ἡ τεκοῦσα αὐτόν. ἐκ παραλλήλου δὲ εἰρῆσθαι νόμιζε τὸν κύριον παῖδα καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τῆς παιδίσκης. ∆ύναται δὲ καὶ υἱὸς παιδίσκης ὁ ἐκ περιτομῆς λαός. σαφῶς γὰρ περὶ τούτων ὁ Παῦλος Γαλάταις ἐπιστέλλων φησὶν ̓Αλλ' ὁ μὲν ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης κατὰ σάρκα γεγέννηται. 865 Ps 85,17 Γένοιτό μοι σημεῖον εἰς ἀγαθὸν τῆς προφητείας περιαιρουμένης τῆς διαγορευούσης ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις γενήσεσθαι τὸν θεόν, παρθένου πρὸ πείρας ἀνδρὸς τικτούσης καὶ διαμενούσης παρθένου καὶ μετὰ τὸν τόκον. τοῦτο εἰς ἀγαθὸν σημεῖον ω φθη ἐπὶ βοηθείᾳ τοῦ γένους ἡμῶν. διὸ καὶ παρεκλήθημεν· πῶς γὰρ οὐκ ἐμέλλομεν πληρεστάτην παραμυθίαν ε ξειν, θεὸν βοηθὸν ἐσχηκότες; 866 Ps 86,4a Τῆς ̔Ραὰβ καὶ τῆς Βαβυλῶνος μνησθήσεσθαι ὁ θεός φησι γινωσκόντων αὐτόν. συνᾴδει τούτοις τὸ Νῦν δὲ γνόντες θεόν, μᾶλλον δὲ γνωσθέντες ὑπὸ θεοῦ. γνῶσιν γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἀναλαβόντες μᾶλλον καὶ μάλιστα γνωσθησόμεθα ὑπ' αὐτοῦ· Εἰ γάρ τις ἀγνοεῖ, ἀγνοεῖται. καὶ πρός τινα ὁ θεὸς λέγει Οτι σὺ ἐπίγνωσιν ἀπώσω, ἀπώσομαί σε τοῦ μὴ ἱερατεύειν μου· ἐπελάθου νόμου θεοῦ σου, κἀγὼ ἐπιλήσομαι τέκνων σου. τῶν φαύλων τοίνυν ἀγνοούντων αὐτὸν ἐπιλέληστο θεός, μνησθεὶς αὐτῶν ο τε καὶ αὐτὸν ε γνωσαν αὐτοί. ̓Ιδοὺ τοίνυν τῆς ̔Ραὰβ τῆς εἰς πλατυσμὸν μεταλαμβανομένης καὶ Βαβυλῶνος συγχύσεως ἑρμηνευομένης μεμνῆσθαι ὁ θεὸς ει πεν ἐγνωκότων αὐτόν. μεταβαλόντες γὰρ οἱ τὴν πλατεῖαν καὶ εὐρύχωρον ὁδεύοντες ὁδὸν ̔Ραάβ εἰσιν ἐγνωκότες θεόν, καὶ οἱ ἐκ
english: To be able to walk in the truth of God, one must progress in it and pass through to the end. The end of knowledge and truth is to bestow upon those who have known it completely and as they possess existence.

He who chooses these very good things rejoices in the possession of them (Ps 85:11c–13). It is also to fear the name of God; the one desiring to have it with joy prays to be made glad in heart by God through fearing His name. Having obtained this, he confesses thankfully to the Lord God with his whole heart, which was made glad by the attainment of his requests. He also glorifies the name of God for eternity—that is, all the time of his life—it having become upon him great divine mercy, by which he was also rescued from the pit of slavery. For he named the lowest pit. For those sinning many and great things fall into the lowest pit, and in order that they might be rescued, they beg for great mercy, as one of them can easily say, 'Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy.' It is therefore fitting for one rescued from such great evil to glorify the name of God for eternity and to confess to Him with his whole heart.

One should not receive unthinkingly the saying that these things are spoken by our Lord Jesus Christ, with the kings of the earth and the rulers standing and gathered together against him (Ps 85:14.15). 'Visit me' (Ps 85:16). For you visit, you look, not at another, but to make well and to have mercy. Therefore also in the following things, the king is worthy to be given and to be guarded the kingdom, which God himself has given to him. For with this will follow his salvation as a child of God. If the prophecy is that concerning Christ, the promised things, then in this manner the upcoming things are smoothed out: David says, 'Looking upon [me], as God, have mercy on me.'

And regarding your giving your power to your child in becoming human and taking the form of a servant. And since he follows the one who became man and died, God will save him, the son of your handmaid who said, 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word' (Luke 1:38). For truly, the handmaid and mother of the Lord is she who bore him. And he thought it to be said in parallel, the Lord as child and the son of the handmaid. And the people from the circumcision can also be a son of the handmaid. For Paul, writing to the Galatians, clearly says concerning these things, 'But he who is born of the handmaid according to the flesh has been born' (Gal 4:31).

'Let a sign be made to me for good of the prophecy being taken up, which forbids among us humans, of a virgin giving birth before the trial of a man and remaining a virgin even after the birth' (Ps 85:17). This is a sign for good, a help to our race. Therefore also we were comforted; for how could we not have been about to have the most complete consolation, having had God as a helper? 'God says he will remember Rahab and Babylon' (Ps 86:4a), for those knowing him. Consenting to this, now having known God, but rather having been known by God. For having taken up the knowledge of him, we shall know him more, and most especially we shall be known by him: 'For if anyone does not know, he is unknown.' And to someone God says, 'Because you cast away knowledge, I will cast you away from ministering to me; you forgot the law of your God, and I will forget you, your children' (Hos 4:6).

Therefore, regarding those who are ignorant of him through faults, God has forgotten them, even though they knew him. Behold, therefore, of Rahab, who takes upon herself the wide way, and of Babylon, being interpreted as confusion, God is said to remember those who have known him. For those turning from the wide and spacious way, they are Rahab, having known God, and those from...

source_text: συγκεχυμένων καὶ τεταραγμένων ἐνθυμημάτων εἰς γαλήνην καὶ κατάστασιν διανοίας ἐληλυθότες Βαβυλών εἰσι θεὸν ἐγνωκότες, ω ν μνημονεύει θεὸς ἀξιῶν τῆς μνήμης αὐτοῦ κριθέντων. ∆ύναται δὲ ὁ πλατυσμὸς σημαίνειν τῶν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν βασιλείαν ἐρχομένων. 867 Ps 86,6 Τῆς ἐκκλησίας οὐ μόνον οἱ α ρχοντες ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ λαοὶ ἐνεγράφησαν εἰς τὴν πολιτείαν τῆς οὐρανίου πόλεως τοῦ ζῶντος θεοῦ, τὴν ἀναφορὰν ἐχόντων ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τῶν πρωτοτόκων τῶν ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανῷ, μόνου θεοῦ διηγήσασθαι δυναμένου τὴν γραφὴν αὐτῶν. οὐ γὰρ τῶν ἐκ συλλαβῶν ὀνομάτων αὐτῶν ἡ ἀναγραφὴ γέγονεν ἀλλὰ τῶν δηλούντων τὴν κατὰ ψυχὴν ποιότητα αὐτῶν η ς μόνος αὐτὸς ε φορός ἐστιν. καὶ ε στιν ἐκ τοῦ ἐναντίου ἐπιστῆσαι τῷ θεωρουμένῳ· ἐν ̔Ιερεμιᾷ γέγραπται ̓Αφεστηκότες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς γραφήσονται. ὡς ου ν οἱ ἀφεστηκότες καὶ πόρρω θεοῦ γεγενημένοι γράφονται ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ χοϊκοῦ περικείμενοι φρονοῦντες τὰ ἐπίγεια καὶ τὰ ὑλικὰ διανοούμενοι, ου τως οἱ τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ ἐπουρανίου 172 φοροῦντες καὶ τὸ πολίτευμα ε χοντες ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἐκεῖ ἐμπολιτογραφούμενοι ἐνετάγησαν τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ βίβλῳ. 868 Ps 87 αργ ̔Υπὲρ μαελέθ, τουτέστιν ὑπὲρ χοροῦ η χορείας τῶν υἱῶν Κορέ, ὑπὲρ τοῦ σύνεσιν καὶ συνετῶς ἀποκρίνεσθαι τῷ τὸν θεὸν φοβουμένῳ καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τυγχάνοντι ἀληθῶς ̓Ισραηλίτῃ. Αἰμὰν γὰρ ἑρμηνεύεται φόβος αὐτῶν, ὡς πάντα τὸν ε χοντα θεῖον φόβον καὶ εὐλάβειαν Αἰμὰν ει ναι, ῳ σύνεσιν ἀποκρίνεσθαι προσήκει ο ντι συνετῷ ἀκροατῇ μετὰ χορείας καὶ χοροῦ θείου τοῦ ψαλμοῦ τὴν ᾠδὴν ἀπαγγέλλοντι. 869 Ps 87,2.3 Κεκράξομαι πρὸς σὲ οὐ μεθ' ἡμέραν μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ νύκτωρ, οὐκ ἐν μόνοις τυγχάνων τοῖς λαμπροῖς καὶ προσηνέσι τοῦ βίου πράγμασιν (ἀδύνατον ἡμέραν ει ναι) ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τοῖς σκυθρωποῖς γεγενημένος νυκτερινὴν κατάστασιν περιέχουσιν· ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μὲν κεκραγώς, ο πως παραμένῃ μοι ἡ τῶν ἀγαθῶν μετουσίᾳ, ἐν νυκτὶ δέ, ο πως τέλος αὐτῆς λαβούσης ἐκ νυκτὸς πρὸς σὲ τὸ πνεῦμά μου ὀρθρίσαι δυνηθῇ. ∆υνατὸν δὲ καὶ ἁπλούστερον εἰπεῖν παραπλησίως τῷ λεχθέντι ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος ̔Ο πατὴρ ποιήσει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν τεκνῶν αὐτοῦ τῶν βοώντων πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός. ὁ γὰρ τὸν νόμον κυρίου μελετῶν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς καὶ δι' αὐτοῦ τοῦ μελετᾶν ε ργοις καὶ διαθέσει κεκράξεται πρὸς τὸν θεὸν τῆς σωτηρίας ἑαυτοῦ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, ὁτὲ μὲν αἰτούμενος σωτηρίαν, ὁτὲ δὲ φυλαχθήσεσθαι αὐτὴν η δη ὑπάρξασαν παρακαλῶν. Πολλὴν δὲ παρρησίαν ε χοντος πρὸς θεὸν ἡ λέγουσα φωνὴ Εἰσελθέτω ἐνώπιόν σου ἡ προσευχή μου. ἐπεὶ γὰρ τοιαῦτα αἰτοῦμαι α κἀμοὶ συμφέρει καὶ σοὶ πρέπει καὶ φίλον διδόναι (αἰτοῦμαι γὰρ τὰ κυρίως ἀγαθά), ἐν ο ψεσί σου ἡ ἡμετέρα προσευχὴ γενέσθω· ου τως γὰρ καὶ ἐπινεύσεις παρασχεῖν α ᾐτησάμην, συγκαταβαίνων καὶ κλίνων πρὸς μὲ τὸ ου ς σου· ου τως γὰρ εἰσακουσθῆναι πεπίστευκα· διὰ τοῦτο δὲ πρὸς σέ, ω δέσποτα, βοῶ. 870 Ps 87,4 Πολλοὶ γὰρ οἱ ἐπικείμενοι πολέμιοι οἱ κατασπάσαι τὴν ζωήν μου εἰς τὸν ᾳ δην θέλοντες, ἐφ' οι ς ἀθυμῶν καὶ ἀγωνιῶν κακῶν ε χω πλησθεῖσαν τὴν ψυχήν, τουτέστιν ἐπιπόνων κακωτικῶν. 871 Ps 87,5 ̓Εκ παραλλήλου τὸν αὐτὸν τόπον ᾳ δην καὶ λάκκον καλεῖν ε θος τῇ θείᾳ γραφῇ. αὐτὸς ου ν γενόμενος ὁ σωτὴρ ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν ο λων σωτηρίας ἐλήλυθε λύτρον δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀντὶ πολλῶν, χάριτι θεοῦ ὑπὲρ παντὸς γευσάμενος θανάτου. Μόνος γὰρ αὐτὸς ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανε καὶ ταύτῃ ει πε Προσελογίσθην μετὰ τῶν καταβαινόντων εἰς λάκκον. ἑκάστου γὰρ εἰκότως κατιόντος εἰς τὸν λάκκον δι' α ε πραξεν η ἐφρόνησεν, ἐγὼ προσελογίσθην καὶ μετ' αὐτῶν ἠριθμήθην, οὐκ ἀκολουθίας ε ργων εἰς τοῦτό με ἀγαγούσης ἀλλ' εὐδοκίας πατρικῆς καὶ ἡμετέρου θελήματος προσλογισθῆναι τούτοις τοῖς εἰς τὸν λάκκον κατιοῦσι κρινάντων· ο θεν αὐθαιρέτως καὶ ἐθελουσίως ἐγενήθην ὡς α νθρωπος ἀβοήθητος, τῆς ὁμοιώσεως οὐκ εἰς τὸν α νθρωπον ἀναφερομένης. Απαγε· α νθρωπος γὰρ κατὰ ἀλήθειαν γέγονεν, ὁμοιῶσθαι δέ φησιν οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἀνθρώπῳ ἀλλ' ἀβοηθήτῳ ἀνθρώπῳ. δυνάμενος γὰρ μὴ παθεῖν μὴ κρατηθῆναι μὴ δεθῆναι, ἑαυτὸν ἐπιδέδωκεν, Γενόμενος ὑπήκοος μέχρι θανάτου, θανάτου δὲ σταυροῦ. ̓Αλλ' εἰ καὶ γέγονεν ἑκουσίως α νθρωπος ἀβοήθητος ὡς καὶ περιβληθῆναι θανάτῳ, ἀλλά γε ἐν νεκροῖς ἐλεύθερος η ν. πάντων γὰρ τῶν εἰς τὸν χῶρον τῶν νεκρῶν ἀπιόντων ὑπό τινων ἀγομένων, οὐ φαύλων μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ σπουδαίων, μόνος ̓Ιησοῦς τεθάρρηκεν εἰπεῖν Οὐδεὶς αι ρει τὴν ψυχήν μου ἀπ' ἐμοῦ· ἐγὼ τίθημι αὐτὴν ἀπ' ἐμαυτοῦ, ι να πάλιν λάβω αὐτήν. ο τι δὲ ἡ πάντων ψυχὴ ὑπό τινων εἰς
english: Having come into the tranquility and stability of the mind from poured-out and disordered affections, they have entered Babylon having known God, whom God remembers, deserving of His remembrance when judged. The expansion may signify those coming from the east and west toward the kingdom (Ps 86:6).

Regarding the Church, not only the rulers but also the peoples have been inscribed into the citizenship of the heavenly city of the living God, having a registration upon the church of the firstborn who are written down in heaven, which only God is able to recount. For their registration has not happened from the mere collection of their names, but from that which reveals the quality of their soul, which only He Himself bears. And it is possible to learn from the opposite by the observer: in Jeremiah it has been written, 'Those having departed from the earth shall be written' (Jer 3:3). Just as those having departed and having become far from God are written upon the earth as the image of the worldly, surrounding themselves with earthly and material things and thinking of them, so those bearing the image of the heavenly and having citizenship in the heavens, being enregistered there, have been enrolled in the book of God.

Regarding 'For Ma'elah,' that is, for the dance or the chorale of the sons of Korah, for the understanding and for answering wisely to him who fears God and because of this truly becomes an Israelite. For their fear is interpreted as having all the divine fear and reverence, and to answer with understanding is proper for a wise listener while announcing the song with the dance and the divine chorale of the psalm.

'I have cried to You not only by day but also by night' (Ps 87:2,3), not occurring in solitude among the bright and pleasant things of life (it is impossible to be so by day), but also having been in the gloomy ones, containing a nocturnal state; having cried out in the day, so that the participation in the good things might remain for me, and in the night, so that when its end is coming out of the night, I might be able to rouse my spirit toward You. And it is possible to say more simply, similarly to what was said by the Savior: 'The Father will avenge His children who cry to Him day and night' (Luke 18:7). For he who meditates on the law of the Lord day and night and through it...

With works and disposition, he cries out to the God of his salvation day and night, at times asking for salvation, at others entreating that it might be preserved, which already exists. And the voice saying, 'Let my prayer enter before you' (Ps 88:4), speaks with much boldness toward God. For I ask such things as are profitable for me and appropriate for you and good to give (for I ask for the truly good things); let our prayer become in your hearing; for in this way you will also grant the responses I have requested, descending and inclining toward my cry; for in this way I have believed to be heard; therefore, O Lord, I cry out to you.

For many are the enemies lying in wait to tear my life into the pit (Ps 88:4), by whom my soul has been filled with despondency and evil struggles, that is, the indulgence of evil circumstances. The Holy Scripture calls the same place both the pit and the grave (Ps 88:5). The Savior himself, having become not [a sinner], came for the salvation of those being slain to give a ransom, by the grace of God, having tasted death above all. For he alone died on behalf of all, and in this way he was counted among those descending into the pit.

For as each one rightly descends into the pit because of what he has done or thought, I was counted and numbered with them; not being led to this by the works of following, but by the Father's good pleasure and our will to be counted among those descending into the pit and being judged; not that I became arbitrarily and voluntarily as a helpless man, the likeness of which is not being raised to the man. 'Depart'; for he has become a man according to truth, and he says that to be like a man is not simply to be a man, but a helpless man. For being able not to suffer, not to be seized, and not to be bound, he gave himself, becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.

But even if he has become a helpless man voluntarily, as also to be cast into death, yet he is free among the dead. For among all those departing to the place of the dead, being led by some, not only the wicked but also the distinguished, Jesus alone has been emboldened to say, 'No one takes my soul from me; I lay it down from myself, so that I may take it again' (John 10:18). But what [is] the soul of all [those] by some into...

english: It will be clear to one who has studied the Gospels. For concerning Lazarus, a distinguished man, it is said: 'And it came to pass that the poor man died and was carried to the bosom of Abraham' (Luke 16:22); and toward something trivial he says, 'In this night they demand your soul from you'; and toward another face he says, 'Until you are brought down.' For the one being brought down by others is brought down there.

Therefore, no one among the dead is free, whether they are those being pulled toward others or those being led to the place of the dead; but Jesus alone, having placed his soul by himself, receiving it from no one, has become free among the dead. And why? Because although all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God (Romans 3:23), being delivered from life with bonds, having difference in what is more and what is less having occurred in Hades, he alone, not having committed sin and not having known sin, has become free among the dead, as also to loose the bonds of death of the other dead in order to raise and vivify them.

For just as he alone on earth is the liberator of sins being given as a gift, he says, 'If the Son sets you free, you will be truly free' (John 8:36); so also, having become in Hades with freedom, he liberated the held souls, making fear work in those holding them; for even the gatekeepers of those places flew away, having seen his authority and his freedom. It follows then that you should interpret the following verses as having been spoken by Christ.

The Savior therefore says to his own Father: 'Even if I have come to be a Savior of the world, having come to seek and to save the lost, being made worthy of eternal salvation for all, but rather, O Father, you are the God of this salvation which I provide for the being saved; for I grant it by your will; therefore, becoming a Paraclete toward you on behalf of those who have sinned, I will save them, interceding for them.' Following this, you will understand the following, as previously foretold.
The Savior says: 'For no one will be able to snatch him who is guarded by the mighty hand of God' (Ps 87:6bc); for he is contained by God, invincible to those desiring to attack and snatch him.
He remains. But someone having become worthless through whom sin occurs, is unworthy to be made a part of the hand, and is cast away, no longer worthy to be held and remembered by God.

Since he says, 'Because I did not come into Hades and death according to my own work, but having tasted death on behalf of others, I bring the cause of falling into the lowest pit and into the very heart of the earth' (Ps 87:7) instead of 'You made me to go into the lowest parts of the pit,' just as having resurrected those in the depth of this, he leads them away from there to bring them into the paradise of God. 'You laid me in the dark and in the shadows of death' (Ps 87:7). For if he says he has become victorious even in death, it is not in death strictly speaking, but in its shadow (for he reached [the third day] having risen), and in the same way, having placed them in the darkness under them, he turned them away, so that they might no longer live in darkness but in me, the light.

The wrath of God is like fire, which takes sin as food (Ps 87:8). Because of these things he underwent, and he himself acts; and as they are being consumed, he also approaches (Ps 87:10a). When many human abominations were occurring, the wrath of God was being carried against them, but the benefactor Savior submitted himself to the wrath of God, so that he might be fixed upon it, no longer moving or acting to find fuel, and so that God might be extinguished, not having been fed by him; because he was not known to sin, having been tested in all things without sin.

And he brought upon himself all those wavering temptations and tribulations, so that having struggled and having been tested in all things, he might be shown proven, so that we are no longer subject to wavering. For he dispelled them; and it is said of God, 'They are not for you,' because they are brought upon them for His judgment. Those of the circumcision who knew him and were known by him were fortunate, but those who responded to the law and the prophets had become far from him, having turned away and having been shown to be traitors, having been cast out from the Father and having been made far from His own Son, whose hand exists from which...

english: He drove them away according to the [psalm]: 'They drove You from my hand' (Ps 52:11). And he says that the pretext for them being distanced from Him is that they made an abomination for themselves. For the Jews, having become sinners, considered piety to be an abomination; for piety is an abomination to a sinner. Therefore, they also made the mystery-initiating abomination of this [piety] an abomination to themselves, not being of such a kind.

'I was handed over and was not delivered away.' For the Savior was not immediately handed over by them unto death and departed, leaving them nothing remaining to them in the providing of a way for repentance. For it was necessary for them to be perceptive, just as His eyes are said to be, and they grew weak as if to see Him no longer. Because of this he says, 'My eyes have grown weak from poverty' (Ps 102:3). For the cause of the weakness is that spiritual poverty has come upon them, for they desired the flesh and, taking everything written according to the letter, they grasp it.

How then can His eyes, the perceptive ones of Israel, be able? It will be clear to you once you have understood: 'You are the body of Christ and members in part' (1 Cor 12:27). For just as those who believed according to the Gospel fulfill the body of Christ—just as the perceptive ones are the eyes, and the understanding ones are the hearers, while the practical ones are called the hands—so also, before the manifestation, those holding to the Scriptures were the body of the Word of God according to the stated analogy.

[Psalm 87:11-13] 'Can a voice be read thus: Will you not do wonders for the unfeeling ones, and will you not perform wonders for the dead who have lost the power to grasp?' For these things happen similarly to those who perceive and are able to marvel, not to those who fight against God, the impious, and because of this they remain unrepentant. For no one will pray for them.

'There shall be a resurrection upon your confession.' For those who happen to be God-fighters are not of a nature to confess. And regarding 'resurrection' here, he is not speaking of the most common sense (for all shall partake of this), but of the one occurring through repentance, as it is said: 'Does not he who falls not rise again?' (Luke 15:18). It is possible to decide: 'Will you not do wonders for the dead?' Only, he is not saying, 'Will you not do wonders for those who have been deadened by other gods,' since even those who become gods by fighting against God will not rise upon the...

To confess. For no one says that to those who have despaired and to those hidden in tombs, the announced mercy of you will be recounted to the living who desire to be shown mercy, but nor will your truth be [recounted] to those who are making a work of perishing and because of this are named perishing. For the Word recounts the mercy to those whose nature is to be shown mercy (for they are not those who show mercy to neighbors; for they say, 'Blessed are the merciful, for they shall be shown mercy'), but also the truth is not recounted in perishing, but to those who have passed over it and have reached salvation. The wonderful things are not to be known in darkness. Those held by superfluous wickedness and ignorance are darkness. For darkness is said of some, but also a land forgotten and a heart unremembered, being filled with thorns of pleasures and worldly cares. The wonderful things of the truth are not to be known in this, nor is practical justice and moral virtue in the land forgotten because of the thorns.

It is fitting for Jesus to speak with boldness, 'Why, Lord, have you rejected my prayer?' (Ps 87:15), for it is not that you have rejected my prayer and turned your face away from me because I have sinned at all; therefore, having received my petition, lead all into salvation, for whom I intercede, shining upon them with your face. When the rich one, who labored for us, became poor for our sake, toiling for our salvation, the text says, not saying at all that he is poor, but from youth. english: Regarding all sin into his own body, all impulses according to various sins and his terrors passed over him as to disturb him, but they are not able to work against him, since he has not known or experienced sin. And it is said that the impulses and terrors of God, which are powers serving through punishments, turn out to be vessels of wrath.

These, having passed over the Savior, disturbed him, saying, 'Now my soul is troubled' (Ps 69:1). For even if he possesses a most perfect soul, yet seeing such a multitude of enemies, he experiences a fore-passion, especially since the water of the day surrounded him all at once, rushing against him and drowning him, if he had not been an excellent diver. For just as perceptible water surrounding someone drowns him, especially if he does not know how to swim, so the evil powers kill the one crushed by them.

But if they have become as water around Jesus, surrounding him all at once during the day, they are not even able to harm him; for much water will not quench the love (Song 8:7). For the perfection which is placed toward God through love is unquenchable. And this existed according to the human nature of Jesus, so that the shield of the hands cannot harm him.

And thus Eusebius of Caesarea, Didymus, and Apollinaris explained. It is said many times that the generation is carried in two ways. It signifies the people from the circumcision and the Gentiles. And it gives the reason for which the mercies of the Lord are for ever, having brought [them] in, that if all, mercy will be built up for ever. For the age which has come has not arrived, God clearly shows mercy and does good; and by this he says mercy is built up for ever. For just as a building is composed of many and various things being fitted together, so a building of many being benefited by the mercy of God takes place. Perhaps mercy is being built up, the building of wisdom...
Having built for itself these things. For its humanization is the foundation and the end of the building of mercy, the removal of the pre-occupying sin of all those being shown mercy.

From these things follows: 'In the heavens your truth shall be prepared' (Ps 88:5). For since we, those on earth, are imagined to be able to perceive divine things not yet with a clear face, but through a mirror and in a riddle (1 Cor 13:12), in the heavens the truth of God is being prepared for those having been prepared from there as if they are about to face it. For then they face face to face the beauty of the truth, having seized the end of knowledge and understanding, the partial reaching of things having been abolished for them. And the truth of God is being prepared in those not thinking of earthly things but having their citizenship in the heavens, by wearing the image of the heavenly through which the heavens are used.

By this God gives to David his father the throne to reign over these people forever, Jacob, into the ages (Ps 88:4), as if there is no end to his kingdom. And so that no one might think that David attained this blessing by chance according to favoritism, God says, 'I have sworn to David my servant'; for since David has been proven a genuine servant and worshiper, I give to him a sign, that a virgin, chaste and untouched by man, shall give birth to the God who is with you among men. For this the voice of Emmanuel signifies; it is not the seed of David being prepared. And the 'I have sworn' spoken by God establishes the stability of the promise toward David. For just as an oath-taker keeps an inviolable intention, being pressed by the word of a binding agreement with God, so also God, regarding whom it is said He eternally and certainly grants by oath, does not act according to another. For He says, 'As for myself, I have sworn, says the Lord, not as to the unfaithful...'

english: He does not use mere words, but promises an unchangeable and unalterable will. Since his will regarding the man from David becoming his son is unalterable, it is fitting that the Lord said to my servant, 'You are my son' (Ps 88:7). No one of those born from God, having received the spirit of adoption, will be able to become like the Lord. For he alone, according to truth, is the offspring of God, while the others are called sons of God to partake in him.

For the sake of a perfect understanding of what is set forth, we shall use the apostolic voice, which sounds thus: 'Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ' (2 Cor 13:14). For having called God Father of himself and of those near him, he was reverent, not assigning to himself an equality with any glory to the only-begotten Son; therefore he added, 'And the Lord Jesus Christ,' having cried out only once: 'if indeed we have become sons by the grace of God, and he himself becomes our Father, yet also we are slaves of Jesus Christ according to the nature of our Lord who is' (Rom 8:17).

This very thought is confirmed by the set-forth word: 'For who shall be like the Lord among the sons of God?' (Exod 35:19). No one is, according to essence, a son of God, except the Savior alone, who is the only one consubstantial with the Father; but those who are not according to essence, but according to quality, shall be made like him, just as they become merciful like the Father and perfect as the Father becomes: 'You shall be holy, because I am holy' (Lev 11:44). For the Lord comes upon the clouds of heaven with much power and glory, and the saints shall be caught up in clouds to meet the Lord in the air, to be with him forever (1 Thess 4:17).

Therefore, of the Lord and the saints being in the clouds, no one of those caught up in clouds shall be equal to the one coming upon the clouds of heaven with much power and glory. For each one was caught up with power, but not with much glory. For that power and glory he possessed, but the Savior will come with much power and glory; and each of those was in a cloud, but not upon the clouds. The expression 'upon the clouds' establishes the authoritative and kingly, whence no one in clouds shall be equal to the Lord; for truly, the cloud of each of the saints, being spiritual, is the intelligible moisture (the clouds...

For he says, 'justice has overwhelmed' (Ps 88:8), no such clouds can be found equal to the Lord, who is also a cloud, since each of them only waters a little, but He waters not only all men but also all rational things.

He is also fearful to those who are opposed, threatening punishments and bringing them down against those who fall away from His divine commands. For you, being near Him in receiving His divine teaching, while sinning, are near the fire, as the words of the Savior say: 'He who is near me is near the fire, and he who is far from me is far from the kingdom.' Thus, in the present word, He is fearful to those around Him who, through having believed in Him, disobey His commandments; how great [is He] to those held by His virtue.

The truth about God is none other than the one saying, 'I am the truth' (John 14:6). If it is around God, it can never not be, lest God should descend from not being once surrounded by truth to this. But it is surrounded by this, generating it, and He alone is the true God. For just as He alone is wise, not participating in wisdom but generating wisdom, so He alone is true and has truth around Him, not taking part in it but being with others and giving it to them.

For the Father exists with the Son in every thought and energy; for the Word, being with God, is God the Word, since the Father is in the Son and the Son is in the Father; for it is fitting for a God-Word to be with God the Father. But also as light, God has light with Him, the Son, as it is said in Daniel: 'And the light is with Him.' For it is not 'was' or 'will be' but 'is,' for this shows eternity, and thus it is said to be an emanation of eternal light. And the truth is said not to have 'become' or 'be going to be' around, but to 'be' of the almighty God. And the eternal power will be present to the almighty God, which exists the same as the wisdom, truth, light, and Word of God, but also 'your truth is around you.'

english: of its violence. And Jesus, demonstrating by word what kind of son he is of the master of the dominion of the sea, rebukes it while it is being agitated and stirring up a storm, and immediately calms it.

But if the sea's allegory signifies the life of men, its dominion may be the evil one in whom the whole world lies, that is, the mortal and perilous state. By this, the master of the sea, providing weakness to its dominion, grants authority to the travelers to suffer against all his power, calming the unstable and irregular surges of its waves, which are called upon it, making it also a firm footing for those receiving authority to walk upon it with Jesus, of whom Peter bears the image.

For no one, apart from Jesus, is able to suffer the sea of life, becoming subject to anxieties and pleasant passions, unless he walks along with Jesus. For he is the one walking as if on dry land upon the sea, as it was said to him: 'Your ways, O God, are in the sea, and your paths in many waters' (Ps 88:12-13). For Jesus has trodden paths in the strong waters; the passions are also life-related anxieties that those following his tracks are able to mount.

Regarding the thought, all those interpreting confess his wonders, and the earth receiving Jesus, being a seed and bearing fruit, becomes his property, reaching one hundred and sixty and thirty. And he established the inhabited world upon its fullness, being no other than the church, in which souls dwell having adhered to the right reason and the truth. But sacred powers also dwell in it, intervening around those fearing him.

And the foundation upon which it was established is not other than that about which Paul writes, for no one else is able to lay a foundation other than the one laid, which is Jesus Christ. And the fullness of this spiritual inhabited world, being founded upon the same foundation, is the fullness of virtues and of the dogmas of piety, along with the divine gifts of the Spirit.
And the Lord created the north and the seas, so that they are no longer as they were before. For just as having created the two into one, a new man from the two, he has...

It has been struck, and the being-created heart is pure, from which it has become pure; and he creates also those outside of faith, so that in Christ they might become a new creation—not by creating the north wind and the seas. But everyone who obtains divine election and is suspended by light, having been enlightened, rejoices in the name of God with a light of knowledge.

Just as Tabor is indeed outside, but Hermonius is a suspension of light; for the Hebrew names of the mountains are taken toward these things. And if Tabor is also interpreted as a pit (for it does not carry the sense), you will understand how it is said 'a praiseworthy pit', having understood how God gives to some in a manner of blessing pits that have been dug; those who have dug them did not dig them out. And if the pit were spoken of in mockery, having changed the voice, it would not be named thus, as one should not enrich wells; the spring will rejoice upon the name of the Lord (Ps 88:14-15).

The poetic power of God (but this is His creative power, His only-begotten Son) is signified to all those who are within by name. For 'arms' is said in the [Psalms]: 'And the arm of the Lord, to whom was it revealed? And your arm, O Most High, and you shall not be afraid.' But also the 'hand of the Lord' is confessed in: 'My high hand has done all these things'; and 'right hand' in: 'Exalt me with the right hand of the Lord.' For the holy one says to God: 'Yours is the arm with might, reigning and holding all things.' And it also says: 'Let your hand be strengthened, performing wonders and accomplishing great powers.'

For Peter says to God: 'Grant to your servants to speak your word with boldness, stretching out your hand for signs and wonders' (Acts 4:29). In thought, the power of the Father is not different; Christ is called these things. For if He is the Son of God and Wisdom and the Word of God and Truth, He is the right hand being lifted up by God, suspending and lifting up all, and He goes forth before your presence as mercy and truth; for no one who is to approach your face has been previously pitied and has conversed with the truth. It is possible, then, as in other places and here, that mercy and truth are not other than the Only-begotten, as in 'God sent forth His mercy and His truth.' It is not other than the Only-begotten Son of God, who is the same.

If we effect power, then our horn shall be exalted in your good pleasure. For our horn was exalted by the good pleasure of God, who says, 'This is my beloved Son in whom I have been well pleased' (Matt 3:17). For He was well pleased to effect our salvation through His own Son. And because of this, he says, our horn was exalted in the good pleasure of God, since the perception of the Lord is that by which He perceives, fighting and defending those who receive this grace from Him.

And this perception belongs to the holy Israel, our king. For the king of the true Israel, seeing God, is a son; the same perception is not of the Lord. The same perception of the Lord can be as being worked by Him, and of the holy Israel as enduring it. And a holy Israel in these things is one who is sanctified in the mind to see Him. And our King, being restored by the Lord who transcends, what is the perception of our Lord the King and of the holy Israel? (Ps 88:20–23).

He who perceives a spoken word, if he only senses it, it is through hearing, if he hears the one speaking; but if he understands the things being announced, he does not perceive by hearing, but by vision of the mind he perceives the speech of the one offering it. Since God was showing things rather than merely announcing them, He speaks to His sons who are being enriched through progress and perfection, not in hearing but in vision. So also it has been written concerning Israel: 'And the people saw the voice of the Lord' (Exod 15:2). It is necessary to say, 'Heard the voice of the Lord,' but if it is said instead 'Saw the voice,' that is to say, he perceived it with the mind.

The prophets were seers of visions; for they did not say they were perceiving by sensing some things or by grasping them with the eyes, but they were striking with the mind at the beauty of intelligible things. 'You spoke in vision to your sons': 'I made help as far as possible,' saying this regarding the Savior who has come from the root of Jesse. For truly in this He set help to help all creation that is able. And the one on whom He set help is the chosen one from the people, exalted not according to divinity but according to the flesh. For concerning him it is also, 'Israel is my chosen one,' and the [people] received him...

english: My soul. For he was chosen from myriads, as in the selection of the elect. And because of this the Father exalted him, granting to him the name which is above every name. 'I have found David my servant' (Ps 89:20); and since the one according to the flesh is of the seed of David, it is possible and sufficient for him to be held by the hand over all the rational creation so that he might teach me in this way; therefore he anointed him with holy oil, proving him priest and king in all things (In holy oil, by the Holy Spirit, clearly meaning anointed, as it is said: 'God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness among your companions' [Ps 45:7]), because my hand shall take hold of him, his arm being strong.

And the arm and hand of God, the divinity of the Only-begotten; and it takes hold of him, performing strange and great works through him. An enemy will not benefit in him; instead of the devil (for he does not know sin, nor is there deceit in his mouth), thinking he can benefit, while he is able to instill deception and other wickedness. But no son of lawlessness, having come to break the law, will be able to harm him by surrounding him with sin. But the benefiting against the enemy lies strictly in overcoming. And in the Gospel, indeed, the deliberating chief priests and Pharisees against Jesus, not overcoming in his gathering, said to one another, 'See, you benefit nothing'; and the whole world went after him (Matt 22:37)—so that they would not overcome at all.

These things, Didymus says, clearly dividing the one Christ, even if in some way he turned away his manifest slanders. For he clearly presents two persons and two sons, and leads toward this kind of life a doctrine; therefore it seems to me that the interpretation of the one before him is more preferable to those wishing to think devoutly. And Eusebius, through similar things to Didymus, almost brings forward recollections in which he selects: 'The one of the prophets etc.'

He says of David, because the one according to the flesh is of the seed of David, it is possible and sufficient for him to be of hand; for this reason the voice of David is taken up. He found and with holy oil anointed him, since my hand shall take hold of him, strengthening him by my arm (Ps 88:27). And the arm and hand of God, the Son of God, has been said. For he overcomes the man, taking hold of him, the one born from the virgin. And the hand overcomes him and takes hold, performing extraordinary works through him. And the enemy will not profit; the devil is in the man who is the Lord's; for he did not know sin, nor was there deceit in his mouth.

He himself (clearly the one anointed with holy oil) will call upon me; 'You are my Father, God,' he says (Ps 88:28). For since having been born from the virgin he has been called the Son of God, he will call upon me, saying 'You are my Father,' the only-begotten Son of God (for he is Son according to essence), but not only calling but confessing God as Father. And he took upon himself man, and was called the Son of God, and calls God his Father and the supporter of his salvation; for he raised him and into the heavens he took him up. And he has become a supporter also of his own salvation, not that he himself is saved, but that he saves those fleeing to him. And having thus called upon the Father, the cause of all, the Father himself sets him as firstborn, bearing the first things of all those who have been called sons of God, not in the same way as he was raised up with the only-begotten; for he alone is the genuine instrument and temple of the God Word.

But do not let him fail you, thinking until then that the throne of Christ will be extended until the fullness of this; for heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away (Ps 88:30). english: His throne lasts until the passing of the heavens, but like the days of heaven; for after the passing, heaven is. It is not possible for its passing to be perishable. And the bright and combatable things can be days of the earth, but the bright and light-like mysteries of truth are days of heaven; likewise, the throne of the Savior, having been placed unshakable, remains forever.

In this, God steadfastly promises by swearing, upon which He has spoken and enters into (Ps 88:36–38). Since He does not change His mind after swearing, giving an unpassable priesthood according to the order of Melchizedek, He remains constant; and having promised to Abraham with an oath that in his seed all the nations of the earth would be blessed, He shows the immovability of the blessing. If indeed He gives something by chance, He does not swear upon it; for indeed, having handed the kingdom to Saul without an oath, He did not change His mind. Since He also willed that the Savior be born from David according to the flesh, and that his seed, having come from David, be unpassable and steadfast, He was faithful to Him regarding the making of the unshakable promises. Therefore, O Moses, David [says]: 'In my holiness, not lying, upon which I promised, his seed remains for ever, sharing the throne of his beginning with the Sun of Righteousness.' And the moon remains most fully illuminated as the gathering of those being enlightened by Christ for ever, when the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the righteous shall shine forth like the sun in the kingdom of their Father (Ps 88:39–46). And a faithful witness concerning this being so in the heavens exists; concerning Job he says, 'Behold, in the heavens is my witness and my supporter in the highest' (Job 16:19).

But Didymus did not give the intellect in the same way as the interpretation of Eusebius: 'You, O Lord, having said the seed of Christ remains for ever, have cast away his seed.' Having rendered him powerless, taking up the Christ, who, having been anointed with holy oil, remains for ever and ever, those descending from him shall be shown mercy. Having overthrown the covenant of your servant, having cast up the Christ, though having said you would not profane your covenant with him.

And having defiled even his sanctuary into the earth, indeed his body is given unto death and a memory, while the church, being near, and his sanctuary having been defiled into that earth in the times during which you permitted or continued persecutions to be accomplished for the sake of the godless.

But Christ, the servant of God, is found having taken the form of a servant, becoming according to what was said to the angel, 'Behold the handmaid of the Lord, let it be to me according to your word' (Luke 1:38). And you demolished all his enclosures from his sons, every most fortified help, so that those attempting to plot against them might be able to act against them. For enclosures, according to the Scripture, are diversely becoming guards from God; and it is possible to call the apostles the enclosures of the Christ's vineyard, whom those seeing them scattered say are being removed by God, having been scandalized in the night of the betrayal of Jesus (Matt 26:56). You reproached his strongholds with cowardice. It has been said that the true disciples of Christ are his strongholds, having been placed in cowardice at the time of the betrayal of Jesus.

It followed that Christ was snatched away by those pursuing or departing from the way. But Christ, being snatched away, is not another from those snatching away his body; for you are the body of Christ and members in part (1 Cor 12:27). And it is possible also to call the strongholds of his church according to various local dwellings his strongholds.

To this also you reproach him toward those called his neighbors because of being toward him and around him. For those who seem to be gathered as neighbors of him through a pseudonymous knowledge, thinking that they contain his Scripture and are near his church, are those through whom they think and act badly, reproaching him. For just as he who works rightly and praises rightly according to the truth glorifies him from the opposite, so those who are disposed oppositely to the right ones reproach him. Because of these things, you reproached him on the right side of his enemies; for they exult as if they had overcome by their own power, and having done so, you abandoned him. english: The sword of his help; for it is carried on both sides. For having gone to war against Christ, his enemies, and hating him, they did not stand against him in the war, as if they had decided to lead him away to be crucified and to bring all other things against him insultingly.

These things will cease from saying, those who have desire toward Christ and having rightly received the providence, not seeing the intention according to which the Father, not sparing his own Son, delivered him to those standing and gathered against him, having learned the salvation having been made straight through his death, not only of the Father having delivered him on behalf of us but also of himself having delivered himself unto this; for he gave his soul a ransom for many.

Having abolished [the debt] from his cleansing, and the following things as of the psalm. Thinking that he had departed from the things promised to him, and they say these things. For they supposed him to be abolished from the cleansing, [thinking] he did not work through his blood; upon which they think also that his throne has been broken down to the earth, the days of his throne having been diminished.

But nothing of this sort will happen concerning his throne, since God has established him as the days of heaven, not as the things that are earthly. But also God remains in opposition to himself if the throne of Christ is as the sun and the completed moon for the age. For having seen him having been crucified and having suffered, they saw him having received the kingdom at the end, his throne having been diminished and overturned, and having taken upon himself the shame upon the cross, concerning which the apostle says: He endured the cross, despising the shame, instead of the joy set before him, having risen from the dead, no longer being abolished by the cleansing but perfecting and working, him removing the sin of the world, according to the said thing: having made a cleansing of sins, he sat at the right hand of majesty in the high places, being raised up and having firmly established the throne, remaining for a long time and an eternal age (Ps 88:47-48a).

Remember, we who are saying these things, what the substance is. For we are unstable and changeable being autonomous; therefore also we fear lest we be drawn into impiety. O God, looking quickly upon your mercy...

For the expressed anger is not of such a nature as to be merely extinguished. The term 'hypostasis' may not signify the essence, as we have interpreted, but rather that which one is able to sustain according to the underlying state.

Since 'who' signifies many things, let us observe what is meant by the various uses of 'Who is man?'. For 'who' sometimes signifies a person, as in 'Who shall ascend the hill of the Lord, and who shall stand in his holy place?' (Ps 24:3). It also denotes the rare or exceptional, as in 'Who is the faithful and prudent servant?' and 'Who is wise and understands these things?' and 'Who is discerning and will know these?'. The word is even applied to the incapable in 'Who knows the Lord?' and 'Who became his counselor?' and 'Who gathered the winds in his bosom?' and 'Who turned the water into a garment?'. The word is also applied to the insignificant, as if he were no one, in 'If God is for us, who is against us?' (Rom 8:31) and 'Behold, the Lord helps me; who will harm me?' (Ps 118:7). It is also applied to one called by a specific name by some, but by others as an individual or a single unit, as in 'a certain noble man'.

Here it is possible to grasp the upcoming passage regarding 'no one': 'For who is the man that shall live and not see death?' (Ps 39:5) instead of 'No one'. And if the discourse is about common death, no one truly lives and does not see death, according to what is said, 'For death passed upon all men, of whom all sinned' (Rom 5:12), and 'For it is appointed unto men once to die' (Heb 9:27). For 'who' is equivalent to 'all men'. No one is a man, since every man is a mortal creature, and every man having fallen from divinity, as in 'You die as men' and 'Wherefore your wrath and indignation, are ye not as men and walk after the manner of men?'. For none of such people have become unhistorical regarding death by sinning; therefore it is said, 'Who is the man that shall live?'. For such a thing is a god, among those called gods through participation in divinity. For they alone shall not see death, since they live by transforming into eternal life; a life which Hades shall not be able to consume or hold, as God saves such people from the hand of Hades.

english: He says that those seated with the apostles, the earth being shaped to be a soul capable of bearing fruit, and the inhabited world in which angels dwell, and the dogmas of truth and the gifts of the Spirit, will speak before all these, just as to the prophets God has become a refuge from generation to generation. And the phrase 'And from the age and as of the age you are' signifies the movement of God from infinity to infinity. For you are the same one remaining forever, not one in one age and another in another age; for you are the same one, unchangeable and immutable, from infinity to infinity.

Having raised man from things of lowliness and debasement to height, guarding him in that suspension and height, do not turn him back to become such as the low things (Ps 89:3). Place our iniquities before you, to punish us for them, as all our age—and time is that which extends our day with bodily life—is manifest and enlightened to you, not only of every transgression in practice but also of that which is manifest and enlightened to you in thoughts (Ps 89:8).

The coming prayer of those standing by is: what God has in his right hand, and to see it, what they are doing (Ps 89:12-17). As those standing say: O Lord God, reveal the providence of the world which you created through your right hand, so that we may grasp not how it does and works through it, but let us know it as it approaches us. The petition of those calling upon the presence of Christ is able, for He himself is the right hand of God. For then the right hand of God became known, who is the Word having become flesh who dwelt among us; for we beheld his glory as of the only-begotten from the Father. And having known the right hand of God, let us know with it those who have been instructed in wisdom in the heart, who are not merely those who claim to be. But we speak of Wisdom in the perfect ones. It is possible even for the prophets to be known as those having been instructed in wisdom in the heart, for whom the brightness of Christ has been revealed. For then the prophets, truly proclaiming beforehand concerning him, were shown to be perhaps able.
Before their prophecies were fulfilled. For their words have reached an outcome through the revealed right hand of God, and they have become manifest as if they were instructed by the wisdom of God.

But the heart is instructed in wisdom by one who has made the mind and the ruling principle wise, as the speaker himself contends in ten thousand ways as if to say they are speaking truly: 'Even if [he is] an unlearned man in speech, yet not in knowledge.' And it is also said, 'Those laid low in heart by wisdom.' For the thought and the memory are laid low from the plains of the wisdom of the wise and the pious one imposing [it] upon things; and it is said concerning the plains of wisdom, that we protect the feet of the soul by stepping into them.

'Turn back, O Lord; how long will you turn your face and your right hand away from us?' (Ps 30:16). For you do this to us for only a little while, yet a long time appears to those exhausted by the longing. Having been discouraged among your servants, turn back to us, having become distant and having turned away from your commands.

'We have been filled in the morning with your mercy' (Ps 89:13). For your right hand, which we were worthy to be made known, having shone upon us, prepared the beginning of a spiritual day, like the sun of righteousness (Mal 4:2). In the beginning, occurring in the morning, we were filled with the mercy from you, as your true light enlightened us in all those days so that we might rejoice and be glad (Ps 119:130). It is not something entering into our minds in the morning that is poetic.

But since it rises to us not in one way but diversely according to various actions and thoughts, we come to be [filled] in many days; in all those [days] let us rejoice and be glad, so much as to be able to loose the dark and evil exterior of the days, in which you humbled us by captivity and delivered us to enemies through ignorance and malice. english: [Guide] your servants and the works of your hands, and those born to us through teaching and the imitation of virtue, being pure and well-tuned, onto the path of salvation. For so shall your brightness as God shine upon us, as the sun in your kingdom. Therefore we pray, direct the works of our hands upon us. But those who are bold are those who spread snares and lie in wait, not wanting the works of his hands to be directed toward the evil, but rather to be surrendered to oblivion.

Hunters are in these things, and deceivers and sophists, men attempting to trap people, so that they might go through wisdom into false doctrines. Therefore, he who interprets their trap is a confused speaker; for nothing stirs up and agitates the mind like an argumentative speech. The evil powers are also hunting through a snare, catching souls through harmful desires and other passions; for he says, 'The eye of a prostitute is a snare to the sinner,' and 'For a woman hunts the precious souls of men.' And they hunt through wealth and through those nearby. But the leader of these hunters is the devil, who himself is a snare. It is said concerning someone, 'Lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.'

This is in accord with the song of Deuteronomy regarding God: 'As an eagle will cover his nest and upon his young ones he has hovered, spreading his wings he received them and carried them upon his feathers.' All those who, through endurance and the other strength of approaching virtue, soar like eagles, are high-flying, being suspended by the wings of understanding and practical virtue. It is from God that they have come to possess such things; therefore they also are his young ones, as it is said in the prophet, 'But those who wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength.'

They shall grow wings like eagles, running and not growing weary. God will cover those who have grown wings like eagles with the young ones of an eagle; for as an eagle covers its young, so God, having desired his young ones, takes them upon his wings to cover them.

And in the present saying, regarding the one dwelling in the help of the Most High, it is said how God takes him up upon his wings to hope and expect good things happening in the wings of God. But it is said: what are the wings of God, and how does one hope, being shaded by them? For it is written: 'In the shadow of your wings I hope' (Ps 90:4c–6).

The defender God, as a shield, and with the side of his truth surrounds all the one guarded by him, so that he may remain unhurt by all those plotting to cast him down, and especially by the one sending out burning arrows. But the one surrounded by the truth of God, having put on the armor of God and having taken up in all things the shield of faith, will not fear even if it becomes night, being illuminated by the circling truth and light that reaches him.

For if ever someone, even having become in ignorance, should seem to be in a nightly state, he will not fear, possessing the light which is the cause of knowledge, which is the same as the truth. And even if night is the harmful and dark things of life, he does not fear even having become in this night, being able to say: 'The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?' (Ps 27:1). For honoring God and therefore being strong, he fears no one except him, having learned: 'Honor God and you shall be strong, but fear no other.' Just as the one in the night does not fear, because he has light and there are those watching the night, so also the one having the one who said: 'Do not fear, for I am with you,' will fear nothing of the aforementioned nightly things.

english: Only those who fear, sleeping and drinking in the night, are [affected]; but the one surrounded by the truth of God is not struck by a flying arrow in the daytime. A heterodox word promises a flying arrow in the daytime.
But he who uses the truth does not fear being led astray by a deed in the darkness. A deed led astray in the darkness is every sin and every ignorance and the working of those evil spirits of error.

Along with these, he will not fear any accident, bearing all things tangibly and bravely, saying the same thing to Job: 'If we have received the good things from the hand of the Lord, shall we not receive the bad?' (Job 2:10). As it seemed good to the Lord, so it happened. For everything brought by the Lord is received as good, knowing that to those who love the Lord all things work together for good (Romans 8:28), even the painful and distressing things brought by temptation.

Therefore, it happens to conquer and to turn against them. For blessed is the man who endures temptation (James 1:12), who having been proved, shall receive the crown of life. He who is found in so many uprightnesses does not even fear the devil transforming himself into an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14). A midday demon is promised a full-strength light through philosophy and empty deception; this very thing is entirely a midday demon.

Not he alone, but also his servants, transforming themselves into servants of righteousness, are midday demons. But even if each one pretends to be such a midday demon, those who pretend will not remain, when the light of the ungodly is extinguished, when Christ has come to enlighten the hidden things of darkness and to reveal the counsels of the hearts (Ps 90:7–9).

He who is upright in practical matters and in the knowledge of the truth holds many who attack treacherously in his hands, but he surrounds all of them, having put on the armor of God. Since fewer attack the moral matters on the left, while many are on the right regarding the spiritual, thousands fall from the bench of the perfect, ten thousands falling from his right. The bench, being said in opposition to the right, implies the notion of the left and the ill-named. Similar to these is also in Deuteronomy...

It is called rightly regarding those who uphold the law: 'If he will pursue a thousand, two thousand shall flee before him' (Ps 64:7). And Paul, not having been perfected, fights against the adversaries through the ships of righteousness of the right and the left, [predicting] a thousand falling from his left and ten thousand from his right.

And in Ecclesiastes, in praise of the right, it is said thus: 'The heart of the wise is at his right hand, but the heart of a fool is at his left' (Eccl 7:4). The wise man, having his mind upon the intelligible and spiritual things, is called right because the precious things are on the right; but he who lacks understanding regarding sensible and material things is second and on the left.

And the falling thousand and ten thousand do not approach the righteous to harm him; for it is written, 'They shall not approach you' (Ps 91:7). For when the zealous one intends to approach, the phalanx of the adversaries falls. For [it is said], 'As they approach to devour my flesh, those who afflict me and my enemies themselves have stumbled and fallen' (Ps 27:2).

These things are fulfilled symbolically in the Gospels; for how closely did those who had come to seize Him dare to approach Jesus, when He said, 'Whom are you seeking?' and they answered, 'Jesus of Nazareth,' and He, Jesus, said, 'I am,' and they went backward and fell to the ground (John 18:4-6).

Besides these things being fulfilled (I am indeed saying regarding the falling thousand and ten thousand of the enemies not approaching the righteous), he will understand with the eyes of his mind, being guarded by that which has been made upright for him by the truth, the things that have been made upright for him, and he will see also the retribution of sinners; having said these things about them, he immediately confesses Him, the Cause of all existing goods. Because of this he says: 'O Lord, all these things have been made upright for me, since no one else but You have established my hope.' For if in the things above [it is said], 'God is my refuge and I hope in Him' (Ps 91:2), and 'Under the wings of God, you hope' (Ps 91:4).

He says 'Perceptions and thus'; since the circumstances of both the unrighteous and the righteous fall together in common, and [he is] named because of the things that have fallen upon him, the words set forth are not regarding these evils. For a bodily scourge has often struck the tent, that is, the body of the righteous; for 'we were being tested, we were being scourged,' says Paul (1 Cor 11:30). And the Savior Himself also...

english: He was scourged while being led to the cross, fulfilling what was foretold through the prophet about himself: 'I gave my back to lashes' (Ps 38:7).

Therefore, of the race of evils, the second kind—which applies indiscriminately to the excellent and the vile—does not approach the one who makes the Most High his refuge. For, clinging to Him and becoming a partaker of the good things, it is said: 'But for me, to cling to God is good.' For this good thing, possessing it, is a cessation from opposing evils, conquering evil through the good and thus doing the good. He who is fulfilled in goodness, in doing and working the good, is not a partaker of true evils.

But since the aforementioned evils do not approach the one who makes the Most High his refuge, neither does the scourge brought upon them approach his dwelling, since he is not a sinner; for only the sinner is scourged in this way. For many are the lashes of the sinner; and it has been said to us in other places that the same circumstances are lashes to the sinners, but contests to the righteous. Never do the burdensome and evil things come upon the pious as a scourge, but as a testing, just as it happened to Job, that the righteous might be revealed (Job 5:7). And also it is said: 'No evil shall come near you' (Ps 90:10). For the nature of wickedness comes from without, having the pretext of virtue; for God made man upright, who, having sought evil thoughts, drew wickedness from without.

These words, spoken as if concerning the Savior, the devil took, as it is carried in the Gospel; but the Psalm is said from the perspective of every righteous person being helped and covered by the Most High, being the God of heaven (Ps 90:11-12). And even if it is said concerning Christ, it is manifest that he is not God but is a man; for all things concerning him are announced to him as a man, and this will also apply to every holy person who imitates him and follows him. And these things [continue] until now.

Let us also see the intention of these words. God gives a command to his angels, that they may guard and protect the righteous, who are ministering spirits sent for service for those about to inherit salvation (Heb 1:14).

Do not worry, for angels intervene around those who fear Him, to rescue them from unseen enemies and foes. Indeed, do not worry, even Jacob the patriarch, when about to face greatest enemies, sees the intervention of God being fulfilled by angels fighting for him, and thus he thanks: 'For God is the one nourishing me from my youth, the angel who rescues me from all my evils.' Likewise also Elisha saw a multitude of angels surrounding him, seen by him, but not by his servant; thus he prays for the eyes of the child to be revealed to see what is greater than those fighting against them.

Having received a command from the Lord, the angels guard the diligent from all deeds and activities, and they lift him up so that his ways may not stumble on a stone (these are the angelic energies) so that the foot of his soul may not trip on a stone. For he who is carried by angels meets the blessing of that which is said: 'He shall not stumble at any stone' (Ps 90:13). For when the light of the true [one] has risen and the intelligent day has dawned, he who walks in this day will not stumble on what the light sees. But the stone upon which those not lifted up by angels stumble is foolishness and most hard sin. And they also stumble upon the cornerstone, an elect one, through unfaithfulness, as if it were a stone of stumbling to them.

Four signifies opposing powers, through the four names of the fallen and cast-out animals. And Paul, surpassing the struggle against flesh and blood, wages struggles against four opposing unseen powers: against principalities, against authorities, against the rulers of the darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil (Eph 6:12). And he who now praises excellence, riding on a shield and a basilisk, having received authority from Jesus to tread upon the lion and the scorpion (Luke 10:19); and trampling, he will also trample all the power of the enemy, the lion and the dragon. english: Revelation. Ps 90:14–16. Since he has set his love upon me, says the Lord, the one who has fled and hoped in me, the one who has said, 'But You, Lord, are my hope' (Ps 90:14)—I will rescue him from the falling of his perch, a thousand and ten thousand from his right side; but also I will cover him, the one having known my name, so that he might remain unharmed, mounting upon a shield and a small buckler, and having subdued the lion and the dragon, the knowledge of my name becoming a protection around him. Having cried out with the great voice of the soul toward me, he will find me hearing and answering him. For I am always present for him, even when he encounters distress; for I am with him in tribulation (especially then is it necessary to be with him, when the painful and distressing things are around us). Not only will I free him from the painful things, but I will also work by watching over him. And I will grant to him also eternal life, upon the long-lasting and long-enduring, the eternal light (for light is for the righteous always). And I will show him my salvation, the salvation from me, the Jesus who is the cause of this, just as the blessed Simeon, having seen, rejoiced saying, 'Now You release your servant, Lord, in peace, since my eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared in the presence of all peoples' (Luke 2:29-30). It is not to be thought that the psalm is spoken only concerning the Lord, as the Arian ones and Eusebius desire, but it is also concerning a righteous man and one having trusted in God, to see the best end of hope, Christ Jesus the salvation of God. And if the devil in the words toward the Lord said to him that the promise lies in the text, 'That he will command his angels concerning you' (Ps 91:11), as that man also conversed with the righteous, seeing clearly and excellently the [truth] in him, lest perhaps he be able to understand what is more than man and more excellent in Christ.

Ps 91:2,3. The one confessing and accusing himself toward the Lord, asking for forgiveness and remission, testing by experience the benefit from confessing, proclaims with his works the mercy of God, having been shown mercy upon those things for which he repented. And he proclaims the mercy of God having become upon him, having been enlightened and having become established at the beginning of the day by the sun of righteousness standing, he proclaims first of all.

If the blessing is that which is from God. And the singing in the name of the Lord the Most High is a premise of theology and theoria; the end has the truth which it is fitting to proclaim, not from the surface or from manifest things, but from deep and hidden things through an excess of knowledge. The obscurity which is named in such things is called night; for by nature the things said concerning the pious and the correct manifest the knowledge of many through the greatness of power. And night is that which is hard to grasp. And this night has a reference to the darkness which God has set as His own hiddenness. The morning proclaims the mercy of God and His truth according to the night (Ps 91:6,7).

And as much as the greatness of them appears to us, so much do I see the reflections concerning their God, which He has made and enlarged. To this is conjoined what is said by the Preacher: 'I said, I will be wise, but wisdom was removed from me; a great and deep depth, who will find it?' (Eccl 1:16). How its depth seems to have appeared incomprehensible to me. But having said 'Your reflections have become very heavy,' he gladdens the lovers of wisdom, saying that a man without understanding and without insight does not know and does not comprehend them, clearly showing that the wise man and the one having the Spirit of God investigates all things and comprehends the depths of God. And 'without understanding and without insight' he says, meaning being deprived of divine prudence and intelligence, though it may seem otherwise to be prudent and intelligent; just as, contrary to the idea in 188, the one having the wisdom of God is most without understanding, not at all, but in relation to the wisdom of men: 'For I am more foolish than all men, and the wisdom of men is not in me; but God has taught me wisdom.' Therefore, let the wise man in this age become a fool, as in relation to mortal wisdom (Ps 91:8–10).

On the day of judgment, of all men being humbled, from which they were exulting in pride over temporary things, the Lord alone is lifted up as King of all, being shown blameless of all and having provided for and arranged all things (Ps 91:10). And it is possible to grasp another thought in the things presented; for the sinners do not rise like the wheat, and iniquity and their hatred toward God are being worked out.

source_text: ἐπιτείνεται, ἀγνοεῖται τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ υ ψος καὶ μέγεθος, τυφλούσης τῆς κακίας τὸ ο μμα τοῦ νοῦ τὸ δυνάμενον προσβάλλειν τῷ κυρίῳ· ο ταν δὲ κατάλυσις τῆς ἁμαρτίας γένηται ὡς ἀπολέσθαι τοὺς διὰ τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν ἐχθροὺς γεγενημένους θεοῦ, ἀπόλλυσθαι δὲ ῃ τοιοῦτοί εἰσι, τὸ τηνικάδε ὁ θεὸς υ ψιστος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα εὑρεθήσεται τῷ καθαρθέντι νῷ. 912 Ps 91,11.12 Σύμμαχον πολλαχοῦ τὸ κέρας τῆς βασιλείας καὶ πρότερον ει πον. οὐ μόνον δὲ ὑψωθήσεται ὡς μονοκέρωτος τὸ κέρας μου ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ γῆράς μου ἐν ἐλαίῳ τῆς ἀγαλλιάσεως πιαινόμενον, γῆρας οὐ τὸ σωματικὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ παριστάμενον τὴν τελείαν τοῦ ε σω ἀνθρώπου ἡλικίαν, περὶ ου γέγραπται Γῆρας γὰρ τίμιον οὐ τὸ πολυχρόνιον οὐδὲ ἀριθμῷ ἐτῶν μεμέτρηται, πολιὰ δέ ἐστι φρόνησις ἀνθρώποις καὶ γῆρας βίος ἀκηλίδωτος. εἰς τοῦτο φθάσας ̓Αβραὰμ ει ρηται ἐν γήρει τετράφθαι καλῷ· γεγράπται γὰρ περὶ αὐτοῦ Καὶ ἐκλείπων ̓Αβραὰμ ἀπέθανε τραφεὶς ἐν γήρει καλῷ πρεσβύτερος καὶ πλήρης ἡμερῶν. περὶ δὲ τῆς σωματικῆς ἡλικίας, εἰ ἐλέγετο, ταῦτα μᾶλλον ει ρητο περὶ τῶν πρὸ τοῦ ̓Αβραὰμ πολυχρονιωτέρων γεγενημένων. Τοῦτ' ου ν τὸ ἑρμηνευθὲν γῆρας ἐλαίῳ πιαίνεται τετρυγωμένῳ ἐκ τῆς ἐλαίας ἐκείνης τῆς ἀληθινῆς τῆς ἐν τῷ οι κῳ τοῦ θεοῦ φασκούσης ̓Εγὼ δὲ ὡσεὶ ἐλαία κατάκαρπος ἐν τῷ οι κῳ τοῦ θεοῦ. τοῦτο τὸ ε λαιον οὐ μόνον πιαίνει τὸ τῆς γνώσεως φῶς, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἰᾶται καὶ πόνους λύει πιαῖνον τὸ προειρημένον γῆρας. Καὶ ἐπεῖδεν ὁ ὀφθαλμός μου ἐν τοῖς ἐχθροῖς μου, καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἐπανισταμένοις ἐπ' ἐμὲ πονηρευομένοις ἀκούσεται τὸ ου ς μου. τάχα τοὺς παρόντας ἐχθροὺς καταβεβλημένους ἐφορᾷ, ἀκούσεται δὲ τὸ ου ς αὐτοῦ περὶ τῶν μελλόντων αὐτῷ ἐπανίστασθαι. ὡς καὶ αὐτῶν η δη διαλυθέντων, ταῦτα δὲ πάντα περὶ πονηρῶν δυνάμεων ἐκληπτέον. κυρίως γὰρ αυ ται ἐχθραίνουσιν ἡμῖν. ̓Επεὶ δέ τινες κατεπιβαίνουσι τῆς γραφῆς ὡς παρέλκοντα καὶ μάταια ἐνίοτε λεγούσης, φέρε ἀπολογησώμεθα καὶ περὶ τῶν προκειμένων. φασὶ γάρ· Τίς οὐκ οι δεν ο τι ἐφορῶν
english: The height and greatness of God is overlooked when the eye of the mind, which is able to approach the Lord, is blinded by evil; and the destruction of sin occurs as if those who have become enemies of God through sinning were to perish, and to perish such are they, but the God who is the victor for all eternity will be found by the purified mind (Ps 91:11-12).

The horn of the kingdom is often an ally and previously was good. Not only shall my horn be exalted like a one-horned beast, but also my old age shall be anointed with the oil of gladness; old age not the bodily one, but the age presenting the perfection of the human soul, for it has been written: for old age is precious, not the long-lived, nor is it measured by number of years, but wisdom is a thing for men and an unblemished life is old age.

Having surpassed this, Abraham was said to be nourished in good old age; for it has been written about him: 'And Abraham died in a good old age, full of days, departing' (Gen 25:8). Regarding the bodily age, if it were said, these things are rather spoken of those who were longer-lived before Abraham.

This is interpreted as old age being anointed with oil, from that true olive tree speaking in the temple of God: 'I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God' (Ps 52:8). This olive tree not only anoints the light of knowledge, but also heals and looses pains, anointing the aforementioned old age.

And my eye has looked upon my enemies, and my ear shall hear of those rising up against me, committing iniquity (Ps 17:8). Perhaps the present enemies are cast down by sight, but his ear shall hear concerning those who are to rise up against him. Just as their strength is dissolved, all these things must be expected concerning evil powers. For strictly these are hating us.

And since some transgress the Scripture saying that it sometimes passes by and speaks in vain, let us bear it and let us defend the text also concerning the things set forth. For they say: 'Who does not see what is appearing...'
