english: For when anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; and in this Christ, the two—the one from circumcision and the one from the Gentiles—are being created into one new man. For the term 'creation' signifies not a change of substance but a change of form or a transformation. According to this, the meaning of 'O God, create in me a clean heart' (Ps 51:10) is expressed.

If this meaning applies to many things, then the Lord's saying 'I have created you as the beginning of his ways for his works' does not signify a change of substance for the person speaking; for he was not created from nothing, but as the beginning of God's ways for his works; and to be created as the beginning of these things denotes a relationship, not a change of substance. Thus, a people being created will praise the Lord, coming to the knowledge of the one God. Furthermore, the term 'being created' is used; for if he had intended a change of substance, the one being created would be called 'a people created'; for it is possible to always remain in the state of being transformed and changed rather than in the state of being a new substance.

The reason for the people being created and praising the Lord is presented in the fact that He descended from His holy height. Because He has taken the form of a servant and has descended to us even unto death, He descended from His holy height, never ceasing to be holy or to be high (Ps 101:20b, 21). Incorporeal and spiritual essence, rather, is how the Lord exists; He is not in a place, for the incorporeal is not limited by place, being uncircumscribable and beyond boundaries. Since He has become accustomed by power to all that comes from Him and is governed by Him (for He was in the world, and the world came through Him), He works within the better and more excellent parts of the world.

If it is said according to 'He who dwells in the heavens' (Ps 103:20) and 'Our Father who is in heaven' (Matt 6:9), we do not consider Him as being contained by places, but we set forth that He exists by an unutterable power toward His own works; therefore, it is said that He is in the heavens, which are the different parts of the world. For indeed, the thought of all things holds this kind of concept. Since God, not being in heaven in the manner spoken of, looks down upon the earth because of those having been made to be provided for by Him here, it is most correctly said, 'The Lord looked down from heaven upon the earth' (Ps 113:6). And the pretext through which the Word does this is...

He immediately brought forward, saying, 'Of those who hear the groans of the bound.' For those bearing the bonds and the shackles of wickedness groan out of repentance. For one used to doing evil with pleasure, he took it lightly and willingly bore the consequences following it; but others have withdrawn from the acts of wickedness, being weighed down by the hand of that evil, having been bound by it; therefore they also groan toward Him who is able to loose the bound. And the Lord, looking upon the earth, also looses the sons of the dead—that is, those born from those who practiced the sin leading to death and because of this have died. And if those coming from the Gentiles are not descendants of sinful and impious fathers, and death having prevailed has swallowed them up; whom He has freed the sons from sins, He has loosed from the bitter bonds through the mystery of rebirth. And it is possible to use these two verses for those bound in persecutions because of the word of Christ, and for the sons of those dead through the witness of the truth.

For the contemplative soul, being Zion, will see those announcing to her the teachers of the name of the Lord, and announcing also His praise in Jerusalem, which by seeing peace profits through thought. If Zion and Jerusalem were to accuse the church because of seeing the greater things and seeing peace in the harmony and the concord of the dogmas, it would follow rightly that in this so-called Zion the name of the Lord and His praise should be announced in this so-called Jerusalem. Who answered Him in the way of His strength? The word does not agree. Does he not say of the people being created, to praise the Lord? Rather, he considers the one who, being poor by predestination, is not despondent and pours out his prayer before the Lord, to be the one answering, not with voice and utterance, but walking strongly in the way of His strength and with rectitude the way of virtuous deeds. For one does not answer God only truly, but not merely with voice. He says: 'Since I have been commanded to achieve much readiness for me and to contemplate the doctrines of your most unshakeable truth, and much...'

english: Because I need time to be perfected in these things, I beseech your goodness to announce to me the brevity of the days of my life which are stretching out toward my life in the flesh, lest I may not be able to grant myself to be perfected by a short prayer; and may you also deem me worthy of this, not to bring me up in the half of days. But he is brought up in the half of days who has not fully nor as he ought fruited here according to virtue. And this is not measured in a chronological interval, because then I receive a full number of days according to Abraham, so that I may be perfected with the knowledge of the truth and of the virtues. For then take me up, so that when the true light has shone upon me, I may become full of all days, having done those things according to virtue and having thought, lest it happen through all things [to exceed] the time of my life.

We previously noted as being toward Christ those words foretold by Paul in the Epistle to the Hebrews (Ps 101:26–29). For the Psalmist does not say such a thing: 'And you, at the beginning, Lord, founded the earth,' that is, you have made it to stand, in agreement with 'In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth.' The thing lying 'at the beginning' is able to refute the glory of all those saying the earth is an element, as if everything came from it and nothing existed before it. For it appears not to be a beginning, but rather that there exist foundations of it according to certain pre-conceived beginnings. It is also said to Job by the Lord, who founded the earth: 'Where were you when I was founding the earth?' But the Lord, through whom all things came to be, is founding the earth; and concerning the Father it is said, 'God founded the earth in wisdom.' And what was said concerning God, hanging the earth upon nothing, shows that the middle part of all things has this [quality]. But since you founded the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands, [and] the hands of your active powers...

Regarding those called [creatures]. For just as the works produced by the hands of craftsmen among us demonstrate truly that they have made these things, so it is demonstrated that the works of God are properly the creatures, because they are called the works of His hand. But since the creatures are being changed because they produce the form of this world, you likewise remain not naturally changing or transforming. For this is a property of creatures, that essence itself begins to derive from them by way of a process.

Furthermore, he says, 'And all shall be worn out like a garment' (Isa 51:6), referring to all things that are under necessity. For having taken a temporal beginning in their becoming, they grow old as much time passes by. But see that you are not deceived hearing in Daniel the 'Ancient of Days' (Dan 7:9). For there, it does not signify having become old through a multitude of days, but that he is ancient and old of days; as it is possible in the Psalms to say, 'He who exists from before the ages' (Ps 90:2). Thus also, 'Before the days,' that is, before all time, he is ancient and old. But the oldness of the heavens signifies not that they are before time, but that they are within time.

Therefore, they are not being worn out like a garment, but they will be rolled up, and like a waistband they will be rolled up by Him who made them, in order to be changed and re-elementalized. Their growing old and being rolled up signifies that the necessity which they contributed to the adornment of the present has passed away. For just as a waistband is rolled up after fulfilling its need, so too, when the heavens will again undergo re-elementalization with the earth after they have passed away, according to the one saying, 'Heaven and earth will pass away' (Matt 24:35), it is rightly said that they are being rolled up like a waistband. To their rolling up, he adds, 'And they shall be changed.' And in Isaiah it is said, 'The heaven shall be rolled up like a scroll' (Isa 51:11). Because of these things, he says, in identity, since these things are not remaining, the eternal things shall not fail. But for You, O Lord, having always the same and the like, You neither began nor [will end].

english: Your ages will not end, for your generations are from age to age (Ps 102:1b). But one should not take the ages of the wills chronologically, for time is not spoken of in this way. Nor does His being end, since His nature remains incorruptible, being alone possessing immortality.

One must not take 'sons of God' entirely according to the flesh, but according to instruction and the imitation of a way of life. For in this way some were called sons of the prophets, because they had perhaps become like them according to the prophetic manner. And Paul, a slave of Christ, has sons: Silvanus and Timothy and those near to them. And it happened that those benefiting from these were their seed. The children previously mentioned will dwell with Paul in the heavenly tabernacles, as will those being directed with them and their seed forever.

Others say that the composite man often speaks of himself as if he were others, saying, 'My soul' or 'My body.' And Paul, indeed, uses this practice, sometimes saying, 'I call God to witness upon my soul,' and sometimes implying, 'My body.' They say this by taking [the parts] as we say a people, rulers, and overseers of a city are not always different from the city itself (for it is filled from among them), but are a different rank of the whole city (for the rulers alone are not the city, nor the councilors privately, nor the people by themselves), but together they are the city—not so, even if the composite man is not another from the soul and the body (for from these two he is composed), but the soul of the whole is called as another of it.

Thus, the one who exhorts his own soul to bless the Lord is not 'uncomposite.' And those saying the soul is the spirit do not say it is such, but that it is under it, having its care. Within it, he calls upon every rational power of man. For it is not to be heard of the Savior saying, 'The kingdom of heaven is within you' (Luke 17:21). And do not view the 'internal' things as something else; for the powers we have, which are resting, are said to be able to act well within us. It is necessary to stir these up and turn them toward activity.

Through which we bless the name of the Lord. For the holy name blesses not powers, but good activities. Even the Savior says to those partaking of virtue and divine knowledge: 'The kingdom of God is within you' (Luke 17:21), saying only once: 'Seek the foundations of faith and virtue within yourselves, being rational and having become according to the image of God; seek not the good outside yourselves.'

Sins are diseases of the soul. For he says, 'My soul, what harm hast thou done to thee?' (Ps 102:3b). He redeems life from corruption, so that you may no longer live a life according to corruption and passion, but in incorruption, loving the Lord Jesus. And providing you an incorruptible body in the resurrection, he redeems your life from corruption.

And he crowns you also in mercy and compassion, the material of this crown being almsgiving and compassion. Just as others receive the crown of righteousness and the incorruptible crown of glory, woven from righteousness and upright glory, so also you, through mercy and compassion which you have worked, shall be crowned, according to 'Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy' (Matt 5:7).

And not thus is the better: not so much that I shall be emboldened in the struggling, but because you are being merciful and pitied by the Lord, you shall be crowned, the Lord returning to your intellect the crown of graces. For by the grace of God and not of our own works we are saved, and we do not deserve sufferings in this present time for the sake of the glory to be revealed to us; so also he crowns us, not looking toward our own striving, but toward his own mercy and compassion.

And fill your desire also with good things. For he gives good things to those asking him. Since even the desiring of good things happens to be asking for them, giving to you all things, he fills your desire with good things through longing; for every desire of the righteous is good.

And since you are becoming according to the image and likeness of God and have become fit to enter into the essence in advance of the good, but having flown away from heedlessness, you cast away virtue both practical and intellectual; without which, being suspended, you would rise to the height, know that you have the power to grow wings, if you should wish it.

english: Working through God. And this shall be to you, your youth being renewed according to the eagle. For just as this old feather is cast off, and immediately it grows new wings, so also you, having grown old through wickedness, are renewed from your antiquity, and your youth comes in completion, and those who once used strong wings are not so, but now being clothed with new ones, you may be lifted up into heaven toward all those who have waited for God. For those waiting for the Lord shall change strength, they shall become wing-bearing like eagles, they shall run and shall run the course.

Father of mercies and alone good is the Lord, who performs acts of mercy, showing compassion to all, doing good (Ps 102:6). God also, toward those being wronged by the devil and by wickedness, making judgment, sent his only Son to heal and to set free those being oppressed by Satan, redeeming souls from bondage and from injustice, having torn the handwriting of our debt and having nailed it to the cross. The one holding us, the devil, had made us debtors, through whom we were practicing, having set up the handwriting of our debt for him. We were rescued from all our injustice, God making judgment for those being wronged, so that through the blood of his Son Jesus Christ we might be cleansed from all injustice, not only the injustice by which we were being wronged but also the injustice which we were practicing. From here we learn, according to the exhortation of Paul, the difference between being wronged and doing wrong. For to those being wronged God performs judgment, doing them good, but to those doing wrong he brings punishment, so that they do not inherit the divine promise: For those who do wrong shall not inherit the kingdom of God (Ps 102:7/1 Cor 6:9).

Virtues are called parallel. For he who says, 'Lord, make known to me your ways' (Ps 102:7), it is worthy that virtues become manifest to him; and that part by Paul toward Elymas, saying, 'You will not cease turning away the straight ways of the Lord' (Acts 13:10), presents the same, signifying that virtues are also the wills of God. And otherwise the coming thing might be understood; for since God gave the law of the things to come through Moses, having a shadow of them, but not every part...

This law bears an image and a type of the intelligible and spiritual, as if it were to move from the sensible things to the spiritual and original ones by a way of analogy. And the Lord will teach such transitions—fittingly, concerning these transitions it is said, 'He made known His ways to Moses' (Ps 105:5). For who else besides Moses, having learned from God how to ascend from the sensible circumcision and bodily sacrifice and the other shadowy things to the truth, knew this way? For He made known His ways to him.

But also, if anyone is a son of Israel, if it is not said, 'Israel is my chosen one,' how will he understand the wills of God, which are made known to the discerning ones by Him, such as the Jews who, hurrying in secret, circumcise not the flesh but the heart; and they also offer a sacrifice of righteousness and pleasingness to God, not as a spiritual sacrifice. All these things spoken are the Lord, since God is true; but a true God is not in the excellence of the aforementioned virtues, but is the source and essence of them. Therefore, we also take courage that He will not be angry with us for having sinned, in order to complete and destroy this. For this was 'He will be angry unto the end,' that is, to remain in anger as an end, and the anger toward the gods is destruction. He does not become angry unto the end, nor does He remain for an age. For the deceiver does not have lasting anger: 'When the anger of my spirit is kindled, I shall be healed' (Ps 102:13).

But the mercy of God takes its beginning upon the earth, according to what was said: 'The earth is full of the mercy of the Lord' (Ps 32:5). If mercy, beginning from there, becomes directed toward the pious, it lifts them up and suspends them upon the height of the heavens: 'For great is your mercy, O Lord, unto the heavens' (Ps 36:5). For ascending into the kingdom of heaven happens more by the mercy of God than by anything else. And the saving virtues appear to be sunrises, while sins are sunsets, entirely deprived of light. Since no one can exist in both virtue and wickedness, he who has associated himself with the aforementioned sunrises, as if to dwell in them, [is like] the one in Eden, planted by God according to sunrises.

english: Having been distanced from paradise, the previously spoken evils of the interpreted Easts hold such a distance from himself. For the evils are far from the virtues.

But as one in the Easts has the previously spoken evils distanced from him by God, so he who is in them, desiring to sin by himself and not from God, is not distanced from the Easts, but is cast out of paradise. But even after these things have happened through disobedience to the divine commands, Jesus comes upon the evils according to 'Make way for him who is stepping upon the evils, the Lord is the law to him' (Ps 102:13), and he will not stay there long, but coming to the pain, saying 'With me you shall be in paradise.' For providing a remission of sins, he removes the evils from the rising toward paradise.

Rather, God excessively and super-abundantly pities those who fear him (Ps 102:13), having set them into the rank of his sons, making known to each of us the creature. For he did not create anything hating, but knowing the hearts of men, he fashioned them individually as he saw fit for each of us. And we have power and a starting point, and these he gives upon us having them by energy to become his sons. It is possible to grasp that he himself knows our creature and thus: let him take experience of our creature; having become flesh, he assumed a natural disposition so as to consider us sons of himself.

Not as a creator of our nature did he create the weakness. For even if not all our construction is from dust (for we have a spiritual nature in ourselves, becoming an icon and likeness of God), but rather in supplications toward God, deeming him a gatherer and benefactor, we say that he brings forward the lesser and weaker of those in us: 'Remember, Lord, what dust we are; therefore help our weakness and our poverty' (Ps 102:14). Following 'Remember, Lord, what dust we are,' it forbids not the inner man, but the outer things lying ahead. For according to the present and after the flesh, we have certain days that complete the extending time of the life after the flesh, surpassing it like a parching meadow.

He sings along with the others, and Isaiah says: 'All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is like the flower of the grass; the sun rises and withers the grass, and its flower falls' (Isa 40:6-8). These things represent the glories, honors, and all the prosperities existing in this life which seem to those living in the flesh to be abundant, yet they depart like a flower and grass, and wither as if they had never even existed (Ps 102:17-18).

You should also perceive in another way the children of righteous men as zealots for their works. Thus, the mercy of God toward those who fear Him is indescribably extended from age to age (Ps 102:17-18). For He does not sometimes show mercy and sometimes not; for being good by nature, He always shows mercy. Moreover, righteousness is the spouse of this mercy; it is not limited by time, but extends to all generations, remaining upon the sons of sons and through all succession, so that He may always have this righteousness with those who guard the covenant of God from age to age, who are also inscribed as heirs of the coming promises through their doing of good. For those guarding it will also remember the commandments of God by doing them. For these are given not as a mere memory, but a memory for the purpose of doing. And regarding that which they are given for the purpose of doing, the Savior also establishes, saying: 'He who has my commandments and does them, he is the one who loves me' (John 14:15). For the promises are the reward and inheritance not of their memory alone, but of their doing.

And in other places it has been said that God is not in a place, but it is said that He dwells in heaven through a certain following and economy. Accordingly, it has been said that they have prepared for Him even here in heaven, that is, they have established the throne of His kingdom and His rule, not only of those in heaven, but of all, holding and dominating universally (Ps 102:19). One should not regard the prophet as a man, but rather the Holy Spirit within him, commanding the angels regarding the things at hand; for all His angels (meaning the Lord's) say, 'Bless Him' (Ps 103:20). The Spirit commands all the angels, being their essence. If this is so, how did some dare with audacity...

english: To show this regarding the order of the angels, although is it not somewhat different for all of them? Ps 103,1: He clothed himself in majesty, and to those in greatness and those who exalt themselves, he gives the appropriate thing; but in confession, he gives to all a harmonious symphony concerning them. For the name of confession signifies also the symphony that is in words. But if you wish him to be clothed in another kind of confession according to repentance and in thanksgiving, it is not for sinners. Corresponding to this signified thing, he will also clothe the virtue of those who succeed, which is called majesty. And just as the Savior says, 'I am naked, and you clothed me' (Matt 25:36), this shows what his clothing and covering becomes: the practice of those living according to him; so also the Father will clothe himself in the virtues of those who strive concerning him.

Ps 103,2a: Just as one who puts on a sensible garment is covered from every side, so God, being filled with knowledge from every side, as his essence turns out to be ungraspable, puts on light as a garment, signifying even here the most sharp-witted knowledge of the light. Agreeing with this concerning God, Paul writes that he has an unapproachable light, or dwells in unapproachable light (1 Tim 6:16). For in this very expression, it is said that the whole is the knowledge of God, and for this reason, that it is difficult to understand for the intellects, that he dwells in unapproachable light.

Ps 103,2b.3a: He roofs the air above us and the wind toward the ether with waters according to the swirling of the clouds. And toward the intellect: he calls the intellectual essence 'heaven,' being stretched out and made simple upon the canopy of the mind, he who roofs the intellectual and divine things with waters, the heavenly things of the soul, that is, its powers which happen to be above the sensible.

Ps 103,6a: You will find the abyss lying upon ungraspability, and in 'Your judgments, O Lord, are many' (Ps 136:7), for his judgments being unsearchable, there is no grasping of them. Therefore also not simply ab...

They are compared to a small abyss, but a great one. And God is not a small abyss, for the greatness of the abyss covers the judgments of the enclosure, being called incomprehensibility. Ps 103:7b: Hearing the sound of thunder—that is, the word being made loudly according to providence—they shall fear. It is fitting that these things should be said concerning the visible things and the waters. It is possible to take 'From the sound of thunder they shall fear' (Ps 103:11) not concerning the waters, but concerning men, rather concerning all living creatures, as it might happen that a thunder, of the invisible and unseen divinity, is perceived.

Through every word the preceding psalm glorifies and doxologizes God, remembering each of the creatures; and God, accepting his providence in the things set forth, marvels and considers his goodness with wisdom, caring for the endurance of the irrational animals. And rightly; for if he himself has made them, he is the provider of both their food and their drink. Ps 103:13–15.

And by ascent you shall understand the words having been fully returned; for the spirit-bearing men are they. They are watered from the heavenly things of this God, being filled with the gifts of the Spirit, the word of wisdom, and the following things which are innumerable. And the heavenly things of God, from which the words water, are sharp and surpassing contemplations of the truth, being called heavenly because they have not ascended beyond themselves. 'The earth shall be satisfied from the fruit of your works.' For he is... Let the earth blossom with grass for pasture and a fruitful tree producing fruit, and the following. And by ascent from Jesus, having much fruit during the visitation, the whole earth is satisfied, receiving those things having been made by Jesus in such a paradoxical way. For this is the fruit of his works. english: Wasting men upon the earth. Even in his super-natural and most high words, it is not possible to provide a meadow for those who are the most irrational.

The discourse concerning sensible things and the letter of the scripture is the meadow in this, but even the more ethical ones will not be able to partake, each of them saying of such things: 'Into the place of clover, there he pitched his tent' (Ps 104:18).
Having once surpassed such a state, being no longer slaves of men but having become men, they will say again, each of them: 'You have prepared a table before me' (Ps 23:5).

The mind rejoices the heart of men; not everyone alone is the one having the generation from the one saying, 'I am the vine, the true vine' (John 15:1), but since all sensible things are named earth because of the material.

From these, it is possible to take a word ascending through some analogy to the intelligible. And the beautiful word is brought forth from the earth by nourishing the endos and the man in secret; and from the bodily narratives of the scripture, the mystical word is brought forth beautifully because of the historical things said of the earth.

And the face of the inner man is appeased and made bright by the oil of the nourishing divine light, which alone dissolves diseases and the pains of the soul, differing from the attributed intellect. For the word of God is like the vine, so also the oil is; for he says, 'as an olive tree flourishing in the grove of God' (Ps 80:8). For his teaching, by a diverse relationship, is both vine and oil and bread.

According to an upward leading: the race of deer is at war against the race of gazelles. They hasten, indeed, to bring them up. Such are certainly the disciples of Christ, being ready to avenge every disobedience. And he also enables the power against the gazelles from the one who has extended authority to them to tread upon the gazelles and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy.

These are not the spiritual deer desiring the springs of the waters, the spiritual ones, which are also called oracles; they wear themselves out upon these oracles. And if souls perfected according to virtue are to leap great leaps, imitating the one leaping upon the oracles and running over the mountains and the valleys because of the sharp-sightedness and...

Insightful. But those souls that have arrived at this state and are weaker, called swine, flee to the rock upon which Jesus founds the church as an unconquerable fortress; and this is the confession of the faith. And in Proverbs it is said, 'And the swine, a people not strong, made their dwellings in rocks' (Prov 30:26). It is nothing wonderful that the rock is spoken of both singularly and plurally, meaning Christ who is simply the rock, and who is also [spoken of as] rocks according to various thoughts.

It is suggested by scripture that 'Rock is a refuge for the hyenas,' as perhaps there is a synonymy between the hyena and the swine. It is not for each one to hear [someone] saying, 'Behold, the Lord helps me; who will harm me?' (Ps 118:6) and 'The Lord is my helper' (Ps 118:7), and 'I will not fear; what can man do to me?' (Ps 118:8). The fact that the 'As' [the simile] here written is a demonstrator not of likeness but of truth, just as also in [the phrase] 'As God is good to Israel,' for he does not say God is like good, but truly good. And in the present [passage] then, that the works of God are magnified, is signified by the 'As' [in] 'As your works have been magnified, O Lord' (Ps 103:24). For everything that comes about in wisdom is great of God. And the wisdom of God in which all things came into being is the Lord; for Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1:24).

Another says that he speaks only concerning the rational [beings]. For to hope and to have expectation toward God, this is hinted at. And they hope to find this at an opportune time, being freed from every deficiency and disease. For when this is given, they will gather it, hastening so much to receive it, so that it may be fed into a basket. And there will exist for them the kindness that is upon such straightness, as [He is] opening for them the hand of your words and the wisdom.

God, providing eternal glory to his own works, rejoices in all that hopes for him. For just as having made all things very good in the beginning (Gen 1:31), he rejoiced in the inhabited world, and he rejoiced in the sons of men when there was not yet transgression, so He would rejoice at the perfection and restoration of the ancient [order] of his works, not out of the joy of God [being] not impassible (for the divine is impassible) but out of the acceptance of those having perfected perfect virtue.

english: If you wish to handle these things spiritually, consider how, when God looks upon [you] according to 'Look upon me' (Ps 103:6) and 'The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous' (Ps 103:9), the earth does not stand firm but trembles as if darkening, as if the material existence were to be cast away and pass away. But God, touching the evil powers because he sees the called ones in their pride, smokes them out, entering into them with a breath, as if into the punishment by fire.

Sing to the Lord, having the presence of the one existing not in voice but in thoughts; and I will sing also in perfect deeds to God, since I have the presence of the one existing, in which I partake of the one existing before the ages and who said 'I am the Being' (Ex 3:14). And conversing in a way pleasing and acceptable to God, I will say, 'Let my conversation be sweet to him.' For he himself says, having accepted the church, 'Your voice is sweet' (Ps 103:2).

Just as according to the history of Samuel ministering continually in the tent of meeting, he saw the face of God, so also those who continually and without interruption examine the dogmas of truth and having practiced the virtues, seek the face of God, desiring to see him with a pure mind. For the face of God is the character of the essence, being an icon of the invisible God; therefore also the one seeing it immediately sees God.

As for his mouth, to perceive his word, he has given you instructions and commands judged to be both law-giving and precise. Having said 'slaves of God from Abraham' because of the bringing in of the race from Abraham, and 'the chosen ones from Jacob' because they are his and bear his name, and 'an election from the nations' then received into an inheritance, their own Lord and God, he says that his providential judgment is such toward all men.

The number of a thousand generations is not said according to a multitude, but by the appropriation toward the unit, just as also in 'When the thousands are increasing', and 'What is good to me is the law of your mouth, surpassing thousands of gold and silver' (Ps 118:72). Because you are evil and yourselves are partakers of Christ.

We have become [such] through being made worthy of the appearance of the Son of God; for He is the Christ, the one who also spoke to them, and He himself, the Savior, teaches in the Psalms that Abraham your father rejoiced to see my day (Ps 104:12), and did rejoice. When did he not look up with his eyes and stand before God at the oak of Mamre? For then the Scripture says, 'God appeared to Abraham.' And these things, even if they are few, were necessary to be announced to the nations by those commanded there to do this.
Regarding Psalm 104:12a, 'brief' instead of 'few.' For the brief lies in respect to magnitude, but the few is arranged in respect to numbers.

Regarding Psalm 104:18-19, they humbled his feet alone, not binding his soul in shackles, but [the soul] having been made free from iron. For they, being surrounded by shackles, bear the affliction, having the soul bowed down by iron. But he endured this not unto all things; for he limits the end of the affliction, saying that he had held it [fast] until the word of God passed through; according to which, having been transferred from the prison, he became a fosterer and nourisher of all, having grasped the word of the Lord, kindling it to boil in the spirit and being filled with the divine light, with which also he is able to give the exhortation saying, 'Do not quench the Spirit' (Ps 104:20).

Regarding Psalm 104:20-21, and Joseph himself did not [follow] this doctrine; therefore, toward the causes, he says, 'Did you not send me here? For you indeed plotted for evil, but God [plotted] for good' (Ps 104:21).

Regarding Psalm 104:26, since not all are able to depart from the harmful ones by themselves and through themselves, God sends to those who are thus weak the ones capable of being guides and leaders of the way that carries toward the good. And the law of God through Moses and the high-priestly word through Aaron are not [the same]; the one forbidding the deeds, the other ministering to God on our behalf and distributing the graces from Him to us; they are the leaders [whom they say], 'Let us flee Egypt.'

english: It happens through good works, every kind of word, and all knowledge, in silver and gold, and outside of Egypt by God. For it is impossible for one being weak and lacking the aforementioned silver and gold to come out of Egypt.

The set-forth voice is especially holy of those before the coming of the Savior, entreating that the Lord might remember them in the good pleasure of His people (Ps 105:4–6), since He was well-pleased in His beloved Son to save, judging His people and the world; thus he says, showing Him: 'This is my beloved Son in whom I am well-pleased' (Matt 3:17). Because the divine prophets, desiring to see and hear the things happening and being spoken concerning Jesus by the eye of the mind, are worthy that their memory be made in the salvation according to the good pleasure.

And Christ is often called the salvation of God, as also in Ezekiel: 'For all flesh is the salvation of our God' (Ezek 36:26). This visitation, the father of the baptizer making manifest concerning God, says: 'Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, in whom he visited us, the sunrise from on high' (Luke 1:78). Having visited us in His salvation, it will be for us to become His chosen ones and to behold in the goodness of His chosen ones the joy being fulfilled, and to be made glad in the divine feast of the nation being completed from all those believing.

And may it be accomplished for us also to be praised with His inheritance, for it is for us as heirs to have the inheritance. Who is this church from the Gentiles, saying, 'Let them depart from me, and I will give you the inheritance of the Gentiles' (Isa 66:8)? For spiritually, remaining according to the Gospel, those attending to the law are praised with the aforementioned inheritance. And they are praised by God and by the holy powers, receiving those who hasten to be well-pleasing to God.

And the divine men, taking up also the countenance of those who repent of those on whom they acted wickedly, and teaching how they must repent after the sins, saying, 'We have not sinned, but we have sinned like our fathers'—calling their fathers the ancestors and those who came before, or those who begat them in wickedness—will not say everything when confessing, saying, 'We have turned away'...

We have acted perversely and done wrong. And even regarding those who are counted among those who repent, they do not appear to have been pious. For we were not made outside of the divinity, but being contained by it, we were defeated by passions and hard toil, and we sinned and did other things. Psalm 105:9: God, who rebuked the Red Sea, is praised by all. If even Jesus, when the sea is tossing, rebukes the sea, so that from a storm a calm becomes, He is proven to be God, He who rebuked the Red Sea, and He is the Son of Him. But because God rebuked the Red Sea, the ancient sea becomes dry, as if it were to be passable, and the abyss is no longer called by the abundance of the waters. Psalm 105:19: And they made a calf in Horeb, having a vision of the Apis brought from Egypt in Memphis. Therefore, they worshiped this calf and other carvings, being bound to the drama of polytheism. Immediately, indeed, having made a calf, they were showing many, saying, 'These are not your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'

The following psalm, its praise being of the divine benefits and mercies toward men that have been done, has the sequence arranged. Psalm 106:1: Those upon whom the surrounding tribulations fall (without any of them bringing this upon themselves), knowing that the good God has these things, says the following verses. And since some are becoming in temporary things thought to be good, they do not simply have a trial of God's mercy, but are being pitied for ever, having the eternal good things from Him. For if even the good God has pitied someone with eternal mercy. He also makes mercy for thousands for those who love Him the same, preparing for them. An eye has not seen, nor has an ear heard, nor has it ascended to the heart of man. It is said also previously that the good is synonymous with the good. english: Because poverty has pre-empted the state of having wealth in every word and in all knowledge and in good works, he having been released from these evils will not be tested by punishment. Ps 106:17: While they were still walking in the way of their lawlessness, God took hold of them, because through a multitude of impieties having been humbled, they were held by those from whom he raised them. And see if you are able to apply this to the thief who repented on the cross; for while he was in the way of lawlessness (for he was condemned by robbery) and having been humbled by punishment because of his lawlessness, he was taken hold of by the one saying to him, 'Today you shall be with me in Paradise' (Luke 23:43). Ps 106:18-19. Generally also, both upon the body and upon the soul, for what sickness of the emaciated [one] he abstains from all nourishment, both bodily and spiritual; but those having the health of the soul hunger and thirst for righteousness. And the gates of death are the sins toward death. These they approach before coming to him, having a life-giving breath and power, I mean indeed the thought concerning God; therefore, in their being afflicted, they cry out to the Lord, and he saves them from all the constraining necessities that hold them. And if they had not cried out to the Lord, they would have perished even until death. Ps 106:22b. And he proclaims in gladness the works of him, everyone announcing those things having happened to himself and having had experience of his goodness, not simply recounting those things having happened to others. Ps 106:26. And the saying of ascending as if to heaven and descending as if from the abyss is said by hyperbole. For indeed in such a way there are countless examples in the Scripture; for concerning the cities of Israel, the enemies, whatever they had been walled up as if to heaven because they had been walled up with high walls, and 'I shall be made white as snow' (Ps 51:7) is said in the same way. Ps 106:38b. Others say:

They are livestock that are in the so-called sheep, which possess abundance and greatness because of their perfected gentleness and learning (Ps 106:42b). But also, if she does not possess the capacity to speak of the divine economy of God, it will shut her mouth. And you will perceive the devil as lawlessness, and all that is established according to it, as those speaking lawlessly with an enclosed mouth (Ps 106:43).

Because much of them belongs to the spiritual intellect, it is for the wise and understanding to comprehend them. His glory is the practical and contemplative life, through which it is divided toward moral and intellectual virtue. Those who raised up the true light, having risen toward the Lord, walking decorously as in the day, striking the harp and striking the lyre, sing to the all-wise God, offering up their hymns rhythmically and harmoniously. And it is said in the psalm: what harp and what lyre?

His mercy is magnified as that of the heaven, beginning from the earth; for the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord (Ps 107:5). The end holds those who began to receive mercy from the earth to reach the heaven, in order to inherit the kingdom of the heavens. And his truth is also magnified in the clouds serving the spiritual, to Moses and the prophets, since their ministry begins from the shadow and ends in the truth, just as they also worship the Father in spirit and truth (John 4:24), as do the apostles and all the disciples of the Spirit.

From the first word, 'As high as the heavens is your glory' (Ps 107:6), and from the sixth verse until the end of the ninety-ninth (Ps 107:99), we are being cut off from the things set forth there. Because of the lifting up of God in those who carry the image of the heavenly, and because of this, called heavens, his glory extends over all the earth that is able.

english: To bear a hundred and sixty and thirty; as God is being lifted up toward the contemplative natures of the world, which are called heavens, His glory is found upon the practical earth, which is called earth.

Not otherwise are those worthy of being loved by you to be rescued from the enemies holding them or those surrounding them, than by you saving with your right hand and by me interceding for them (Ps 107:7). An oath is interpreted as a symbol of work (Ps 107:8–10). The Lord, having been lifted up on the cross and having ascended, divided the works of men as to justifying some and rejecting others; for He is a just judge.

Therefore, even the place near the surface, because it is called a valley below due to the human bodies dwelling in it, is called the measurement of the dwellings of the souls inhabiting it, to provide for both the things below and these things. Indeed, He sent the heralds of truth into all the nations, so that the gospel of justification might be proclaimed.

Gilead is interpreted as migration, Manasseh as being from oblivion, and Ephraim as fruitfulness. The Savior says, 'My Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine,' meaning migrating from evil to truth, or from evil to virtue, or from earth to heaven; and mine also is the one who has surpassed all the oblivion of good things and has come from it. For he who comes from oblivion into memory is Manasseh, that is, having left and abandoned the oblivion by which the good things of God were forgotten.

But also the great fruitfulness of the believing nations has become a covering and a perception of the Savior; for as Paul writes to those who were benefited by him, saying they are his joy and crown (1 Thess 2:19), so also the Savior has a perception, a crown being woven for him by those bearing up righteousness and truth. And Judah is his king, not by his ruling, but by the king being made to dwell in him. Such is David, or perhaps everyone confessing on behalf of whom Judah was strengthened, being interpreted as confession.

Moab, however, because of being a punishment for those handed over to him by the Lord, is the lion of the saying of hope. And the lion often signifies punishment among the prophets. Since punishments fall upon a good intention, they bring good hope.

english: A few days, being enlightened, before he betrays the truth. Being enlightened by the true light, and receiving also the oversight of this instead of himself, becoming a teacher who both remained and progressed in the truth.

The fathers of Judah, who begot him through betrayal (Ps 108:14a), and those who are able to do this through the giving of silver, and what Satan, having cast [it] into his heart, incited him to betray the Lord; and those having the wisdom of this age, the rulers concerning whom Paul says, 'For if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory' (1 Cor 2:8). And he put him to death, because he became the one handed over unto death (Ps 108:16c).

He who is clothed in the form of the slave speaks as to the Lord the Father (Ps 108:21–23). And he says to the Lord how he will do mercy with him, benefiting those who are his body; for the things happening to his body are reckoned to himself. Therefore he says, 'Do with me for the sake of your name, since in this I have come to those whom you sent, saying, I have come in the name of the Father; because of this name do it, for your mercy is good, benefiting and full of goodness; do it, since also my heart is troubled within me.' You say 'heart,' and the apostles are his equal-souled ones, the lesser ones having become believing ones who were found to be his body. Since the disciples were not scattered having been scandalized in that night, but Judas and the crowd of the Pharisees stood over to hold him, it happened that their being troubled was his heart. But even if his heart was troubled, he did not depart from him, being contained by him and dwelling in his disciples. But also everyone whose heart is being troubled from thoughts or suffering, doing nothing and saying nothing according to the trouble, says, 'My heart was troubled within me.' Since, indeed, the Savior is to live always among men (for indeed he was taken up after the resurrection into the heavens), he speaks concerning human life as not permanent nor standing, like a shadow in its vanishing: 'You were cast away from me like a chaff.' For just as the chaffs are scattered away through weakness of nature.

They are tossed about; not that I, having taken on a weak life through men, was quickly driven out of weakness to be crucified, but having been taken up after the resurrection. It is possible also to say concerning all the disciples as it is said concerning Him, 'I was tossed about like locusts' (Ps 108:30-31), since, being persecuted and tossed about by those desiring evil, they are not humbled but are carried away flying upward. And all the martyrs, having been tossed about like locusts, having left the things below, pursue the prize of the high calling.

Giving the reason for confessing and praising Him, He brought [it] so that He might stand at the right hand of the poor; it is evident regarding Him who became poor for all, that through my poverty they might become rich. He stands at the right hand of Him who does all things rightly and thinks [all things] rightly. Again, the God, having set the pretext of standing at His right hand, says, 'To save my soul' (Ps 109:1).

Having fulfilled the economy, both having been raised from the dead and having been taken up into heaven, the Lord Jesus says, 'Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet' (Ps 109:6), that is, the Father. Paul, therefore, says that after this ascension, the voice was spoken through [Him] to say, 'Having made a cleansing of sins, He sat in the right hand of majesty in the high places.' For to which of the angels was it ever said, 'Sit at my right hand?' (Heb 1:8).

The Lord, therefore, who is the Father of all those having been brought forth with Him, says to the Lord of creation, 'Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.' And the Father says to the Son, as if a father to a son and a son to a father, for He does not converse using speech; for He is His own thought, truth, wisdom, and word. And the Lord of the Lord sits in the right hands.

It is not locally, in the body, that He says these things, as if we were seeking the right hand in a place. Rather, those partaking of God are indeed in the right hand, since God is holy and good; no one else will be counted holy, reigning with the Father. For the 'Sit at my right hand' declares the co-reigning of the Son toward the Father. If it is regarding the rational [beings]: those having wisdom and the most keen virtue are thrones of God; and in these, the Savior sits at the right hand of God.

english: He sits. But those who have rushed toward wickedness and malice are enemies of the Word and the truth. But the Father also wills these to be changed through repentance, making them followers of the path and the feet of the Word, since having become his footstool, they fall from his feet; but with a turning toward virtue and wisdom, becoming more mobile, they themselves shall become a throne from [being] a footstool. Therefore Paul says, 'For he must reign until he has put all enemies under his feet' (Ps 110:1). And there God says, 'Until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet' (Ps 110:1). For he indeed sits at the right hands of the Father reigning, while the enemies oppose him. But having set for them the beginning of benefit by subduing them and making them his footstool, he raises their desiring hand, so that they themselves might be counted among the right-handed, no longer in the wickedness through which they happened to be on the left; so that in the end, the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father, and all the rational beings, having been perfected, become toward the Father and the Son of God, all things becoming in all things.

Thoughts and not thus: the name of the beginning, 'kingdom,' here signifies not as with the Savior in the day of his power, but after the resurrection in which he rose from the dead; for if he was crucified out of weakness, but lives by the power of God. It signifies the beginning kindred to him which is coming, through which he holds and rules (that is, the day of his power), not in things happening by chance, but in the brightness of the saints through which they possess [light], being illuminated and made bright by the true light, as one might say, 'Let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us.' If, however, he says 'beginning' regarding those who are beginning, according to what is signified, it is said that God prevails over every beginning, and his beginning was made at his own time; and you do not say thus, but rather those who are beginning are under him in the day of his power, when the sun of righteousness shines (Mal 4:2). For he himself says concerning those being ruled by him toward the Father, 'I want that where I am, they also may be, that they may see my glory' (Ps 110:3). All the ecclesiastics were not before now...

But they also always say that the appointed voice is said towards the Father, joined to the beginning of the psalm thus: 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, so that I may make your enemies a footstool for your feet; from the womb before the dawn I begot you' (Psalm 110:1; Psalm 89:12)—through the middle of the other half-verses.

And indeed the apostle, having followed this thought, has said: 'For which of the angels did he ever say, Sit at my right hand?' (Hebrews 1:5) saying only once. Not to any of the born, but to his only-begotten Son alone: 'Sit at my right hand,' since he himself is alone the only-begotten who is in the bosom of the Father.

Let us see also what this very word intends. And it must be said that God is indeed simple and undivided; and even while he is thus, if the divine Word wishes to truly present himself as a maker, from whom we are, he says, speaking of his hands, that the heavens and the rest of creation are the work of his hands.

Just so, with genuine parents, whom we call a star, if we mean not the adoptive ones but the genuine ones, since some are truly sons and others are adoptive and placed; if we do not mean the placed ones but the genuine ones, we say they are the offspring of the womb of those who bore them. And God, wishing to present a genuine Son and the only-begotten from himself, remembers the womb.

But just as he makes it with hands in a God-befitting way, so also we hear 'to have been begotten from the womb.' But the works of the hands are many, while the only-begotten offspring of the womb is one; therefore, it is not to be said of God that creating and begetting are the same, as some say.

For all things were made through the Word and in wisdom (John 1:3), and the wisdom and the Word were not through something, but were begotten from God. Therefore, begetting is not the same as making; for if there were no difference, nothing would prevent saying: 'My hands made you, and the heavens are the work of my womb.'

But just as the word has many variations, so also the things signified by it. But the Father does not say these things to the Son in ignorance, but so that we might know the intimacy of the Father toward the Son and of the Son toward the Father, these things were written. Just as what was said by that same only-begotten Wisdom: 'Before all mountains he begets me' (Proverbs 8:25), therefore also there, before the dawn...

english: It is said to have been born, and as a morning-bearing light, not only perceptible but also intelligible. And even regarding the intelligible, it is manifest what is said also of all creation, according to what is said: 'He himself is before all things' (Heb 1:3).

As for us, the Savior defines the Yes as Yes and the No as No; moreover, God, being truthful, is said to swear, not using an unchangeable or a changeable method. Therefore, 'The Lord has sworn and will not repent' (Ps 109:4), since the gifts and the calling of God are unchangeable; and the greatest calling is that of the Savior, into priesthood and an unchangeable gift, a priesthood not according to the order of Aaron but of Melchizedek unto the age.

For the priesthood of Aaron, lying ahead until a time of correction, was transferred, as Paul says, 'When the priesthood is changed, there is a change also of law by necessity' (Heb 7:12). But the covenant made toward the Savior is eternal, preserving the priesthood without transgression, being able to save those coming to God through him into perfection, the one who lives always to intercede for them.

Likewise also the spiritual sacrifices, a sacrifice of praise and of righteousness, he offers to the Father on our behalf, but he has also offered himself as a sacrifice for all, for the salvation of those being saved. As the Father says, 'Sit at my right hand, my Son' (Ps 109:5), now it is said, 'The Lord is at your right hand' (Ps 109:5), so that it might be manifest not locally that the Son is at the right hand of the Father.

For behold, both he is at the right hand and his Father is at the right hand, which is impossible if one thinks of 'at the right hand' locally. Just as the Father is in the Son and the Son is in the Father, so the Son is at the right hand of the Father. And the Father of the Son crushes the intelligible kings at his right hand on the day of his wrath, who are found to be nothing other than rulers and powers and cosmocrators of the darkness. They are the same ones being placed under the feet of the Savior because of the wickedness and malice they have...

His [enemies] will cease to be enemies after being crushed, as every such authority and power is being abolished by the Lord. The day of the Lord, the time of the judgment of all, is spoken of in the Scriptures.

When these things are thus fulfilled, God will fill the dead with corpses, not being empty or a non-participant of His fullness regarding those fallen from salvation, so that they might rise into eternal life. For the saints themselves have not received [life] from the fullness except for the fall and resurrection of many, casting down and making to fall those having a bad standing who seem to be established through wickedness and impiety, in order to raise them to a resurrection of life, so that they might serve Him as Head, after the bad kingdoms have been crushed as heads of many, who are called to be poured out because of wickedness. For since not only those but He himself has the head, that is, the king, first upon the earth that exists, having crushed the rulers of the nations upon evil, He himself legally reigns over them, being the Head of every man according to the inner human and of the blameless church.

The cause of all these things was established by Him having become one who is plucked from a streamlet in the way of the human life. For this the last verse alludes to, saying, 'From a streamlet in the way water is drawn'; because of this, He will lift up the head. [Ps 109:7] A streamlet signifies trial in many places, and to draw from it is to receive it. Jesus has been tested, having become for salvation in the way of men, as the apostle says writing: 'For He himself has suffered having been tested, He is able to help those being tested' [Heb 4:15]; and having been shown to be King, authority being given to Him in heaven and upon the earth, He will lift up the head, a ruler not only of those upon the earth but also of those in the heavens, having been ordained by the Spirit so that every knee should bend to Him.

Πάντα δὲ ταῦτα περὶ τοῦ γενομένου σαρκὸς λόγου εἰρήσεται. εἰ γὰρ καὶ ει ς καὶ αὐτὸς τυγχάνει, ἀλλ' ου ν κατὰ τὴν ἐπίνοιαν ἁρμόσει τῇ ἐνσάρκῳ αὐτοῦ παρουσίᾳ τὰ προκείμενα. 1044 Ps 110,1 Καὶ ὀλίγῳ δὲ πρότερον η ν ε γνωμεν παράδοσιν ἀρχαίων ἐθήκαμεν ἐκείνων ει ναι τοὺς μετὰ τοῦ ̓Αλληλουϊὰ ἐπιγραφομένους ψαλμοὺς τῶν ἐν τοῖς προτέροις συντεταγμένων οι ς καὶ ἐνταῦθα ἀπὸ τοῦ ΡΙ ψαλμοῦ ε ως τοῦ ΡΙΗ τὸ ̓Αλληλουϊὰ προγέγραπται, οὐ παρεμφαινομένου προσώπου ῥητοῦ ου ε καστος τούτων τυγχάνει. ἐπεὶ ου ν ὁ ΡΘ τοῦ ∆αυὶδ ἐπιγέγραπται, ἀνάγκη ο σον ἐπὶ τῇ παραδόσει αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς καθεξῆς ει ναι πάντας μέχρι τοῦ ΡΙΗ. καὶ ε στω καθόλου παρατήρησις αυ τη ἐπὶ πάντων τῶν ἀνεπιγράφων ψαλμῶν. Εἰ δ' ε ργα θεοῦ λάβοι τις τὰ παραδόξως καὶ τεραστίως ἐπιτελούμενα (τοῦτο μὲν διὰ Μωυσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν, τοῦτο δὲ διὰ ̓Ιησοῦ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν), ῥηθείη καὶ περὶ τούτων τὰ προκείμενα ῥητά. τὰς γὰρ ἀναστάσεις τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ τὰς τῶν λεπρῶν καθάρσεις καὶ ἀναβλέψεις τῶν τυφλῶν καὶ τὰ ὁμογενῆ τούτοις ̓Ιησοῦς ἐπιτελῶν συμβολικῶς ἐδήλου δι' αὐτῶν τὰς τοῦ ε σω ἀνθρώπου ἰάσεις, α περ πάντα προηγουμένως θελήματά ἐστι θεοῦ. Εἰ δὲ καὶ τὰς ἀρετὰς λάβοι τις θελήματα θεοῦ λέγεσθαι διὰ τὸ Ος ποιήσει πάντα τὰ θελήματά μου, ἐρεῖ ε ργα μεγάλα ἐξεζητημένα εἰς πάντα τὰ θελήματα τοῦ θεοῦ ει ναι τὰς κατ' ἀρετὴν ἐνεργείας. 1046 Ps 110,5.6 Καὶ κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν μέντοι τροφὴν ἐξαιρέτως δίδωσι τοῖς φοβουμένοις αὐτὸν μετά τινος παραδοξοποιΐας, ὡς τῷ ∆ανιὴλ τὸ α ριστον τυγχάνοντι ἐν τῷ λάκκῳ τῶν λεόντων ἐν τῇ Βαβυλῶνι· ἐκ τῆς ̔Ιερουσαλὴμ τὸν ̓Αμβακοὺμ μετάρσιον α ρας η γαγεν εἰς Βαβυλῶνα κομίζοντα τὴν τροφὴν αὐτῷ τῷ ∆ανιήλ. ἀλλὰ καὶ κόραξιν ἐντειλάμενος α ρτους τὸ πρωῒ καὶ κρέας τὸ δείλης φέρειν τῷ ̓Ηλίᾳ (λιμοῦ πολλῆς τυγχανούσης) ε θρεψεν αὐτὸν φοβούμενον τὸν κύριον. Τῆς δὲ παλαιᾶς διαθήκης αὐτοῦ ε ως καιροῦ διορθώσεως δοθείσης τέλος ἀναλαβούσης, μνησθήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τῆς κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον καινῆς διαθήκης ἀδιαδόχου μενούσης. διὸ καὶ τῷ λαῷ ου ς περιεποιήσατο τῷ ἰδίῳ αι ματι διὰ λουτροῦ παλιγγενεσίας καὶ ἀνακαινώσεως πνεύματος ̓Ιησοῦς δίδωσι τὴν ἰσχὺν τῶν ε ργων αὐτοῦ, φανερῶν αὐτοῖς οι ας δυνάμεώς ἐστιν ε καστον ω ν προσέταξεν ἐργάζεσθαι τὸν λαὸν καὶ τοὺς λόγους τῶν γεγονότων. Μνησθήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα διαθήκης αὐτοῦ. ο τε πώρωσις ἀπὸ μέρους τῷ ̓Ισραὴλ γέγονε, τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς τὴν σωτηρίαν εἰσῆλθεν. ἀλλ' ἐπεὶ ἀγαθὸς ὁ θεός ἐστιν οὐκ ἀρκεσθεὶς τῷ μόνον τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ἀκήρατον καὶ δεδοξασμένην κληρονομίαν, μιμνήσκεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τῆς πρὸς τοὺς υἱοὺς ̓Ισραὴλ διὰ τοὺς πατέρας αὐτῶν διαθήκης. τὴν ἰσχὺν ω ν ἐποίησεν ε ργων ἀναγγελεῖ τῷ ̓Ισραηλιτικῷ λαῷ, ι να τῆς οἰκονομίας τὴν δύναμιν θεωρήσαντες σωθῶσι καὶ αὐτοὶ μετὰ τὸ εἰσελθεῖν τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν λαμβάνοντες θεόθεν τὴν προσοικειωθεῖσαν καὶ βεβαιωθεῖσαν τοῖς ε θνεσι κληρονομίαν. 1047 Ps 110,7.8 Πολλαχοῦ τῶν θείων λογίων χεῖρα τοῦ
english: of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth and of every tongue confessing what the Lord Jesus Christ does for the glory of God the Father. The cross bears as a symbol this exaltation. And all these things shall be spoken concerning the happening of the Word made flesh. For if even he himself happens to be [one of them], yet according to the thought it will not fit the things set forth to his incarnate presence.

And a little before, we set down as a known tradition those psalms which are written after the Alleluia among those arranged previously, and here from Psalm 150 to Psalm 178 the Alleluia is written; none of these is of a different character. Since the righteous one of David is not written [on them], it is necessary according to his tradition to [include] all the following until 178. And let this be a general observation upon all the unwritten psalms. And the saint, about to proclaim the things having happened concerning the salvation of all by the Lord, pre-announces the voices set forth. And everyone confesses with all his heart, and he alone who has loved God with all his heart, soul, and mind; and, having turned away all his loving power toward God, he loves God with all his heart; and, having consumed all his hymnographic and eucharistic power toward God, he confesses to him with all his heart in the assembly of the important ones, not in a random place or with random people. It is possible to read 'With all his heart' as follows: 'In the counsel of the upright and in the assembly, the great works of the Lord' (Ps 110:2).

Generally and broadly called the will of the Lord, the things concerning his works in part are his individual wills. If not all things he willed, he did; the creation extends broadly to his will, the individual works being fitted to the specific wills. Therefore, since the Creator is great, his works are also great, most accurately fitted to the harmony of his wills; for they do not happen as they chance, but they happen as having been sought out for all the wills. Therefore, of the works having been sought out, let no one say 'to what purpose?' For all things were created for their need; therefore, all the works of God are very good. If, indeed, the works of God are taken...

Since things happening paradoxically and marvelously (some through Moses and the prophets, others through Jesus our savior) are spoken of, the preceding words are also spoken of these. For the resurrections of the dead, the cleansings of lepers, the sight of the blind, and things similar to these, Jesus performs symbolically through them, manifesting the healings of his own humanity, which are always previously the will of God.

And if one calls virtues the will of God because he will do all my wills, he will say great works have been sought out for all the wills of God, namely the activities according to virtue. Ps 110:5,6: And indeed he gives food without exception to those fearing him with a certain paradoxicalness, just as Daniel found the best in the lion's den in Babylon; from Jerusalem, the transport of Habakkuk was brought to Babylon, carrying food to Daniel. But also, having commanded the ravens to bring bread in the morning and meat in the evening to Elijah (during a time of much famine), he nourished him who feared the Lord.

And of his old covenant, when the time of correction having been given, the end is taking up, he shall be remembered for an eternity during the age of the new covenant according to the gospel, which remains without a successor. Therefore also, to the people, he appropriated his own blood; through the bath of regeneration and the renewal of the spirit, Jesus gives the power of his works, making manifest to them what power he has commanded them to work, the people, and the words of the things that have happened. His covenant shall be remembered for an eternity.

He who partial hardening happened to Israel, the fullness of the nations has entered into salvation. But since God is good, not being satisfied with only the fullness of the nations entering into the pure and glorified inheritance, he is remembered for an eternity of the covenant toward the sons of Israel through their fathers. He will announce to the Israelite people the power he made his works, so that, having seen the power of the economy, they also might be saved, after the fullness of the nations has entered, receiving from God the inheritance appropriated and confirmed to the nations. english: When calling the Father, we find the Lord, as 'The high hand has done all these things' (Ps 118:74). For the Word—through whom all things were made and in whom all things exist, which the Father made—is His hand creating the all. But also in a strong hand, having brought the people out of Egypt, God accomplished this in the same Son, as one of the apostles writes: 'Jesus, having saved a people once out of Egypt, twice destroyed those who did not believe' (Heb 12:26).

And since other scriptures also say that God has made all things by one hand, such as the one saying 'The heavens are the works of your hands' (Ps 89:11), and the one announcing 'The hands did not create all the host of heaven' (Isa 48:7) (this is consistent with the one who said 'Your hands made me and fashioned me' [Ps 139:13]), someone might rightly seek and find the Holy Spirit being called the hand of God; from which it is shown that the Holy Spirit is creative, in the Son and Holy Spirit of the Father, having worked the heavens and having created the host of heaven.

Among these works of the hand of God in all the saints, truth and judgment are found, happening to be truth. For He gives through the Holy Spirit a practical power, and judgment is that which judges and, with examination, defines, so that one must choose good and flee evil; but truth is what Christ gives through the Holy Spirit, namely a word of wisdom and a word of knowledge. The knowledge of truth and moral virtue are works of the hands of God, being truth and judgment; therefore, following this, all His commandments were brought forth, not spoken so as to be believed merely, but because of the immovable and certain, as it is written, 'I will give you an eternal covenant, the faithful things of David' (2 Sam 7:16).

These faithful commandments stand for ever and ever because they are of God and cannot be overturned. Concerning them, indeed, the Savior says, 'Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away' (Matt 24:35). But do not err by thinking that the things set forth concern the commandments which are according to the shadow. For those passed away until a time of correction was given. For concerning the spiritual laws according to Him, it is necessary to hear the things set forth, as the coming thing teaches thus: 'Having been made in truth and rectitude.'

For they become understood in truth according to the doctrine of godliness. But they are also completed in rectitude with the best of guarding, as the work of the hands of the Lord, and these being found to be being accomplished in each godliness, [are] truth and judgment. But take hold of judgment for the sake of rectitude, to direct the soul toward practical and ethical virtue, and [judgment is] to be critical of things to be done and not to be done.

As God sent redemption to his people (Ps 110:9ab: He has sent redemption to his people; there is nothing else to the one saying), the Son of Man came to give his soul as a ransom for many. By the same precious grace of God, having tasted every death, we were redeemed from our ancestral vain conduct. For Christ has become to us as wisdom and righteousness and sanctification from God, and also as redemption, saying, 'I was sent to proclaim liberty to the captives' (Luke 4:18). For the redeemer and benefactor of all has released from captivity those held by the devil and by wickedness, forgiving the sins and impieties of those fleeing to him. But his goodness was not satisfied with merely redeeming the captives and their heirs, those of his own father, but he set them as co-heirs of himself, having enjoined upon them an eternal testament, so that possessing it with brevity and perfect readiness, they might receive an immortal inheritance according to the eternal and incorruptible promises.

His name, he says, is holy to the saints, but fearful to the unholy (Ps 110:9c). For just as the fountain of holiness makes those participating in it become saints, so it is fearful to those who sin by bearing it.

As the doing of righteous things is the beginning of the good way (for this is the contemplation of truth) (Ps 110:10), so the fear of God is the same beginning and introduction into the wisdom of God, which is called the same as the contemplation of truth, which to the practically righteous belongs. For as the doing of righteous things leads toward the good way, so this fear of God leads toward wisdom. The name 'beginning' can be here, not instead of an introduction, but as being a cause, since the fear of God is that which is called the cause and the beginning. And the struggle with this wisdom is understanding.

english: Goodness is not for those who have merely thought about doing it, but for those who are actually doing it. For those who practice understanding, no benefit will be other than that of virtue, from whose benefit they learn the goodness of it.

Regarding all that has been theologized in the present Psalm, it is said that the end of it is that his understanding remains. For this is a fitting end for those who theologize: to say that his understanding (clearly of the one theologized about) remains forever. Since the one being praised is immortal, it is necessary that his understanding also be without end, as it lasts for all the ages.

He who does not act for the sake of anything else, but through human glory, or to avoid falling into the punishment that entices sinners, or for reward, but by choosing and acting for the sake of the good itself—for such a one will truly be blessed (Ps 111:1bc). The seed of the blessed man, who has the fear of the Lord, sows into the good land, his diligent and beautiful heart; it is possible for him to bring forth a hundredfold fruit (Ps 111:2,3). For those sowing the seeds of evils sow into the flesh, which is their weak and earthly existence (and so they reap corruption from the flesh), but those sowing into the Spirit, the powerful seed, they sow and reap into eternal life. For each of the imperfect and sinful, the Word commands: Sow for yourselves into righteousness, reap for yourselves into the fruit of life. Glory and wealth in his cosmos.

He who has heard the words of Jesus and turned them into works builds his house upon the rock, laying down the foundations of his theoretical and practical life upon the unshakable Word of God. Each one who fears the Lord has built such a house upon having willed to do what is in the commands of the Lord (that is, to have intensely willed the words of Jesus), filling it with the glory of the notions of truth and the wealth composed of every word, every knowledge, and every working good. Thus, the promise of his righteousness extends into the age of ages. Such imperfect houses they have built for themselves, having feared the Lord, so that they might not dwell in the [er...]
They wander halfway according to Isaiah, but they dwell according to the formed Jacob as a house. Others have also taken the things set forth according to the literal sense.

And the words ought not to be regarded as human. For the words of the stewards are not believed, as they are said. For indeed, one has been placed in advance by prophecy from God, Amos, who became upon the uncircumcised, and Solomon, stripping the matter bare: 'My words,' he says, 'if they are said by God.' Careless also is the divine Gospel, sometimes regarding the giver and sometimes the ministers; from the ministers he says, as Paul says, 'My Gospel,' but from the one handing it over, Paul again says, 'Just as we were approved by God to be believed to have the Gospel,' and 'That [they are] set apart for the Gospel of God'; and this is not a wonder. For it is the Holy Spirit that fills the holy men with divine things, sometimes of God and sometimes of those possessing [it], as it is said in [Luke] 'The Spirit of the Lord has rested upon him,' and 'In Spirit and in Power' [Acts].

But do not think because it is said chronologically, 'Until he goes against his enemies, he is not shaken,' that what is shaken after the destruction of the enemies is [not the same]. For how could he be moved, the one who, having the enemies removed, did not suffer this while threatening and looming over them? For it is customary in the Scripture to use such a way in many places; for regarding Mary, the Gospel says she remained a virgin until she bore her firstborn son, and so on. Since it is proper to show that the birth of Jesus came from a virgin without marriage, it is fitting that she was once in doubt. Did the virgin not undergo corruption? He says also 'she conceived'; having gone around this doubt, he says she remained a virgin until the childbirth. For if it is not said that a virgin remains until she bears, a virgin did not conceive from a man, nor did a virgin bring forth a child without [conception]. By this thought, 'I am, I am' is said by God, and 'as you may be reproached, I am.'

He says, 'God is [my] horn.' For all the righteous say this, being confident: 'In you we horn our enemies.' And he who therefore blesses his enemies in the Lord, having horned his horn against them...

To sing: for God says the Son glorifies the Father and the slave fears his lord; and if I say, 'I am lord,' where is my fear? and if I say, 'I am father,' where is my glory? (Ps 112:3,4). Perhaps also regarding the sun of righteousness, if it is in some rises according to which it rises. These have a relationship (or are themselves) to the rises in which paradise is planted. If they have a harmony in these rises, it is fitting to praise the name of the Lord according to the rises by which it rises and the settings. For he was able for Israel, but he rose for the believing nations. Since not with unwise and unjust judgment he was able to rise for those also, having received the judgments of providence everywhere and happening upon all from the Lord: Praise his name; the Lord is high above all nations, his glory is above the heavens.

And the words being taken more simply declare that as God of all things he provides, being high above all nations as a king, and having his glory in the heavens ruling also the rational ranks there. But with a deeper mind, the Lord is high above all believing nations, being praised by them with pure life, both practical and contemplative. And upon the heavens, which no longer bear the image of the swine but the heavenly, his glory reaches, just as he announces it to his own disciples: for the heavens declare the glory of God (Ps 19:1). For certainly some declare it. If you are able to say the glory of the Lord, the radiance of his glory, the Lord and our savior, you would follow what was said to the one being illuminated: And the glory of God has shone upon you (Lk 1:79).

And through the coming words, foreseeing the God of all, we learn, regarding how incomparably the Holy One is compared to all created things, he says: Who is like the Lord our God? (Ps 112:5-9). For there is no one like him, since he is alone.
