Αννα γοῦν ἡ μήτηρ Σαμουὴλ κατοικεῖσθαι ἐν οι κῳ μήτηρ λέγεται τέκνων εὐφραινομένη, ο λων ε ξ τέκνων γεναμένη μήτηρ. καὶ περὶ τῆς Σάρρας καὶ ̔Ρεβέκκας ̓Ελισάβετ τε καὶ πρὸ ταύτης τῆς μητρὸς γεναμένης τοῦ Σαμψὼν λέγοι τις εὐλόγως περὶ ἑκάστης αὐτῶν ο τι κατῴκισεν αὐτὴν μητέρα τέκνων εὐφραινομένην. 1060 Ps 113,1.2 Πρὸς δὲ διάνοιαν· ὁρῶν θεὸν νοῦς τυγχάνων τοῦ πτερνιστοῦ τῶν ἀντικειμένων τῇ ἀληθείᾳ οι κου τῆς Αἰγύπτου ἀναχωρῶν ἐπὶ τῷ μηκέτ' Αἰγυπτιάζειν μηδὲ τῶν Αἰγυπτιακῶν δεισιδαιμονιῶν περιέχεσθαι ι λεω θεὸν ε σχε τὸν ἁγιάζοντα τὴν ὁμολογουμένην γνησίως ψυχήν, ο τε καὶ ἐξουσιάσει καὶ οι α βασιλεὺς κρατήσει τοῦ διορατικοῦ· ̓Ιουδαία γὰρ ἐξομολόγησις, ̓Ισραὴλ δὲ νοῦς ὁρῶν θεὸν ἑρμηνεύεται. πρότερον μὲν ου ν ἐξομολογήσασθαι προσήκει, ι ν' εἰς ἁγίασμά τις θεοῦ γεγένηται οι κος καὶ α γιος ναὸς αὐτοῦ κατασκευαζόμενος, ι ν' ου τως τελειωθεὶς διὰ θεωρίας τῆς ἀληθείας ̓Ισραὴλ ἀποδειχθῇ γενόμενος ὑπὸ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ 227 ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τῷ δυνηθῆναι, βασιλευόμενος ὑπ' αὐτοῦ, μακαρισμοῦ τυχεῖν ὀψόμενος τὸν θεὸν καρδίᾳ καθαρᾷ. 1061 Ps 113,10.11 Σοῦ, δέσποτα, ἡμᾶς εὐεργετοῦντος, οὐχ ε ξει χώραν τὰ ε θνη λέγειν Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς αὐτῶν. ἐπεὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ τοπικοὺς θεοὺς ε χουσι καὶ ἱδρυμένους που, καὶ περὶ σοῦ τοῦτο τοπάζουσι λέγοντες Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς αὐτῶν. η τάχα χλευαστικῶς τοῦτό φασιν οἰόμενοι μὴ ε χειν ἡμᾶς θεόν. ἀλλ' εἰ κἀκεῖνοι πλανώμενοι τοῦτο λέγουσιν, ἀλλ' ου ν γε ἡμεῖς ἠκριβωμένῃ ὑπολήψει ι σμεν ο τι ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ α νω ἐστίν, οὐ τοπικῶς ἀλλ' ὑπεροχῇ μεγαλειότητος φρονοῦντες. εἰ γὰρ η ν α νω τόπος, ἀλλαχόσε ει ναι ἐκωλύετο. Εστι δὲ καὶ αἰτία πᾶσι τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἐπείπερ ο σα ἠθέλησεν ἐποίησεν, α λλος ω ν παρὰ πάντα. διὸ οὐ περιέχεται ὑπὸ πάντων, ἀλλὰ καὶ ε ξω πάντων καὶ ἐν αὐτοῖς ὑπάρχει κατὰ τὸν τῆς δημιουργίας καὶ προνοίας λόγον. ου τω γὰρ πληροῖ τὸν
english: He is both maker and provider of all things. These things he says, not separating the Son from the Father or the Father from the Son; for the divinity is one, and there is no other God besides the Son and no other the Father.

In Isaiah, indeed, concerning the Father, it is said: 'In you is God, and there is no God besides you; for you are God, and we are not afraid' (Isa 25:6-7). For if there were another God in the Son who is beside him, how could he subsequently bring forth: 'And there is no God besides you?' and immediately: 'For you are God, and we are not afraid, the God of Israel is Savior'? Therefore, even concerning the Father, when it is [said], 'Who is like our God, the Lord?' (Isa 40:25), the Son has not been excluded; but even concerning the Savior, the Father has not been set apart from the one divinity of Father and Son.

Who says: 'Who is the Lord our God, the one dwelling in the heights and looking down upon the lowly things?' For all lowly creatures and works are toward God, not only those upon the earth but also those in the heavens. And he sees these lowly things providentially.

For he sees the poor man cast down upon the earth and the needy man upon the refuse, and he raises them up from those standing in evils of want and poverty; and not merely to raise and make stand, but strengthening their goodness, seating them with rulers, preparing them to be equal to them. And he will seat them not with simple rulers, but with the rulers of his own people. And a woman, formerly dwelling in barrenness, will become a mother having borne many children.

It can also be said concerning the people from among the Gentiles, for whom the prophecy is: 'For this the poor people shall bless you' (Gal 3:14). Therefore, having raised this poor and needy people from the lowly things and from the refuse of Greek customs, he will seat them with the rulers of Israel, being their people. And the apostles are the rulers of the Hebrew people, whom we say are sitting on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

And the church from among the Gentiles, formerly barren, is called into joy, saying: 'Rejoice, barren one who does not bear children; break forth and cry out, you who do not labor in childbirth; for many more are the children of the desert than of her who has a man' (Isa 54:1). For truly, the church from among the Gentiles has become very much with children, more than she who has [a man].

The law of the man is the assembly of the Jews. Every soul, through chastity, is inhabited by God as a child in the church of the living God, a mother working out thoughts and words to rejoice in the offspring produced by the Word of God dwelling within her. This also happened according to the history of the Scripture. For instance, Anna, the mother of Samuel, is called a mother inhabiting the church, a mother having become such from children, rejoicing in children. And concerning Sarah and Rebekah and Elizabeth, and before this mother, the one born to Samson, someone says wisely concerning each of them what inhabited her: a mother of children, rejoicing (Ps 113:1,2).

For the intellect: the mind, seeing God, becomes like the wing of the things opposed to the truth, withdrawing from the dwellings of Egypt so as to no longer 'Egyptize,' nor to be contained by Egyptian superstitions, but to implore God, who sanctifies the soul that confesses sincerely; and he shall have authority and the king shall hold the discerning one. For Judah is confession, but Israel is the intellect seeing God. Previously, it was not fitting to confess, but now, since one has become a sanctuary of God, and His holy temple is being constructed, thus, having been perfected through the vision of the truth, Israel shall be shown to have come under the authority of God in order to be able to reign under Him, about to experience blessedness, seeing God with a pure heart (Ps 113:10,11).

'Where is their God?' the mortals say, when You, Lord, are doing us good. For they have local gods established in places, and they mock You by this, saying, 'Where is their God?' Perhaps they say this mockingly, thinking we have no God. But even if those wandering say this, we do not hold the precise opinion that our God is in the heavens above, but we think of Him not locally, but with a superabundance of majesty. For if He were in a place, He would be prevented from being elsewhere. And there is also a cause for all the heavens and upon the earth, since whatever He willed, He made, surpassing all things. Therefore, He is not contained by all things, but is also outside all things and exists in them according to the logic of creation and providence. For thus He fills the...

english: heaven and the earth. But if all the heavens and those in them, the earth and all that is in it, should come into being as the essence of God's will, some are very impiously thinking and suddenly snatching away the substance of the Son, the will of the Father, making him a will of those in the heavens who are substantial. But let the impious hear how creation alone was subject to the will of God. For it is fitting for the Maker that he wills to create (God and James agree in writing: 'Having willed, he brought us forth,' [Rom 8:28] as he says in the word of God, a word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of his own creatures and works) that the will of God be the cause. But the Son is neither a creature nor a work; he is a generation not of essence, but of will. For if he were a son of will, he would be an image and a character of God's will; but the divine words say he is a character of his subsistence and an image of the invisible God. If the Son is not a character of the subsistence and an image of the invisible God, then it is fitting that the Only-begotten be a generation of the essence of the invisible God and of his subsistence. For indeed, those being born by the word of truth, they are such; and the Word and the Truth himself is the Only-begotten of God. Since he is not brought forth by a word of truth, he himself is the will of the Father; for in the same way that wisdom and truth are, so also the will of God is. Indeed, it is the same in wisdom and in will to do all things.

All the perceptive race has the mind to see God (Israel signifies by chance the church of the living God) [Ps 113:17] and hopes in the Lord, whereas all other men hope for nothing. And the one who is among those healing the divine, by chance being a priest, hopes in a greater Lord and in a hope witnessed by Israel; for of those who have ascended above by contemplation and practice, the hope is greater, asking more greatly to have him as a helper and a defender. But also all those fearing the Lord (these are not the proselytes and those added to the law from the Gentiles) hoping themselves in the Lord, call upon him to be a helper and a defender [Ps 113:20-21]. For God remembers all of those who have remembered him.

Remaining in memory. Therefore he says, 'Seek the law of your God, and I will seek [you],' children of yours. For the one forgetting the divine law immediately forgets also that which was given to him; but when a god remembers something blessed, he immediately turns toward it, giving spiritual and heavenly blessings according to the proportion of the greatness of faith, just as he gives the other gifts. Stand firm, for it is necessary for the small ones to receive [blessings] along with the great ones, among those alone fearing the Lord, and upon all the mentioned ranks, so that you may not differ in these things, where some are great and others small.

Blessed are we by the Lord, who made heaven and earth (Ps 113:23). For it is not that we observe the laws. Lest anyone think the divinations belong to another, Moses served; following this, the hierophant handed down the things concerning creation before the giving of the laws, through which he teaches that there is a God, but all the parts of the world and He himself are created. But he who wishes to contemplate these things more deeply will say that something is exceptionally said in the Scripture, a heaven characterized for God, in which God alone is; but I speak of God concerning the Trinity.

This heaven, far from being a place, is a property of essence for the created things, as these things are in the heavens. Take care lest, before the transgression, the devil, who finds himself below this heaven as in heaven, said, 'I will ascend into heaven, and above the stars of heaven I will set my throne' (Ps 113:24); for these things were said to him before he fell from heaven; indeed, this is also remembered as the cause of his fall. No one has ascended into this heaven except the one descending from heaven, since having been sent from there, he has come, saying, 'I have descended from heaven.' But also the Holy Spirit was sent from this heaven, which Peter says: 'Truly it has been announced to us through those who evangelized us by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven' (2 Pet 1:21). For the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit [are thus]. english: The preceding description of the heaven mentioned signifies a superiority and a state of being, if one may say so. None of those deadened by sin praises God (for a beautiful praise is not in the mouth of a sinner, Ps 113:25-26), nor do those descending into the tropical Hades become those who die the death following sin (for there is no one remembering God in death, Ps 114:6), nor anyone in Hades confessing himself.

Therefore, since they do not praise Him, we who live and partake of eternal life praise Him, concerning which the Savior says, 'And this is the eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and whom you sent, Jesus Christ' (John 17:3). The Lord himself protects those who, according to the commandment of Jesus, are childlike in turning and becoming, so that enemies do not attack them before the time of struggle. Just as He protects those who are such children, He humbled me, having set me against a struggle, as if I had ascended far above the age of children, and instead of being tested by many strong things, He made me; and just as He humbled me, so also He saved me, having clothed me with a strength surpassing the struggle and an invincible panoply.

Regarding this word, the Apostle says to the Corinthians, 'Having this, we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written: I believed, therefore I spoke; and we also believe, therefore we also speak' (2 Cor 4:13). By saying 'spirit of faith,' he signifies the being which is near from it, the spirit provided by God to the one having faith. 'I believed, therefore I spoke' is in accord with the heart, for it is believed in the heart unto righteousness, but with the mouth it is confessed unto salvation; for he says, 'If you confess the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved' (Rom 10:9). For by this one is immediately brought to the heart, for it is believed in the heart unto righteousness, and the following. You will also receive this understanding, and 'If you do not believe, you will not understand' (Acts 5:25); for first one believes, if he understands, and after this he speaks, as the Psalm says, 'I believed, therefore I spoke.' When, having believed, I spoke exceedingly and great things, then, seeing nothing of myself, I was greatly humbled. Such is that which is [said] by John concerning Jesus.

Regarding the saying, 'That He must increase and I must decrease,' John was not diminishing in terms of actual magnitude, but was comparing himself to the superiority of Jesus's teaching and way of life (John 3:30). He who said, after speaking from the beginning, that he had believed, 'I have become exceedingly humbled,' did not suffer this by a subtraction of honor, but by seeing the greater and above himself. If even the death of many signifies God, those who die with Christ and carry His death in the flesh, and who recognized how well to give thanks, will receive the cup of such a saving death, and he who receives it will drink it blamelessly, if he calls upon the name of the Lord to drink it bravely.

If we have said of the lesser ones that they call upon the name of the Lord, let it not trouble you now to receive the Lord while not yet perfect; for the saints, being blind, give the lesser things to themselves that they possess. For Moses and Samuel did not say of themselves, 'We called upon the Lord,' but it is said of others. The word concerning salvation is not complete unless the memory of the saved is also taken up. For having said in that [psalm] as the end of the shadow approaching, 'I will offer to You a sacrifice of thanksgiving' (Ps 116:1), he immediately calls all nations into eternity, just as these also offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving through the ages, after one nation and people has been cast away, since a sinful nation and people having become full of sins is tossed about. But after this nation and people has been cast away, the mercy of God has reached all, as a certain and strong thing for His mercy to become upon us. And because this has surpassed, 'The truth of the Lord remains forever' (Ps 117:2). For the truth accepted the shadow as an end and a lot, limiting it, but the truth itself, being eternal, will receive nothing that is nothing above it, but itself above all, in an incomparable excess. For indeed, as with a cause, He has given that the remaining truth remains forever. english: Truth is spoken of in the Savior and in the [psalm where] God sent His mercy and His truth and rescued my soul from the midst of troubles (Ps 117:1). Thus truth and the hope of the nations are one; therefore, having shone upon the human race, it calls all the nations and all the peoples, teaching [them] to give thanks to the Father who strengthens His mercy and makes His truth remain unto the age.

Since God is good and wills the repentance of the sinner rather than his death, you who are responsible for sin, by performing confession through repentance upon him, you will have him forgiving those for whom you confess. For His mercy is found inseparable from Him unto the age, since it is always [so]; in His mercy, not only now but also formerly from the beginning, all those having experience of His goodness confess to Him.

A righteous man having become in affliction does not so much entreat to be outside of it, but how to bravely and cheerfully bear it (Ps 117:5–9). For indeed the one being distressed in the stadium against opponents does not wish the contest to pass by him, lest he become exhausted, but entreats the trainer to cooperate with him, so that, strengthening himself against those advancing toward the opponent, he may win with the hope of victory and the glory of the crown which is given through which the crown is granted.

And it is possible to say different things concerning mortals, 'I shall not fear what man shall do to me' (Ps 117:9), but concerning invisible enemies, 'I also shall see my enemies' (Ps 117:8); for some enemies are even the men who rise up against us, waging war against us and setting themselves against us lethally. And if 'I shall not fear what man shall do to me' is referred to the devil, because 'Man has made this,' it is evident what it is: to sow the weeds (Matt 13:25) and 'But you...'

source_text: σοφιστικῶς κατεσκευασμένα ἀπατηλὰ δόγματα. ̓Εκύκλωσάν με ὡσεὶ μέλισσαι κηρίον, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς· ὁμοιότητα φέρει πρὸς τὰς μελίσσας κηφήνων τὸ γένος· αυ ται γὰρ εἰ καὶ μείζους τῶν μελισσῶν τῷ ο γκῳ τυγχάνουσιν, ἀλλ' ου ν γε ἀπατῶσι τοὺς ἀνιστορήτους ὡς ου σαι μέλισσαι· ου τε δὲ μελισσουργοῦσιν η πλάττουσι κηρὸν οὐδ' αυ κέντρον ε χουσι τὸ ἀλεξοῦν τὰ βλάπτειν ἐπιχειροῦντα τὸν κηρόν. ἐκ τοῦ ἐναντίου δὲ ἐσθίοντες τὸ μέλι ἐκπολεμοῦσι κατ' αὐτῶν τὰς μελίσσας ὡς χρησαμένας κατ' αὐτῶν τῷ ἰδίῳ κέντρῳ σωρηδὸν ἀναιρεῖν τοὺς κηφῆνας ὡς λυμηναμένους τῷ καρπῷ αὐτῶν. ἐστὶν ου ν πρὸς ἀλληγορίαν ἡ μελισσουργοῦσα καὶ κηροπλαστοῦσα μέλιττα ἡ τιμήσασα τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ σοφίαν ἐκκλησία, η ς ἐργάτιδος ου σης ποθεινῆς τυγχανούσης καὶ ἐπιδόξου τοὺς πόνους βασιλεῖς καὶ ἰδιῶται πρὸς ὑγίειαν προσφέρονται· καίπερ ου σης τῇ ῥώμῃ ἀσθενοῦς τῷ τὸ κήρυγμα αὐτῆς μὴ ἐν πειθοῖς ἀνθρωπίνης σοφίας λόγοις ει ναι, ο μως δ' ε χει τὸ κέντρον ἐν ἀποδείξει πνεύματος καὶ δυνάμεως θεοῦ τῆς πίστεως τὸν λόγον ε χουσα, ὡς καὶ ἀναιρεῖν κηφήνων δίκην τὰς αἱρέσεις διχοτομοῦσα αὐτὰς ἐλέγχῳ τῆς ἀληθείας. καὶ μία μὲν ἡ τιμήσασα τὴν σοφίαν μέλισσα, πολλαὶ δὲ αἱ ἀποστᾶσαι τοῦ τιμᾶν τὴν σοφίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ μέλισσαι ἀλλ' ὡς μέλισσαι τυγχάνουσαι, α ς ει ναι κηφῆνας λέγων οὐχ ἁμαρτήσεις κυκλούσας ὡς κηρίον ἐπὶ τῷ ἀναλῶσαι τὸ περὶ αὐτὸ μέλι καὶ ἐκκαυθείσας ὡσεὶ πῦρ ἐν ἀκάνθαις. ἐξάπτουσι γὰρ οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν αἱρέσεων καὶ τὸ τῶν αἰσχρῶν καὶ ἐπιθυμιῶν πῦρ, ῃ φησιν ὁ Παῦλος Τὰ γὰρ κρυφῆ γινόμενα ὑπ' αὐτῶν αἰσχρόν ἐστι καὶ λέγειν. ἀκάνθας δὲ τὰς ἡδονὰς ἡρμήνευσε τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον. Ομως δὲ εἰ καὶ ἐκύκλωσαν τὸν σοφὸν ὡσεὶ κηρίον μέλισσαι καὶ ἐξεκαύθησαν ὡσεὶ πῦρ ἐν ἀκάνθαις, ἀλλ' ου ν αὐτὸς τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου ἠμύνατο αὐτούς. οὐ γὰρ ἀζήμιος μόνον ε μεινεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ καθεῖλεν αὐτῶν πάντα σοφιστικὸν λογισμόν, ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶν υ ψωμα ἐπαιρόμενον 231 κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐπείπερ τὰ ο πλα αὐτοῦ οὐ σαρκικὰ ἀλλὰ δυνατὰ τῷ θεῷ οὐχ ε τερα ο ντα τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ προσηγορίας ἠμύνατο αὐτούς. 1075 Ps 117,14b Γενόμενος εἰς σωτηρίαν ὁ κύριος οὐκ ἀρχὴν οὐσιώσεως δέχεται· ἀΐδιος γὰρ καὶ αἰώνιός ἐστι. γίνεται δὲ εἰς σωτηρίαν κατὰ τὸ ἀναλαμβάνειν σχέσιν τὴν πρὸς τοὺς σῳζομένους. ο θεν πάντα γεγονέναι τὸν Χριστὸν λέγοντα ταῦτα ὑποβάλλεται τῇ διανοίᾳ· οὐ γὰρ γέγονε θεὸς λόγος οὐκ ἀλήθεια οὐ σοφία οὐχ υἱός, ἀλλὰ γέγονεν ἡμῖν σοφία, οὐχ ἁπλῶς γενόμενος σοφία ἀλλ' αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἡμῖν δικαιοσύνη καὶ ἁγιασμὸς καὶ ἀπολύτρωσις. ω ν γὰρ ἁπλῶς καὶ ἀϊδίως ταῦτα ἡμῖν γεγονέναι κατὰ ἀναφορὰν τὴν πρὸς ἡμᾶς λέγεται· ου τω καὶ χριστὸν καὶ κύριον πεποίηκεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεός, χριστὸν μὲν τουτέστι βασιλέα καὶ ἱερέα τοῖς βασιλευομένοις καὶ τοῖς ὑπὲρ ω ν προσάγει τὰς θυσίας. ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς δουλεύειν ἐθέλουσιν αὐτῷ κύριον καὶ καθόλου τὰ σχετικῶς περὶ αὐτοῦ λεγόμενα ου τω διανοούμενος οὐκ ἀσεβήσεις. 1076 Ps 117,15a Σκηνὰς δὲ δικαίων νοήσεις τὰς παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ μονὰς κατὰ τὴν ἀπόδοσιν τῶν ἐπαγγελιῶν, περὶ ω ν ὁ σωτήρ φησιν Οταν ἐκλίπῃ (δηλονότι ὁ μαμωνᾶς), δέξονται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς. ἐν ταύταις ταῖς σκηναῖς πάντες εἰσὶν οἱ δίκαιοι ἀγαλλιώμενοι· τετύχασι γὰρ τῶν προσδοκωμένων ἀγαθῶν. ο θεν καλῶς ει ρηται Φωνὴ ἀγαλλιάσεως καὶ ἐξομολογήσεως ἐν σκηναῖς δικαίων, ἀποδρασάσης λύπης καὶ στεναγμοῦ. Εἰ δὲ καὶ τὰ σώματα τῶν δικαίων σκηνὰς αὐτῶν ἐρεῖς ἀφθάρτων καὶ πνευματικῶν ἀποδοθεισῶν αὐτοῖς, οὐκ ἀμφισβητήσεις ὡς καὶ ἐν ταύταις ταῖς σκηναῖς αὐτῶν φωνὴ ἀγαλλιάσεως καὶ ἐξομολογήσεως ε σται. Φέρεται Φωνὴ ἀγαλλιάσεως καὶ σωτηρίας τῷ ὡς ἐν ταῖς προειρημέναις σκηναῖς ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι τοὺς δικαίους ἐπὶ τῷ αἰωνίαν σωτηρίαν ἀπειληφέναι οὐκ α λλην ου σαν τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς. 1077 Ps 117,15b–17 Αυ τη τοιγαροῦν ἐποίησε δύναμιν τοῖς μετειληφόσιν αὐτοῦ, ὡς ε καστον φάναι Πάντα ἰσχύω ἐν τῷ ἐνδυναμοῦντί με Χριστῷ. αυ τη τὸν μετέχοντα ὑψοῖ καὶ μετεωρίζει, ὡς φαιδρότερον καὶ μειζόνως ὑπὸ τῆς δεξιᾶς κυρίου δυναμωθέντα καὶ δεύτερον εἰπεῖν ∆εξιὰ κυρίου ἐποίησε δύναμιν. διό φησιν Οὐκέτι θνήξομαι τὸν ἑπόμενον τῇ κακίᾳ θάνατον, ἀλλὰ ζήσομαι μετασχὼν τῆς ἐναντίας τοῦ πονηροῦ θανάτου ζωῆς ἐπὶ τῷ ἐκδιηγήσασθαι τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς ἐμὲ γενόμενα θαυμαστὰ ε ργα. ποιεῖ δὲ δύναμιν ἡ δεξιὰ αὐτοῦ ἐν παντὶ τῷ δεξιὰ φρονοῦντι καὶ πράττοντι ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑψοῖ αὐτὸν ὡς καὶ δευτέραν γενέσθαι ἐν αὐτῷ τῆς προτέρας δυνάμεως δύναμιν ἐφ' ῃ ἀθανασίαν κεκτημένος ἐρεῖ τὸ Οὐκ ἀποθανοῦμαι, ἀλλὰ
english: Deceptive doctrines constructed sophistically. They have surrounded me like bees [surround] wax, and the following: the genus of wax-makers is similar to bees; for although they are greater than bees in size, they do not deceive the unreasoning ones as bees do; nor do they make honey or mold wax, nor do they have a sting to repel those attempting to harm the wax. But eating the honey from the opposite, they wage war against the bees, just as those having used their own sting to safely destroy the wax-makers as having defiled their fruit.

The honey-making and wax-molding bee is not an allegory, but the Church which has honored the wisdom of God, whose labors, though not of a precious or glorious kind, are offered by kings and laymen for health; even though she is weak in strength, her preaching is not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but she possesses the sting in the demonstration of the spirit and power of God, having the word of faith, just as she destroys heresies like wax-makers, dividing them by the reproof of the truth. And one is the bee that has honored the wisdom, but many are those that depart from honoring the wisdom of God—not bees, but those who are like bees; he is not sinning, saying [they are] wax-makers surrounding like wax to consume the honey and having been burned like fire in thorns. For those from the heresies and the fire of shameful things and desires escape, as Paul says, 'For what is shameful to speak of is made known by them' (2 Cor 13:1). And the Gospel interpreted the thorns as pleasures.

However, even if they surrounded the wise one like wax, bees, and were burned like fire in thorns, they did not defend themselves by the name of the Lord alone. For he did not only remain undefiled, but he also cast down all their sophistical reasoning, and every high thing boasting itself against the knowledge of God, since his works are not fleshly but are powerful in God, not being defeated by the approach of God. The Lord becoming salvation does not receive a beginning of being; for he is both eternal and everlasting. And he becomes for salvation according to the taking up of the relation...

Regarding those being saved, God submits to the mind these things said by the one declaring that all things have become Christ; for it has not become [that] God is Word, not truth, not wisdom, not Son, but he has become to us wisdom, not merely having become wisdom, but this himself to us is righteousness and sanctification and redemption. For the reference to these things having become to us simply and eternally is said according to the relation toward us; thus God has made him both Christ and Lord, Christ meaning king and priest to those who reign and to those for whom he offers the sacrifices, but also to those who wish to serve him as Lord, and in general, the things said concerning him are not thought to be impieties.

You will understand the dwellings of the righteous, which are alone with the Father according to the fulfillment of the promises, concerning which the Savior says: 'When [Mammon] departs' (meaning that), 'they will receive you into the eternal dwellings' (Ps 117:15a). In these dwellings all the righteous are rejoicing; for they have attained the promised good things. Thus it is well said, 'A voice of joy and confession in the dwellings of the righteous' (Ps 117:15b), with sorrow and sighing fleeing away. And if you say that even the bodies of the righteous, their dwellings, will be returned to them incorruptible and spiritual, you will not dispute that in these dwellings of theirs there will also be a voice of joy and confession. A voice of joy and salvation is brought forward, as the righteous rejoice in the aforementioned dwellings having received the eternal salvation, not different from eternal life.

He has thus made power for those partaking of him, as it is possible to say, 'I can do all things in Christ who strengthens me' (Phil 4:13). He thus lifts up and exalts the one partaking, as one having been strengthened by the right hand of the Lord more brightly and more greatly, and to say a second time, 'The right hand of the Lord made power' (Ps 117:16). Therefore he says, 'I shall no longer die, he who follows the evil death, but I shall live' (Ps 118:17), partaking of the life opposite the evil death, in order to recount the wonderful works of God that have become in me. And his right hand makes power in everyone who thinks and acts according to the right, but also lifts him up as a second power in him of the former power, through which having obtained immortality, he says, 'I shall not die, but...'

english: I shall live, and the following. The gates were formerly the law and the prophets through which Israel entered toward God (Ps 117:19-20), but now the gate is faith, through which we are more closely brought near, being testified to by the law and the prophets. Into this understanding one should take also that which is said in Jeremiah: 'Stand in the paths and ask for the ancient well-trodden ways of the Lord, and examine what is the good way, and walk in it, and you will find cleansing for your souls.' For if someone stands here in the many paths—I mean the private virtues—he will examine those worn down from eternity by the saints, in order to know who, after this, according to the theory, is the good way; he who walks finds cleansing for his soul, having cleansed it through obedience to the truth.

Understand this (Ps 117:18-20): he who is being educated by divine discipline and most profitably by the Lord does not fall into the death that holds those who sin. For death encounters those who are uneducated, but he who is being educated by the Lord, having excellent thought and practice, is not handed over to the death that receives those handed over to the passions of dishonor and unproven mind. When the name of righteousness is being accused against every moral virtue, its gates—the private virtues—must be spoken of, into which those who are through asceticism and care for them enter, knocking at them. And they enter upon confessing those things which they have done outwardly, being of the gates of righteousness. He says 'into them' and not 'through them'; for one must not bypass the activities of the virtues, but must travel through them. But having entered into the gates of righteousness and having confessed within them, another gate is shown to be superior and more honorable, the one according to the theory of the truth, into which those having perfected righteousness enter, so as to be called righteous as a nickname from it.

I will praise you immediately having opened to me the gates of righteousness, and I thank you that you heard me and received the petition and provided salvation (Ps 117:21). For every day of sensation occurring under the sun, the sun may rise over the earth; the day shown under the sun of righteousness being the Lord was constructed, which they also show to one another (Ps 117:24).

english: Regarding His distance, some find Him coming near to them (Draw near to God and He will draw near to you [Ps 117:27bc]), while those who are distanced are not departing locally but, as I have previously said, by relationship; for God is far from the ungodly (Ps 117:27). And not in this way: they are pruning the shoots and the fruits just as they bear them.

In these things, not finding [them], establish a feast extending until the horns of the spiritual altar, from which, having taken a coal with tongs, the other of the seraphim is sent to the prophet to cleanse him and to take away his iniquities and his sins. But to whom is it commanded to establish a feast—the teachers and priests? Perhaps you will even say to the angels. But to do what is necessary and to think the truth is a feast established according to the guidance of God. This has especially much room among those who have cast off oldness in order to become a new planting.

And since the Passover is fulfilled in the month of the new [moons], it is possible to conceive that anyone passing from wickedness and the sensible things to virtue and the intelligible things, being renewed, prunes, so as to celebrate and to bring forward spiritual sacrifices, as those showing the altar to be royal by its horns. And if these things were said concerning our feast of the weeks, they would not be lacking truth (Ps 117:28-29).

He who is thanking God through the Psalm for having made such great and so many blessings proclaims: 'You are my God, and I will confess to you; you are my God, and I will exalt you' (Ps 118:2-3). Glorifying, theologizing you, I say: 'You have done wonderful things in me; for having exalted me and having made strength, so that I might not die but living, I might recount your works.' And second, I will confess that you heard my petitions and became my salvation. Having learned through experience your great mercy and your goodness, and exhorting others, I say to many, proclaiming: 'Confess to the Lord, what is good, what has mercy extending into the age, according to how he shows mercy by his much goodness' (Ps 118:2a). For if even the words of God were to testify to Him and to His truth.

Blessed then are those searching out his testimonies and seeking him with all their heart, turning away from all human haste and approaching him through good works and right understanding. But the blessing is not for those who have gone [away], but for those who are going; even though those working lawlessness in his law have not gone, it is evident that they have never attempted to test the divine law as if it were among them; for whoever sins lawlessly, lawlessly he shall perish. Nor are they those who have never heard the divine teaching; for those who, after being initiated into this, stumble, are said to have sinned against the law and to be transgressors of it.

Then I shall not be ashamed in keeping all your commandments; not on one thing, but on all (Ps 118:6). For according to those commandments I do not look, I shall be ashamed (Ps 118:8b). For I am often abandoned for a little while for the sake of testing and my trial, having bravely endured circumstances to be benefited. But immediately, with your helping, having run the race, I shall be crowned; therefore, so that I may not be defeated by those striving mightily, do not leave me exceedingly. He who does not receive the words of God from above and hides them in his heart, so that having made his mind and purpose according to these, is without sin before God who sees the hidden, not only not committing adultery but not even reaching for the shameful thing (Ps 118:11).

The Son also agrees with what is set forth: if, having received the word of my commandment, you hide it with yourself, your intellect will obey wisdom. So that I may not be glorified for nothing having had your judgments performed, repay me the divine and blessed life, so that living according to it I may keep your words; for after remembering them, to keep them following (Ps 118:17). To this end you will take that which was said by Jesus: 'He who holds my commandments and keeps them' (John 14:15/21); for he who remembers them also keeps them, doing them as well. Another, saying 'judgments' instead of 'rights/statutes', did not explain it thus: 'God's rights always benefit, being truly good. Desiring them at all times, he has loved them, not wanting to do them out of grief or out of necessity, as those do...'

english: They do these things through fear of falling into punishment, but with desire and longing. For from this it will happen to bear all things soberly and courageously, not only the pleasant things but also the painful and unpleasant ones, and to go toward every diligent task with eagerness.

Since some reproach and belittle me for seeking your testimonies (Ps 118:22), you have removed the reproach and the belittling from me. How could these be removed? For the coming knowledge of the truth of those formerly reproaching and belittling me; and if this exists, they themselves will seek your testimonies.

Another scripture says, 'I have declared your ways' (Ps 118:26), meaning: the ways that lead to you are not other ways of virtues, O Lord; I have declared them practically with diligent intention and in appropriate works, and you heard me; therefore, toward those who obey I say, 'Teach me your statutes' (Ps 118:29).

He who will turn away from the way of unrighteousness and approaching the law of God wants to be perfected and established toward God, who brings the ends of good things (Ps 118:29). For as one having hated ignorance has had a longing for the opposing knowledge, so one who has turned himself from ignorance and approached by faith asks the teacher: 'Turn ignorance away from me and have mercy on me by your knowledge.'

The voice is not one who is conscious of sin, but of one suspecting, as in 'From my secret things cleanse me' (Ps 118:39). But I am confident in what you will remove, the suspected reproach, being convinced of what your judgments are, being full of kindness and love for mankind.

If it is possible to say all things about the spoken word, stand by; for he himself is both mercy and salvation of the Lord (Ps 118:41-42). Therefore, it is necessary for us to seek the mercy of the Lord, the salvation according to his mercy. For having been shown mercy and having been saved...
We answer those who previously reproached us as lacking the mercy and salvation of God (Ps 118:43-44).

I ask for insights, not merely such words; even if I sometimes fall into difficulties regarding providence and similar matters, I do not wish to give an answer that merely resolves the contradictions of those who wander, but rather, since you have opened my mouth with your own goodness, give me an interpretation of the truth through your word, so that the word of truth may not be entirely torn from my mouth, but that I may be able to speak somewhat regarding the unanswerable ones, saying: 'I have erred concerning your judgments, your examined and tested words; how do you judge and provide for men?' (Ps 118:51).

Do not let the word of truth depart vehemently from my mouth. For indeed, keeping your law will not only happen in this age but unto the age, the words of Jesus not passing away. We therefore keep God's law according to the image of things, previously kept by the Jews according to a shadow, to be kept for us according to the future good things unto the age of ages (Ps 118:51).
Regarding the heterodox who boast against the law by slandering it (Ps 118:53), I was intensely occupied with its keeping, and how much I was shaken in my assent to it, not enduring [the slander].

Since of the sinners some sin lawlessly, not even attempting the beginning of laws, and others transgress it while in law, discouragement seized me from the sinners who abandon God's law; for if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; and if one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it. And it is fitting to be grieved for our brothers who sin, what kind of people they are, and not to be divided against this holy one (Ps 118:58).

english: Fixing the heart upon this, he considers it having become pure, and through not staring intensely at it, he may be shown mercy according to the word of his teaching, if the spoken words are such. But how great is the one seeing the face of God. Jesus teach you, saying, 'Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God' (Matt 5:8).

And what are the ropes, namely the evil thoughts and the evil powers that subvert these, which they undertake to cast down the standing against God? But the zeal of those surrounding the righteous with ropes is unceasing, those who with rapid zeal remember the law. The same circumstances occurring to the righteous through the sinners can also be ropes for them; but the righteous, bearing these patiently, does not forget the law of God. And those who entangle ropes into sin through deceptive words; but if one remains sober, he does not forget the law of God (Ps 118:63).

Let us also consider the friend and companion, which says the Preacher, 'that if he falls, the one is to raise his companion' (Eccl 4:9-10). He does not at any time intend to say, 'I am a friend and companion to all who fear God and keep his commandments,' while he himself fears him and keeps his commandments.

If there is not kindness and severity concerning God according to the apostle, the kindness becomes for those standing in faith, but the severity for those having fallen away from it. Since the saint was confirmed in faith, 'Kindness, O God, you have done with your servant,' he says; but he says, wanting to present not through destruction the kindness of God with someone, but with the one serving him, whomsoever he may be. And 'according to your word' approaching implies that the kindness of the Lord becomes with someone with word and a logical cause. Therefore, he who wishes to know the logical and wise part of it, deserves no other teacher to be with him concerning it, so that he may learn with it both instruction and knowledge: instruction indeed the ethical, and knowledge the intellectual virtue of good things. And in Proverbs, 'Get instruction and not silver, and knowledge rather than tested gold' (Prov 4:7).

english: Regarding the mediator, the prophet says to him that the law of the divine mouth is good above all the pleasures of the world, which he showed through thousands of gold and silver. For contemplation, it must be said that silver stands for the word, and gold stands for the mind; for many thousands of such silver and gold are found in those who philosophize about the things of the world and heresies. Above all these things, the law of the mouth of God is good to the lover of the wisdom and truth of God, for those who attend to it alone receive the proper benefit.

Psalm 118:74: 'Understand and not thus: those fearing God are perfect, they not lacking anything; and such are found good, they do not lack fear.' Therefore they desire all to progress and to have benefit, and they rejoice over those things pleasing to God, imitating those in heaven who rejoice over the benefit of the penitents. It is also possible to take the inferior [understanding] regarding 'they shall be glad,' as it says: 'They shall see and be glad,' where the mind of the things said is such. 'Hoping in your words, I desire to become completely [one with you], I act and think according to your instruction'; and those fearing lest they fall into the punishment following the judgment which pursues sinners, they avoid evil. If those fearing you in this way are not able to see me, they shall be glad, no longer avoiding sins out of grief and necessity, but with zeal to take them up, hoping also themselves in your words.

Psalm 118:77a: Since the mercies of God are said to be not only here but also in many other places, one must watch lest the only-begotten and the Holy Spirit, the providers of life, are not [seen as] the mercies of God. And Father is said, according to the apostle's philosophy of the mercies.
Psalm 118:78a: Of a great man, he says: 'Unjustly I have transgressed against me.'

Psalm 118:81: 'My soul fails for the salvation of God, but the end of faith shall bring salvation'; for there remains no soul, setting aside the state through which the soul used to exist, but desiring the salvation of God and continuing in hope, the spirit and mind becoming [one] with his word. For the name of the soul does not declare its essence, but the relationship toward the communion of the body. But if it might pass over to incorporeal life and be uncorrupted...

Receiving bread and a spiritual body from a resurrection, the body which was formerly joined to it, corruptible and psychic in being possessed by a soul, shall become mind and spirit, leaving behind the divine salvation and being in spirit toward God through Him. And this is to deny oneself; for he who has denied himself will become one thing instead of another, not according to the underlying substance but according to that which makes it, sometimes soul, sometimes mind. For even if the evangelical sayings are exhortations toward martyrdom, they are not to be understood according to the aforementioned mystical word.

The word of God is a spiritual dew (Ps 118:83a), since dew and rain are often called; it cools my unbridled flame from passions and makes my flesh weak, as to bear the death of Jesus in it. Many attempt to interpret the divine writings of the Church and those outside it, both heretics and Jews and Samaritans (Ps 118:85), but not all speak well; for rare is the one possessing the grace from God for this, speaking of many things promised, but living not well and unlawfully. If they say anything, it is wandering and babbling; for a word cannot be vigorous, strong, and salutary in an unlawful soul.

Those pursuing righteousness and the teaching of Christ will healthily speak the aforementioned word (Ps 118:87a), and all the prophets also. And to be accomplished is in the earth, not the common dying, but that which was called into the material existence as earth, to come to an end in order to be done according to it. To live according to the word of God is to live with piety (Ps 118:88), not simply this sensory life. For having obtained this, he will be in well-being, as to guard the testimonies of the mouth of God testified and demonstrated by the word of God, which are in His mouth.

The day remains by Your ordinance (Ps 118:91a), as to circle regularly and uniformly according to the annual cycles, the day not deviating, never having toward night an ordinance of inequality or inequality. Just as from a great sickness, through certain medical helps, one has taken up health steadily and certainly through him of...

english: those who followed him
Turn away from evil and do good; for he who turns away from evil from every wicked way restrains his feet, so that having done good, he may guard the words of God (Ps 118:105).

The law is a lamp to those walking in the night before the rising of the sun of righteousness (Ps 118:106); just as the night has passed and the day has approached, they are illuminated not by a lamp but by the sun of the true light, so that it is possible to walk decorously during the day.

And to set [it] here and to define firmly signifies to stand fast, and to swear is not merely to name God, but to set this thing unchangeably and to guard it without transgression, performing the work of an oath by power (Ps 118:124).

Not as if, not having attained the petition, he approaches it again, but as having learned the ordinances of God according to a prior worthiness; as one who is spending time with them, desiring to contemplate them more greatly, he needs and always does this, so that he may reach the goal of their understanding (Ps 118:125).

Since, however, regarding the learning of the ordinances, various things are becoming [different], I will say this also concerning the knowledge of the testimonies: that through progress, their knowledge is always becoming ascended for the one spending time with their comprehension (Ps 118:127).

'Your mouth's law is more precious to me than ten thousands of gold and silver' (Ps 118:127), and 'Take instruction and do not forsake knowledge, which is tested above silver' (Prov 8:10); for wisdom is more excellent than precious stones, and every precious thing is not of equal value to it. Therefore it is also said to companions concerning it to Job: 'The balance of Ethiopia shall not equal it' (Job 28:15). These things are not said by comparison but in relation to the value of men.

He who has come to fulfill the law and all the prophets, making manifest the words contained in them (Ps 118:130), does this by fulfilling the prophecies, and does this by uncovering the law, so that it is seen no longer as letter and shadow but as spiritual. For thus the manifestation of the divine words that has occurred will prove the prophet to be sensible and will enlighten those called from the nations after Israel, who are infants in their weakness and have late or tardy come to a generation from faith. english: The wise one announced the law and the prophets, saying, 'The revelation of your words makes me understand'; but he did not see these things in a prophetic spirit, for whoever possesses their understanding desired that which was to be revealed before the coming of Christ.

He is worthy to see and learn the shining forth of the Savior this time, saying to the Savior about it, 'Let your face shine, so that whoever seeing you may see you' (Ps 118:135). For he himself says about himself, 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9). For since this exists, he says, it will be possible for me to learn your ordinances. And to learn that is to walk in them, not according to the flesh but according to grace.

Therefore your judgment is straight, because you are just, judging all those who received your judgments straight according to the canons of righteousness, since I commanded truth and righteousness intensely (Ps 118:137). For I commanded your divine writings to men, not only the new ones but also the old ones, being justice according to ethics and truth intensely, that is, being precise according to the view of things according to which I commanded us to make judgments, so that we might judge the great and the small, judging a just judgment intensely, they are truth and righteousness (Ps 118:138).

Therefore that word so ignited is made to him intensely loved by something, making him a servant of God burning in the spirit (Ps 118:140). Such a person, when the Scriptures are made clear by Jesus, is amazed in heart, as saying according to the [Road to] Emmaus, 'Did not our heart burn within us when he opened the Scriptures to us?' (Luke 24:32).

For he is unswerving and unchangeable, never having or not having righteousness, being the source and generator of it (Ps 118:142); and his word is truth, being truth to those hearing for all eternity, not being such a human word; for the word of human wisdom, to become in glory...

Being false, after the truth has been revealed, he will be convicted of being false (Ps 118:144). I have given you testimonies not for a short time, but they prove to be useful righteousness for eternity, justifying the one who possesses them by drawing near to them.

First, in an unseasonable time—that is, what is called night in this present age, often called day as if for the coming age, according to 'The night has passed, and the day is near' (Ps 118:147)—but the perceptive powers of his eyes, acting as eyes, reach forward toward the righteousness coming from the rising of the sun. Therefore, having been enlightened and finding himself in the light, he meditates on the commandments of God, which cause him to fly to be lifted up and to approach the true light nakedly, so that he may find himself no longer in an unseasonable time, but in a peak and midday light.

Another scripture says: 'And all your ways are truth' (Ps 118:151), clearly meaning those paths leading to Him; for the end of all these ways is He who said, 'I am the way, and the truth, and the life' (John 14:6). He who has reached the goal of these ways is in truth, having both it and its Father within himself. And since He also approaches the sinners in another way, He is near to them; and all His ways are truth, for as one travels them, He performs the examination and judgment of their affairs.

The testimonies were established by God so that no one would be able to shake or overturn them; for your word is wisdom, and your Son is their foundation. Therefore, presenting their unassailable and unshakeable nature, He says, 'My words will never pass away, even if heaven and earth pass away' (Matt 24:35).
Often, when 'the beginning' is taken in a certain sense, we say the beginning is the truth of the words of God, as that which is first. For to make it known...

english: The legal and prophetic writers and even the words of God's new covenant are given naked of types. For, exercising themselves through them and being led according to their spiritual will, we reach the point of meeting face to face with the truth. If the beginning of those bearing them is the truth itself and they become so because of it, and if God's words also bear toward the truth (for they are spoken because of it), it is rightly said that their beginning is the truth. Since also that which exists in some is called a beginning by another meaning, and truth exists in God's words, they are themselves true by that, and because of this they are called their beginning. Similarly, the true state is held to be upon the true words, by which the divinely-breathed scriptures—which are the words of God—are said to be from self-truth. And because of this, it is right to say that the truth is the beginning of God's words.

And what is it? Since the Lord says, 'I am the truth,' the word of God is also that itself; he says to the Father, 'Your word is truth,' who becomes with each prophet. And likewise: those established according to the truth, being truth-receivers, become the beginning of God's words. Just as the truth was the beginning of your words, so all your judgments of justice are found indestructible and shown forever (Ps 118:161c).

Cowardice is twofold: one part is the irrational regarding the emotional part of the soul, the other is the logical established regarding the heart and the intellect, not of reason, and perhaps it can pertain to the same divine fear. Throughout his life, the righteous man, being enlightened, will be in a perfect day not intercepted by night and will praise God sevenfold (Ps 118:164), having become transcendent to be separated from the world that has become in days of exile, even having been in God's paradise, having contemplated the word of God's creation and providence, will confess the judgments of the justice of God, according to the judgments of each varied creation and providence. If he also awaits the Savior, as it is said, 'All flesh shall see the salvation of God' (Ps 118:166), following this he loves the commandments of God.
And he has expected salvation, so that both his practice is pure and his expectation is contemplative, always expecting and contemplating that God has come to seek and to save the lost.

He prays for such a worthy condition to be tested, certain and unshakeable, as if to enter before the Lord. 'And I will know if my worthiness enters before you, if I am rescued by you according to your word and your wisdom' (Ps 118:170). For He, being above all passions, irrational and the evils working from irrationality, having departed from them, is rescued by God according to His word.

'Oh that you would teach me, so that I might act from it and know them clearly; I would bring to you a thankful hymn from my lips, O Lord, of your man' (Ps 118:171). If the impulse of hymnody to God is clearly the beginning of its nourishment, it constitutes full theology.

'Your various commandments are instructions; they all possess the virtues of those who are wise, the general virtue being to follow the particular virtues, as one possessing the one perfectly possesses all' (Ps 118:172). 'I utter your word with my lips toward your man' (Ps 118:173a). But the word concerning righteousness is uttered principally not by voice alone, not by merely bringing it forth, but also by works and by practical intention, being corrected according to the right word.

'Let your hand be done to save me' (Ps 118:174a) does not signify here the generation of it according to essence, but the relation toward the ones being saved. The same thought is carried in 'Become for me a protector toward God'. The path of the one longing for the salvation of God is the one who has the study of the law as his desire, pre-sounding his arrival here. By 'law' he calls here the ancient and divine Scripture.

'Since remembering your judgments and being set apart, I turn away from the death that follows sin' (Ps 118:175). Not merely sinning, but performing those things, which follow the living of the soul and the praising of you thankfully, through which you provide it with immortal life. Since remembering your judgments, I turn away from the death following sin by not sinning; my soul shall live, having worked out those of life and praising the thankful ones, through which you provide it with immortal life.

english: Having lost a sheep from the hundred, the Savior comes seeking it, having left the ninety-nine in the wilderness; the human race has gone astray through Adam's transgression. The human race is the lost sheep from the hundred, while the rational things that do not stumble remain part of creation in the desert, staying high in virtue and truth, except for man who has gone into error.

Therefore, like the sheep, but rather a part of it, [the Psalmist says]: 'I have gone astray; seek me, your servant; for you came to seek and save the lost; seek me so that you may find me ready for this; for I have longed for your commandments' (Ps 119). It is to be understood that he in the Jerusalem temple has fifteen steps, and standing on each of them, those appointed to sing hymns were saying an ode. Therefore, the number of odes coincided with the steps. The arrangement concerning the odes and those singing them on each step of the temple lies in the Chronicles.

You shall understand the temple of God to be a holy, intelligible, and spiritual thing—the theology—and the steps to be the stages of progress. He who has ascended to the second step of the temple begins to be transformed into perfection, no longer thinking of something lowly. Therefore, he says he has lifted the eyes of the intellect toward the height. Thus, the ode of the second step has attained a familiar number. For the one hundred and twentieth limits the perfection of human life.

Indeed, it has been said concerning men after the flood: 'Their days shall be [one hundred and twenty]' (Gen 6:3). Thus also Moses, the great hierophant and servant of God, having perfected human life into one hundred and twenty years, describes his own life, setting forth his own life as a pattern for those under him who receive the laws. It can also be strongly understood regarding the exodus: the exodus of God guarding from evil for one turning away from evil, and likewise the exodus of one guarding the doing of the good, an exodus from the sensible toward the intelligible and spiritual. He who...

He who stretches himself forward toward those before him does not forget them, nor does he run back again. For he who hastens toward the prize of the higher calling goes toward the higher things. Therefore, having begun the ascent toward the temple, he does not return after having traveled; having ascended to the third degree, he does not even depart from the flight of the soul, but, having received a vision, he hastens toward that which he is being urged to lead the entrance of, being in good spirit.

Those having firmly established the feet of their own souls previously in the courts of Jerusalem (Ps 121:2–4), have a desire also to ascend to the temple. And the most sharp-witted theology is the temple, while the partial contemplations are the courts of the vision of peace, the specific virtues that occur. The vision of the aforementioned peace, having begun to be transformed, becomes as a city built by the Lord, and its participation consists of the same aforementioned courts, in which the feet of the firm ones are standing. And it is not a low-lying thing, but exists in some height, so that the citizen who wishes to become of it does not descend, but ascends toward it.

And indeed, the various ranks of the saved, having the choice of confession, ascend there as watches of the Lord, having been well testified by the Lord to ascend and having confessed, and they increase in zeal and progress, doing these things, Israel. David the savior has said many things (Ps 121:5); therefore, because it is from the seed of David, it is according to the flesh, and because it is sufficiently by hand, it is so; for David is interpreted as being 'capable by hand.' For how is he not capable by hand, he who performs wondrous powers? This is the church of David, in which thrones are seen for judgment, upon which the apostles sit judging the twelve tribes of Israel. For the faith and the citizenship of each apostle is a throne of his kingdom, judging and condemning those who have not conformed to what is prophesied in the divine scriptures, nor believed in those whom he made and taught with words.

english: Jerusalem, because she reigns with power, has become peaceful, having previously been at war with enemies whom she overcomes by her might, finding tranquility in her high towers. For the great towers in the walls are being constructed for the purpose of watching for the coming enemies. For among the Syrians, large houses are called heavy dwellings, and some, having taken height upon the walled cities, having their position, are called high towers. Therefore, Jerusalem, having used her own power which is from God, has subjected those who oppose her; she will make peace, and tranquility will follow in her high towers.

If, however, in allegory, the high towers are those who, through the height of the commonwealth and the vision of the truth, not only watch for the enemies coming for war but also cast them down from on high in reproofs. According to the vision, he who is born from God, doing righteousness and believing that Jesus is the Christ, has brothers who perform the same things and believe, and neighbors who approach through the doing of righteousness and the faith of Jesus Christ.

But since of both these ranks, of his brothers and of his neighbors, I say that Jerusalem, who is to be given, says she speaks peace and is peaceful (Ps 122:8,9), I wish for them, both the brothers and the neighbors of the fatherland, but since they seek the goods of the Lord their God, seeking the truly good things for Jerusalem. For he says concerning the one who began to ascend (Ps 122:2), since seeking the good things for Jerusalem, the keeping of the divine commandments and the right understanding of the true faith.

It is possible for slaves having eyes to take into the hands of masters the nations which are being managed under the angels, according to how the nations stood according to the number of the angels of God; but the circumcision assembly having eyes, a little girl into the hands of the mistress, a little girl because she is called a spirit of slavery; but her mistress, calling the unblemished and spotless church of God, no one stumbles. But we do not have [our eyes] in the hands of those masters, but we approach to the Lord our God for mercy.

And [it] shows mercy to us (Ps 123:4a). The Ara does not speak in a way that is merely formal, but in a way that is collective. An unsubstantial gift is one that is possible to receive without Christ sustaining it. If someone signifies evil as an unsubstantial gift, it must be said that evil is called unsubstantial because it lacks essence and its own subsistence; for it does not exist as a substance in those who are acting, not having its own nature.

Just as the mountain of Zion is unshakable and immovable (for the Word of God is [it]), so also those trusting in God have an immovable standing, imitating Him as they hasten to be. For the upcoming text is not said regarding the sensible mountain, similarly to all those mountains that are steadfast, but regarding that [mountain] about which the Spirit commands the prophet, saying, 'Ascend upon a high mountain, O you who preach Zion.' For Zion, being interpreted as the watchtower of the holy Church's contemplation of good things, is the high mountain; and regarding the mountain of the heavenly Zion, it is said, 'But you have come to the mountain of Zion and to the city of the living God, Jerusalem the heavenly' (Ps 125:2). Let us therefore establish the trust toward God, so as to chance upon both blessedness and the other promises, as the prophecy exhorts us: 'And having trusted in the Lord, He will lift you up upon the good things of the earth' (Ps 124:1). For the beginning of being lifted up upon the good things of the earth of the living and gentle ones is to have trusted in Him.

As for the Church, it is seen being enriched in the 'Shine, shine, Jerusalem, Jerusalem built as a city.' Therefore, he who thinks perfectly and genuinely that the things of the Church will dwell in it forever will not be shaken, nor will he be removed from this habitation, having received the things to be practiced and thought about with certainty and immovability. And it will be said specifically that he dwells in it forever, the living one and the believing one in the Lord, who shall not die forever, having here received the pledge of eternal life. But if he should ever become negligent, as if it were possible through attention and desire for the good, the habitation will be moved; for this reason it says in Proverbs, 'A righteous man will not be moved forever' (Prov 10:25). english: High doctrines of truth, distinct laws and ecclesiastical canons, and with these all the saints—not only those before the epidemic but also those after it—for each of these is a circle concerning the church, so that from all of them a continuous and inseparable circle has come to be in the midst of the church.

And with these the announcements can be made, placing around those who fear the Lord the mountains that surround Jerusalem. But greater than the security of the mountains exists for the people dwelling in Jerusalem, through whom especially the one dwelling in it is not shaken for ever, the Lord becoming a circle around him. And the Lord becomes a circle not locally and bodily, limiting himself within certain bounds, but participating with them and being with all of them, not only according to the present age but also the coming one.

Regarding the rod, indeed there is a purpose to strike, to stretch out the hands of the righteous against lawlessness; but the will of the Lord is for the righteous to stretch out their hands toward righteousness, lifting them up piously without anger or inner deliberation (Ps 124:3). Good are those who have been benefited by the mindset of virtue and are straight in heart, those who truly and rightly think the things of piety (Ps 124:4). Yet these differ not in their essence but in their way of thinking. For those dwelling in Jerusalem unshakeably are all good and straight in heart, being both active and knowing. And God does good to them, giving them good things as they ask him: an addition of faith and of the rest of virtue, along with the provision of participation in divine gifts, in order to bring them into the heavenly promises and the kingdom of heaven (Ps 124:5a-b). 'He will deliver,' he says, meaning to have let go of desires toward uncleanness and toward passions of dishonor, and to stop making an unproven mind do what is not fitting. And he says also in the Psalms...
according to the inclinations of their hearts

english: Those striving for the care of life give to those with them the bread of pain, eating it constantly. Therefore they are deprived of the beloved of God, those who advise moderately that reaching the Lord is the end and providence.

If the beloved of God, those raising themselves toward piety, do not despise this, but instead a spirit becomes for them a private rest, having been turned and having changed from this life, with watchfulness being maintained according to the common way of living, then those previously mentioned eat the bread of pain. All their striving is done in vain, rising and standing up after sitting, and having sleep, sitting, standing, and rising up become to them useless. For they were not able to do these things not in vain, nor to eat the bread of pain, if they had given attention to the beloved of God before receiving the spirit from God.

And those who seem to go toward godliness, if they thought they were being enlightened by themselves, rise in vain; for it is not fitting that it be said of those who do not say, 'My spirit rises to you, O God, through the night.' But they also rise in vain for the energy of good things, sitting and resting again, thinking they are doing this not from God but from themselves. But the one who confesses this is from God says to the Lord, 'You have known my seat and my rising.' And it is necessary to have joy and gladness, eating the bread that supports the heart of man; they eat it with pain from grief and necessity, but not approaching its use cheerfully. Therefore, they are altogether incomplete and do all things in vain.

And the former inheritance of Israel was made; for a portion of his inheritance is Israel; he was the firstborn son of God, saying, 'Israel is my firstborn son' (Ps 126:3). And all were sons by chance through a concordant and united will according to one law of life. But second after them are the sons concerning whom it was said by the Father to the Savior, 'I will make you heirs in my place, and I will give you an inheritance.' And from both of the two inheritances, one has become, which the Spirit says, showing it in the Son, 'Behold, the inheritance of the Lord is the Son.'
Indeed, all possess the spirit of adoption and are born from God to practice righteousness. And a reward is this, being the fruit of the womb of the Lord who has come to visit.

For it is said to her by Elizabeth, 'Blessed is the fruit of your womb' (Luke 1:42). And 'fruit of the womb' is the name for that which is not from a man, but from Mary alone, through the Holy Spirit having come upon her and the power of the Most High having overshadowed her. For those who have received seed from the fathers are those fruits; for it is said to David, 'From the fruit of your loins I will set [someone] upon your throne' (2 Sam 7:12), teaching him that his kingdom shall not fail like that of Saul, but that this shall be directed from his succession. And if the Son can also be the fruit of the father's womb, it follows, as [it is said], 'From the womb before the morning star you were born, visit [them].'

Who is the powerful one, the Savior, who is able to send the arrows of wisdom and truth sufficiently to wound for love? For it has been written, 'Your arrows are unavailing' (Ps 126:4). Similarly, those who are born of the sons of the stretched-out ones, those born of the holy men, are archers. And those who are stretched-out do not consist of all the dust of material things and soil, having sent forth by a rational movement a discerning soul capable of following the sequence of the dogmas.

And because of this, the Word, seeing peace and exhorting toward it, entreats, saying, 'Shake off your dust, Jerusalem.' Since the young ones, being stretched-out in the ancestral tradition of the Hebrews, are called and are capable for war, as we learn from Ezra, it is fitting that those who have put on the new man should stretch out the old man from themselves through his deeds, becoming imitators of the Powerful through their deeds, and through their hands being called to the word, they possess the arrows to strike the unavailing words. And the sayings of Ezra concerning the stretched-out ones are thus: 'And it came to pass from that day that half of those who were stretched-out were doing the work, and half of them were resisting, with spears and shields and bows and breastplates, and the leaders behind all the men of Judah who were building on the wall, and the...'

english: Next, through the spoken words, we understand that the sons of those stretching themselves out to build the house of the Lord hold stones and swords and other weapons, as with one hand doing the work of the building, and with the other throwing stones to hinder those wishing to stop the construction of the divine house.

For the divine teachers strive in each soul being educated to build for God and to fight against thoughts and evil powers attempting to obstruct the growth of the building. He blesses the man who, because he has preserved that which remains according to the image of God, has had his desire fulfilled from the arrows of the Mighty (Ps 126:5). For having been directed toward the desire of good things by them, he has been shown blessed. And possessing unashamed and undaunted boldness in the gate of the beneficial entrance, he speaks without being shamed by the enemies, who were striving to be obstacles to the fulfillment of desire and to the building.

And it is no wonder that he has blessed a man singularly; he has blessed in the plural, that those speaking in the gate shall not be shamed; for the word is not about one, but about everyone who has fulfilled his desire from the arrows (Ps 127:2). And in another way, if they nourish their own soul with virtue, so as to be according to God, desirable foods and joyful for the soul. He who does not fear the Lord eats the labors of his fruit, but he who loves him as perfect will eat the bread, the heavenly one, according to 'Blessed is he who eats bread in the kingdom of heaven' (Ps 127:3). And he says 'fruits' here, so that it might be in some way 'He shall eat the labors of your hands,' that is, of the practical powers.

The word is indeed somewhat shorthand, smoothing these promises to be given to the one fearing the Lord, as if they were complete, but not to the one loving him with all heart and all soul and strength; for 'Eye has not seen and ear has not heard, nor has it come up upon the heart of man, what God has prepared for those who love him' (1 Cor 2:9). To the one fearing the Lord, a gift of God is given, a partner and a companion, not a woman by chance, but one grafted into the true vine.

Who can find a woman of worth, a good wife, and a woman of manly strength? Such a thing is more precious than costly stones. Just as the opposite of evil is good, and the wrath of God is a spouse in a harsh manner, so also sons from God are given to the one fearing the Lord; they are not like many sons, but like young olive shoots surrounding and crowning his table. You will also understand these from the perfection of the one saying, 'But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God' (Ps 52:8). For the offspring of such an olive tree are called like young olive shoots. If anyone says that those not fearing the Lord often possess much in the property of children and in the prosperity of a wife, we will say that the present beatitude does not simply promise a wife and children, but all of this is depicted as a woman in a vineyard and children as young olive shoots; such things are not the lot of the ungodly.

From there: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, since the wife accompanying you is fertile, finding herself like a vine rejoicing with fruits (Ps 127:4). But also your offspring are not weak or female, but strong sons being around your table, bearing the food of light like young olive shoots. And your spiritual table exists, full of all those who nourish mind and soul. Be having in these things a blessing from the Lord; no one else, but the God-fearing shall receive from the Lord. This is shown through 'the Man' and 'every man.' Therefore, regarding the present things, one ought not to take them as being about a sensible woman and bodily children, since many having obtained the fear of God have possessed neither wife nor children. If, then, the things of the word are not entirely literal, the spiritual sense of the things expressed must be sought by every one existing in piety.

By ascent you will understand thus: those being captured by the enemy in a single blow would not say this, but the one alone, driving the enemies into flight anew until old age, becoming always a victor and a triumphalist over them (Ps 128:1-4). And he brought forward the proof of having fought them many times: 'For even I was not able; for He was strengthening me, the Lord, who crushes the enemies.' Regarding those being announced with boldness, not the one happening by chance, but the one seeing God...

english: He calls [him] a witness of the mind. And they show what is 'from my youth' (Psalm 71:5), and that having dared to speak from the womb and being drawn up for godliness, he opposes the devil and his allies and bodyguards, who are arrayed against him and fighting against him, and by no measure was he defeated by them.

The 'from my youth' is able to show that [he] is strong and being strengthened by Christ, from whom I have cast off old age, having cast away the old man with his deeds; having clothed himself with the new man, fighting against the aforementioned enemies, he was never overturned by them, but conquering unceasingly and steadily, and turning them to witness for Israel.

And the boast is not small, to be fought against by the devil and those around him, who do not possess this [strength]; for they are his friends and obedient ones. And everyone alone says, 'For indeed you were not able to trample upon me, having received authority from the Word of God, upon the lion and the scorpion, and to trample the lion and the dragon' (Luke 10:19). For having escaped all such things, the God crushing Satan under his feet, he says, 'Many times they have fought against me from my youth, and indeed they were not able; but I was able against them, being strengthened by the Lord. The sinners have stretched out their necks upon my back, they have lengthened their lawlessness' (Psalm 74:18).

It is a stain and very dangerous to have the enemies before [one's] face, having them sufficiently according to thought, and to harm and destroy them merely through seeing and through the senses, those whom we have perceived of them; it is proper to always turn away from them, casting them upon the back. For he who hastens toward God and virtue turns away from wickedness.

For if the sinners have stretched out [their necks] upon the face and before [one], they have harmed the heart, timely casting it into evil thoughts, and the sight through destructive spectacles, and the other senses harming through those things belonging to them. But he has the sinners behind, the one forgetting those behind, and stretching out [himself] toward those before, and going behind the Lord God; but he who follows the interpreted sinners turns away from the Lord, as to say God, 'They turned their backs upon me and not their faces' (Psalm 74:18). Mis—

For they have cast your instruction behind them, following the demons who are lovers of their heart. The lengthening of their lawlessness reveals the persistent wickedness of sinners who weave a series of sins like a rope, and by adding to those who have already received, they lengthen their lawlessness. The word weighs such people down: 'Woe to those who pile up sins,' as with a long rope and as with a heavy yoke, subduing their lawlessness. For their hands weave injustice, and as adding sin upon sin, they lengthen their own lawlessness. The Lord is righteous and has cut off the necks of sinners. The righteous Lord cuts off the neck of those who do not submit to his good yoke. But he makes this addition good for those who, having cast off their inclination and strength toward worthless things, submit to the Lord, who is all naked and bowed down.

And the wise of this world are themselves like stubble, having only their promise until this present life; and they are a heap of roofs for those who through them act and think that they have surpassed all. Therefore, it is a dried-up stubble, not casting its roots into the soil (that is, the sensible things), nor hastening toward a spiritual planting instead of stubble. Before they are even cut, they dry up, not filling the hands of the one harvesting this stubble, because they have unbelief. For the ungodly shall not rise in judgment, and 'he who does not believe is condemned' (John 3:18). Not only hands, but even the bosom of himself the harvester of this stubble will not fill, by not receiving them first into the bosom of Abraham, and then thereafter into the bosoms of the harvesting angel; for the Savior interpreted the harvesting angels as the harvester wielding a sickle in the prophet: 'Therefore I have cast away your prophets' (Matt 23:37). He himself also cleanses his threshing floor, having the winnowing fan in his hand to gather the wheat into the granary, but the chaff to burn with unquenchable fire. And who are those who hate Zion? They become not stubble, but like stubble, the weeds sown among the good seed by the evil one and being burned in the future.
